akhfash:1-1.t: He said: ﴿غَيْرَ مُحِلِّي ٱلصَّيْدِ﴾ — ﴿أَوْفُواْ بِٱلْعُقُودِ﴾ ﴿غَيْرَ مُحِلِّي ٱلصَّيْدِ﴾: (غيرَ) is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

akhfash:2-2.t:
[And] He said ﴿لاَ تُحِلُّواْ شَعَآئِرَ ٱللَّهِ﴾; its singular is "شعيرة" (rite).
 [And] He said ﴿وَلاَ يَجْرِمَنَّكُمْ شَنَآنُ قَوْمٍ﴾: "الشَنَئانُ" (hatred) is vowelled [in its second letter], like "الدَرَجان" and "المَيَلان"; it is from "شَنِئْتُه" (I hated him), so "أنا أشنَؤه" "شَنَئاناً". And He said ﴿لاَ يَجْرِمَنَّكُمْ﴾, i.e. let it not make it right (lawful) for you; because His saying ﴿لاَ جَرَمَ أَنَّ لَهُمُ ٱلْنَّارَ﴾ is only "it is true (ḥaqq) that theirs is the Fire". The poet said [in the kāmil metre; this is the one hundred and eightieth shāhid]:
وَلَقَدْ طَعَنْتُ أَبّا عُيَيْنَةَ طَعْنَةً * جَرَمَتْ فَزارَةُ بَعْدَها أَنْ يَغْضَبُوا
(I struck Abū ʿUyayna a thrust after which it became right for Fazāra to be angry.)
i.e. it was made right for them.
And His saying ﴿أَن صَدُّوكُمْ﴾ means "because they barred you". It has also been read ﴿إِنْ صَدُّوكُم﴾ in the sense of "if they bar you", i.e. "if they do [it]", i.e. if they intend* [it] and have not yet done it. You may also say that when they have already done it, as though you were relating what had not happened; as in the saying of Allah the Exalted ﴿قَالُوۤاْ إِن يَسْرِقْ فَقَدْ سَرَقَ أَخٌ لَّهُ مِن قَبْلُ﴾, when in their view the theft had already taken place.
And He said ﴿أَن تَعْتَدُواْ﴾, i.e. let not hatred of a people make it right for you to transgress, i.e. let that not drive you to aggression. Then He said ﴿وَتَعَاوَنُواْ عَلَى ٱلْبرِّ وَٱلتَّقْوَىٰ﴾.

akhfash:3-3.t:
And He said ﴿وَٱلْمَوْقُوذَةُ﴾, from (وُقِذَتْ) (it was beaten to death), so "هِيَ مَوْقُوذَةٌ".
﴿وَٱلنَّطِيحَةُ﴾ has the hāʾ [tāʾ marbūṭa] because it has been made like a noun, like "أَكِيلَةِ الأَسَدِ" (the lion's prey). [Otherwise] you would say "هِيَ أَكِيلٌ" and "هِيَ نَطِيحٌ", because whatever has [the sense of] "مَفْعُولَة", its "فَعِيل" is without the hāʾ, e.g. "القَتيِل" (slain) and "الصَريع" (felled) when you mean a woman, and "هِيَ جَريحٌ" (she is wounded), because you say "مَجْرُوحَةٌ".
And He said ﴿وَمَآ أَكَلَ ٱلسَّبُعُ﴾; in one dialect they lighten it to "السَبْع".
﴿وَمَا ذُبِحَ عَلَى ٱلنُّصُبِ﴾: its plural is "الأنْصاب".
﴿وَأَنْ تَسْتَقْسِمُواْ بِٱلأَزْلاَمِ﴾ means: "and that is forbidden"; its singular is "زُلَم" and "زَلَمَ" (divining arrow).
And He said ﴿مَخْمَصَةٍ﴾: you say "خَمَصَهُ الجُوع" (hunger emptied his belly); [مَخْمَصة] is like "المَغْضَبَة", because He meant the maṣdar (verbal noun).
[And He said] ﴿يَئِسَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ﴾ with hamza on the second yāʾ; it is of [the pattern] "فَعِل", "يَفْعِل". Giving kasra to the first yāʾ is a dialect usage, as with "لِعْبَ": some of them give kasra to the lām and the ʿayn, and they also make the ʿayn unvowelled while giving the lām fatḥa or kasra; and likewise "يئس". That is because when "فعل" has as its second letter one of the six [guttural] letters, they give its first letter kasra and leave it with kasra, as they do in "فعيل", e.g. "شِعير" and "صِهيل". Some of them make [the second] unvowelled and give the first kasra, as in "رِحْمَهُ اللهُ"; therefore you say "يِئْسَ", giving the yāʾ kasra and making the hamza unvowelled. [Translator's note: the text has «تسكر الياء», evidently for «تكسر الياء» "you give the yāʾ kasra".] This verse has been read ﴿نِعِمَّا يَعِظُكُمْ بِهِ﴾ according to that dialect in which they say "لِعِبَ". And some people say "نَعِمَ الرَّجُلُ زَيْدٌ"; it is permissible to give kasra to this nūn in "نَعِمَ", because what follows it is one of the six letters, just as "لِعِب" was given kasra. As for their saying that the ʿayn of "نِعِمّا" is unvowelled when assimilated, it is a mistake, because two unvowelled letters do not meet. But if you wish, you may make it covert (ikhfāʾ), putting it between assimilation and full pronunciation, so that it has the weight of a vowelled letter, just as ﴿إِنِّي لَيَحْزُنُنِيۤ﴾ was read with the first nūn given a trace (ishmām) of the ḍamma.
And He said ﴿ٱلْيَوْمَ أَكْمَلْتُ لَكُمْ دِينَكُمْ﴾, because Islam [still] had some obligations [to come]; when Allah had completed what He willed of it, He said ﴿ٱلْيَوْمَ أَكْمَلْتُ لَكُمْ دِينَكُمْ﴾ ﴿وَرَضِيتُ لَكُمُ ٱلأِسْلاَمَ دِيناً﴾ — not in any sense other than this.
And He said ﴿فَمَنِ ٱضْطُرَّ فِي مَخْمَصَةٍ غَيْرَ مُتَجَانِفٍ لإِثْمٍ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَّحِيمٌ﴾, as if He said: "then Allah is Forgiving, Merciful to him", as you say "عبدُ اللهِ ضَرَبْتُ" (ʿAbdullāh, I struck) meaning: I struck him. The poet said [in the wāfir metre; this is the one hundred and eighty-first shāhid]:
ثَلاثٌ كُلُّهُنَّ قتلتُ عَمْداً * فَأَخْزَى اللهُ رابعَةً تَعُود
(Three — all of them I killed deliberately; may Allah disgrace a fourth that returns.)
And another said [in the rajaz metre; this is the one hundred and eighty-second shāhid]:
قدْ أَصْبَحَتْ أُمُ الخِيارِ تَدَّعي * عَلَيَّ ذَنْباً كُلَّهُ لَمْ أَصْنعِ
(Umm al-Khiyār has come to accuse me of a sin, all of which I did not commit.)

akhfash:4-4.t:
And He said ﴿مَاذَآ أُحِلَّ﴾: if you wish, you take "ذا" as having the status of "الذي" (that which), and if you wish, you take it as zāʾida (redundant), as the poet said [in the basīṭ metre; this is the one hundred and eighty-third shāhid]: 
يا خُزْرَ تَغْلِبَ ماذا بالُ نِسْوَتِكُم * لا يَسْتَفِقنَ الى الدَيْرَيْنَ تَحْنانا
(O squint-eyed ones of Taghlib, what is the matter with your women, who never cease yearning for the two monasteries?)
"ذا" can only be zāʾida here, [since] if you said "ما الذي بال نسوتكم" it would not be [proper] speech. 
[And] He said ﴿ٱلْجَوَارِحِ﴾: these are the earners (hunting animals), as you say "فُلانٌ جارِحَةُ أَهْلِهِ" (so-and-so is the earner of his family) and "مالَهُمْ جارِحَةٌ", i.e. they have no slaves "ولا حافِرَةْ" (nor beasts of burden).
[And] He said ﴿كُلُواْ مِمَّآ أَمْسَكْنَ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾: [so] He put in ﴿مِنْ﴾, as He put it in [one's] saying "كانَ مِنْ حَديث" (there was some talk) and "قَدْ كانَ مِنْ مَطَرٍ" (there has been some rain); and His saying ﴿وَيُكَفِّرُ عَنكُم مِّن سَيِّئَاتِكُمْ﴾ and ﴿يُنَزِّلُ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مِن جِبَالٍ فِيهَا مِن بَرَدٍ﴾, which according to one explanation is "He sends down from the sky mountains in which there is hail". Some said ﴿وَيُنَزِّلُ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مِن جِبَالٍ فِيهَا مِن بَرَدٍ﴾ [means]: in the sky are mountains of hail, i.e. He makes the mountains of hail in the sky, and makes the sending down from them.

akhfash:5-5.t:
And He said ﴿مُحْصِنِينَ غَيْرَ مُسَافِحِينَ وَلاَ مُتَّخِذِيۤ أَخْدَانٍ﴾: by it He means the men. 
And He said ﴿أُحِلَّ لَكُمُ ٱلطَّيِّبَاتُ﴾ (and) there are made lawful ﴿لَكُمْ المُحْصنات﴾ of the women ﴿مُحْصِنِينَ غَيْرَ مُسَافِحِينَ﴾, i.e. they are made lawful for you in this state.

akhfash:6-6.t:
And He said ﴿وَٱمْسَحُواْ بِرُؤُوسِكُمْ وَأَرْجُلَكُمْ﴾: in the reading of some, He referred it back to "washing", because He had said ﴿فٱغْسِلُواْ وُجُوهَكُمْ﴾. And some read ﴿وَأَرْجُلَكُمْ﴾ as [referring to] wiping, i.e. and wipe your feet; this, people do not recognise. [Translator's note: the second reading is evidently meant to be the genitive «وَأَرْجُلِكُمْ», as the explanation shows; the text repeats the accusative form.] Ibn ʿAbbās said: "Wiping the two feet suffices." The genitive is permissible by proximity-agreement (itbāʿ) while in meaning it is "washing", as in "هذا جُحْرُ ضَبٍّ خَرِبٍ" (this is the ruined hole of a lizard, with "ruined" in the genitive next to "lizard"). The accusative is safer and better than this forced usage. Like it is the Arabs' saying "أَكَلْتُ خبزا ولبنا" (I ate bread and milk), though milk is not eaten; and they say "ماسَمِعْتُ برائحةٍ اطيبَ من هذهِ ولا رأيتُ رائحةً أطيبَ من هذِه" (I have not heard of a scent better than this, nor seen a scent better than this), and "ما رأيتُ كلاماً أصوبَ من هذا" (I have not seen speech more correct than this). The poet said [in the majzūʾ al-kāmil metre; this is the one hundred and eighty-fourth shāhid]: 
يا لَيْتَ زَوجَكِ قَدْ غَدا * مُتَقَلِّداً سَيْفاً وَرُمْحاً 
(Would that your husband had gone out in the morning girded with a sword and a spear.) [i.e. a spear is not "girded", but carried.]
And like it is ﴿لاَ تُحِلُّواْ شَعَآئِرَ ٱللَّهِ﴾ [2] ﴿وَلاۤ آمِّينَ ٱلْبَيْتَ ٱلْحَرَامَ﴾ [2].
And He said ﴿مَا يُرِيدُ ٱللَّهُ لِيَجْعَلَ عَلَيْكُم مِّنْ حَرَجٍ﴾, i.e. Allah does not will to place upon you hardship.

akhfash:9-9.t: And He said: ﴿وَعَدَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّالِحَاتِ لَهُم مَّغْفِرَةٌ وَأَجْرٌ عَظِيمٌ﴾: it is as if He explained the promise in order to make clear what He promised them, i.e. thus He promised them, and He said ﴿لَهُم مَّغْفِرَةٌ وَأَجْرٌ عَظِيمٌ﴾.

akhfash:12-12.t: [And He said] ﴿وَقَالَ ٱللَّهُ إِنِّي مَعَكُمْ لَئِنْ أَقَمْتُمُ ٱلصَّلاَةَ وَآتَيْتُمْ ٱلزَّكَاةَ وَآمَنتُمْ بِرُسُلِي﴾ ﴿لأُكَفِّرَنَّ عَنْكُمْ سَيِّئَاتِكُمْ﴾: the first lām is in the sense of an oath, and the second is for another oath.

akhfash:14-14.t: And He said ﴿وَمِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ قَالُواْ إِنَّا نَصَارَىٰ أَخَذْنَا مِيثَاقَهُمْ﴾, as you say "مِنْ عبدِ اللهِ أخَذْتُ دِرْهَمَه" (from ʿAbdullāh I took his dirham).

akhfash:22-22.t: [And] He said ﴿إِنَّ فِيهَا قَوْماً جَبَّارِينَ﴾: He made ﴿إِنَّ﴾ govern "القوم" and made "جَبْارِينَ" its qualifier, because ﴿فِيها﴾ is not a noun.

akhfash:26-26.t: [And] He said ﴿فَلاَ تَأْسَ عَلَى ٱلْقَوْمِ ٱلْفَاسِقِينَ﴾: it is from "أَسَي", "يَأْسىَ", "أَسَىَ شَدِيداً", which is grief. And "يَئِسَ" is from "اليَأس" (despair), which is the cutting off of hope, from "يَئِسوا"; and His saying ﴿وَلاَ تَيْأَسُواْ مِن رَّوْحِ ٱللَّهِ﴾ is from the cutting off of hope; it is from "يئست", and is like "إِيٍس" in its conjugation, or if you wish, like "خَشِيْتُ" in its conjugation. As for "أسَوْتَ", "تَأْسُوا", "أَسْواً", it is treating a wound. And "أُسْتُ", "أَؤُوسُ", "أَوْساً" is in the sense of: I gave. "أُسْتُ" is on the analogy of "قُلْتُ", and "أَسَوْتُ" [is on the analogy of] "غَزَوْتُ".

akhfash:27-27.t: [And] He said ﴿وَٱتْلُ عَلَيْهِمْ نَبَأَ ٱبْنَيْ آدَمَ بِٱلْحَقِّ﴾: the hamza belongs to "نَبَأ", because it is from "أَنْبَاتُهُ" (I informed him). The alif of "ابْنَيْ" goes [in pronunciation] because it is a connecting alif (alif waṣl) in the diminutive. [Translator's note: «في التصغير» "in the diminutive" is as written; it may be a corruption, perhaps of «في الدَّرْج» "in continuous speech".] When you pause, [you say] "نبأ" short, and you do not say "نبا", because it is the first term of an iḍāfa, so the alif is not retained in it*.

akhfash:30-30.t: And He said ﴿فَطَوَّعَتْ لَهُ نَفْسُهُ﴾, like "فَطَوَّعَتْ", meaning: "it made [it] seem permissible (rakhkhaṣat)". And you say "طَوَّقْتُهُ إمْريِ", i.e. I bound him with it. [Translator's note: the text compares «فطوّعت» with itself, and «طوّقته إمري» appears corrupt; translated as written.]

akhfash:31-31.t: And He said ﴿أَعَجَزْتُ أَنْ أَكُونَ مِثْلَ هَـٰذَا ٱلْغُرَابِ فَأُوَارِيَ﴾: ﴿فَأُوَارِيَ﴾ is accusative because you have conjoined it with fāʾ to [the verb after] ﴿أَنْ﴾. It does not have hamza, because it is from "وَارَيْتُ" (I concealed). And it is ﴿عَجَزْتُ﴾ [with fatḥa on the jīm] only because it is from "عَجَزَ", "يَعْجِزُ"; some say "عَجَزَ", "يَعْجُزُ", and "عَجِزَ", "يَعْجَزُ".

akhfash:32-32.t:
[And] He said ﴿مِنْ أَجْلِ ذٰلِكَ كَتَبْنَا عَلَىٰ بَنِيۤ إِسْرَائِيلَ﴾. If you wish, you drop the hamza of ﴿أَجْلِ﴾ and give the nūn its vowel, in the dialect of those who lighten the hamza. "الأَجْلُ" is wrongdoing (jināya), from "أَجَلَ", "يَأْجِلُ"; you say "قَدْ أَجَلْتَ عَلَيْنٰا شَرْاً" (you have brought evil upon us). Some Arabs say ﴿مِنْ جَرّا﴾, from "الجَريرة" (crime), putting it on [the pattern] "فَعْلَى".
And He said ﴿أَنَّهُ مَن قَتَلَ نَفْساً بِغَيْرِ نَفْسٍ أَوْ فَسَادٍ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ﴾, meaning: "or without corruption in the land".

akhfash:36-36.t: And He said ﴿لَوْ أَنَّ لَهُمْ مَّا فِي ٱلأَرْضِ جَمِيعاً وَمِثْلَهُ مَعَهُ لِيَفْتَدُواْ بِهِ مِنْ عَذَابِ يَوْمِ ٱلْقِيَامَةِ مَا تُقُبِّلَ مِنْهُمْ﴾, meaning: "if they had this with them for ransom, it would not be accepted from them".

akhfash:41-41.t:
And He said ﴿لاَ يَحْزُنكَ﴾, light, with fatḥa on the yāʾ; the people of Medina read ﴿يُحْزِنْكَ﴾, taking it from "أحْزَنَ". The Arabs say "أَحْزَنْتُه" and "حَزَنْتُهُ" (I grieved him).
And He said ﴿ٱلَّذِينَ يُسَارِعُونَ فِي ٱلْكُفْرِ مِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ قَالُوۤاْ آمَنَّا بِأَفْوَاهِهِمْ﴾, i.e. "from these and from these"; then He said, as a new start, ﴿سَمَّاعُونَ لِقَوْمٍ آخَرِينَ﴾, i.e. they are listeners. And if you wish, you take it with ﴿وَمِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ هِادُواْ﴾ ﴿سَمَّاعُونَ لِقَوْمٍ آخَرِينَ﴾ and then cut it off from the first speech. Then He said ﴿سَمَّاعُونَ لِلْكَذِبِ أَكَّالُونَ لِلسُّحْتِ﴾, according to that nominative of the first. As for His saying ﴿لَمْ يَأْتُوكَ﴾, here the speech is cut off, and the meaning is: "and among those who are Jews are listeners to falsehood — they listen to the speech of the Prophet ﷺ in order to lie about him — listeners for another people who have not yet come to you", meaning: "they listen on their behalf and inform them, while they have not come to you".

akhfash:45-45.t: And He said ﴿وَٱلْجُرُوحَ قِصَاصٌ﴾: if it is conjoined to what follows "أَنَّ", it is accusative, and the nominative is as a mubtadaʾ (subject), as you say "إنَّ زَيْداً منْطَلِقٌ وعَمْرٌ ذاهبٌ" (Zayd is leaving and ʿAmr is going); and if you wish, you say "وَعَمْراً ذاهبٌ" — accusative and nominative.

akhfash:46-46.t: [And] He said ﴿وَآتَيْنَاهُ ٱلإِنجِيلَ فِيهِ هُدًى وَنُورٌ﴾ [with a masculine pronoun], because some say "هِيَ الإِنْجيل" (it [fem.] is the Gospel) and some say "هُوَ الإِنجيل" (it [masc.] is the Gospel). It may also be because "the Gospel" is a book, so it is masculine in meaning, and they made it masculine on that basis — as He said ﴿وَإِذَا حَضَرَ ٱلْقِسْمَةَ أُوْلُواْ ٱلْقُرْبَىٰ﴾ and then said ﴿فَٱرْزُقُوهُمْ مِّنْهُ﴾, using the masculine, while "القِسْمَةُ" (the division) is feminine, because in meaning it is "the inheritance" and "the wealth", so He used the masculine on that basis.

akhfash:48-48.t:
And He said ﴿وَمُهَيْمِناً عَلَيْهِ﴾, meaning: "and as a witness over it" — accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). 
And He said ﴿شِرْعَةً وَمِنْهَاجاً﴾: "الشِّرْعَةُ" is religion (law), from "شَرَعَ", "يَشْرَعُ"; and "المِنْهٰاجُ" is the road, from "نَهَجَ", "يَنْهَجُ".

akhfash:51-51.t: And He said ﴿لاَ تَتَّخِذُواْ ٱلْيَهُودَ وَٱلنَّصَارَىٰ أَوْلِيَآءَ﴾, then He said ﴿بَعْضُهُمْ أَوْلِيَآءُ بَعْضٍ﴾ as a mubtadaʾ (subject) [i.e. a new sentence].

akhfash:53-53.t:
[And] He said ﴿وَيَقُولُ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ﴾ — accusative, because it is conjoined to His saying ﴿فَعَسَى ٱللَّهُ أَن يَأْتِيَ بِٱلْفَتْحِ﴾; and it has been read in the nominative as a new start (ibtidāʾ). Abū ʿAmr said the accusative is impossible, because "and perhaps Allah that those who believe say" is not permissible; this is only [possible as] "perhaps that they say", making ﴿أَنْ يَقُولَ﴾ conjoined to what follows "عَسَى", or it is a following [by association], as in their saying "أَكَلْتُ خُبْزاً وَلَبَنَاً" (I ate bread and milk) and: 
....................... * مُتَقَلِّداً سَيْفاً وَرُمْحاً
(… girded with a sword and a spear.)

akhfash:60-60.t:
And He said ﴿بِشَرٍّ مِّن ذٰلِكَ مَثُوبَةً عِندَ ٱللَّهِ﴾, as He said ﴿بِخَيْرٍ مِنْ ذلِك﴾*.
And He said ﴿وَعَبَدَ ٱلطَّاغُوتَ﴾, i.e. ﴿مَن لَّعَنَهُ ٱللَّهُ﴾ ﴿وَعَبَدَ ٱلطَّاغُوتَ﴾ (and [who] worshipped the ṭāghūt).

akhfash:63-63.t: And He said ﴿وَأَكْلِهِمُ ٱلسُّحْتَ﴾ and He said ﴿عَن قَوْلِهِمُ ٱلإِثْمَ﴾: He put both in the accusative because the verb [the verbal noun] falls upon them.

akhfash:64-64.t: And He said ﴿وَقَالَتِ ٱلْيَهُودُ يَدُ ٱللَّهِ مَغْلُولَةٌ غُلَّتْ أَيْدِيهِمْ﴾. They mentioned that it [the hand] is "the gift" and "the favour"; and likewise ﴿بَلْ يَدَاهُ مَبْسُوطَتَانِ﴾ — as you say "إنَّ لِفُلانٍ عِنْدِي يَداً" (so-and-so has a hand with me), i.e. a favour. And He said ﴿أُوْلِي ٱلأَيْدِي وَٱلأَبْصَارِ﴾, i.e. possessors of favours. "اليَد" (hand) may occur in [various] senses: you say "بَيْنَ يَدَي الدارِ" (between the two hands of the house), meaning: in front of it, though the house has no hands. [Translator's note: this is the author's interpretation, translated as written.]

akhfash:67-67.t: And He said ﴿فَمَا بَلَّغْتَ رِسَالَتَهُ﴾, and some read ﴿رِسالاتِهِ﴾. Both are correct, because "الرِّسالَة" (the message) may comprise "الرَّسائِل" (messages), as you say "هَلَكَ البَعِيرُ والشَّاةُ" (the camel and the sheep perished) and "أَهْلَكَ الناسَ الدينارُ والدِرْهَمُ" (the dinar and the dirham have destroyed people), meaning the collective.

akhfash:69-69.t: And He said: ﴿وَٱلصَّابِئُونَ وَٱلنَّصَارَىٰ﴾, and He said in another place ﴿والصّابِئِينَ﴾. The accusative is the regular analogy, by conjunction to what follows ﴿إِنّ﴾. As for this one, its nominative is on two lines. [First,] it is as if His saying ﴿إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ﴾ is in the position of the nominative in meaning, because it is a sentence that is a new start: one's saying "إنَّ زَيْداً مُنْطَلِقٌ" and "زَيْدٌ مُنْطَلِقٌ" without "إنّ" are the same in meaning; so if you wish, when you conjoin something to it, you make it follow the meaning, as you said "إنَّ زيداً مُنْطَلِقٌ وعمرٌو". But when it is put after the khabar (predicate) it is better and more frequent. [Second,] some said: since before it there is a verb, it was likened in form to what follows what precedes it — though its meaning is not within the verb before it, which is ﴿ٱلَّذِينَ هَادُواْ﴾ — so he made it follow it and put it in the nominative by it, even though it is not so in meaning. That is because things occur in the wording that are not so in the meanings; among them their saying "هذا جُحْرُ ضَبٍّ خَرِبٍ" (this is the ruined hole of a lizard), and their saying "كَذَبَ عَلَيْكُمْ الحَجُّ", putting "الحَجّ" in the nominative by "كَذَبَ", whereas its meaning is only "عَلَيْكُم الحَجَّ" (upon you is the pilgrimage), accusative by their command. And you say "هذا حَبُّ رُمّانِي" (these are the seeds of my pomegranate), attaching "the pomegranate" to yourself, though only "the seeds" are yours, not "the pomegranate". So the likes of this are permissible while the meaning is otherwise.

akhfash:71-71.t:
[And] He said ﴿ثُمَّ عَمُواْ وَصَمُّواْ كَثِيرٌ مِّنْهُمْ﴾ and did not say "ثُمَّ عَمِيَ وَصَمَّ" although it is a verb placed first, because He informed about a people that they became blind and deaf, then explained how many of them did that, as you say "رأيتُ قَوْمَك ثُلُثَيْهِم" (I saw your people — two thirds of them). Like that is ﴿وَأَسَرُّواْ ٱلنَّجْوَى ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُواْ﴾. And if you wish, you assign the verb to the latter [noun], putting it in the dialect of those who say "أَكَلُوني البَراغِيثُ" (the fleas ate me, with a plural verb), as he said [in the ṭawīl metre; this is the one hundred and eighty-fifth shāhid]: 
ولكِنْ دِيافِيٌّ أَبُوهُ وأُمُّهُ * بِحَوْراَنَ يَعْصُرْنَ السَّلِيطُ أَقارِبُه
(But [he is] one from Diyāf, his father and his mother; in Ḥawrān his kinsfolk press oil.)

akhfash:73-73.t:
[And] He said ﴿لَّقَدْ كَفَرَ ٱلَّذِينَ قَالُوۤاْ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ ثَالِثُ ثَلاَثَةٍ﴾. That is because they put "Jesus" and "Mary" with Him. So it is in speech: when one is with two, one says "ثالِثُ ثلاثَةٍ" (the third of three), as He said ﴿ثَانِيَ ٱثْنَيْنِ﴾ when there was only one with him. Whoever says "ثالثَ اثْنَيْنِ" (making two into three) is obliged to say "ثَانِيَ واحِدٍ" (making one into two). This is permissible in poetry, and in analogy it is sound. The poet said [in the wāfir metre; this is the one hundred and eighty-sixth shāhid]: 
وَلكِنْ لا أَخُونُ الجارَ حَتّىَ * يُزيلُ اللهُ ثالِثَةَ الأَثافِي
(But I do not betray the neighbour, until Allah removes the third of the hearthstones [i.e. never].)
Whoever says "ثانِيَ اثْنَيْنِ" and "ثالثُ ثَلاثَةٍ" says "حاديَ أَحَدَ عَشَرَ" (the eleventh of eleven) when a man is with ten. Whoever says "ثالثُ اثْنَيْنِ" says "حاديَ عَشْرَةَ" (the one making ten into eleven). As for the Arabs' saying "حاديَ عَشَرَ" and "ثانيَ عَشَر", this is in counting, when you say "second", "third", "fourth", "tenth" without saying "the tenth of such-and-such". When it passed ten and he wanted to say "حادي" and "ثاني", its meaning would not be known except by mentioning the ten, so he joined to it something of the letters of "ten".

akhfash:94-94.t: And He said ﴿لَيَبْلُوَنَّكُمُ ٱللَّهُ بِشَيْءٍ مِّنَ ٱلصَّيْدِ﴾ as an oath, i.e. by Allah, He will surely test you. Likewise this lām followed by the nūn occurs * only after an oath.

akhfash:95-95.t:
And He said: ﴿فَجَزَآءٌ مِّثْلُ مَا قَتَلَ مِنَ ٱلنَّعَمِ﴾, i.e. then upon him is a compensation like what he killed, of livestock. 
[And] He said ﴿يَحْكُمُ بِهِ ذَوَا عَدْلٍ مِّنْكُمْ هَدْياً﴾: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), and ﴿بَالِغَ ٱلْكَعْبَةِ﴾ is its qualifier. Your saying ﴿بَالِغَ ٱلْكَعْبَةِ﴾ is not definite, because it has the sense of tanwīn: when one says "هذا ضاربُ زَيْدٍ" in the dialect of those who drop the nūn, and he has not yet done it, it is indefinite. Like that is ﴿هَـٰذَا عَارِضٌ مُّمْطِرُنَا﴾: in it is some [sense of] tanwīn, except that it cannot be reached because of the implied noun [the pronoun]. 
Then He said ﴿أَوْ كَفَّارَةٌ طَعَامُ مَسَاكِينَ﴾, i.e. or upon him is an expiation — nominative with tanwīn — then He explained, saying "it is the feeding of poor people". Some read ﴿كَفّارَةُ طَعَامِ مَساكِينَ﴾, putting "expiation" in iḍāfa (genitive construct) with it. 
[And] He said ﴿أَو عَدْلُ ذٰلِكَ صِيَاماً﴾, meaning: or upon him is the equivalent of that in fasting — as you say "عَليْها مثلُها زُبْداً" (on it is its like in butter). Some read ﴿أَوْ عِدلُ ذلك صياما﴾ with kasra, and that is the [proper] way, because "العِدْل" is the equivalent. As for "العَدْل", it is the maṣdar (verbal noun): you say "عَدَلْتُ هذا بهذا عَدْلاً حَسَنا" (I balanced this with this well); and "العَدْل" is also the equivalent. He said ﴿وَلاَ يُقْبَلُ مِنْهَا عَدْلٌ﴾, i.e. an equivalent. So they distinguished between this and "عدل المتاع" (the pack-load of goods), as you say "امرأَةٌ رَزانٌ" (a sedate woman) and "حَجَرٌ رَزِينٌ" (a heavy stone).

akhfash:97-97.t: And He said ﴿جَعَلَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلْكَعْبَةَ ٱلْبَيْتَ ٱلْحَرَامَ قِيَاماً لِّلنَّاسِ﴾, and He said ﴿وَٱلْهَدْيَ وَٱلْقَلاَئِدَ﴾, i.e. and He made for you the sacrificial animals and the garlands.

akhfash:105-105.t: And He said ﴿يٰأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ عَلَيْكُمْ أَنْفُسَكُمْ لاَ يَضِرْكُمْ﴾, light, in the jussive because the answer to a command is jussive, taking it from "ضَارَ", "يَضِير". Some read ﴿يُضِرَّكُمْ﴾ and ﴿يَضُرُّكْمْ﴾, making the position jussive in both, except that he vowelled it because the rāʾ is doubled: its first [rāʾ] is unvowelled, so making its last unvowelled is not sound, since two unvowelled letters would meet. The best of these is ﴿لا يَضُرُّكُمْ﴾, nominative as a new start, because it is not a consequence of His saying ﴿عَلَيْكُمْ أَنْفُسَكُمْ﴾; He only informed [them] that it will not harm them.

akhfash:106-106.t: And He said ﴿شَهَادَةُ بَيْنِكُمْ﴾, then He said ﴿ٱثْنَانِ ذَوَا عَدْلٍ مِّنْكُمْ﴾, i.e. the testimony between you is the testimony of two. When "the testimony" was dropped, "the two" took its place and became nominative by its nominative, as He said ﴿وَسْئَلِ ٱلْقَرْيَةَ﴾, meaning: the people of the town; (القريةَ) became accusative by the accusative of "الأَهْل" and took its place. Then He conjoined ﴿أَوْآخَرَانِ﴾ to "the two".

akhfash:107-107.t:
And He said: ﴿مِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱسْتَحَقَّ عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلأَوْلَيَانِ﴾, i.e. of the first ones (الأَوَّلَيْنِ) against whom [the claim] was established*. And some read ﴿ٱلأَوْلَيَانِ﴾, and that is how we read it. [Translator's note: the quotation in the first sentence was evidently meant to give the other reading «ٱلأَوَّلِينَ», as the gloss shows; the text has ﴿ٱلأَوْلَيَانِ﴾ both times.] Because when He said ﴿يَقُومَانِ مَقَامَهُمَا مِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱسْتَحَقَّ عَلَيْهِمُ﴾, it was as if He had defined the two of them until they became like a definite noun in meaning; so He said ﴿ٱلأَوْلَيَانِ﴾, making the definite noun follow them as a badal (substitute). The like of this, which follows the meaning, is frequent. The rajaz poet said [this is the one hundred and eighty-seventh shāhid]:
عَلَيَّ يومَ تَملكُ الأُمُورَا * صَوْمُ شُهورٍ وَجَبَتْ نُذُورا
* وَبَدَناً مُقَلَّداً مَنْحُورا *
(Incumbent on me, on the day you take charge of affairs, is a fast of months that became binding as vows, and a garlanded sacrificial camel slaughtered.)
He made it [بَدَناً, accusative] depend on "أَوْجَبَ" (he made binding), because it has the meaning of "قَدْ أَوْجَبَ".

akhfash:114-114.t:
[And He said] ﴿قَالَ عِيسَى ٱبْنُ مَرْيَمَ ٱللَّهُمَّ رَبَّنَآ أَنزِلْ عَلَيْنَا مَآئِدَةً مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ تَكُونُ لَنَا عِيداً لأَوَّلِنَا وَآخِرِنَا﴾: He made ﴿تكونُ﴾ a qualifier of "the table", as He said ﴿هَبْ لِي مِن لَّدُنْكَ وَلِيّاً يَرِثُنِي﴾ — nominative if he makes it a qualifier, and jussive if he makes it an answer — as you say "أَعْطِني ثَوْباً يَسَعُني" (give me a garment that fits me) when you mean a roomy one, and "يَسَعْني" [jussive] when you make it an answer, as if you were stipulating that it fit you.
[And] He said ﴿وَآيَةً مِّنْكَ﴾, conjoined to "عيد" (festival), as if He said: "it will be a festival and a sign". It is mentioned that the reading of Ibn Masʿūd is ﴿تَكُنْ لَنَا عِيداً﴾.
Their saying ﴿هَلْ يَسْتَطِيعُ﴾ is not because they thought he was unable. Rather it is like the Arabs' saying: "أَتَسْتَطيعُ أَنْ تَذْهَبَ في هذهِ الحاجَةِ وتدَعَنا من كَلامِكَ" (can you go off on this errand and spare us your talk?), and you say "أَتَسْتَطيعُ أَنْ تَكُفَّ عَنّي فإِنِّي مَغْمُوم" (can you leave me alone, for I am distressed?). This is not because he is unable; rather he means "leave me alone", and he mentions ability to him in order to argue against him, i.e. you are able; when he reminds him of it, he knows that it is an argument against him. ﴿هَلْ تَسْتَطيعُ رَبَّكَ﴾ was read, as far as I know, only because of the obscurity of this other meaning — and Allah knows best. It is permissible, as if the verb were implied, meaning "can you call upon your Lord?" or "can you [ask] your Lord that you call upon Him?" — all of this is permissible.
"المائِدَةُ" is food, and the "فَعَلْتُ" form from it is "مِدْتُ", "أَمِيدُ". The poet said [in the rajaz metre; this is the one hundred and eighty-eighth shāhid]:
نُهْدِى رُؤوسَ المُجْرِمينَ الأَندادْ * إلى أمِيرِ المؤمِنِينَ المُمْتاد
(We send the heads of the rival criminals as gifts to the Commander of the Faithful, the one from whom bounty is sought.)
[And "المُمْتاد"] is "مُفْتَعِلٌ" from "مِدْتُ".

celaleyn:4-4.t: ﴿يَسْأَلُونَكَ﴾ O Muhammad, ﴿مَاذَا أُحِلَّ لَهُمْ﴾ of food? ﴿قُلْ أُحِلَّ لَكُمُ الطَّيِّبَاتُ﴾ the delightful things; ﴿وَ﴾ the game of ﴿مَا عَلَّمْتُمْ مِنَ الْجَوَارِحِ﴾ the hunting [animals], among dogs, beasts of prey and birds, ﴿مُكَلِّبِينَ﴾ a ḥāl (circumstantial), from كَلَّبْتُ الْكَلْبَ with a doubled consonant, i.e. "I sent it out after game"; ﴿تُعَلِّمُونَهُنَّ﴾ a ḥāl from the pronoun of مُكَلِّبِينَ, i.e. you train them ﴿مِمَّا عَلَّمَكُمُ اللَّهُ﴾ of the etiquette of hunting. ﴿فَكُلُوا مِمَّا أَمْسَكْنَ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ even if they killed it, provided that they did not eat of it — unlike [animals] that are not trained, whose game is not lawful. The sign [of being trained] is that it goes forth when it is sent, stops when it is checked, holds the game and does not eat of it; the least by which this is known is three times. If it eats of it, then it is not among what they "have held for" their owner, and eating it is not lawful, as in the hadith of the two Ṣaḥīḥs; and in it [is also] that the game of an arrow, when it is shot and the name of Allah is mentioned over it, is like the game of a trained hunting animal. ﴿وَاذْكُرُوا اسْمَ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ﴾ when sending it out; ﴿وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ إِنَّ اللَّهَ سَرِيعُ الْحِسَابِ﴾

celaleyn:5-5.t: ﴿الْيَوْمَ أُحِلَّ لَكُمُ الطَّيِّبَاتُ﴾ the delightful things; ﴿وَطَعَامُ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتَابَ﴾ i.e. the slaughtered animals of the Jews and the Christians, ﴿حِلٌّ﴾ lawful ﴿لَكُمْ وَطَعَامُكُمْ﴾ [given] to them ﴿حِلٌّ لَهُمْ وَالْمُحْصَنَاتُ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنَاتِ وَالْمُحْصَنَاتُ﴾ the free women ﴿مِنَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتَابَ مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ﴾ — it is lawful for you to marry them — ﴿إِذَا آتَيْتُمُوهُنَّ أُجُورَهُنَّ﴾ their dowers, ﴿مُحْصِنِينَ﴾ being married, ﴿غَيْرَ مُسَافِحِينَ﴾ committing fornication with them openly, ﴿وَلَا مُتَّخِذِي أَخْدَانٍ﴾ from among them, with whom you commit fornication secretly. ﴿وَمَنْ يَكْفُرْ بِالْإِيمَانِ﴾ i.e. apostatizes, ﴿فَقَدْ حَبِطَ عَمَلُهُ﴾ the righteous [deeds] before that, so it is not counted and he is not rewarded for it, ﴿وَهُوَ فِي الْآخِرَةِ مِنَ الْخَاسِرِينَ﴾ if he dies upon it.

celaleyn:6-6.t: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِذَا قُمْتُمْ﴾ i.e. you intend to stand ﴿إِلَى الصَّلَوةِ﴾ while you are in a state of ritual impurity (ḥadath), ﴿فَاغْسِلُوا وُجُوهَكُمْ وَأَيْدِيَكُمْ إِلَى الْمَرَافِقِ﴾ i.e. together with them, as the Sunna has made clear; ﴿وَامْسَحُوا بِرُءُوسِكُمْ﴾ the bāʾ is for attachment (ilṣāq), i.e. make the wiping cling to them without pouring water; and it is a generic noun (ism jins), so the least to which it truly applies suffices, which is the wiping of part of one's hair — and al-Shāfiʿī holds this; ﴿وَأَرْجُلَكُمْ﴾ in the accusative, conjoined to أَيْدِيَكُمْ, and in the genitive by proximity (jiwār), ﴿إِلَى الْكَعْبَيْنِ﴾ i.e. together with them, as the Sunna has made clear; they are the two protruding bones in each foot at the joint of the shank and the foot. Separating the washed hands and feet by the wiped head indicates that the order (tartīb) in the purification of these limbs is obligatory — and al-Shāfiʿī holds this; and from the Sunna it is taken that intention (niyya) is obligatory in it, as in the other acts of worship. ﴿وَإِنْ كُنْتُمْ جُنُبًا فَاطَّهَّرُوا﴾ then bathe; ﴿وَإِنْ كُنْتُمْ مَرْضَى﴾ with an illness that water harms, ﴿أَوْ عَلَى سَفَرٍ﴾ i.e. travelling, ﴿أَوْ جَاءَ أَحَدٌ مِنْكُمْ مِنَ الْغَائِطِ﴾ i.e. has broken his ablution, ﴿أَوْ لَامَسْتُمُ النِّسَاءَ﴾ the like of it preceded in the verse of al-Nisāʾ, ﴿فَلَمْ تَجِدُوا مَاءً﴾ after seeking it, ﴿فَتَيَمَّمُوا﴾ betake yourselves to ﴿صَعِيدًا طَيِّبًا﴾ pure earth, ﴿فَامْسَحُوا بِوُجُوهِكُمْ وَأَيْدِيكُمْ﴾ together with the two elbows ﴿مِنْهُ﴾ with two strikes; and the bāʾ is for attachment. The Sunna has made clear that what is meant is covering the two limbs entirely with the wiping. ﴿مَا يُرِيدُ اللَّهُ لِيَجْعَلَ عَلَيْكُمْ مِنْ حَرَجٍ﴾ narrowness, through what He has made obligatory for you of ablution, bathing and tayammum, ﴿وَلَكِنْ يُرِيدُ لِيُطَهِّرَكُمْ﴾ from ritual impurities and sins, ﴿وَلِيُتِمَّ نِعْمَتَهُ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ through Islam, by making clear the laws of the religion, ﴿لَعَلَّكُمْ تَشْكُرُونَ﴾ His blessings.

celaleyn:7-7.t: ﴿وَاذْكُرُوا نِعْمَةَ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ through Islam, ﴿وَمِيثَاقَهُ﴾ His covenant ﴿الَّذِي وَاثَقَكُمْ بِهِ﴾ which He covenanted with you upon, ﴿إِذْ قُلْتُمْ﴾ to the Prophet ﷺ when you pledged allegiance to him, ﴿سَمِعْنَا وَأَطَعْنَا﴾ in everything you command and forbid, of what we like and dislike. ﴿وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ﴾ regarding His covenant, lest you break it. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَلِيمٌ بِذَاتِ الصُّدُورِ﴾ of what is in the hearts — so of other things all the more.

celaleyn:8-8.t: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا كُونُوا قَوَّامِينَ﴾ upholding ﴿لِلَّهِ﴾ His rights, ﴿شُهَدَاءَ بِالْقِسْطِ﴾ with justice; ﴿وَلَا يَجْرِمَنَّكُمْ﴾ let not … induce you, ﴿شَنَآنُ﴾ hatred of ﴿قَوْمٍ﴾ i.e. the disbelievers, ﴿عَلَى أَلَّا تَعْدِلُوا﴾ so that you harm them because of their enmity. ﴿اعْدِلُوا﴾ towards enemy and friend; ﴿هُوَ﴾ i.e. justice, ﴿أَقْرَبُ لِلتَّقْوَى وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ إِنَّ اللَّهَ خَبِيرٌ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ﴾ and He will requite you for it.

celaleyn:9-9.t: ﴿وَعَدَ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ﴾ a goodly promise: ﴿لَهُمْ مَغْفِرَةٌ وَأَجْرٌ عَظِيمٌ﴾ which is Paradise.

celaleyn:10-10.t:
﴿وَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وَكَذَّبُوا بِآيَاتِنَا أُولَئِكَ أَصْحَابُ الْجَحِيمِ﴾
[Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:11-11.t: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اذْكُرُوا نِعْمَتَ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ إِذْ هَمَّ قَوْمٌ﴾ they are Quraysh, ﴿أَنْ يَبْسُطُوا﴾ to stretch out ﴿إِلَيْكُمْ أَيْدِيَهُمْ﴾ to assault you, ﴿فَكَفَّ أَيْدِيَهُمْ عَنْكُمْ﴾ and protected you from what they intended against you. ﴿وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَعَلَى اللَّهِ فَلْيَتَوَكَّلِ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ﴾

celaleyn:12-12.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ أَخَذَ اللَّهُ مِيثَاقَ بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ﴾ with what is mentioned afterwards; ﴿وَبَعَثْنَا﴾ — in it there is an iltifāt (shift) away from the third person — We appointed ﴿مِنْهُمُ اثْنَيْ عَشَرَ نَقِيبًا﴾ from every tribe a chief, to be a guarantor over his people for the fulfilment of the covenant, as an assurance against them. ﴿وَقَالَ﴾ to them ﴿اللَّهُ إِنِّي مَعَكُمْ﴾ with help and support. ﴿لَئِنْ﴾ a lām of oath, ﴿أَقَمْتُمُ الصَّلَوةَ وَآتَيْتُمُ الزَّكَوةَ وَآمَنْتُمْ بِرُسُلِي وَعَزَّرْتُمُوهُمْ﴾ supported them, ﴿وَأَقْرَضْتُمُ اللَّهَ قَرْضًا حَسَنًا﴾ by spending in His way, ﴿لَأُكَفِّرَنَّ عَنْكُمْ سَيِّئَاتِكُمْ وَلَأُدْخِلَنَّكُمْ جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهَارُ فَمَنْ كَفَرَ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ﴾ covenant ﴿مِنْكُمْ فَقَدْ ضَلَّ سَوَاءَ السَّبِيلِ﴾ has missed the path of truth; and al-sawāʾ originally means "the middle". Then they broke the covenant. Allah the Exalted said:

celaleyn:13-13.t: ﴿فَبِمَا نَقْضِهِمْ﴾ — mā is redundant (zāʾida) — ﴿مِيثَاقَهُمْ لَعَنَّاهُمْ﴾ We removed them far from Our mercy, ﴿وَجَعَلْنَا قُلُوبَهُمْ قَاسِيَةً﴾ which do not soften to accept faith. ﴿يُحَرِّفُونَ الْكَلِمَ﴾ that is in the Torah, of the description of Muhammad ﷺ and other things, ﴿عَنْ مَوَاضِعِهِ﴾ in which Allah placed it, i.e. they alter it; ﴿وَنَسُوا﴾ they abandoned ﴿حَظًّا﴾ a portion ﴿مِمَّا ذُكِّرُوا﴾ they were commanded ﴿بِهِ﴾ in the Torah, of following Muhammad. ﴿وَلَا تَزَالُ﴾ an address to the Prophet ﷺ, ﴿تَطَّلِعُ﴾ come upon ﴿عَلَى خَائِنَةٍ﴾ i.e. treachery ﴿مِنْهُمْ﴾ by breaking the covenant and other things, ﴿إِلَّا قَلِيلًا مِنْهُمْ﴾ of those who embraced Islam. ﴿فَاعْفُ عَنْهُمْ وَاصْفَحْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ الْمُحْسِنِينَ﴾ And this is abrogated by the Verse of the Sword.

celaleyn:14-14.t: ﴿وَمِنَ الَّذِينَ قَالُوا إِنَّا نَصَارَى﴾ attached to (mutaʿalliq) His saying ﴿أَخَذْنَا مِيثَاقَهُمْ﴾ as We took [it] from the Children of Israel, the Jews; ﴿فَنَسُوا حَظًّا مِمَّا ذُكِّرُوا بِهِ﴾ in the Gospel, of faith and other things, and they broke the covenant. ﴿فَأَغْرَيْنَا﴾ We cast ﴿بَيْنَهُمُ الْعَدَاوَةَ وَالْبَغْضَاءَ إِلَى يَوْمِ الْقِيَمَةِ﴾ through their splitting up and the difference of their desires, so that every sect declares the other to be disbelievers. ﴿وَسَوْفَ يُنَبِّئُهُمُ اللَّهُ﴾ in the Hereafter ﴿بِمَا كَانُوا يَصْنَعُونَ﴾ and He will requite them for it.

celaleyn:15-15.t: ﴿يَا أَهْلَ الْكِتَابِ﴾ the Jews and the Christians, ﴿قَدْ جَاءَكُمْ رَسُولُنَا﴾ Muhammad, ﴿يُبَيِّنُ لَكُمْ كَثِيرًا مِمَّا كُنْتُمْ تُخْفُونَ﴾ conceal ﴿مِنَ الْكِتَابِ﴾ the Torah and the Gospel, such as the verse of stoning and his description, ﴿وَيَعْفُوا عَنْ كَثِيرٍ﴾ of that, not making it clear when there is no benefit in it other than exposing you. ﴿قَدْ جَاءَكُمْ مِنَ اللَّهِ نُورٌ﴾ he is the Prophet ﷺ, ﴿وَكِتَابٌ﴾ the Qurʾān, ﴿مُبِينٌ﴾ clear and manifest,

celaleyn:16-16.t: ﴿يَهْدِي بِهِ﴾ i.e. by the Book ﴿اللَّهُ مَنِ اتَّبَعَ رِضْوَانَهُ﴾ by believing, ﴿سُبُلَ السَّلَامِ﴾ the paths of safety, ﴿وَيُخْرِجُهُمْ مِنَ الظُّلُمَاتِ﴾ disbelief ﴿إِلَى النُّورِ﴾ faith ﴿بِإِذْنِهِ﴾ by His will, ﴿وَيَهْدِيهِمْ إِلَى صِرَاطٍ مُسْتَقِيمٍ﴾ the religion of Islam.

celaleyn:17-17.t: ﴿لَقَدْ كَفَرَ الَّذِينَ قَالُوا إِنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ الْمَسِيحُ ابْنُ مَرْيَمَ﴾ in that they made him a god — they are the Jacobites, a sect of the Christians. ﴿قُلْ فَمَنْ يَمْلِكُ﴾ i.e. can avert ﴿مِنَ﴾ the punishment of ﴿اللَّهِ شَيْئًا إِنْ أَرَادَ أَنْ يُهْلِكَ الْمَسِيحَ ابْنَ مَرْيَمَ وَأُمَّهُ وَمَنْ فِي الْأَرْضِ جَمِيعًا﴾ i.e. no one has power over that; and if the Messiah were a god he would have been able to do it. ﴿وَلِلَّهِ مُلْكُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا يَخْلُقُ مَا يَشَاءُ وَاللَّهُ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ﴾ that He wills ﴿قَدِيرٌ﴾

celaleyn:18-18.t: ﴿وَقَالَتِ الْيَهُودُ وَالنَّصَارَى﴾ i.e. each of the two: ﴿نَحْنُ أَبْنَاءُ اللَّهِ﴾ i.e. like His sons in nearness and rank, and He is like our father in mercy and compassion, ﴿وَأَحِبَّاؤُهُ قُلْ﴾ to them, O Muhammad: ﴿فَلِمَ يُعَذِّبُكُمْ بِذُنُوبِكُمْ﴾ if you are truthful in that? A father does not punish his child, nor a beloved his beloved; yet He has punished you, so you are liars. ﴿بَلْ أَنْتُمْ بَشَرٌ مِمَّنْ﴾ among the totality of those ﴿خَلَقَ﴾ of mankind: you have what they have and owe what they owe. ﴿يَغْفِرُ لِمَنْ يَشَاءُ﴾ forgiveness for, ﴿وَيُعَذِّبُ مَنْ يَشَاءُ﴾ punishment for; there is no objecting to Him. ﴿وَلِلَّهِ مُلْكُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا وَإِلَيْهِ الْمَصِيرُ﴾ the return.

celaleyn:19-19.t: ﴿يَا أَهْلَ الْكِتَابِ قَدْ جَاءَكُمْ رَسُولُنَا﴾ Muhammad, ﴿يُبَيِّنُ لَكُمْ﴾ the laws of the religion, ﴿عَلَى فَتْرَةٍ﴾ an interruption ﴿مِنَ الرُّسُلِ﴾ since there was no messenger between him and Jesus, and the length of that was five hundred and sixty-nine years, so that ﴿أَنْ﴾ [you might] not ﴿تَقُولُوا﴾ when you are punished: ﴿مَا جَاءَنَا مِنْ﴾ redundant (zāʾida) ﴿بَشِيرٍ وَلَا نَذِيرٍ فَقَدْ جَاءَكُمْ بَشِيرٌ وَنَذِيرٌ﴾ so you have no excuse then. ﴿وَاللَّهُ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ﴾ and among that is punishing you if you do not follow him.

celaleyn:20-20.t: ﴿وَ﴾ remember ﴿إِذْ قَالَ مُوسَى لِقَوْمِهِ يَا قَوْمِ اذْكُرُوا نِعْمَةَ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ إِذْ جَعَلَ فِيكُمْ﴾ i.e. from among you ﴿أَنْبِيَاءَ وَجَعَلَكُمْ مُلُوكًا﴾ possessors of servants and retinue, ﴿وَآتَاكُمْ مَا لَمْ يُؤْتِ أَحَدًا مِنَ الْعَالَمِينَ﴾ of the manna and the quails, the splitting of the sea, and other than that.

celaleyn:21-21.t: ﴿يَا قَوْمِ ادْخُلُوا الْأَرْضَ الْمُقَدَّسَةَ﴾ the purified, ﴿الَّتِي كَتَبَ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ﴾ He commanded you to enter it, and it is al-Shām, ﴿وَلَا تَرْتَدُّوا عَلَى أَدْبَارِكُمْ﴾ by fleeing in fear of the enemy, ﴿فَتَنْقَلِبُوا خَاسِرِينَ﴾ in your striving.

celaleyn:22-22.t: ﴿قَالُوا يَا مُوسَى إِنَّ فِيهَا قَوْمًا جَبَّارِينَ﴾ from the remnants of ʿĀd, tall and possessed of strength, ﴿وَإِنَّا لَنْ نَدْخُلَهَا حَتَّى يَخْرُجُوا مِنْهَا فَإِنْ يَخْرُجُوا مِنْهَا فَإِنَّا دَاخِلُونَ﴾ it.

celaleyn:23-23.t: ﴿قَالَ﴾ to them ﴿رَجُلَانِ مِنَ الَّذِينَ يَخَافُونَ﴾ disobeying the command of Allah — they were Joshua (Yūshaʿ) and Caleb (Kālib), of the chiefs whom Moses sent to discover the condition of the tyrants — ﴿أَنْعَمَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِمَا﴾ with protection [from sin], so they concealed what they had learned of their condition except from Moses, unlike the rest of the chiefs, who divulged it, and so [the people] became cowardly: ﴿ادْخُلُوا عَلَيْهِمُ الْبَابَ﴾ the gate of the town, and do not fear them, for they are bodies without hearts; ﴿فَإِذَا دَخَلْتُمُوهُ فَإِنَّكُمْ غَالِبُونَ﴾ they said that out of certainty in Allah's help and the fulfilment of His promise. ﴿وَعَلَى اللَّهِ فَتَوَكَّلُوا إِنْ كُنْتُمْ مُؤْمِنِينَ﴾

celaleyn:24-24.t: ﴿قَالُوا يَا مُوسَى إِنَّا لَنْ نَدْخُلَهَا أَبَدًا مَا دَامُوا فِيهَا فَاذْهَبْ أَنْتَ وَرَبُّكَ فَقَاتِلَا﴾ them; ﴿إِنَّا هَاهُنَا قَاعِدُونَ﴾ from fighting.

celaleyn:25-25.t: ﴿قَالَ﴾ Moses then: ﴿رَبِّ إِنِّي لَا أَمْلِكُ إِلَّا نَفْسِي وَ﴾ except ﴿أَخِي﴾ and I have power over no one other than these two, so that I could compel them to obey; ﴿فَافْرُقْ﴾ so separate ﴿بَيْنَنَا وَبَيْنَ الْقَوْمِ الْفَاسِقِينَ﴾

celaleyn:26-26.t: ﴿قَالَ﴾ the Exalted to him: ﴿فَإِنَّهَا﴾ i.e. the Holy Land ﴿مُحَرَّمَةٌ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ for them to enter ﴿أَرْبَعِينَ سَنَةً يَتِيهُونَ﴾ wandering bewildered ﴿فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ — and it was nine farsakhs, as Ibn ʿAbbās said. ﴿فَلَا تَأْسَ﴾ grieve ﴿عَلَى الْقَوْمِ الْفَاسِقِينَ﴾ It is narrated that they would travel by night in earnest, and when morning came they would be in the very place from which they had started; and they would travel by day likewise, until all of them perished except those who had not reached twenty. It is said that they were six hundred thousand. Aaron and Moses died in the wilderness (al-tīh), and it was a mercy for them both and a punishment for those others. Moses asked his Lord at his death to bring him near to the Holy Land, a stone's throw, and He brought him near, as in the hadith. Joshua was made a prophet after the forty [years] and was commanded to fight the tyrants; so he marched with those who remained with him and fought them. It was a Friday, and the sun stood still for him for an hour until he had finished fighting them. Aḥmad narrated in his Musnad the hadith: "The sun was never held back for any human being except for Joshua, on the nights he marched to Bayt al-Maqdis."

celaleyn:27-27.t: ﴿وَاتْلُ﴾ O Muhammad, ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ to your people ﴿نَبَأَ﴾ the story of ﴿ابْنَيْ آدَمَ﴾ Abel (Hābīl) and Cain (Qābīl) ﴿بِالْحَقِّ﴾ attached to (mutaʿalliq) اتْلُ, ﴿إِذْ قَرَّبَا قُرْبَانًا﴾ to Allah — it was a ram from Abel and crops from Cain — ﴿فَتُقُبِّلَ مِنْ أَحَدِهِمَا﴾ he was Abel, in that a fire came down from the sky and consumed his offering, ﴿وَلَمْ يُتَقَبَّلْ مِنَ الْآخَرِ﴾ he was Cain; so he became angry and harboured envy within himself until Adam went on pilgrimage. ﴿قَالَ﴾ to him: ﴿لَأَقْتُلَنَّكَ﴾ He said: "Why?" He said: "Because your offering was accepted and not mine." ﴿قَالَ إِنَّمَا يَتَقَبَّلُ اللَّهُ مِنَ الْمُتَّقِينَ﴾

celaleyn:28-28.t: ﴿لَئِنْ﴾ the lām of oath, ﴿بَسَطْتَ﴾ you stretch out ﴿إِلَيَّ يَدَكَ لِتَقْتُلَنِي مَا أَنَا بِبَاسِطٍ يَدِيَ إِلَيْكَ لِأَقْتُلَكَ إِنِّي أَخَافُ اللَّهَ رَبَّ الْعَالَمِينَ﴾ in killing you.

celaleyn:29-29.t: ﴿إِنِّي أُرِيدُ أَنْ تَبُوءَ﴾ return ﴿بِإِثْمِي﴾ with the sin of killing me ﴿وَإِثْمِكَ﴾ which you committed before, ﴿فَتَكُونَ مِنْ أَصْحَابِ النَّارِ﴾ and I do not want to return with your sin if I kill you, and so be one of them. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿وَذَلِكَ جَزَاءُ الظَّالِمِينَ﴾

celaleyn:30-30.t: ﴿فَطَوَّعَتْ﴾ made attractive ﴿لَهُ نَفْسُهُ قَتْلَ أَخِيهِ فَقَتَلَهُ فَأَصْبَحَ﴾ and became ﴿مِنَ الْخَاسِرِينَ﴾ by killing him. And he did not know what to do with him, because he was the first dead person of the children of Adam on the face of the earth; so he carried him on his back.

celaleyn:31-31.t: ﴿فَبَعَثَ اللَّهُ غُرَابًا يَبْحَثُ فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ digging up the earth with its beak and its feet and throwing it over a dead crow that was with it, until it covered it, ﴿لِيُرِيَهُ كَيْفَ يُوَارِي﴾ cover ﴿سَوْءَةَ﴾ the corpse of ﴿أَخِيهِ قَالَ يَا وَيْلَتَا أَعَجَزْتُ﴾ [so as to be incapable] of ﴿أَنْ أَكُونَ مِثْلَ هَذَا الْغُرَابِ فَأُوَارِيَ سَوْءَةَ أَخِي فَأَصْبَحَ مِنَ النَّادِمِينَ﴾ over having carried him; and he dug for him and covered him.

celaleyn:32-32.t: ﴿مِنْ أَجْلِ ذَلِكَ﴾ which Cain did, ﴿كَتَبْنَا عَلَى بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ أَنَّهُ﴾ i.e. the matter (al-shaʾn) [is that] ﴿مَنْ قَتَلَ نَفْسًا بِغَيْرِ نَفْسٍ﴾ which it had killed ﴿أَوْ﴾ without ﴿فَسَادٍ﴾ it committed ﴿فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ such as disbelief, fornication, highway robbery or the like, ﴿فَكَأَنَّمَا قَتَلَ النَّاسَ جَمِيعًا وَمَنْ أَحْيَاهَا﴾ by refraining from killing it, ﴿فَكَأَنَّمَا أَحْيَا النَّاسَ جَمِيعًا﴾ Ibn ʿAbbās said: in respect of violating its sanctity and preserving it. ﴿وَلَقَدْ جَاءَتْهُمْ﴾ i.e. the Children of Israel ﴿رُسُلُنَا بِالْبَيِّنَاتِ﴾ the miracles, ﴿ثُمَّ إِنَّ كَثِيرًا مِنْهُمْ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ فِي الْأَرْضِ لَمُسْرِفُونَ﴾ exceeding the limit through disbelief, killing and other things. And [the following] was revealed concerning the ʿUranīs, when they came to Medina sick; the Prophet ﷺ permitted them to go out to the camels and drink of their urine and milk, and when they recovered they killed the herdsman of the Prophet ﷺ and drove off the camels:

celaleyn:33-33.t: ﴿إِنَّمَا جَزَاءُ الَّذِينَ يُحَارِبُونَ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ﴾ by waging war on the Muslims ﴿وَيَسْعَوْنَ فِي الْأَرْضِ فَسَادًا﴾ by highway robbery ﴿أَنْ يُقَتَّلُوا أَوْ يُصَلَّبُوا أَوْ تُقَطَّعَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَأَرْجُلُهُمْ مِنْ خِلَافٍ﴾ i.e. their right hands and their left feet, ﴿أَوْ يُنْفَوْا مِنَ الْأَرْضِ﴾ — aw is for arranging [the penalties] according to the cases: killing is for one who only killed; crucifixion for one who killed and took property; amputation for one who took property and did not kill; and banishment for one who only caused fear. Ibn ʿAbbās said this, and al-Shāfiʿī holds it; the sounder of his two opinions is that the crucifixion is for three [days] after the killing, and it is said: shortly before it. Attached to banishment is whatever resembles it in exemplary punishment, such as imprisonment and other things. ﴿ذَلِكَ﴾ the penalty mentioned ﴿لَهُمْ خِزْيٌ﴾ humiliation ﴿فِي الدُّنْيَا وَلَهُمْ فِي الْآخِرَةِ عَذَابٌ عَظِيمٌ﴾ which is the punishment of the Fire.

celaleyn:34-34.t: ﴿إِلَّا الَّذِينَ تَابُوا﴾ of the warmakers and the highway robbers ﴿مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ تَقْدِرُوا عَلَيْهِمْ فَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ﴾ to them for what they committed, ﴿رَحِيمٌ﴾ to them. It was expressed thus, rather than "then do not apply the ḥadd punishment to them", to convey that by his repentance only the ḥudūd [rights] of Allah fall from him, not the rights of human beings. This is what has appeared to me, and I have not seen anyone who has addressed it; and Allah knows best. So if he killed and took property, he is killed and [his hand] cut off, but not crucified; this is the sounder of al-Shāfiʿī's two opinions. And his repentance after he has been overpowered avails him nothing; this too is the sounder of his two opinions.

celaleyn:35-35.t: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ﴾ fear His punishment by obeying Him, ﴿وَابْتَغُوا﴾ seek ﴿إِلَيْهِ الْوَسِيلَةَ﴾ what brings you near to Him of obedience to Him, ﴿وَجَاهِدُوا فِي سَبِيلِهِ﴾ to raise His religion high, ﴿لَعَلَّكُمْ تُفْلِحُونَ﴾ that you may triumph.

celaleyn:36-36.t: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لَوْ﴾ it were established ﴿أَنَّ لَهُمْ مَا فِي الْأَرْضِ جَمِيعًا وَمِثْلَهُ مَعَهُ لِيَفْتَدُوا بِهِ مِنْ عَذَابِ يَوْمِ الْقِيَمَةِ مَا تُقُبِّلَ مِنْهُمْ وَلَهُمْ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ﴾

celaleyn:37-37.t: ﴿يُرِيدُونَ﴾ they wish ﴿أَنْ يَخْرُجُوا مِنَ النَّارِ وَمَا هُمْ بِخَارِجِينَ مِنْهَا وَلَهُمْ عَذَابٌ مُقِيمٌ﴾ perpetual.

celaleyn:38-38.t: ﴿وَالسَّارِقُ وَالسَّارِقَةُ﴾ the al in both is a relative [particle], [and it is] the mubtadaʾ (subject); because of its resemblance to a conditional, the fāʾ has entered its khabar (predicate), which is ﴿فَاقْطَعُوا أَيْدِيَهُمَا﴾ i.e. the right [hand] of each of them, from the wrist. The Sunna has made clear that that for which [the hand] is cut is a quarter of a dinar or more, and that if he does it again his left foot is cut off at the ankle joint, then the left hand, then the right foot, and after that he is given a discretionary punishment (yuʿazzar). ﴿جَزَاءً﴾ accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun) ﴿بِمَا كَسَبَا نَكَالًا﴾ a punishment for them ﴿مِنَ اللَّهِ وَاللَّهُ عَزِيزٌ﴾ prevailing over His affair, ﴿حَكِيمٌ﴾ in His creation.

celaleyn:39-39.t: ﴿فَمَنْ تَابَ مِنْ بَعْدِ ظُلْمِهِ﴾ turned back from theft ﴿وَأَصْلَحَ﴾ his conduct, ﴿فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ يَتُوبُ عَلَيْهِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾ In expressing it thus there is what was mentioned before: so by his repentance the right of the human being — the amputation and the return of the property — does not fall. Yes, the Sunna has made clear that if [the victim] pardons him before [the case] is brought to the imam, the amputation falls; and al-Shāfiʿī holds this.

celaleyn:40-40.t: ﴿أَلَمْ تَعْلَمْ﴾ the interrogative in it is for affirmation (taqrīr), ﴿أَنَّ اللَّهَ لَهُ مُلْكُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ يُعَذِّبُ مَنْ يَشَاءُ﴾ punishment for ﴿وَيَغْفِرُ لِمَنْ يَشَاءُ﴾ forgiveness for. ﴿وَاللَّهُ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ﴾ and among that are punishment and forgiveness.

celaleyn:41-41.t: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الرَّسُولُ لَا يَحْزُنْكَ﴾ the doing of ﴿الَّذِينَ يُسَارِعُونَ فِي الْكُفْرِ﴾ falling into it quickly, i.e. displaying it when they find an opportunity, ﴿مِنَ﴾ for explication (bayān) ﴿الَّذِينَ قَالُوا آمَنَّا بِأَفْوَاهِهِمْ﴾ with their tongues — attached to (mutaʿalliq) قَالُوا — ﴿وَلَمْ تُؤْمِنْ قُلُوبُهُمْ﴾ and they are the hypocrites, ﴿وَمِنَ الَّذِينَ هَادُوا﴾ a people ﴿سَمَّاعُونَ لِلْكَذِبِ﴾ which their rabbis fabricated, hearing it with acceptance, ﴿سَمَّاعُونَ﴾ from you ﴿لِقَوْمٍ﴾ for the sake of a people ﴿آخَرِينَ﴾ of the Jews ﴿لَمْ يَأْتُوكَ﴾ — they were the people of Khaybar: two married persons (muḥṣanān) among them committed fornication, and they disliked stoning them, so they sent Qurayẓa to ask the Prophet ﷺ about the ruling concerning them. ﴿يُحَرِّفُونَ الْكَلِمَ﴾ that is in the Torah, such as the verse of stoning, ﴿مِنْ بَعْدِ مَوَاضِعِهِ﴾ in which Allah placed it, i.e. they alter it, ﴿يَقُولُونَ﴾ to those whom they sent: ﴿إِنْ أُوتِيتُمْ هَذَا﴾ altered ruling, i.e. flogging — i.e. if Muhammad gives you a fatwa with it — ﴿فَخُذُوهُ﴾ then accept it, ﴿وَإِنْ لَمْ تُؤْتَوْهُ﴾ but he gives you a fatwa contrary to it, ﴿فَاحْذَرُوا﴾ against accepting it. ﴿وَمَنْ يُرِدِ اللَّهُ فِتْنَتَهُ﴾ his being led astray, ﴿فَلَنْ تَمْلِكَ لَهُ مِنَ اللَّهِ شَيْئًا﴾ in averting it. ﴿أُولَئِكَ الَّذِينَ لَمْ يُرِدِ اللَّهُ أَنْ يُطَهِّرَ قُلُوبَهُمْ﴾ from disbelief — had He willed it, it would have been. ﴿لَهُمْ فِي الدُّنْيَا خِزْيٌ﴾ humiliation through exposure and the jizya, ﴿وَلَهُمْ فِي الْآخِرَةِ عَذَابٌ عَظِيمٌ﴾

celaleyn:42-42.t: They are ﴿سَمَّاعُونَ لِلْكَذِبِ أَكَّالُونَ لِلسُّحْتِ﴾ with ḍamma on the ḥāʾ and with sukūn [لِلسُّحْتِ], i.e. the unlawful, such as bribes. ﴿فَإِنْ جَاءُوكَ﴾ for you to judge between them, ﴿فَاحْكُمْ بَيْنَهُمْ أَوْ أَعْرِضْ عَنْهُمْ﴾ this choice is abrogated by His saying {وَأَنِ احْكُمْ بَيْنَهُمْ} to the end of the verse; so it is obligatory to judge between them when they bring their case to us — this is the sounder of al-Shāfiʿī's two opinions. If they bring their case to us together with a Muslim, it is obligatory by consensus. ﴿وَإِنْ تُعْرِضْ عَنْهُمْ فَلَنْ يَضُرُّوكَ شَيْئًا وَإِنْ حَكَمْتَ﴾ between them ﴿فَاحْكُمْ بَيْنَهُمْ بِالْقِسْطِ﴾ with justice. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ الْمُقْسِطِينَ﴾ those who are just in judgement, i.e. He rewards them.

celaleyn:43-43.t: ﴿وَكَيْفَ يُحَكِّمُونَكَ وَعِنْدَهُمُ التَّوْرَاةُ فِيهَا حُكْمُ اللَّهِ﴾ of stoning — an interrogative of astonishment (taʿjīb), i.e. they did not intend by that to know the truth, but rather what is easier for them — ﴿ثُمَّ يَتَوَلَّوْنَ﴾ turn away from your ruling of stoning, which agrees with their Book, ﴿مِنْ بَعْدِ ذَلِكَ﴾ seeking of judgement; ﴿وَمَا أُولَئِكَ بِالْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾

celaleyn:44-44.t: ﴿إِنَّا أَنْزَلْنَا التَّوْرَاةَ فِيهَا هُدًى﴾ from error ﴿وَنُورٌ﴾ an exposition of the rulings; ﴿يَحْكُمُ بِهَا النَّبِيُّونَ﴾ of the Children of Israel ﴿الَّذِينَ أَسْلَمُوا﴾ submitted to Allah ﴿لِلَّذِينَ هَادُوا وَالرَّبَّانِيُّونَ﴾ the learned among them ﴿وَالْأَحْبَارُ﴾ the jurists, ﴿بِمَا﴾ i.e. because of that which ﴿اسْتُحْفِظُوا﴾ was entrusted to them, i.e. Allah charged them with guarding it, ﴿مِنْ كِتَابِ اللَّهِ﴾ [against] their altering it, ﴿وَكَانُوا عَلَيْهِ شُهَدَاءَ﴾ that it is true. ﴿فَلَا تَخْشَوُا النَّاسَ﴾ O Jews, in disclosing what you have of the description of Muhammad ﷺ, stoning and other things, ﴿وَاخْشَوْنِ﴾ in concealing it; ﴿وَلَا تَشْتَرُوا﴾ exchange ﴿بِآيَاتِي ثَمَنًا قَلِيلًا﴾ of this world, which you take for concealing them. ﴿وَمَنْ لَمْ يَحْكُمْ بِمَا أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ فَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ الْكَافِرُونَ﴾ in it.

celaleyn:45-45.t: ﴿وَكَتَبْنَا﴾ We prescribed ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ فِيهَا﴾ i.e. the Torah, ﴿أَنَّ النَّفْسَ﴾ is killed ﴿بِالنَّفْسِ﴾ when it has killed it, ﴿وَالْعَيْنَ﴾ is gouged out ﴿بِالْعَيْنِ وَالْأَنْفَ﴾ is cut off ﴿بِالْأَنْفِ وَالْأُذُنَ﴾ is cut off ﴿بِالْأُذُنِ وَالسِّنَّ﴾ is pulled out ﴿بِالسِّنِّ﴾ — and in one reading [these are] in the nominative in all four — ﴿وَالْجُرُوحَ﴾ in both ways ﴿قِصَاصٌ﴾ i.e. retaliation is taken in them where possible, such as the hand, the foot, the male organ and the like; and where it is not possible, [there is] an assessed compensation (ḥukūma). This ruling, although it was prescribed for them, is affirmed in our law. ﴿فَمَنْ تَصَدَّقَ بِهِ﴾ i.e. with the retaliation, by giving himself up [to it], ﴿فَهُوَ كَفَّارَةٌ لَهُ﴾ for what he committed. ﴿وَمَنْ لَمْ يَحْكُمْ بِمَا أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ﴾ in retaliation and other matters, ﴿فَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ الظَّالِمُونَ﴾

celaleyn:46-46.t: ﴿وَقَفَّيْنَا﴾ We caused to follow ﴿عَلَى آثَارِهِمْ﴾ i.e. of the prophets ﴿بِعِيسَى ابْنِ مَرْيَمَ مُصَدِّقًا لِمَا بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ﴾ before him ﴿مِنَ التَّوْرَاةِ وَآتَيْنَاهُ الْإِنْجِيلَ فِيهِ هُدًى﴾ from error ﴿وَنُورٌ﴾ an exposition of the rulings, ﴿وَمُصَدِّقًا﴾ a ḥāl (circumstantial), ﴿لِمَا بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ مِنَ التَّوْرَاةِ﴾ for the rulings in it, ﴿وَهُدًى وَمَوْعِظَةً لِلْمُتَّقِينَ﴾ and We said:

celaleyn:47-47.t: ﴿وَلْيَحْكُمْ أَهْلُ الْإِنْجِيلِ بِمَا أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ فِيهِ﴾ of rulings — and in one reading with the accusative of يَحْكُمَ and kasra on its lām, conjoined to the governed [element] of آتَيْنَاهُ. ﴿وَمَنْ لَمْ يَحْكُمْ بِمَا أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ فَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ الْفَاسِقُونَ﴾

celaleyn:48-48.t: ﴿وَأَنْزَلْنَا إِلَيْكَ﴾ O Muhammad ﴿الْكِتَابَ﴾ the Qurʾān ﴿بِالْحَقِّ﴾ attached to (mutaʿalliq) أَنْزَلْنَا, ﴿مُصَدِّقًا لِمَا بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ﴾ before it ﴿مِنَ الْكِتَابِ وَمُهَيْمِنًا﴾ a witness ﴿عَلَيْهِ﴾ — and al-kitāb [here] means the books. ﴿فَاحْكُمْ بَيْنَهُمْ﴾ between the People of the Book when they bring their cases to you ﴿بِمَا أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ﴾ to you, ﴿وَلَا تَتَّبِعْ أَهْوَاءَهُمْ﴾ deviating ﴿عَمَّا جَاءَكَ مِنَ الْحَقِّ لِكُلٍّ جَعَلْنَا مِنْكُمْ﴾ O nations, ﴿شِرْعَةً﴾ a law ﴿وَمِنْهَاجًا﴾ a clear way in religion upon which they walk. ﴿وَلَوْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ لَجَعَلَكُمْ أُمَّةً وَاحِدَةً﴾ upon a single law, ﴿وَلَكِنْ﴾ He divided you into groups ﴿لِيَبْلُوَكُمْ﴾ to test you ﴿فِيمَا آتَاكُمْ﴾ of the differing laws, to see the obedient among you and the disobedient. ﴿فَاسْتَبِقُوا الْخَيْرَاتِ﴾ hasten to them. ﴿إِلَى اللَّهِ مَرْجِعُكُمْ جَمِيعًا﴾ by the resurrection, ﴿فَيُنَبِّئُكُمْ بِمَا كُنْتُمْ فِيهِ تَخْتَلِفُونَ﴾ of the matter of religion, and He will requite each of you for his deeds.

celaleyn:49-49.t: ﴿وَأَنِ احْكُمْ بَيْنَهُمْ بِمَا أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ وَلَا تَتَّبِعْ أَهْوَاءَهُمْ وَاحْذَرْهُمْ﴾ lest ﴿أَنْ﴾ [— i.e. so that they do] not — ﴿يَفْتِنُوكَ﴾ lead you astray ﴿عَنْ بَعْضِ مَا أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ إِلَيْكَ فَإِنْ تَوَلَّوْا﴾ from the revealed ruling and want something else, ﴿فَاعْلَمْ أَنَّمَا يُرِيدُ اللَّهُ أَنْ يُصِيبَهُمْ﴾ with punishment in this world ﴿بِبَعْضِ ذُنُوبِهِمْ﴾ which they committed, among them the turning away; and He will requite them for all of them in the Hereafter. ﴿وَإِنَّ كَثِيرًا مِنَ النَّاسِ لَفَاسِقُونَ﴾

celaleyn:50-50.t: ﴿أَفَحُكْمَ الْجَاهِلِيَّةِ يَبْغُونَ﴾ with yāʾ and tāʾ — do they seek [the judgement of the Jāhiliyya], of compromise and partiality, when they turn away? An interrogative of disavowal (istifhām inkārī). ﴿وَمَنْ﴾ i.e. no one ﴿أَحْسَنُ مِنَ اللَّهِ حُكْمًا لِقَوْمٍ﴾ in the view of a people ﴿يُوقِنُونَ﴾ in Him? They are singled out for mention because they are the ones who reflect on it.

celaleyn:51-51.t: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لَا تَتَّخِذُوا الْيَهُودَ وَالنَّصَارَى أَوْلِيَاءَ﴾ befriending them and loving them; ﴿بَعْضُهُمْ أَوْلِيَاءُ بَعْضٍ﴾ because of their being united in disbelief. ﴿وَمَنْ يَتَوَلَّهُمْ مِنْكُمْ فَإِنَّهُ مِنْهُمْ﴾ among their number. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يَهْدِي الْقَوْمَ الظَّالِمِينَ﴾ through their befriending the disbelievers.

celaleyn:52-52.t: ﴿فَتَرَى الَّذِينَ فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ مَرَضٌ﴾ weakness of belief, such as ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy the hypocrite, ﴿يُسَارِعُونَ فِيهِمْ﴾ in befriending them, ﴿يَقُولُونَ﴾ excusing themselves for it: ﴿نَخْشَى أَنْ تُصِيبَنَا دَائِرَةٌ﴾ with which fortune turns against us, such as drought or defeat, and Muhammad's affair is not completed and so they [the Jews] would not supply us with provisions. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿فَعَسَى اللَّهُ أَنْ يَأْتِيَ بِالْفَتْحِ﴾ with victory for His Prophet by making his religion prevail ﴿أَوْ أَمْرٍ مِنْ عِنْدِهِ﴾ by tearing away the cover of the hypocrites and exposing them, ﴿فَيُصْبِحُوا عَلَى مَا أَسَرُّوا فِي أَنْفُسِهِمْ﴾ of doubt and befriending the disbelievers ﴿نَادِمِينَ﴾

celaleyn:53-53.t: ﴿وَيَقُولُ﴾ in the nominative as a resumption (istiʾnāf), with wāw and without it, and in the accusative, conjoined to يَأْتِيَ, ﴿الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾ to one another when their cover has been torn away, in astonishment: ﴿أَهَؤُلَاءِ الَّذِينَ أَقْسَمُوا بِاللَّهِ جَهْدَ أَيْمَانِهِمْ﴾ with the utmost of their effort in them, ﴿إِنَّهُمْ لَمَعَكُمْ﴾ in religion? Allah the Exalted said: ﴿حَبِطَتْ﴾ have come to nothing ﴿أَعْمَالُهُمْ﴾ righteous ones, ﴿فَأَصْبَحُوا﴾ and they have become ﴿خَاسِرِينَ﴾ [losers of] this world through exposure and of the Hereafter through punishment.

celaleyn:54-54.t: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مَنْ يَرْتَدِدْ﴾ with the separated form and with assimilation (idghām) [يَرْتَدَّ], turns back ﴿مِنْكُمْ عَنْ دِينِهِ﴾ to disbelief — a report of what Allah the Exalted knew would happen; and a group did apostatize after the death of the Prophet ﷺ — ﴿فَسَوْفَ يَأْتِي اللَّهُ﴾ in their place ﴿بِقَوْمٍ يُحِبُّهُمْ وَيُحِبُّونَهُ﴾ He ﷺ said: "They are the people of this one, and he pointed to Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī" — al-Ḥākim narrated it in his Ṣaḥīḥ; ﴿أَذِلَّةٍ﴾ gentle ﴿عَلَى الْمُؤْمِنِينَ أَعِزَّةٍ﴾ severe ﴿عَلَى الْكَافِرِينَ يُجَاهِدُونَ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ وَلَا يَخَافُونَ لَوْمَةَ لَائِمٍ﴾ in it, as the hypocrites fear the blame of the disbelievers. ﴿ذَلِكَ﴾ the attributes mentioned ﴿فَضْلُ اللَّهِ يُؤْتِيهِ مَنْ يَشَاءُ وَاللَّهُ وَاسِعٌ﴾ abundant in bounty, ﴿عَلِيمٌ﴾ of who is worthy of it. And [the following] was revealed when Ibn Salām said, "O Messenger of Allah, our people have shunned us":

celaleyn:55-55.t: ﴿إِنَّمَا وَلِيُّكُمُ اللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُ وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا الَّذِينَ يُقِيمُونَ الصَّلَوةَ وَيُؤْتُونَ الزَّكَوةَ وَهُمْ رَاكِعُونَ﴾ humble, or [it means] they pray voluntary prayers.

celaleyn:56-56.t: ﴿وَمَنْ يَتَوَلَّ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾ and so helps and supports them, ﴿فَإِنَّ حِزْبَ اللَّهِ هُمُ الْغَالِبُونَ﴾ because of His supporting them. He put it in the place of "then they [will prevail]" to make clear that they are of His party, i.e. His followers.

celaleyn:57-57.t: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لَا تَتَّخِذُوا الَّذِينَ اتَّخَذُوا دِينَكُمْ هُزُوًا﴾ an object of mockery ﴿وَلَعِبًا مِنَ﴾ for explication (bayān) ﴿الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتَابَ مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ وَالْكُفَّارِ﴾ the idolaters — in the genitive and the accusative [وَالْكُفَّارَ] — ﴿أَوْلِيَاءَ وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ﴾ by abandoning friendship with them, ﴿إِنْ كُنْتُمْ مُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ truthful in your faith.

celaleyn:58-58.t: ﴿وَ﴾ those who, ﴿إِذَا نَادَيْتُمْ﴾ you call ﴿إِلَى الصَّلَوةِ﴾ with the adhān, ﴿اتَّخَذُوهَا﴾ i.e. the prayer ﴿هُزُوًا وَلَعِبًا﴾ by mocking it and laughing among themselves. ﴿ذَلِكَ﴾ taking [it so] ﴿بِأَنَّهُمْ﴾ i.e. because they are ﴿قَوْمٌ لَا يَعْقِلُونَ﴾ And [the following] was revealed when the Jews said to the Prophet ﷺ, "Which of the messengers do you believe in?" and he said: {بِاللَّهِ وَمَا أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْنَا} to the end of the verse; and when he mentioned Jesus they said, "We know of no religion worse than your religion."

celaleyn:59-59.t: ﴿قُلْ يَا أَهْلَ الْكِتَابِ هَلْ تَنْقِمُونَ﴾ do you reproach ﴿مِنَّا إِلَّا أَنْ آمَنَّا بِاللَّهِ وَمَا أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْنَا وَمَا أُنْزِلَ مِنْ قَبْلُ﴾ to the prophets, ﴿وَأَنَّ أَكْثَرَكُمْ فَاسِقُونَ﴾ conjoined to أَنْ آمَنَّا. The meaning: you reproach nothing except our faith and our differing from you in your not accepting it, which is expressed by the fisq (transgression) that follows necessarily from it; and this is not something to be reproached.

celaleyn:60-60.t: ﴿قُلْ هَلْ أُنَبِّئُكُمْ﴾ shall I inform you ﴿بِشَرٍّ مِنْ﴾ the people of ﴿ذَلِكَ﴾ which you reproach ﴿مَثُوبَةً﴾ a recompense, in the sense of requital, ﴿عِنْدَ اللَّهِ﴾? It is ﴿مَنْ لَعَنَهُ اللَّهُ﴾ removed him far from His mercy ﴿وَغَضِبَ عَلَيْهِ وَجَعَلَ مِنْهُمُ الْقِرَدَةَ وَالْخَنَازِيرَ﴾ by transformation, ﴿وَ﴾ who ﴿عَبَدَ الطَّاغُوتَ﴾ Satan, by obeying him. In مِنْهُمْ He took into account the meaning of مَنْ, and in what precedes it its wording; and they are the Jews. In one reading [it is] with ḍamma on the bāʾ of عَبَدَ and annexed to what follows it — a collective noun for ʿabd — and its accusative is by conjunction with الْقِرَدَةَ. ﴿أُولَئِكَ شَرٌّ مَكَانًا﴾ a tamyīz (specification), because their abode is the Fire, ﴿وَأَضَلُّ عَنْ سَوَاءِ السَّبِيلِ﴾ the path of truth; the origin of al-sawāʾ is "the middle". "Worse" and "further astray" are mentioned in response to their saying, "We know of no religion worse than your religion."

celaleyn:61-61.t: ﴿وَإِذَا جَاءُوكُمْ﴾ i.e. the hypocrites of the Jews, ﴿قَالُوا آمَنَّا وَقَدْ دَخَلُوا﴾ to you, enveloped ﴿بِالْكُفْرِ وَهُمْ قَدْ خَرَجُوا﴾ from you, enveloped ﴿بِهِ﴾ and ﴿لَمْ يُؤْمِنُوا﴾ [Translator's note: لَمْ يُؤْمِنُوا is al-Jalalayn's gloss, not Quranic text, though the source places it within ﴿…﴾.] ﴿وَاللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ بِمَا كَانُوا يَكْتُمُونَ﴾ [it — هُ in the source], of hypocrisy.

celaleyn:62-62.t: ﴿وَتَرَى كَثِيرًا مِنْهُمْ﴾ i.e. the Jews, ﴿يُسَارِعُونَ﴾ falling quickly ﴿فِي الْإِثْمِ﴾ lying ﴿وَالْعُدْوَانِ﴾ wrongdoing ﴿وَأَكْلِهِمُ السُّحْتَ﴾ the unlawful, such as bribes. ﴿لَبِئْسَ مَا كَانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ﴾ [it — هُ in the source], this deed of theirs.

celaleyn:63-63.t: ﴿لَوْلَا﴾ why do not ﴿يَنْهَاهُمُ الرَّبَّانِيُّونَ وَالْأَحْبَارُ﴾ among them ﴿عَنْ قَوْلِهِمُ الْإِثْمَ﴾ lying ﴿وَأَكْلِهِمُ السُّحْتَ لَبِئْسَ مَا كَانُوا يَصْنَعُونَ﴾ [it — هُ in the source], their failure to forbid them.

celaleyn:64-64.t: ﴿وَقَالَتِ الْيَهُودُ﴾ when they were straitened because of their denying the Prophet ﷺ, after having been the wealthiest of people: ﴿يَدُ اللَّهِ مَغْلُولَةٌ﴾ withheld from pouring out provision on us — by it they alluded to miserliness; Allah is exalted far above that. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿غُلَّتْ﴾ may [their hands] be held back ﴿أَيْدِيهِمْ﴾ from doing good deeds — an imprecation against them — ﴿وَلُعِنُوا بِمَا قَالُوا بَلْ يَدَاهُ مَبْسُوطَتَانِ﴾ an intensification in describing [Him] with generosity; and "hand" is put in the dual to convey abundance, since the utmost a generous person can give of his wealth is to give with both his hands. ﴿يُنْفِقُ كَيْفَ يَشَاءُ﴾ whether expanding or restricting; there is no objecting to Him. ﴿وَلَيَزِيدَنَّ كَثِيرًا مِنْهُمْ مَا أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْكَ مِنْ رَبِّكَ﴾ of the Qurʾān ﴿طُغْيَانًا وَكُفْرًا﴾ because of their disbelief in it. ﴿وَأَلْقَيْنَا بَيْنَهُمُ الْعَدَاوَةَ وَالْبَغْضَاءَ إِلَى يَوْمِ الْقِيَمَةِ﴾ so every sect of them opposes the other. ﴿كُلَّمَا أَوْقَدُوا نَارًا لِلْحَرْبِ﴾ i.e. for war against the Prophet ﷺ, ﴿أَطْفَأَهَا اللَّهُ﴾ i.e. whenever they intended it, He turned them back; ﴿وَيَسْعَوْنَ فِي الْأَرْضِ فَسَادًا﴾ i.e. causing corruption through acts of disobedience; ﴿وَاللَّهُ لَا يُحِبُّ الْمُفْسِدِينَ﴾ in the sense that He punishes them.

celaleyn:65-65.t: ﴿وَلَوْ أَنَّ أَهْلَ الْكِتَابِ آمَنُوا﴾ in Muhammad ﷺ ﴿وَاتَّقَوْا﴾ disbelief, ﴿لَكَفَّرْنَا عَنْهُمْ سَيِّئَاتِهِمْ وَلَأَدْخَلْنَاهُمْ جَنَّاتِ النَّعِيمِ﴾

celaleyn:66-66.t: ﴿وَلَوْ أَنَّهُمْ أَقَامُوا التَّوْرَاةَ وَالْإِنْجِيلَ﴾ by acting on what is in them, and among it is faith in the Prophet ﷺ, ﴿وَمَا أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْهِمْ﴾ of the books ﴿مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ لَأَكَلُوا مِنْ فَوْقِهِمْ وَمِنْ تَحْتِ أَرْجُلِهِمْ﴾ in that provision would be made ample for them and would pour forth from every direction. ﴿مِنْهُمْ أُمَّةٌ﴾ a group ﴿مُقْتَصِدَةٌ﴾ that acts upon it — they are those who believed in the Prophet ﷺ, such as ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām and his companions; ﴿وَكَثِيرٌ مِنْهُمْ سَاءَ﴾ evil is ﴿مَا﴾ a thing ﴿يَعْمَلُونَ﴾ [it — هُ in the source].

celaleyn:67-67.t: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الرَّسُولُ بَلِّغْ﴾ all of ﴿مَا أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْكَ مِنْ رَبِّكَ﴾ and conceal nothing of it for fear of being harmed. ﴿وَإِنْ لَمْ تَفْعَلْ﴾ i.e. you do not convey all that has been sent down to you, ﴿فَمَا بَلَّغْتَ رِسَالَتَهُ﴾ in the singular and the plural, because concealing part of it is like concealing all of it. ﴿وَاللَّهُ يَعْصِمُكَ مِنَ النَّاسِ﴾ from their killing you. He ﷺ used to be guarded until it was revealed, and then he said: "Go away, for Allah has protected me" — al-Ḥākim narrated it. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يَهْدِي الْقَوْمَ الْكَافِرِينَ﴾

celaleyn:68-68.t: ﴿قُلْ يَا أَهْلَ الْكِتَابِ لَسْتُمْ عَلَى شَيْءٍ﴾ of religion that counts, ﴿حَتَّى تُقِيمُوا التَّوْرَاةَ وَالْإِنْجِيلَ وَمَا أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْكُمْ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ﴾ by acting on what is in it, and among it is faith in me. ﴿وَلَيَزِيدَنَّ كَثِيرًا﴾ ﴿مِنْهُمْ مَا أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْكَ مِنْ رَبِّكَ﴾ of the Qurʾān ﴿طُغْيَانًا وَكُفْرًا﴾ because of their disbelief in it; ﴿فَلَا تَأْسَ﴾ grieve ﴿عَلَى الْقَوْمِ الْكَافِرِينَ﴾ if they do not believe in you, i.e. do not be concerned about them.

celaleyn:69-69.t: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَالَّذِينَ هَادُوا﴾ they are the Jews — a mubtadaʾ (subject) — ﴿وَالصَّابِئُونَ﴾ a sect of them, ﴿وَالنَّصَارَى﴾ — and from the mubtadaʾ is made a badal (substitute): ﴿مَنْ آمَنَ﴾ of them ﴿بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ وَعَمِلَ صَالِحًا فَلَا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ﴾ in the Hereafter — the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ, and indicating the khabar of inna.

celaleyn:70-70.t: ﴿لَقَدْ أَخَذْنَا مِيثَاقَ بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ﴾ upon faith in Allah and His messengers, ﴿وَأَرْسَلْنَا إِلَيْهِمْ رُسُلًا كُلَّمَا جَاءَهُمْ رَسُولٌ﴾ of them ﴿بِمَا لَا تَهْوَى أَنْفُسُهُمْ﴾ of the truth, they denied him: ﴿فَرِيقًا﴾ of them ﴿كَذَّبُوا وَفَرِيقًا﴾ of them ﴿يَقْتُلُونَ﴾ such as Zakariyyā and Yaḥyā. Expressing it thus, rather than "they killed", is a narration of the past situation (ḥikāyat al-ḥāl al-māḍiya), for the sake of the verse-ending (fāṣila).

celaleyn:71-71.t: ﴿وَحَسِبُوا﴾ they thought ﴿أَ﴾ n ﴿لَا تَكُونُ﴾ — in the nominative, so that an is lightened (mukhaffafa), and in the accusative [تَكُونَ], so that it is the one that puts [the verb] in the accusative — i.e. there would not occur ﴿فِتْنَةٌ﴾ punishment upon them for denying the messengers and killing them; ﴿فَعَمُوا﴾ to the truth, so they did not see it, ﴿وَصَمُّوا﴾ to listening to it; ﴿ثُمَّ تَابَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ when they repented, ﴿ثُمَّ عَمُوا وَصَمُّوا﴾ a second time, ﴿كَثِيرٌ مِنْهُمْ﴾ a badal (substitute) from the pronoun. ﴿وَاللَّهُ بَصِيرٌ بِمَا يَعْمَلُونَ﴾ and He will requite them for it.

celaleyn:72-72.t: ﴿لَقَدْ كَفَرَ الَّذِينَ قَالُوا إِنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ الْمَسِيحُ ابْنُ مَرْيَمَ﴾ the like of it has preceded. ﴿وَقَالَ﴾ to them ﴿الْمَسِيحُ يَا بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ اعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ رَبِّي وَرَبَّكُمْ﴾ for I am a servant and not a god. ﴿إِنَّهُ مَنْ يُشْرِكْ بِاللَّهِ﴾ another in worship, ﴿فَقَدْ حَرَّمَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ الْجَنَّةَ﴾ has barred him from entering it, ﴿وَمَأْوَاهُ النَّارُ وَمَا لِلظَّالِمِينَ مِنْ﴾ redundant (zāʾida) ﴿أَنْصَارٍ﴾ to protect them from the punishment of Allah.

celaleyn:73-73.t: ﴿لَقَدْ كَفَرَ الَّذِينَ قَالُوا إِنَّ اللَّهَ ثَالِثُ﴾ gods ﴿ثَلَاثَةٍ﴾ i.e. one of them, the other two being Jesus and his mother — they are a sect of the Christians. ﴿وَمَا مِنْ إِلَهٍ إِلَّا إِلَهٌ وَاحِدٌ وَإِنْ لَمْ يَنْتَهُوا عَمَّا يَقُولُونَ﴾ of the Trinity, and affirm [His] oneness, ﴿لَيَمَسَّنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا﴾ i.e. persisted in disbelief ﴿مِنْهُمْ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ﴾ painful, which is the Fire.

celaleyn:74-74.t: ﴿أَفَلَا يَتُوبُونَ إِلَى اللَّهِ وَيَسْتَغْفِرُونَهُ﴾ for what they said? An interrogative of rebuke (tawbīkh). ﴿وَاللَّهُ غَفُورٌ﴾ to whoever repents, ﴿رَحِيمٌ﴾ to him.

celaleyn:75-75.t: ﴿مَا الْمَسِيحُ ابْنُ مَرْيَمَ إِلَّا رَسُولٌ قَدْ خَلَتْ﴾ passed away ﴿مِنْ قَبْلِهِ الرُّسُلُ﴾ so he passes away like them and is not a god as they claimed — otherwise he would not have passed away. ﴿وَأُمُّهُ صِدِّيقَةٌ﴾ an intensive [form] of truthfulness. ﴿كَانَا يَأْكُلَانِ الطَّعَامَ﴾ like other living creatures; and whoever is like that is not a god, because of his being composite, his weakness, and the urine and excrement that result. ﴿انْظُرْ﴾ in wonder ﴿كَيْفَ نُبَيِّنُ لَهُمُ الْآيَاتِ﴾ of Our oneness, ﴿ثُمَّ انْظُرْ أَنَّى﴾ how ﴿يُؤْفَكُونَ﴾ they are turned away from the truth despite the proof being established.

celaleyn:76-76.t: ﴿قُلْ أَتَعْبُدُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ﴾ i.e. other than Him ﴿مَا لَا يَمْلِكُ لَكُمْ ضَرًّا وَلَا نَفْعًا وَاللَّهُ هُوَ السَّمِيعُ﴾ of your words, ﴿الْعَلِيمُ﴾ of your states. And the interrogative is for disavowal (inkār).

celaleyn:77-77.t: ﴿قُلْ يَا أَهْلَ الْكِتَابِ﴾ the Jews and the Christians, ﴿لَا تَغْلُوا﴾ exceed the limit ﴿فِي دِينِكُمْ﴾ with an excess ﴿غَيْرَ الْحَقِّ﴾ by lowering Jesus or raising him above his due, ﴿وَلَا تَتَّبِعُوا أَهْوَاءَ قَوْمٍ قَدْ ضَلُّوا مِنْ قَبْلُ﴾ through their excess — they are their forebears — ﴿وَأَضَلُّوا كَثِيرًا﴾ of people ﴿وَضَلُّوا عَنْ سَوَاءِ السَّبِيلِ﴾ the path of truth; and al-sawāʾ originally means "the middle".

celaleyn:78-78.t: ﴿لُعِنَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مِنْ بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ عَلَى لِسَانِ دَاوُدَ﴾ in that he invoked [Allah] against them and they were transformed into apes — they were the people of Ayla — ﴿وَعِيسَى ابْنِ مَرْيَمَ﴾ in that he invoked [Allah] against them and they were transformed into swine — they were the people of the Table. ﴿ذَلِكَ﴾ cursing ﴿بِمَا عَصَوْا وَكَانُوا يَعْتَدُونَ﴾

celaleyn:79-79.t: ﴿كَانُوا لَا يَتَنَاهَوْنَ﴾ i.e. they did not forbid one another ﴿عَنْ﴾ returning to ﴿مُنْكَرٍ فَعَلُوهُ لَبِئْسَ مَا كَانُوا يَفْعَلُونَ﴾ this doing of theirs.

celaleyn:80-80.t: ﴿تَرَى﴾ O Muhammad, ﴿كَثِيرًا مِنْهُمْ يَتَوَلَّوْنَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا﴾ of the people of Mecca, out of hatred for you. ﴿لَبِئْسَ مَا قَدَّمَتْ لَهُمْ أَنْفُسُهُمْ﴾ of deeds for their return [to Allah], which necessitate for them ﴿أَنْ سَخِطَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِمْ وَفِي الْعَذَابِ هُمْ خَالِدُونَ﴾

celaleyn:81-81.t: ﴿وَلَوْ كَانُوا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِاللَّهِ وَالنَّبِيِّ﴾ Muhammad ﴿وَمَا أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْهِ مَا اتَّخَذُوهُمْ﴾ i.e. the disbelievers ﴿أَوْلِيَاءَ وَلَكِنَّ كَثِيرًا مِنْهُمْ فَاسِقُونَ﴾ departing from faith.

celaleyn:82-82.t: ﴿لَتَجِدَنَّ﴾ O Muhammad, ﴿أَشَدَّ النَّاسِ عَدَاوَةً لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا الْيَهُودَ وَالَّذِينَ أَشْرَكُوا﴾ of the people of Mecca, because of the multiplying of their disbelief and ignorance and their absorption in following desire; ﴿وَلَتَجِدَنَّ أَقْرَبَهُمْ مَوَدَّةً لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا الَّذِينَ قَالُوا إِنَّا نَصَارَى ذَلِكَ﴾ i.e. the nearness of their affection to the believers ﴿بِأَنَّ﴾ is because ﴿مِنْهُمْ قِسِّيسِينَ﴾ scholars ﴿وَرُهْبَانًا﴾ devout worshippers, ﴿وَأَنَّهُمْ لَا يَسْتَكْبِرُونَ﴾ from following the truth, as the Jews and the people of Mecca are arrogant. It was revealed concerning the delegation of the Negus (al-Najāshī) who came to him from Abyssinia; he ﷺ recited Sūrat Yā Sīn, and they wept and embraced Islam, and said: "How like this is to what used to be sent down upon Jesus!"

celaleyn:1-1.t: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا أَوْفُوا بِالْعُقُودِ﴾ the binding covenants that are between you and Allah and people ﴿أُحِلَّتْ لَكُمْ بَهِيمَةُ الْأَنْعَامِ﴾ camels, cattle and sheep, to eat after slaughter ﴿إِلَّا مَا يُتْلَى عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ its prohibition, in {حُرِّمَتْ عَلَيْكُمُ الْمَيْتَةُ} — the ayah; so the exception is disconnected (munqaṭiʿ), and it may be connected (muttaṣil), the prohibition being because of what befell [the animal] of death and the like ﴿غَيْرَ مُحِلِّي الصَّيْدِ وَأَنْتُمْ حُرُمٌ﴾ i.e. in the state of iḥrām; and the accusative of غَيْرَ is as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun of لَكُمْ ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَحْكُمُ مَا يُرِيدُ﴾ of making lawful and otherwise; there is no objecting to Him

celaleyn:2-2.t: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لَا تُحِلُّوا شَعَائِرَ اللَّهِ﴾ plural of شَعِيرَة, i.e. the landmarks of His religion, by hunting while in iḥrām ﴿وَلَا الشَّهْرَ الْحَرَامَ﴾ by fighting in it ﴿وَلَا الْهَدْيَ﴾ the livestock offered to the Sanctuary, by interfering with it ﴿وَلَا الْقَلَائِدَ﴾ plural of قِلَادَة, which is what one used to garland himself with from the trees of the Sanctuary so as to be safe; i.e. do not interfere with them or with their wearers ﴿وَلَا﴾ violate [تُحِلُّوا] ﴿آمِّينَ﴾ those heading for ﴿الْبَيْتَ الْحَرَامَ﴾ by fighting them ﴿يَبْتَغُونَ فَضْلًا﴾ provision ﴿مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ﴾ through trade ﴿وَرِضْوَانًا﴾ from Him by heading for it, according to their corrupt claim. This is abrogated by the ayah of Barāʾa ﴿وَإِذَا حَلَلْتُمْ﴾ from iḥrām ﴿فَاصْطَادُوا﴾ a command of permission ﴿وَلَا يَجْرِمَنَّكُمْ﴾ let not ... earn you ﴿شَنَآنُ﴾ with fatḥa on the nūn and with sukūn: hatred of ﴿قَوْمٍ﴾ because [لِأَجْلِ] ﴿أَنْ صَدُّوكُمْ عَنِ الْمَسْجِدِ الْحَرَامِ أَنْ تَعْتَدُوا﴾ against them by killing and otherwise ﴿وَتَعَاوَنُوا عَلَى الْبِرِّ﴾ by doing what you were commanded ﴿وَالتَّقْوَى﴾ by abandoning what you were forbidden ﴿وَلَا تَعَاوَنُوا﴾ in it there is omission of one of the two tāʾs in the original ﴿عَلَى الْإِثْمِ﴾ sins ﴿وَالْعُدْوَانِ﴾ transgressing the limits of Allah ﴿وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ﴾ fear His punishment by obeying Him ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ شَدِيدُ الْعِقَابِ﴾ for whoever opposes Him.

celaleyn:3-3.t: ﴿حُرِّمَتْ عَلَيْكُمُ الْمَيْتَةُ﴾ i.e. eating it ﴿وَالدَّمُ﴾ i.e. what is shed, as in al-Anʿām ﴿وَلَحْمُ الْخِنْزِيرِ وَمَا أُهِلَّ لِغَيْرِ اللَّهِ بِهِ﴾ by being slaughtered in the name of another than Him ﴿وَالْمُنْخَنِقَةُ﴾ that which died by strangling ﴿وَالْمَوْقُوذَةُ﴾ that which was killed by beating ﴿وَالْمُتَرَدِّيَةُ﴾ that which fell from a height to below and died ﴿وَالنَّطِيحَةُ﴾ that which was killed by another goring it ﴿وَمَا أَكَلَ السَّبُعُ﴾ of it ﴿إِلَّا مَا ذَكَّيْتُمْ﴾ i.e. of these things, in which you caught life and slaughtered it ﴿وَمَا ذُبِحَ عَلَى﴾ the name of ﴿النُّصُبِ﴾ plural of نِصَاب, and they are the idols ﴿وَأَنْ تَسْتَقْسِمُوا﴾ seek an allotment and a decision ﴿بِالْأَزْلَامِ﴾ plural of زَلَم, with fatḥa or ḍamma on the zāy and fatḥa on the lām: a small arrow (qidḥ, with kasra on the qāf) without feathers or head. There were seven of them with the custodian of the Kaʿba, with marks on them, and they used to let them decide: if they commanded them, they obeyed, and if they forbade them, they refrained ﴿ذَلِكُمْ فِسْقٌ﴾ departure from obedience. And it was revealed on the day of ʿArafa in the year of the Farewell Pilgrimage: ﴿الْيَوْمَ يَئِسَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مِنْ دِينِكُمْ﴾ of your apostatising from it, after their hoping for that, because of the strength of it they saw ﴿فَلَا تَخْشَوْهُمْ وَاخْشَوْنِ الْيَوْمَ أَكْمَلْتُ لَكُمْ دِينَكُمْ﴾ its rulings and obligations; after it no [ruling on the] lawful or unlawful was revealed ﴿وَأَتْمَمْتُ عَلَيْكُمْ نِعْمَتِي﴾ by completing it; and it is said: by entering Mecca in safety ﴿وَرَضِيتُ﴾ i.e. chose ﴿لَكُمُ الْإِسْلَامَ دِينًا فَمَنِ اضْطُرَّ فِي مَخْمَصَةٍ﴾ famine, to eating something of what was forbidden to him, and he ate it ﴿غَيْرَ مُتَجَانِفٍ﴾ inclining ﴿لِإِثْمٍ﴾ to a sin ﴿فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ﴾ to him for what he ate ﴿رَحِيمٌ﴾ to him in permitting it to him — unlike the one inclining to sin, i.e. engaged in it, such as the highway robber and the rebel, for example: eating is not lawful for him

celaleyn:83-83.t: Allah the Exalted said: ﴿وَإِذَا سَمِعُوا مَا أُنْزِلَ إِلَى الرَّسُولِ﴾ of the Qurʾān, ﴿تَرَى أَعْيُنَهُمْ تَفِيضُ مِنَ الدَّمْعِ مِمَّا عَرَفُوا مِنَ الْحَقِّ يَقُولُونَ رَبَّنَا آمَنَّا﴾ we have affirmed the truth of Your Prophet and Your Book, ﴿فَاكْتُبْنَا مَعَ الشَّاهِدِينَ﴾ who acknowledge the truth of both.

celaleyn:84-84.t: ﴿وَ﴾ they said, in reply to those of the Jews who reproached them for [embracing] Islam: ﴿مَا لَنَا لَا نُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ وَمَا جَاءَنَا مِنَ الْحَقِّ﴾ the Qurʾān? I.e. there is nothing preventing us from believing while what calls for it is present. ﴿وَنَطْمَعُ﴾ conjoined to نُؤْمِنُ, ﴿أَنْ يُدْخِلَنَا رَبُّنَا مَعَ الْقَوْمِ الصَّالِحِينَ﴾ the believers, into Paradise. Allah the Exalted said:

celaleyn:85-85.t: ﴿فَأَثَابَهُمُ اللَّهُ بِمَا قَالُوا جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهَارُ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا وَذَلِكَ جَزَاءُ الْمُحْسِنِينَ﴾ through faith.

celaleyn:86-86.t: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وَكَذَّبُوا بِآيَاتِنَا أُولَئِكَ أَصْحَابُ الْجَحِيمِ﴾ And [the following] was revealed when a group of the Companions resolved to keep constantly to fasting and night prayer, and not to approach women or perfume, nor eat meat, nor sleep on a bed:

celaleyn:87-87.t: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لَا تُحَرِّمُوا طَيِّبَاتِ مَا أَحَلَّ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ وَلَا تَعْتَدُوا﴾ overstep the command of Allah; ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يُحِبُّ الْمُعْتَدِينَ﴾

celaleyn:88-88.t: ﴿وَكُلُوا مِمَّا رَزَقَكُمُ اللَّهُ حَلَالًا طَيِّبًا﴾ a mafʿūl (object), and the preposition and its genitive noun before it are a ḥāl (circumstantial) attached to (mutaʿalliq) it. ﴿وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ الَّذِي أَنْتُمْ بِهِ مُؤْمِنُونَ﴾

celaleyn:89-89.t: ﴿لَا يُؤَاخِذُكُمُ اللَّهُ بِاللَّغْوِ﴾ that occurs ﴿فِي أَيْمَانِكُمْ﴾ — it is what the tongue rushes into without intending an oath, such as a person's saying, "No, by Allah," and "Yes, by Allah" — ﴿وَلَكِنْ يُؤَاخِذُكُمْ بِمَا عَقَّدْتُمُ﴾ with the lightened and the doubled form, and in one reading [عَاقَدْتُمُ], ﴿الْأَيْمَانَ﴾ upon it, by swearing intentionally. ﴿فَكَفَّارَتُهُ﴾ i.e. of the oath, when you break it, ﴿إِطْعَامُ عَشَرَةِ مَسَاكِينَ﴾ for each poor person a mudd, ﴿مِنْ أَوْسَطِ مَا تُطْعِمُونَ﴾ of it ﴿أَهْلِيكُمْ﴾ i.e. the most moderate and most usual of it, not the highest nor the lowest, ﴿أَوْ كِسْوَتُهُمْ﴾ with what is called clothing, such as a shirt, a turban and a waist-wrapper; and giving what has been mentioned to a single poor person does not suffice — al-Shāfiʿī holds this; ﴿أَوْ تَحْرِيرُ﴾ freeing ﴿رَقَبَةٍ﴾ i.e. a believing one, as in the expiation for killing and for ẓihār, construing the unrestricted (muṭlaq) in the light of the restricted (muqayyad). ﴿فَمَنْ لَمْ يَجِدْ﴾ any one of what has been mentioned, ﴿فَصِيَامُ ثَلَاثَةِ أَيَّامٍ﴾ is his expiation; its apparent sense is that consecutiveness is not a condition — al-Shāfiʿī holds this. ﴿ذَلِكَ﴾ which has been mentioned ﴿كَفَّارَةُ أَيْمَانِكُمْ إِذَا حَلَفْتُمْ﴾ and break [them]. ﴿وَاحْفَظُوا أَيْمَانَكُمْ﴾ from breaking them, so long as they are not against doing a good deed or making peace between people, as in Sūrat al-Baqara. ﴿كَذَلِكَ﴾ i.e. like His making clear to you what has been mentioned, ﴿يُبَيِّنُ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ آيَاتِهِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَشْكُرُونَ﴾ [Him — هُ in the source] for that.

celaleyn:90-90.t: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِنَّمَا الْخَمْرُ﴾ the intoxicant that clouds (yukhāmir) the mind, ﴿وَالْمَيْسِرُ﴾ gambling, ﴿وَالْأَنْصَابُ﴾ idols, ﴿وَالْأَزْلَامُ﴾ divining arrows, ﴿رِجْسٌ﴾ foul and filthy, ﴿مِنْ عَمَلِ الشَّيْطَانِ﴾ which he makes attractive. ﴿فَاجْتَنِبُوهُ﴾ i.e. the filth by which these things are expressed — avoid doing it — ﴿لَعَلَّكُمْ تُفْلِحُونَ﴾

celaleyn:91-91.t: ﴿إِنَّمَا يُرِيدُ الشَّيْطَانُ أَنْ يُوقِعَ بَيْنَكُمُ الْعَدَاوَةَ وَالْبَغْضَاءَ فِي الْخَمْرِ وَالْمَيْسِرِ﴾ when you engage in them, because of the evil and strife that arise in them, ﴿وَيَصُدَّكُمْ﴾ through being occupied with them ﴿عَنْ ذِكْرِ اللَّهِ وَعَنِ الصَّلَوةِ﴾ He singled it out for mention to magnify it. ﴿فَهَلْ أَنْتُمْ مُنْتَهُونَ﴾ from engaging in them? I.e. desist!

celaleyn:92-92.t: ﴿وَأَطِيعُوا اللَّهَ وَأَطِيعُوا الرَّسُولَ وَاحْذَرُوا﴾ acts of disobedience. ﴿فَإِنْ تَوَلَّيْتُمْ﴾ from obedience, ﴿فَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّمَا عَلَى رَسُولِنَا الْبَلَاغُ الْمُبِينُ﴾ the clear conveying, and your requital is upon Us.

celaleyn:93-93.t: ﴿لَيْسَ عَلَى الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ جُنَاحٌ فِيمَا طَعِمُوا﴾ consumed of wine and gambling before the prohibition, ﴿إِذَا مَا اتَّقَوْا﴾ the forbidden things ﴿وَآمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ ثُمَّ اتَّقَوْا وَآمَنُوا﴾ remained firm in godfearing and faith, ﴿ثُمَّ اتَّقَوْا وَأَحْسَنُوا﴾ in deeds. ﴿وَاللَّهُ يُحِبُّ الْمُحْسِنِينَ﴾ in the sense that He rewards them.
