Rather it is made to include the meaning of «جاء» and made transitive with the bāʾ, and it reaches «آثارهم» with على. This is the summary of what Abū Ḥayyān said. He dwelt at length on this question in order to refute al-Zamakhsharī's analysis, for al-Zamakhsharī said, in his own words — what al-Zamakhsharī says:
«قفيته is like عقبته, when you make him follow. Then one says قفيته بفلان and عقبته به, making it transitive to the second object by adding the bāʾ. If you say: where then is the first object in the verse? I say: it is omitted, and the adverbial phrase, «على آثارهم», as it were stands in its place, because when He makes him follow upon his trace, He has made him follow him.»

Abū Ḥayyān's digression:
Abū Ḥayyān went further in refuting al-Zamakhsharī and said: His words need interpretation. That is because he made the doubled «قفيّته» mean «قفوته», so that «فعّل» would be in the sense of «فعل», as in قدّر الله and قدر الله, which is one of the meanings for which «فعّل» comes. Then he made it transitive with the bāʾ; and making a verb that is transitive to one object reach a second object by the bāʾ is rarely found, so that some even claimed that it does not occur and is not permissible: so for طعم زيد اللحم one does not say أطعمت زيدا باللحم. The correct view is that it has come, but rarely. You say دفع زيد عمرا ("Zayd pushed ʿAmr"), then make it transitive with the bāʾ and say دفعت زيدا بعمرو, i.e. "I made Zayd push ʿAmr". Likewise صكّ الحجر الحجر ("the stone struck the stone"), then you say صككت الحجر بالحجر, i.e. "I made it strike it". As for his saying that the first object is omitted and the adverbial phrase as it were stands in its place, this is not sound, because the object is an explicit mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and an adverbial phrase does not stand in its place.
Until he says: and al-Zamakhsharī's saying «فقد قفى به إياه» separates the pronoun, whereas it should properly be attached.

* I'rab:
(وَقَفَّيْنا عَلى آثارِهِمْ بِعِيسَى ابْنِ مَرْيَمَ مُصَدِّقاً لِما بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ مِنَ التَّوْراةِ): resumptive speech, brought to begin setting out the rulings of the Gospel after setting out the ruling of the Torah. قفينا is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); على آثارهم and بعيسى are attached to (mutaʿalliq) قفينا; ابن مريم is a badal (substitute) or a naʿt (adjective); مصدقا is a ḥāl (circumstantial); لما is attached to «مصدقا»; بين يديه is an adverb attached to an omitted ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, which is «ما»; and من التوراة is attached to an omitted ḥāl. (وَآتَيْناهُ الْإِنْجِيلَ فِيهِ هُدىً وَنُورٌ): the wāw is conjunctive; آتيناه is a past verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi, and الإنجيل is a second mafʿūl bihi; فيه is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted, fronted khabar (predicate); هدى is a delayed mubtadaʾ (subject), and نور is conjoined to هدى; the nominal clause is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl. (وَمُصَدِّقاً لِما بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ مِنَ التَّوْراةِ): مصدقا is conjoined to the position of the clause, so it has the status of an accusative as a ḥāl; لما is attached to «مصدقا»; بين يديه is an adverb attached to an omitted ṣila; and من التوراة is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl. (وَهُدىً وَمَوْعِظَةً لِلْمُتَّقِينَ): the wāw is conjunctive, and هدى is conjoined, in line with «مصدقا», so both are accusative as ḥāl.
Some permitted them to be two mafʿūl li-ajlihi (objects of purpose), but this is far-fetched because of the presence of the wāw. موعظة is conjoined to هدى, and للمتقين is attached to an omitted naʿt. (وَلْيَحْكُمْ أَهْلُ الْإِنْجِيلِ بِما أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ فِيهِ): the wāw is conjunctive and the lām is the lām of command; يحكم is an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by the lām of command; أهل الإنجيل is the fāʿil of يحكم, and بما is attached to يحكم. In one of the seven readings: «وليحكم», making the lām one of purpose, with يحكم an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after the lām of purpose, and the preposition and its genitive noun attached to آتينا or to قفينا [Translator's note: the source writes the reading with the same letters «وليحكم»; the variant meant is وَلِيَحْكُمَ, with kasra on the lām and the verb in the accusative]. فيه is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يحكم. (وَمَنْ لَمْ يَحْكُمْ بِما أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ فَأُولئِكَ هُمُ الْفاسِقُونَ): the i'rab of this clause has been repeated, and the repetition conveys the meaning of emphasis.

* Rhetoric:
1- al-tashbīh al-balīgh (the eloquent simile): the likening of the Gospel to light and guidance, with the particle of comparison omitted so that they are the Gospel itself, for hyperbole.
2- Repetition: in the clauses, for added emphasis, as has preceded.

dervis-irab:83-84.t:
* I'rab:
(وَإِذا سَمِعُوا ما أُنْزِلَ إِلَى الرَّسُولِ): the wāw is resumptive, and it may also be conjunctive, so that the clause is conjoined to His words «لا يستكبرون». إذا is an adverb of future time containing the sense of a condition; the clause سمعوا is in the position of the genitive (majrūr) as the adverb is put in construct with it; the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); ما is a relative noun in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause أنزل has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause); and إلى الرسول are attached (mutaʿalliq) to أنزل. (تَرى أَعْيُنَهُمْ تَفِيضُ مِنَ الدَّمْعِ): the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition. ترى is an imperfect verb, and its agent is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, implied as "you" (أنت); أعينهم is the object of ترى, which is the verb of visual seeing; the clause تفيض is a ḥāl (circumstantial); and من الدمع is a preposition and its genitive noun in the position of the accusative as tamyīz (specification). More explanation of this i'rab will come in the section on rhetoric. (مِمَّا عَرَفُوا مِنَ الْحَقِّ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to تفيض; the clause عرفوا is the ṣila; and من الحق is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl. (يَقُولُونَ: رَبَّنا آمَنَّا فَاكْتُبْنا مَعَ الشَّاهِدِينَ): the clause يقولون is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from the pronoun in «عرفوا», namely the wāw, or from the genitive pronoun in «أعينهم»; the ḥāl may come from the muḍāf ilayhi here because the muḍāf is a part of it. It may also be resumptive, brought to answer an implied question, as if it were said: "So what is their state on hearing the Qur'an?" ربنا is a vocative in construct (munādā muḍāf); آمنا is a verb and its agent, and the clause is in the position of the accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); فاكتبنا: the fāʾ is resumptive, and اكتبنا is an imperative verb and its direct object, with the agent latent; and مع الشاهدين is an adverb attached to اكتبنا. (وَما لَنا لا نُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ وَما جاءَنا مِنَ الْحَقِّ): the wāw is resumptive; ما is an interrogative noun in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); لنا is attached to an omitted khabar (predicate); the clause لا نؤمن بالله is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl; بالله is attached to نؤمن; ما is conjoined to الله; the clause جاءنا has no grammatical position because it is a ṣila; and من الحق is attached to an omitted ḥāl. (وَنَطْمَعُ أَنْ يُدْخِلَنا رَبُّنا مَعَ الْقَوْمِ الصَّالِحِينَ): the wāw is conjunctive; نطمع is an imperfect verb whose agent is "we" (نحن); أن and what follows it are interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun) that is accusative by removal of the preposition, and the [implied] preposition and its genitive noun are attached to نطمع; ربنا is the agent; and the adverb مع القوم الصالحين is attached to يدخلنا. The whole clause is conjoined to the clause نؤمن. The wāw may also be circumstantial (ḥāliyya), with the clause in the accusative as a ḥāl.

* Rhetoric:
1- Metaphor (majāz) in the overflowing of the eyes, the relationship being fullness.
2- Hyperbole in the tamyīz, which is one of the most eloquent constructions, because the intensification in it rises through three degrees: the first is "the tear of his eye overflowed" (فاض دمع عينه); the second is in converting the agent into a tamyīz; and the third is in presenting the tamyīz in the form of a cause (taʿlīl), so that alongside specification it conveys causation. Speech with causation is farther from the original than speech with tamyīz only because, in such cases, the tamyīz is established as having originally been an agent, as in طاب محمد نفسا ("Muhammad was pleased in soul") and اشتعل الرأس شيبا ("the head blazed with white hair"). So when you say فاضت عينه دمعا ("his eye overflowed with tears"), this origin is understood, given the habitual usage in its like; but with causation, that is not something customary.

dervis-irab:85-86.t:
* I'rab:
(فَأَثابَهُمُ اللَّهُ بِما قالُوا جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهارُ): the fāʾ is conjunctive; أثابهم is a verb and a fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object); الله is the fāʿil (agent); and the clause is conjoined to the clause قالوا آمنا. بما is attached (mutaʿalliq) to أثابهم; the clause قالوا is a ṣila (relative clause). The reward is coordinated with their saying «آمنا» because saying, when joined with sincere action, is faith. جنات is a second direct object of أثابهم, because it contains the sense of giving; the clause تجري is a naʿt (adjective) of جنات; من تحتها is attached to تجري; and الأنهار is the agent of تجري. (خالِدِينَ فِيها وَذلِكَ جَزاءُ الْمُحْسِنِينَ): خالدين is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «أثابهم»; فيها is attached to خالدين; the wāw is circumstantial or resumptive; ذلك is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and جزاء المحسنين its khabar (predicate); and the clause is in the accusative as a ḥāl, or resumptive. (وَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وَكَذَّبُوا بِآياتِنا): the wāw is resumptive; الذين is a mubtadaʾ; the clause كفروا is a ṣila; كذبوا is conjoined to كفروا — denial is coordinated with disbelief because lying is a kind of it; and بآياتنا is attached to كذبوا. (أُولئِكَ أَصْحابُ الْجَحِيمِ): the demonstrative is a mubtadaʾ; أصحاب الجحيم is the khabar of the demonstrative; and the clause is the khabar of الذين.

dervis-irab:87-88.t:
* I'rab:
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا تُحَرِّمُوا طَيِّباتِ ما أَحَلَّ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ): resumptive speech, brought to address some of the believers who had agreed upon austerity and monasticism, wearing wool and turning away from permitted pleasures, and to forbid them from that.
لا is prohibitive; تحرموا is an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by لا; the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); طيبات is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ما is a relative noun in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; the clause أحل is a ṣila (relative clause); الله is the agent; and لكم is attached (mutaʿalliq) to أحل. (وَلا تَعْتَدُوا إِنَّ اللَّهَ لا يُحِبُّ الْمُعْتَدِينَ): the wāw is a conjunction; لا is prohibitive; تعتدوا is an imperfect verb in the jussive by لا; and the clause is conjoined to the clause لا تحرموا. The meaning of transgression here is going beyond the lawful to the unlawful. إن and its noun; the clause لا يحب المعتدين is its khabar (predicate); and the clause إن الله etc. is causal (taʿlīliyya) with no grammatical position. (وَكُلُوا مِمَّا رَزَقَكُمُ اللَّهُ حَلالًا طَيِّباً): the wāw is conjunctive; كلوا is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn; مما is attached to كلوا; the clause رزقكم الله is the ṣila of the relative; and حلالا is a direct object, or a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the relative noun or from its omitted referring pronoun, or a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), being an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "an eating that is lawful" (أكلا حلالا). The first is simplest. (وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ الَّذِي أَنْتُمْ بِهِ مُؤْمِنُونَ): the wāw is conjunctive; اتقوا is an imperative verb conjoined to كلوا; الله is its object; الذي is an adjective of الله; أنتم is a mubtadaʾ (subject); به is attached to «مؤمنون»; and the nominal clause has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of the relative.

dervis-irab:89-89.t:
* Vocabulary:
(اللغو) of oaths: that which falls away and to which no ruling attaches. There is a juristic disagreement about it: according to al-Shāfiʿī it is what comes from a person without intent, such as his saying:
"No, by Allah" (لا والله) and "Yes, by Allah" (بلى والله); according to Abū Ḥanīfa it is to swear about something one believes to be so, when it is not as one thought.
(عَقَّدْتُمُ الْأَيْمانَ): it was read with a doubled consonant (tashdīd) and without it, and it was also read:
«عاقدتم». The binding (taʿqīd) of oaths is their confirmation by intent and resolve. Al-Farazdaq put this meaning into verse: it is related that al-Ḥasan was asked about the inadvertent oath while al-Farazdaq was with him, and he said: "Let me answer for you, O Abū Saʿīd," and recited:
ولست بمأخوذ بلغو تقوله ... إذا لم تعمّد عاقدات العزائم
(You are not held to account for idle words you say, so long as firmly bound resolves did not intend them.) That is: you are not taken to task for idle speech that falls away. تعمّد is originally تتعمد, one of the two tāʾs having been dropped; and عاقدات العزائم means the firm, decisive resolves; and attributing the requital to them is a rational metaphor (majāz ʿaqlī).
(فَكَفَّارَتُهُ): the expiation (kaffāra) is the act whose function is to "cover" (takfīr) the sin, i.e. to conceal it.

* I'rab:
(لا يُؤاخِذُكُمُ اللَّهُ بِاللَّغْوِ فِي أَيْمانِكُمْ): resumptive speech establishing the ruling on inadvertent oaths. لا is negating; يؤاخذكم الله is an imperfect verb, a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and a fāʿil (agent); باللغو is attached (mutaʿalliq) to يؤاخذكم; and في أيمانكم is attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). (وَلكِنْ يُؤاخِذُكُمْ بِما عَقَّدْتُمُ الْأَيْمانَ): the wāw is conjunctive; لكن is inoperative (muhmala); بما: the bāʾ is a preposition, and ما is maṣdariyya, which together with عقدتم is interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the genitive by the bāʾ; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to يؤاخذكم; and الأيمان is the direct object. (فَكَفَّارَتُهُ إِطْعامُ عَشَرَةِ مَساكِينَ مِنْ أَوْسَطِ ما تُطْعِمُونَ أَهْلِيكُمْ): the fāʾ is the faṣīḥa ("disclosing") fāʾ, i.e. "if you break what you have bound by oaths"; it is thus the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition. كفارته is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the pronoun refers back to the breaking of the oath (al-ḥinth) understood from the implied condition, as has been stated. Al-Zamakhsharī held that it refers back to the relative ما, and a muḍāf must then be implied, i.e. "the expiation of breaking it". There are other views which we have passed over because they are far-fetched. إطعام is the khabar (predicate); عشرة مساكين is muḍāf ilayhi; من أوسط is attached to an omitted adjective of عشرة مساكين; ما is a relative noun, muḍāf ilayhi; the clause تطعمون is the ṣila (relative clause), and the referring pronoun is omitted, i.e. تطعمونه — that is, neither the highest nor the lowest; and أهليكم is the object of تطعمون.
(أَوْ كِسْوَتُهُمْ أَوْ تَحْرِيرُ رَقَبَةٍ): conjoined to طعام [Translator's note: the text reads «طعام»; the word in the verse is «إطعام».], and likewise تحرير رقبة. (فَمَنْ لَمْ يَجِدْ فَصِيامُ ثَلاثَةِ أَيَّامٍ): the fāʾ is resumptive; من is a jussive conditional noun and a mubtadaʾ; لم is a particle of negation, conversion [of tense] and jussive; يجد is an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by لم, and it is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the fāʾ links its apodosis; and صيام is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, i.e. "then upon him is fasting", or "his expiation"; and ثلاثة أيام is muḍāf ilayhi. (ذلِكَ كَفَّارَةُ أَيْمانِكُمْ إِذا حَلَفْتُمْ): the clause is explicative; the demonstrative is a mubtadaʾ; كفارة is the khabar; أيمانكم is muḍāf ilayhi; إذا is an adverb of future time containing the sense of a condition, attached to the omitted apodosis, indicated by what precedes it; and the clause حلفتم is in the position of the genitive by construct (iḍāfa). (وَاحْفَظُوا أَيْمانَكُمْ كَذلِكَ يُبَيِّنُ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ آياتِهِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَشْكُرُونَ): the wāw is conjunctive; احفظوا is an imperative verb and its agent; أيمانكم is the direct object; كذلك is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) or ḥāl; يبين الله is an imperfect verb and its agent; لكم is attached to يبين; آياته is the direct object; لعلكم: لعل and its noun; the clause تشكرون is its khabar; and the clause of hope is circumstantial.

dervis-irab:90-91.t:
* I'rab:
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِنَّمَا الْخَمْرُ وَالْمَيْسِرُ وَالْأَنْصابُ وَالْأَزْلامُ رِجْسٌ مِنْ عَمَلِ الشَّيْطانِ)
Resumptive speech to show that wine and gambling are not included among the good things that Allah has made lawful. إنما is [إنّ with] the restraining mā (kāffa and makfūfa); الخمر is a mubtadaʾ (subject); الميسر, الأنصاب and الأزلام are conjoined to it; رجس is the khabar (predicate); and من عمل الشيطان is attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of رجس, or it is a second khabar of الخمر. (فَاجْتَنِبُوهُ لَعَلَّكُمْ تُفْلِحُونَ): the fāʾ is the faṣīḥa ("disclosing") fāʾ; اجتنبوه is an imperative verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); لعل and its noun; the clause تفلحون is its khabar; and the clause of hope is a ḥāl (circumstantial). (إِنَّما يُرِيدُ الشَّيْطانُ أَنْ يُوقِعَ بَيْنَكُمُ الْعَداوَةَ وَالْبَغْضاءَ فِي الْخَمْرِ وَالْمَيْسِرِ): resumptive speech giving further clarification of the reasons leading to the prohibition of the two.
إنما is kāffa and makfūfa; يريد الشيطان is an imperfect verb and its agent; أن and what follows it are interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun) that is the object of يريد; بينكم is an adverb attached to يوقع or to an omitted ḥāl; العداوة is the direct object; البغضاء is conjoined to العداوة; في الخمر is attached to an omitted ḥāl; and الميسر is conjoined to الخمر.
(وَيَصُدَّكُمْ عَنْ ذِكْرِ اللَّهِ وَعَنِ الصَّلاةِ فَهَلْ أَنْتُمْ مُنْتَهُونَ): the wāw is a conjunction; يصدكم is conjoined to يوقع; عن ذكر الله is attached to يصدكم; عن الصلاة is also attached to يصدكم; the fāʾ is resumptive; هل is an interrogative particle whose meaning is a command; أنتم is a mubtadaʾ; and منتهون is the khabar.

dervis-irab:7-8.t:
* I'rab:
(وَاذْكُرُوا نِعْمَةَ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ وَمِيثاقَهُ الَّذِي واثَقَكُمْ بِهِ): the wāw — the wāw is resumptive, and the speech is resumptive, introduced to remind the believers of His favours upon them and of His covenant by which He bound them. (اذكروا نعمة الله) is an imperative verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (عليكم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (نعمة); (ميثاقه) is conjoined to (نعمة الله); (الذي) is a naʿt (adjective) of (ميثاق); and the clause (واثقكم به) is the ṣila (relative clause).
(إِذْ قُلْتُمْ سَمِعْنا وَأَطَعْنا): (إذ) is an adverb of past time attached to (واثقكم); the clause (قلتم) is in the position of genitive by annexation; the clause (سمعنا) is the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl), and the clause (وأطعنا) is conjoined to it.
(وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَلِيمٌ بِذاتِ الصُّدُورِ): resumptive speech. (اتقوا الله) is an imperative verb, its agent and its object; the clause of (إن) and what falls within its scope is causal (taʿlīliyya). (ذات الصدور) means the matters hidden in the breasts.
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا كُونُوا قَوَّامِينَ لِلَّهِ شُهَداءَ بِالْقِسْطِ): resumptive speech, introduced to begin setting out matters concerning what passes between them and others. (كونوا) is a defective (nāqiṣ) imperative verb, the wāw its noun and (قوامين) its khabar (predicate); (لله) is attached to (قوامين); (شهداء) is a second khabar of (كونوا); and (بالقسط) is attached to (شهداء).
(وَلا يَجْرِمَنَّكُمْ شَنَآنُ قَوْمٍ عَلى أَلَّا تَعْدِلُوا): the wāw is a conjunction; (لا) is prohibitive; (يجرمنكم) is an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa, in the position of jussive (majzūm) by (لا); the kāf is the direct object; (شنآن قوم) is the agent; (على) is a preposition, and (أن) with what falls within its scope is interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the genitive by (على); the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (يجرمنكم), because it contains the meaning of «لا يحملنكم» (let it not drive you).
(اعْدِلُوا هُوَ أَقْرَبُ لِلتَّقْوى): the clause (اعدلوا) is explicative; (هو) is a detached pronoun, a mubtadaʾ (subject), referring to the maṣdar understood from His saying «اعدلوا»; (أقرب) is the khabar, and the clause is resumptive; (للتقوى) is attached to (أقرب).
(وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ إِنَّ اللَّهَ خَبِيرٌ بِما تَعْمَلُونَ): the parsing of its like has been given shortly before.

* Rhetoric:
Repetition (takrīr) in demanding justice; the secret in it is emphasising justice and arousing longing for it. The gist of the meaning: let not your hatred of the polytheists drive you to abandon justice so that you transgress against them. This is the utmost that the highest ideals and the loftiest human values can reach.

dervis-irab:9-11.t:
* I'rab:
(وَعَدَ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ): resumptive speech introduced to set out His promise, Glorified is He, for the human soul is by nature inclined to ask for an explanation of this promise. (وعد الله) is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); (الذين) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause (آمنوا) is the ṣila (relative clause), and (عملوا الصالحات) is conjoined to the ṣila.
(لَهُمْ مَغْفِرَةٌ وَأَجْرٌ عَظِيمٌ): (لهم), the preposition and its genitive noun, is attached to an omitted fronted khabar (predicate); (مغفرة) is a delayed mubtadaʾ (subject). The clause may be explicative of the omitted second object of the verb «وعد», whose implied form is «الجنة» (Paradise); or it may be an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī), as though He said: a people have a promise; and it was asked: what is it that He promised them? So He said: for them is forgiveness and a great reward. On this view too it has no grammatical position.
You may also make it the object of an omitted verb of saying, which contains additional confirmation of what was promised and emphasis on its occurrence. It has also been said: it is a clause in the position of accusative as the second object of His saying «وعد», in the sense: He promised them that for them is forgiveness, or He promised them forgiveness. So the clause stood in the place of a single word and dispensed with it.
(وَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وَكَذَّبُوا بِآياتِنا أُولئِكَ أَصْحابُ الْجَحِيمِ): the wāw is resumptive; (الذين) is a mubtadaʾ; the clause (كفروا) is the ṣila, and the clause (كذبوا بآياتنا) is conjoined to the ṣila; (أولئك) is a second mubtadaʾ; (أصحاب الجحيم) is the khabar of (أولئك); and the nominal clause is the khabar of (الذين).
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا): its parsing has been given many times.
(اذْكُرُوا نِعْمَتَ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ): its parsing has been given shortly before; the clause is resumptive.
(إِذْ هَمَّ قَوْمٌ أَنْ يَبْسُطُوا إِلَيْكُمْ أَيْدِيَهُمْ): (إذ) is an adverb for the favour, attached to it; it may also be attached to (اذكروا). The clause (همّ قوم) is in the position of genitive by annexation; (أن يبسطوا) is an interpreted maṣdar, accusative by removal of the preposition, and the [implied] preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «همّ»; (إليكم) is attached to (يبسطوا); and (أيديهم) is the direct object.
(فَكَفَّ أَيْدِيَهُمْ عَنْكُمْ): conjoined to what precedes.
(وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَعَلَى اللَّهِ فَلْيَتَوَكَّلِ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ): the wāw is resumptive; (اتقوا الله) is a verb, its agent and its object; (على الله) is attached to (يتوكل); the fāʾ is resumptive and the lām is the lām of command; (يتوكل) is an imperfect verb, jussive by the lām of command; and (المؤمنون) is the agent.

* Rhetoric:
"Stretching out the hand" is an expression of loose metaphor (majāz mursal) whose relation is causality, because the hand is the cause of harm; just as "stretching out the tongue" is a metaphorical expression whose relation is causality.

dervis-irab:12-12.t:
* Vocabulary:
(نَقِيباً): the «نقيب» of a people is the one who investigates their conditions and looks into their affairs. It is of the pattern «فعيل» in the sense of an active participle (fāʿil), derived from «التنقيب», which is searching.
From it is the saying of the Exalted: «فنقّبوا في البلاد» (and they searched through the lands). He is so called because he searches into the conditions and secrets of the people. It has also been said that it is in the sense of a passive participle (mafʿūl), as though the people chose him knowingly. It has also been said that it is for intensiveness, like «عليم» and «خبير».
(عَزَّرْتُمُوهُمْ): you supported them. In al-Mukhtār: «التعزير» is honouring and exalting.

* I'rab:
(وَلَقَدْ أَخَذَ اللَّهُ مِيثاقَ بَنِي إِسْرائِيلَ): resumptive speech introduced to mention some of what issued from the Children of Israel; in it is an urging of the believers to remember the favour of Allah and to observe the right of the covenant, and a warning against breaking it. The lām is [in] the answer to an omitted oath; (قد) is a particle of affirmation (taḥqīq); (أخذ الله) is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); (ميثاق) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and (بني إسرائيل) is the muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
(وَبَعَثْنا مِنْهُمُ اثْنَيْ عَشَرَ نَقِيباً): (بعثنا) is conjoined to (أخذ); (منهم) is attached to «نقيبا», or is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «اثني عشر»; (اثني عشر) is the direct object of (بعثنا); and (نقيبا) is a tamyīz (specification).
(وَقالَ اللَّهُ إِنِّي مَعَكُمْ): the wāw is a conjunction, by way of iltifāt (shift of person); (قال الله) is a verb and its agent; (إني) is inna with its noun; (معكم) is an adverb attached to its omitted khabar (predicate); and (إن) with what falls within its scope is the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl).
(لَئِنْ أَقَمْتُمُ الصَّلاةَ وَآتَيْتُمُ الزَّكاةَ): the lām prepares for the omitted oath (al-lām al-muwaṭṭiʾa); (إن) is conditional; (أقمتم) is a verb and its agent, in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); (الصلاة) is the direct object; (آتيتم الزكاة) is conjoined to (أقمتم الصلاة); and the oath clause is resumptive.
(وَآمَنْتُمْ بِرُسُلِي وَعَزَّرْتُمُوهُمْ وَأَقْرَضْتُمُ اللَّهَ قَرْضاً حَسَناً): conjoined to what precedes; (برسلي) is attached to (آمنتم); (عزرتموهم) is also conjoined: a verb and its agent, the wāw being for prolonging the ḍamma, and the hāʾ the direct object; (أقرضتم الله) is a verb, its agent and its direct object; (قرضا) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); and (حسنا) is an adjective.
(لَأُكَفِّرَنَّ عَنْكُمْ سَيِّئاتِكُمْ وَلَأُدْخِلَنَّكُمْ جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهارُ): the lām occurs in the answer to the oath; the clause has no grammatical position because it is the answer to the oath, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by the answer to the oath that precedes it. (عنكم) is attached to (أكفرن); (سيئاتكم) is the direct object; (لأدخلنكم) is conjoined to «لأكفرن»; (جنات) is a second object by extension of usage (ʿalā al-saʿa), or accusative by removal of the preposition; and the clause (تجري من تحتها الأنهار) is an adjective of (جنات).
(فَمَنْ كَفَرَ بَعْدَ ذلِكَ مِنْكُمْ فَقَدْ ضَلَّ سَواءَ السَّبِيلِ):
the fāʾ is resumptive. (من) is conditional, a mubtadaʾ (subject); (كفر) is a past verb in the position of jussive as the protasis; (بعد ذلك) is an adverb attached to (كفر); (منكم) is attached to an omitted ḥāl; in (فقد) the fāʾ links the apodosis, and the clause is in the position of jussive as the apodosis; the protasis and its apodosis form the khabar of «من»; and (سواء السبيل) is the object of (ضل).

* Rhetoric:
In the saying of the Exalted «وأقرضتم الله قرضا حسنا» there is an explicit metaphor (istiʿāra taṣrīḥiyya).
Spending in the way of Allah for His sake is likened to a loan, by way of metaphor, because by giving the deserving person what is his for the sake of Allah, it is as though he lent it to Him.

dervis-irab:13-13.t:
* Vocabulary:
(لَعَنَّاهُمْ): We expelled them and removed them far from Our mercy.
(خائِنَةٍ): «الخائنة» here means treachery (الخيانة). The Arabs sometimes express the maṣdar (verbal noun) with the form of the active participle, and the reverse; thus «القائلة» was used in the sense of «القيلولة» (the midday nap), and «الخاطئة» in the sense of «الخطيئة» (sin). Or it is an adjective of an omitted noun: either masculine, with the hāʾ for intensiveness, as they said «راوية للشعر» for one who transmits poetry a great deal; [the poet] said:
حدثت نفسك بالوفاء ولم تكن ... للغدر خائنة مغلّ الإصبع
(You told yourself of loyalty, yet you were not one given to treachery, a finger that steals [from the spoils].)
and «داعية» for one who has devoted himself to calling to something. Or it is feminine, with the implied form:
or «فرقة» (a faction). «[Translator's note: the text appears abridged here; the usual wording is «نفس خائنة أو فرقة خائنة» (a treacherous soul or a treacherous faction).]»

* I'rab:
(فَبِما نَقْضِهِمْ مِيثاقَهُمْ لَعَنَّاهُمْ): resumptive speech introduced to show that the expulsion and removal from mercy that befell them arose from their breaking the covenant. The bāʾ is a preposition; (ما) is redundant (zāʾida), to emphasise the statement; (نقضهم) is genitive by the bāʾ, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (لعناهم); (ميثاقهم) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the maṣdar, namely «النقض»; and (لعناهم) is a verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its direct object.
(وَجَعَلْنا قُلُوبَهُمْ قاسِيَةً): (جعلنا) is conjoined to (لعناهم); (قلوبهم) is the first object and (قاسية) the second object.
(يُحَرِّفُونَ الْكَلِمَ عَنْ مَواضِعِهِ): the clause is resumptive, introduced to show the extent of the hardness of their hearts; (الكلم) is the object of (يحرفون); and (عن مواضعه) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (يحرفون).
(وَنَسُوا حَظًّا مِمَّا ذُكِّرُوا بِهِ): conjoined to what precedes; (نسوا حظا) is a verb, its agent and its direct object; (مما), a preposition and its genitive noun, is attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of «حظا»; and the clause (ذكروا به) has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause).
(وَلا تَزالُ تَطَّلِعُ عَلى خائِنَةٍ مِنْهُمْ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا مِنْهُمْ): the wāw is a conjunction; (لا تزال) is a defective (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb, its noun latent (mustatir), implied as «أنت»; the clause (تطلع) is the khabar (predicate) of (لا تزال); (على خائنة) is attached to (تطلع); (منهم) is attached to an omitted adjective of (خائنة); (إلا) is a particle of exception, and (قليلا) is excepted from the genitive pronoun in «منهم»; (منهم) is attached to an omitted adjective of «قليلا». By "the few of them" He meant those who embraced Islam, such as ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām and his companions.
(فَاعْفُ عَنْهُمْ وَاصْفَحْ): the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (implying an omitted condition), i.e. if you know this, then pardon whoever comes to you declaring his repentance and his joining under the banner of the upright religion. (اعف) is an imperative verb; (عنهم) is attached to «اعف»; and (اصفح) is conjoined to (فاعف).
(إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ الْمُحْسِنِينَ): inna and its noun; the clause (يحب المحسنين) is the khabar of (إن); and the clause of (إن) and what falls within its scope is causal, with no grammatical position.

dervis-irab:92-93.t:
* I'rab:
(وَأَطِيعُوا اللَّهَ وَأَطِيعُوا الرَّسُولَ وَاحْذَرُوا): the wāw is conjunctive, and the speech is conjoined to the interrogative in the preceding verse, because the interrogative has the meaning of a command, as has been stated. The meaning is: "Desist, and obey." You may also make it resumptive. أطيعوا الله is a verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); أطيعوا الرسول is conjoined to أطيعوا الله; and احذروا is likewise conjoined. (فَإِنْ تَوَلَّيْتُمْ فَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّما عَلى رَسُولِنَا الْبَلاغُ الْمُبِينُ): the fāʾ is resumptive; إن is conditional; توليتم is a past verb and its agent, in the position of the jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the fāʾ links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and the apodosis is omitted, its implied form being "then your requital is upon Us" (فجزاؤكم علينا); the clause فاعلموا is conjoined to the apodosis. أنما is [أنّ with] the restraining mā (kāffa and makfūfa), and together with what it governs it stands in place of the two objects of اعلموا; على رسولنا is a preposition and its genitive noun attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted fronted khabar (predicate); البلاغ is a delayed mubtadaʾ (subject); and المبين is a naʿt (adjective). (لَيْسَ عَلَى الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ جُناحٌ فِيما طَعِمُوا): the clause is resumptive, brought in reply to the question of some of the Companions who said: "O Messenger of Allah, what then of our brothers who died while they were drinking [Translator's note: the text has the misprint «بشربون» for «يشربون».] wine and consuming [the proceeds of] gambling?" So there was revealed: ليس ... ليس is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb; على الذين is attached to the omitted fronted khabar of ليس; the clause آمنوا has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause); the clause وعملوا الصالحات is conjoined to the ṣila; جناح is the delayed noun of ليس; فيما is attached to an omitted adjective of جناح; and the clause طعموا has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila. (إِذا مَا اتَّقَوْا وَآمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ): إذا is an adverb of future time containing the sense of a condition; ما is redundant (zāʾida); the clause اتقوا is in the position of the genitive as the adverb is put in construct with it; what governs إذا is the sense of negation in ليس, i.e. "sin is negated from them"; the apodosis of إذا is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, i.e. "then there is no blame upon them"; آمنوا is conjoined to اتقوا; and عملوا الصالحات is likewise conjoined to what precedes. (ثُمَّ اتَّقَوْا وَآمَنُوا ثُمَّ اتَّقَوْا وَأَحْسَنُوا): likewise conjoined; the secret of this marvellous repetition will come in the section on rhetoric. (وَاللَّهُ يُحِبُّ الْمُحْسِنِينَ): the wāw is resumptive; الله is a mubtadaʾ; the clause يحب is the khabar; and المحسنين is the direct object.

* Rhetoric:
The discussion of repetition (al-takrār or al-tikrār — both maṣdars of the doubled verb كرّر) has preceded, and we said that its definition is that the writer or poet repeats a word, or two words or more, to emphasize what he is speaking about, so that it becomes more firmly fixed in the mind, or for some other purpose. In this verse the repetition may be an allusion to the relationships by which a person is bound in his life, namely: a person's relationship with himself, his relationship with others, and his relationship with his Lord; that is why it is followed by iḥsān (excellence) the third time. It may also be an allusion to the three stages of life through which a person passes on his life's journey: the stage of the beginning of life, the stage of the middle of life, and the final stage. Perhaps both possibilities are intended in this marvellous repetition, as an increase in piety, in adornment [of character] and in the upholding of just scales in all the stages of his life and his three states. There will come in this book instances of repetition that enchant the minds. Listen to the words of al-Buḥturī in love poetry:
ويوم تثنّت للوداع وسلّمت ... بعينين موصول بلحظهما السحر
توهمتها ألوى بأجفانها الكرى ... كرى النوم أو مالت بأعطافها الخمر
(And on the day she swayed for the farewell and greeted with two eyes whose glance is joined with magic, I imagined that drowsiness — the drowsiness of sleep — had bent her eyelids, or that wine had made her sides sway.) الكرى is sleep, but in repeating it here there is a meaning grasped intuitively, resembling the seizure of magic.
And listen to the words of al-Musāwir ibn Hind:
جزى الله عنّي غالبا من عشيرة ... إذا حدثان الدهر نابت نوائبه
فكم دافعوا من كربة قد تلاحمت ... عليّ وموج قد علتني غواربه
(May Allah reward on my behalf [the tribe of] Ghālib as kinsfolk, when the calamities of time strike; how many a distress that closed in upon me did they repel, and how many a wave whose crests had towered over me!) The first and second halves of the second verse indicate one meaning, because the closing in of distresses upon him is like the towering of the waves above him. What made this acceptable is that it is a context of praise and eulogy; do you not see that he describes the kindness of these people at the calamities of his time through repetition! And conversely, were the speaker satirizing, satire in this would be like praise.
Here we would like to add a qualification and say: not all repetition is good; some of it is insipid, such as the words of Abū al-Ṭayyib al-Mutanabbī from his marvellous ode which opens:
أفاضل الناس أغراض لذا الزمن ... يخلو من الهمّ أخلاهم من الفطن
(The most excellent of people are targets for this age; the one freest of care is the one most devoid of intelligence.)
This is among the most beautiful and splendid poetry; yet soon afterwards he said:
العارض الهتن ابن العارض ال ... هتن العارض الهتن ابن العارض الهتن
(The pouring raincloud, son of the pouring raincloud, the pouring raincloud, son of the pouring raincloud.) This is not commendable repetition, because it is like your saying: "the one described as such-and-such, son of the one described as such-and-such", i.e. that he is of deep-rooted lineage in this quality; so he brought nothing new. Moreover, the wording is not acceptable in the way it has been used here, for using it in the compound state takes away its beauty. Among the delightful instances of repetition are the words of al-Muqannaʿ al-Kindī:
وإنّ الذي بيني وبين بني أبي ... وبين بني عمي لمختلف جدا
إذا أكلوا لحمي وفرت لحومهم ... وإن هدموا مجدي بنيت لهم مجدا
وإن ضيعوا غيبي حفظت غيوبهم ... وإن هم هووا غيّي هويت لهم رشدا
(What lies between me and my father's sons and my cousins is very different indeed: if they eat my flesh, I preserve their flesh; if they demolish my glory, I build glory for them; if they neglect me in my absence, I guard them in theirs; and if they desire my going astray, I desire right guidance for them.)
What has preceded is sufficient for us for now.

dervis-irab:94-94.t:
* Vocabulary:
(لَيَبْلُوَنَّكُمُ): He will surely test your obedience.

* I'rab:
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لَيَبْلُوَنَّكُمُ اللَّهُ بِشَيْءٍ مِنَ الصَّيْدِ): resumptive speech brought to [speak of] testing them in relation to what the servants understand; as for the reality of testing, it is impossible with respect to Him the Exalted. ليبلونكم: the lām is [the lām of] the answer to an omitted oath, i.e. "By Allah, He will surely test you"; يبلون is an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa because it is attached to the heavy nūn of emphasis; الله is its fāʿil (agent); بشيء is attached (mutaʿalliq) to يبلونكم; من الصيد is attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of شيء; and the clause يبلونكم has no grammatical position because it is the answer to the omitted oath. (تَنالُهُ أَيْدِيكُمْ وَرِماحُكُمْ لِيَعْلَمَ اللَّهُ مَنْ يَخافُهُ بِالْغَيْبِ): the clause is an adjective of شيء; أيديكم is the agent of تناله; رماحكم is conjoined to أيديكم; the lām is causal; يعلم is an imperfect verb in the accusative by an implied أن after the lām; الله is the agent of يعلم; من is a relative noun, the object of يعلم; the clause يخافه has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause); and بالغيب is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of يخاف, i.e. he fears Allah while being absent from Allah [Translator's note: so in the text: «غائبا عن الله».], or from the mafʿūl bihi (direct object), i.e. he fears Allah while being clothed in the unseen. (فَمَنِ اعْتَدى بَعْدَ ذلِكَ فَلَهُ عَذابٌ أَلِيمٌ): the fāʾ is resumptive; من is a jussive conditional noun; اعتدى is a past verb in the position of the jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the adverb بعد ذلك is attached to اعتدى, and the demonstrative is muḍāf ilayhi; فله: the fāʾ links the apodosis, and له is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted fronted khabar (predicate); عذاب is a delayed mubtadaʾ (subject); أليم is an adjective; the nominal clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); and the protasis and its apodosis are the khabar of «من».

* Rhetoric:
In His words «بشيء من الصيد» there is a diminishing and belittling of this trial, as if He were saying: this trial is not of the kind of great tribulations and great ordeals before which neither strength nor bodies stand firm. This is what the great exegetes have mentioned, especially al-Zamakhsharī, whose wording most of them have transmitted almost verbatim. It is a strong intellectual leap, but it shrinks and weighs light in the balance when we recall that He, glory be to Him, used it for great tribulations and grievous ordeals, saying in another place: «ولنبلونكم بشيء من الخوف والجوع ونقص من الأموال والأنفس والثمرات وبشر الصابرين». This is an objection that overturns what al-Zamakhsharī said and what many exegetes have transmitted from him, such as al-Khāzin, al-Nasafī, al-Bayḍāwī and others. The best that can be said in reply to this objection is that all ordeals, calamities, trials and tribulations are, in relation to what lies within the power of Allah the Exalted, nothing but a small part fit to be belittled and diminished, and that He, glory be to Him, inclined to addressing the believers with this formulation to lighten things for them, as a motive for them to be patient and an incentive for them to endure, out of gentleness toward them and kindness regarding what they suffer from it. So glory be to the One who is unique in this eloquence.

dervis-irab:14-14.t:
* Vocabulary:
(نَصارى): In Mukhtār al-Ṣiḥāḥ: «النصير» is the helper (الناصر), and its plural is «أنصار», like «شريف» and «أشراف»; the plural of «الناصر» is «نصر», like «صاحب» and «صحب». «النصارى» is the plural of «نصران» and «نصرانة», like «الندامى», plural of «ندمان» and «ندمانة». «نصران» is only used with the yāʾ of relation (nisba). In al-Miṣbāḥ: a «نصراني» man, with fatḥa on the nūn, and a «نصرانية» woman. It is said to be a relation to a village named «نصرى»; for this reason one says in the singular «نصري», according to rule; then «النصراني» came to be applied to everyone who worships by this religion. In al-Munjid it says: «النصراني» is a relation to the city of al-Nāṣira (Nazareth), irregularly: one who follows the religion of the Lord Christ; the plural is «نصارى» and the feminine «نصرانية». In al-Lisān it says: «نَصَرى» with two fatḥas, «نَصْرى» with fatḥa then sukūn, «ناصرة» and «نصورية»: a village in Syria, and the Naṣārā are named after it. Ibn Sīdah said: this is the view of the lexicographers. He said: it is weak, except that irregular nisba forms can accommodate it. He said: As for Sībawayh, he said: as for «نصارى», al-Khalīl held that it is the plural of «نصري» and «نصران», just as they said «ندمان» and «ندامى»; but they deleted one of the two yāʾs, as they deleted [one] from «أثفيّة», and substituted an alif in its place, as they said «صحارى». He said: as for the way we ourselves explain it, it came on «نصران», because that has been spoken; so it is as though you pluralised «نصر» as you pluralised «مسمع», and said «نصارى» as you said «ندامى».
(أغرينا): We attached and made binding. It is from «غري بالشيء» when one clings to a thing and sticks to it; and «الغراء» means that by which something is stuck, «الغراء» being on the pattern of «كتاب». In al-Miṣbāḥ: «غري بالشيء غريا», of the pattern of «تعب»: he became infatuated with it without anyone driving him to it; «أغريته به إغراء», so «أغري به», in the passive; the noun is «الغَراء», with fatḥa and prolongation, and «الغِراء», like «كتاب»: that with which things are stuck (glue), made from hides, and sometimes made from fish.
«الغرا», like «العصا», is a dialectal form of it. «غروت الجلد أغروه», of the pattern of «عدا»:
I stuck it with glue. «أغريت بين القوم» is like «أفسدت» (I sowed discord) in form and meaning. «غروت غروا», of the pattern of «قتل»: I was amazed; and «لا غرو»: no wonder.

* I'rab:
(وَمِنَ الَّذِينَ قالُوا: إِنَّا نَصارى أَخَذْنا مِيثاقَهُمْ): resumptive speech introduced to speak about the Christians. The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (أخذنا); the clause (قالوا) has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause); (إن) with its noun, and (نصارى) its khabar (predicate); the clause (أخذنا) is resumptive, as stated; (ميثاقهم) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and the clause (إنا نصارى) is the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl). There are other views, which you will see in the section on benefits.
(فَنَسُوا حَظًّا مِمَّا ذُكِّرُوا بِهِ): the fāʾ is a conjunction; (نسوا) is conjoined to (أخذنا), the wāw being the fāʿil (agent); (حظا) is the direct object; (مما) is attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of «حظا»; the clause (ذكروا) is the ṣila; (به), a preposition and its genitive noun, is attached to (ذكروا); and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).
(فَأَغْرَيْنا بَيْنَهُمُ الْعَداوَةَ وَالْبَغْضاءَ إِلى يَوْمِ الْقِيامَةِ): conjoined to what precedes; (أغرينا) is a verb and its agent; the adverb is attached to (أغرينا); (العداوة) is the direct object; and (إلى يوم القيامة) is attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e.:
extending to the Day of Resurrection.
(وَسَوْفَ يُنَبِّئُهُمُ اللَّهُ بِما كانُوا يَصْنَعُونَ): the wāw is a conjunction; (سوف) is a particle of futurity; (ينبئهم) is a verb, its agent and its direct object; (بما) is attached to (ينبئهم); the clause (كانوا) is the ṣila; and the clause (يصنعون) is the khabar of (كانوا).

* Benefits:
Some parsers have brought the views they allowed in this verse to a number, among them the one we chose, which is the view of al-Zamakhsharī, except that he made the pronoun in (ميثاقهم) refer back to the Children of Israel, the implied form being: "and We took from the Christians a covenant like the covenant of the Children of Israel." There is a view worth mentioning: that His saying «ومن الذين» is attached to an omitted [element], being the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject) whose adjective stands in its place, the implied form being: "and among those who said 'We are Christians' are a people whose covenant We took."

dervis-irab:15-16.t:
* I'rab:
(يا أَهْلَ الْكِتابِ قَدْ جاءَكُمْ رَسُولُنا): resumptive speech introduced to address the People of the Book in general, by way of iltifāt (shift of person). (يا) is a vocative particle for the one at a middle distance; (أهل الكتاب) is a vocative in construct, accusative; (قد) is a particle of affirmation (taḥqīq); (جاءكم) is a past verb with a fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and (رسولنا) is the delayed fāʿil (agent).
(يُبَيِّنُ لَكُمْ كَثِيراً مِمَّا كُنْتُمْ تُخْفُونَ مِنَ الْكِتابِ): the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «رسولنا»; (لكم) is attached to (يبين); (كثيرا) is the direct object; (مما), a preposition and its genitive noun, is attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of «كثيرا»; (ما) is a relative noun; (كنتم) is kāna with its noun, and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause); the clause (تخفون) is in the position of accusative as the khabar (predicate) of (كنتم); and (من الكتاب), a preposition and its genitive noun, is attached to an omitted ḥāl from the omitted referent pronoun.
(وَيَعْفُوا عَنْ كَثِيرٍ): the clause is conjoined to the circumstantial clause «يبين» and enters into its ruling.
(قَدْ جاءَكُمْ مِنَ اللَّهِ نُورٌ وَكِتابٌ مُبِينٌ): a resumptive clause introduced to set out the benefit of the Messenger's coming. (من الله), a preposition and its genitive noun, is attached to an omitted ḥāl, because it was originally an adjective of (نور) and was placed before it. (نور) is the agent of «جاءكم»; (كتاب) is conjoined to «نور»; and (مبين) is an adjective.
(يَهْدِي بِهِ اللَّهُ مَنِ اتَّبَعَ رِضْوانَهُ سُبُلَ السَّلامِ): the clause is an adjective of (كتاب); (به) is attached to (يهدي); (الله) is the agent; (من) is a relative noun, the direct object; the clause (اتبع رضوانه) is the ṣila; and (سبل السلام) is a second object of (يهدي) by extension of usage (ʿalā al-saʿa), or accusative by removal of the preposition, the [implied] preposition and its genitive noun being attached to (يهدي).
(وَيُخْرِجُهُمْ مِنَ الظُّلُماتِ إِلَى النُّورِ بِإِذْنِهِ): the wāw is a conjunction; (يخرجهم) is conjoined to (يهدي), the hāʾ being the direct object; (من الظلمات) is attached to (يخرجهم), and likewise (إلى النور); and (بإذنه), a preposition and its genitive noun, is attached to an omitted ḥāl.
(وَيَهْدِيهِمْ إِلى صِراطٍ مُسْتَقِيمٍ): conjoined to what precedes; its parsing has been given many times.

* Rhetoric:
In the saying of the Exalted «من الظلمات إلى النور» there are two explicit, primary metaphors (istiʿāra taṣrīḥiyya aṣliyya): by the first is meant misguidance, and by the second guidance and faith; the relation is resemblance. The word for the thing likened was dropped «[Translator's note: the printed text reads «وقد لفظ المشبه», apparently for «وقد حذف لفظ المشبه» (the word for the thing likened was omitted)]», and the word for the thing it is likened to was borrowed in its place to stand for it, by claiming that the thing likened-to is the very thing likened. This reaches further in eloquence and is more deeply rooted in it. Since the thing likened-to is stated explicitly in this figurative usage, the metaphor is called explicit (taṣrīḥiyya); and it is called primary (aṣliyya) because it occurs in a noun. Among explicit metaphors is the saying of Abū al-Ṭayyib [al-Mutanabbī]:
وأقبل يمشي في البساط فما درى ... إلى البحر يسعى أم إلى البدر يرتقي
(He came forward walking on the carpet, not knowing whether he was striding to the sea or climbing to the full moon.)
He likened Sayf al-Dawla to the sea; then the word denoting the thing likened-to, namely the sea, was borrowed for the thing likened, namely Sayf al-Dawla, by way of explicit metaphor; the contextual clue (qarīna) is "he came forward walking on the carpet." The same is said of likening Sayf al-Dawla to the full moon.

dervis-irab:17-17.t:
* Vocabulary:
(يَمْلِكُ): The Arabs say «ملك فلان على فلان أمره» when he has gained mastery over him, so that he can neither carry out any matter nor do anything except through him and with his permission.
Ibn Durayd said, describing wine whose sharpness has not been broken by mixing and whose effect fire has not nullified:
لم يملك الماء عليها أمرها ... ولم يدنّسها الضّرم المحتضى
(Water did not gain mastery over her affair, nor did the stirred-up blaze defile her.)
His saying, the Exalted, «فمن يملك من الله شيئا» is more eloquent than a saying like this, because it denies that anyone has power over any part of His affair, the Exalted, let alone power over His whole affair; so the meaning becomes that there is no one who can turn back His command and divert it from His will in any way.

* I'rab:
(لَقَدْ كَفَرَ الَّذِينَ قالُوا: إِنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ الْمَسِيحُ ابْنُ مَرْيَمَ): the lām occurs in the answer to an omitted oath; (قد) is a particle of affirmation (taḥqīq); (كفر) is a past verb and (الذين) its fāʿil (agent); the clause (قالوا) is the ṣila (relative clause); the oath clause is resumptive; the clause (قد كفر) has no grammatical position because it is the answer to the oath. (إن) with its noun and its khabar (predicate) is the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl); (هو) is a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl) conveying restriction, with no governing effect, and (المسيح) is the khabar of (إن); or «هو» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and (المسيح) its khabar, the clause being the khabar of (إن); and (ابن مريم) is a badal (substitute) or a naʿt (adjective).
(قُلْ فَمَنْ يَمْلِكُ مِنَ اللَّهِ شَيْئاً): the clause is resumptive; (قل) is an imperative verb whose agent is «أنت»; the fāʾ conjoins to an omitted clause which is the object of «قل», i.e.:
say [this] by way of rebuke and to show the falsehood of their saying. (من) is a noun of rhetorical (denying) interrogation, a mubtadaʾ; the clause (يملك) is the khabar; (من الله), a preposition and its genitive noun, is attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) or to (يملك); and (شيئا) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
(إِنْ أَرادَ أَنْ يُهْلِكَ الْمَسِيحَ ابْنَ مَرْيَمَ وَأُمَّهُ): the conditional clause is explicative, with no grammatical position. (إن) is conditional; (أراد) is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); (أن) with what falls within its scope is interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun), the object of (أراد); (المسيح) is the direct object; (ابن مريم) is a badal or a naʿt; (أمه) is conjoined to (المسيح); and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes, i.e. "then who has any power at all against Allah."
(وَمَنْ فِي الْأَرْضِ جَمِيعاً): the wāw is a conjunction; (من) is a relative noun conjoined to (المسيح) and (أمه); (في الأرض) is attached to an omitted ṣila; and (جميعا) is a ḥāl.
(وَلِلَّهِ مُلْكُ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَما بَيْنَهُما): the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); (لله), a preposition and its genitive noun, is attached to an omitted fronted khabar; (ملك السموات والأرض) is the delayed mubtadaʾ; as for (وما بينهما): the wāw conjoins to (ملك), (ما) is a relative noun, and the adverb is attached to an omitted ṣila.
(يَخْلُقُ ما يَشاءُ): the clause is resumptive, introduced to show that He, Glorified is He, creates creation according to His will.
(وَاللَّهُ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ): the speech is resumptive, introduced to set out His power, the Exalted, over everything: everything to which His will is connected is carried out by His power, and some of His creation is counted strange only relative to deficient human knowledge, not relative to Him, the Exalted. Its parsing has been given before.

dervis-irab:18-19.t:
* Vocabulary:
(فترة): from «فتر الشيء», when a thing became still or its sharpness subsided. Al-Rāghib said:
«الفتور» is stillness after sharpness, softness after severity, and weakness after strength; and he mentioned the verse. What is meant by it here is the cessation of revelation and of the appearance of messengers for several centuries.

* I'rab:
(وَقالَتِ الْيَهُودُ وَالنَّصارى): the wāw is resumptive; (قالت اليهود) is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); (النصارى) is conjoined to (اليهود).
(نَحْنُ أَبْناءُ اللَّهِ وَأَحِبَّاؤُهُ): the clause is the object of their saying (maqūl al-qawl); (نحن) is a mubtadaʾ (subject), (أبناء الله) the khabar (predicate), and (أحباؤه) is conjoined to (أبناء الله).
(قُلْ: فَلِمَ يُعَذِّبُكُمْ بِذُنُوبِكُمْ؟): the speech is resumptive, introduced to refute these claims. (قل) is an imperative verb, the agent being «أنت»; the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (implying an omitted condition), i.e. if you are as you claim, then why does He punish you for the sins you commit! In (لم), the lām is a preposition and (ما) is an interrogative noun whose alif was dropped because the preposition entered upon it; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (يعذبكم). (يعذبكم) is an imperfect verb and its object, the agent being «هو»; (بذنوبكم), a preposition and its genitive noun, is also attached to (يعذبكم). The whole clause is the object of their saying «[Translator's note: so in the text; the clause is in fact the object of «قل» (say)]», and the clause (لم يعذبكم) has no grammatical position because it occurs as the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
(بَلْ أَنْتُمْ بَشَرٌ مِمَّنْ خَلَقَ): (بل) is a particle of digression (iḍrāb) and conjunction, conjoining to an omitted [clause] drawn from the sense of the preceding speech, i.e. "so you are not, then, of this standing in nearness to Him, Glorified is He." (أنتم) is a mubtadaʾ and (بشر) the khabar; (ممن), a preposition and its genitive noun, is attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of (بشر); and the clause (خلق) is the ṣila (relative clause) of «من».
(يَغْفِرُ لِمَنْ يَشاءُ وَيُعَذِّبُ مَنْ يَشاءُ): the clause is resumptive; (لمن), a preposition and its genitive noun, is attached to (يغفر); the clause (يشاء) is the ṣila; and the clause (يعذب من يشاء) is conjoined to the foregoing clause.
(وَلِلَّهِ مُلْكُ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَما بَيْنَهُما وَإِلَيْهِ الْمَصِيرُ): the clause is resumptive; (لله) is attached to an omitted fronted khabar; (ملك السموات) is the delayed mubtadaʾ; (الأرض) is conjoined to (السموات); (ما) is also conjoined; the adverb is attached to an omitted ṣila. In (وإليه المصير), the wāw is a conjunction; (إليه), a preposition and its genitive noun, is attached to an omitted fronted khabar; (المصير) is the delayed mubtadaʾ; and the clause is conjoined to the clause (ولله ملك السموات والأرض).
(يا أَهْلَ الْكِتابِ قَدْ جاءَكُمْ رَسُولُنا): (يا) is a vocative particle; (أهل الكتاب) is a vocative in construct; (قد) is a particle of affirmation (taḥqīq); (جاءكم رسولنا) is a verb, its mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and its agent; and the clause is resumptive.
(يُبَيِّنُ لَكُمْ عَلى فَتْرَةٍ مِنَ الرُّسُلِ): the clause (يبين) is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «رسولنا», i.e. "explaining to you"; (لكم) is attached to (يبين); (على فترة), a preposition and its genitive noun, is attached to (جاءكم), i.e. he came to you at a time of lapse in the sending of messengers and the cessation of revelation; or [it is attached] to an omitted [element] occurring as a ḥāl from the pronoun of (يبين), or from the pronoun of (لكم).
I.e. he explains to you what has been mentioned while he is [coming] after a lapse of messengers, or while you are in it, at a time you were most in need of explanation. (من الرسل), a preposition and its genitive noun, is attached to an omitted adjective of (فترة), i.e. "occurring from the messengers."
(أَنْ تَقُولُوا: ما جاءَنا مِنْ بَشِيرٍ وَلا نَذِيرٍ): in (أن تقولوا), the maṣdar formed from «أن» and the verb after it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose) with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "out of aversion to your saying"; or it is accusative by removal of the preposition, with negation implied, i.e. «لئلا تقولوا» (lest you say). The clause (ما جاءنا) is in the position of accusative as the object of saying; (من) is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition, and (بشير) is the agent of (جاءنا) in position; and (ولا نذير) is conjoined to (من بشير).
(فَقَدْ جاءَكُمْ بَشِيرٌ وَنَذِيرٌ): the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa, i.e. if you excuse yourselves with that, then a bearer of good tidings and a warner has come to you.
(جاءكم بشير) is a verb, its direct object and its agent; (نذير) is conjoined to (بشير); and the clause has no grammatical position because it occurs as the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
(وَاللَّهُ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ): the wāw is resumptive; (الله) is a mubtadaʾ and (قدير) its khabar; and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (قدير).

dervis-irab:48-48.t:
* Vocabulary:
(مُهَيْمِناً): i.e. a witness and a watcher over all the Books, because it bears witness to their soundness and firmness. Ḥassān ibn Thābit said:
إنّ الكتاب مهيمن لنبيّنا ... والحقّ يعرفه ذوو الألباب
(The Book is a guardian for our Prophet, and the truth is recognised by those of understanding.) [Translator's note: the source prints «لنبيّا»; the verse is usually cited «لنبيّنا», and it is glossed accordingly.]
There is disagreement about the origin of its verb: is it a root in itself, i.e. not substituted from anything? One says هيمن يهيمن, and the active participle is مهيمن, like بيطر يبيطر, so he is مبيطر. Or is its hāʾ substituted from a hamza, it being the active participle of آمن غيره من الخوف ("he made another safe from fear")? The original form would be مؤأيمن with two hamzas; the second was changed into a yāʾ out of dislike for two hamzas coming together, and then the first was changed into a hāʾ.
(شِرْعَةً): الشرعة with kasra on the shīn is religion, and الشرع is like it; it is taken from الشريعة, which is the watering place where people come to draw water. It is so called because of its clarity and evidentness. Its plural is شرائع. شرّع الله لنا كذا يشرعه: He made it evident and clear. المشرعة, with fatḥa on the mīm and the rāʾ, is the watering place (شريعة الماء). Al-Azharī said: The Arabs do not call it مشرعة until the water is perennial, never ceasing, like river water, and also exposed, not drawn with a well-rope. If it is from rainwater, it is الكرع, with two fatḥas. And "people are شرع in this matter", with two fatḥas, the rāʾ also being made vowelless for lightness: i.e. equal.
(مِنْهاجاً): In al-Mukhtār: النهج, on the pattern of الفلس, is المنهج, i.e. the way (المذهب). المنهاج is the clear road. نهج الطريق: he made the road clear; and نهجه also means he travelled it; the conjugation class of both is that of قطع. النهج with two fatḥas is panting. In al-Miṣbāḥ: «نهج الطريق ينهج, with two fatḥas, means it became clear and evident, and أنهج with alif is like it; نهجته and انتهجته mean I made it clear; they are used both intransitively and transitively.»

* I'rab:
(وَأَنْزَلْنا إِلَيْكَ الْكِتابَ بِالْحَقِّ): the wāw is conjunctive; أنزلنا is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); إليك is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) أنزلنا; and بالحق is attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of الكتاب. (مُصَدِّقاً لِما بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ مِنَ الْكِتابِ): مصدقا is a ḥāl of الكتاب; لما is attached to «مصدقا»; بين is an adverb attached to an omitted ṣila (relative clause), and يديه is a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); من الكتاب is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl.
By الكتاب He meant the genus, i.e. the genus of the Books sent down from heaven. (وَمُهَيْمِناً عَلَيْهِ فَاحْكُمْ بَيْنَهُمْ بِما أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ): مهيمنا is conjoined to «مصدقا», and عليه is attached to «مهيمنا». فاحكم: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (implying an omitted condition), i.e. "since such is the status of the Qur'an, judge between the People of the Book, when they bring their disputes to you, by what Allah has sent down". احكم is an imperative verb; بينهم is an adverb attached to «فاحكم»; بما is attached to احكم; and the clause أنزل الله is the ṣila. (وَلا تَتَّبِعْ أَهْواءَهُمْ عَمَّا جاءَكَ مِنَ الْحَقِّ): the wāw is conjunctive; لا is prohibitive; تتبع is an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by the prohibitive لا; أهواءهم is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); عما جاءك is attached to an omitted ḥāl, i.e. "deviating"; and the clause جاءك is the ṣila. It has been said that «تتبع» includes the meaning of «تنحرف» ("deviate") or «تتزحزح» ("shift away"), so that the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to it. من الحق is attached to an omitted ḥāl of the fāʿil of جاءك, or of the relative «ما» itself. (لِكُلٍّ جَعَلْنا مِنْكُمْ شِرْعَةً وَمِنْهاجاً): resumptive speech, brought to induce the people of the two Books among his contemporaries to submit to what he brought. لكل is attached to «جعلنا», or it is the first object of جعلنا; منكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of the omitted noun replaced by the tanwīn of compensation that attaches to «لكل», i.e. "for every nation among you"; شرعة is the object of جعلنا, and منهاجا is conjoined to شرعة. (وَلَوْ شاءَ اللَّهُ لَجَعَلَكُمْ أُمَّةً واحِدَةً): the wāw is resumptive; لو is conditional; شاء الله is a verb and its fāʿil; the lām occurs in the apodosis of لو; the clause جعلكم has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition; أمة is the second object of جعلكم, and واحدة is a naʿt. (وَلكِنْ لِيَبْلُوَكُمْ فِي ما آتاكُمْ): the wāw is circumstantial; لكن is a particle of rectification (istidrāk), inoperative because it is lightened; in ليبلوكم the lām is of purpose, and يبلوكم is an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after the lām of purpose; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to something omitted, its implied form being "He willed"; فيما is attached to يبلوكم, and the clause آتاكم is the ṣila. (فَاسْتَبِقُوا الْخَيْراتِ إِلَى اللَّهِ مَرْجِعُكُمْ جَمِيعاً): the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa, i.e. "if the aspect of wisdom in this has become clear to you, then race". استبقوا is a verb and its fāʿil; الخيرات is a mafʿūl bihi, or accusative by removal of the preposition (manṣūb bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ), and perhaps this is preferable, because the basic usage of «استبق» is to make it transitive with «إلى», unless «استبق» is made to include the meaning of «ابتدر» ("hasten to"), in which case it is transitive by itself. إلى الله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted, fronted khabar (predicate), and مرجعكم is a delayed mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause is resumptive, brought as a reason for racing to good deeds. جميعا is a ḥāl of the kāf, because it is an agent in meaning, i.e. "you will return all together". (فَيُنَبِّئُكُمْ بِما كُنْتُمْ فِيهِ تَخْتَلِفُونَ): the fāʾ is conjunctive, joining to the meaning of مرجعكم, i.e. "you will return, and He will inform you"; the kāf is a mafʿūl bihi; بما is attached to ينبئكم; the clause كنتم is the ṣila; the tāʾ is the noun of كان, and the clause تختلفون is its khabar.

* Rhetoric:
In making the pronoun overt in His saying «الكتاب» [Translator's note: i.e. using the noun الكتاب again where a pronoun would have sufficed] there is a statement of its importance, and that it is the reference, the refuge and the safeguard when a matter becomes grave; this falls within the domain of the science of meanings (ʿilm al-maʿānī).
An instance of it in poetry is the saying of al-Buḥturī at the opening of his Sīniyya (ode rhyming in sīn):
صنت نفسي عما يدنس نفسي ... وترفعت عن جدا كلّ جبس
(I guarded my soul from what defiles my soul, and rose above the bounty of every base wretch.)

dervis-irab:49-49.t:
* I'rab:
(وَأَنِ احْكُمْ بَيْنَهُمْ بِما أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ): the wāw is resumptive, and the speech is resumptive, setting out how to judge between them. Al-Zamakhsharī made it conjunctive, joining to الكتاب, and how far-fetched that is is not hidden. أن with what follows it is to be interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun), accusative by removal of the preposition (manṣūb bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ), and what the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) is omitted, i.e. "and We enjoined you to judge". Abū Ḥayyān chose that the interpreted maṣdar be a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is omitted, the implied form being: "and your judging by what Allah has sent down is Our command and Our word"; or you may give its implied form by saying: "and among what is obligatory is your judging by what Allah has sent down". There is nothing wrong with what he said.
بينهم is an adverb attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); بما is attached to «احكم»; and the clause أنزل الله is the ṣila (relative clause). (وَلا تَتَّبِعْ أَهْواءَهُمْ وَاحْذَرْهُمْ أَنْ يَفْتِنُوكَ): the clause is conjoined to «احكم»; لا is prohibitive; تتبع is an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by «لا»; أهواءهم is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); احذرهم is also conjoined; and أن يفتنوك is an interpreted maṣdar, accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. "of their tempting you". You may make the interpreted maṣdar a badal ishtimāl (substitute of inclusion) for the hāʾ in «واحذرهم», because they contain the temptation. They also permitted the maṣdar to be a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), with an implied lām of cause and a negating لا [Translator's note: i.e. "lest they tempt you"]; I see this as strained, but many of the analysts have analysed it so. (عَنْ بَعْضِ ما أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ إِلَيْكَ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to يفتنوك; ما is a relative noun in the position of a genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause أنزل الله is the ṣila; and إليك is attached to أنزل. (فَإِنْ تَوَلَّوْا فَاعْلَمْ أَنَّما يُرِيدُ اللَّهُ أَنْ يُصِيبَهُمْ بِبَعْضِ ذُنُوبِهِمْ): the fāʾ is resumptive; إن is conditional; تولوا is a past verb and its fāʿil (agent), in the position of a jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the fāʾ links the apodosis; the clause اعلم is in the position of a jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); أنما is the restraining (kāffa) ما with the restrained particle, and it with what is in its scope stands in place of the two objects of اعلم; يريد is an imperfect verb and الله its fāʿil; the interpreted maṣdar is the object of يريد; and ببعض is attached to يصيبهم. (وَإِنَّ كَثِيراً مِنَ النَّاسِ لَفاسِقُونَ): the wāw is resumptive; inna and its noun; من الناس is attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of كثير; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); and فاسقون is the khabar of «إن».

* Rhetoric:
Ambiguity (ibhām) in His saying: «ببعض ذنوبهم». Turning away — for all its enormity and gravity and the grievousness of the presumption in it — is one of them. What is meant is that they have sins great in number, and the turning away is among them and one of them. How great a loss is their bargain, and how hideous is what they committed! The use of «بعض» for ambiguity occurs often in their speech; an instance is the saying of Labīd ibn Rabīʿa in his Muʿallaqa:
ترّاك أمكنة إذا لم أرضها ... أو يعتلق بعض النفوس حمامها
(One who readily leaves places when he is not pleased with them — unless death seizes some soul.)
He meant his own soul, and intended to magnify its standing by this ambiguity. He says: I readily leave places when I am not pleased with them, unless its death seizes my soul so that it cannot depart. Whoever made «بعض النفوس» mean "all souls" has erred, because بعض does not convey generality and comprehensiveness; it is as though he said: "a great soul".

dervis-irab:50-51.t:
* I'rab:
(أَفَحُكْمَ الْجاهِلِيَّةِ يَبْغُونَ): the speech is conjoined to what preceded, brought to show one pattern of their obstinacy and their following the path of falsehood. The hamza is for the interrogative of disapproval; the fāʾ is conjunctive, joining to something implied that the context requires, i.e. "Do they turn away from your judgement and seek the judgement of the Jāhiliyya?" حكم is a fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of His saying «يبغون»; الجاهلية is a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); يبغون is an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent). (وَمَنْ أَحْسَنُ مِنَ اللَّهِ حُكْماً لِقَوْمٍ يُوقِنُونَ): the wāw is resumptive; من is an interrogative noun in the position of a nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and أحسن is its khabar (predicate); من الله is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) أحسن; حكما is a tamyīz (specification); and لقوم is attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). Al-Jalāl and others said: the lām means عند ("in the view of"), attached to أحسن, i.e. "in the view of a people who are certain". The clause يوقنون is a naʿt (adjective) of قوم. (يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا تَتَّخِذُوا الْيَهُودَ وَالنَّصارى أَوْلِياءَ): the i'rab of the vocative has preceded. لا is prohibitive; تتخذوا is an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by «لا», and the wāw is the fāʿil; اليهود is a mafʿūl bihi, النصارى is conjoined to اليهود, and أولياء is a second mafʿūl bihi; the clause is resumptive. (بَعْضُهُمْ أَوْلِياءُ بَعْضٍ): بعضهم is a mubtadaʾ and أولياء بعض the khabar; the nominal clause is a naʿt of أولياء, or inceptive, mentioned as a reason for the prohibition. (وَمَنْ يَتَوَلَّهُمْ مِنْكُمْ فَإِنَّهُ مِنْهُمْ): the wāw is resumptive; من is a conditional noun that makes the verb jussive, in the position of a nominative as mubtadaʾ; يتولهم is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), jussive, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the weak letter; منكم is attached to an omitted ḥāl. فإنه: the fāʾ is linking, إنّ and its noun, and منهم its khabar; the nominal clause joined with the fāʾ is in the position of a jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); and the protasis with its apodosis is the khabar of «من». (إِنَّ اللَّهَ لا يَهْدِي الْقَوْمَ الظَّالِمِينَ): inna and its noun; لا is negative; يهدي is an imperfect verb; القوم is a mafʿūl bihi and الظالمين a naʿt; the clause gives the reason and has no grammatical position.

* Rhetoric:
In His saying: «أفحكم الجاهلية يبغون ومن أحسن من الله حكما لقوم يوقنون» there is a delightful art, the art of īghāl (penetration): the speaker completes his speech before bringing its close, and when he wishes to bring the close he brings something that conveys a meaning additional to the meaning of that speech. It is of two kinds:
1- Īghāl of choice (īghāl takhyīr): as in this verse, for the meaning was complete with His saying: «ومن أحسن من الله حكما». When the speech needed a verse-ending (fāṣila) suited to what is before and after it, it came conveying an additional meaning which would not have been obtained without it. That is because none knows that Allah's judgement is better than every judgement except one who is certain that He is One, Wise and Just — so that His oneness negates any partner in the judgement in which He alone is unique, there being no rival to Him in it and none to contradict Him; and from His wisdom follows putting each thing in its place, so that putting the right out of its place is safe from Him; and justice negates from Him injustice in judgement. Then He turned away from saying «يعلمون» ("who know") to saying «يوقنون» ("who are certain"), so that their knowledge of their Lord would be knowledge of conclusiveness and certainty.

Precautionary īghāl in poetry:
As for precautionary īghāl in poetry, it occurs specifically in the rhymes and does not go beyond them; some call it al-tablīgh. Al-Ḥātimī related from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar from Muḥammad ibn Yazīd al-Mubarrad, who said: al-Tawwazī told me: I said to al-Aṣmaʿī: "Who is the greatest of poets?" He said: "The one who makes a mean meaning great by its wording, or comes to a great meaning and makes it mean, or completes his speech before the rhyme and, when he needs the rhyme, conveys a meaning by it." I said: "Such as whom?" He said: "Such as al-Aʿshā, when he says:
كناطح صخرة يوما ليوهنها ... فلم يضرها وأوهى قرنه الوعل
(Like one butting a rock one day to weaken it; it did not harm it, and the mountain goat weakened its own horn.)
The comparison was complete with his saying: وأوهى قرنه ('and weakened its horn'); then, when he needed the rhyme, he said: «الوعل» ('the mountain goat')." I said: "And how did the mountain goat come to be preferred over everything that butts?" He said: "Because it hurls itself down from the mountain peak onto its horn and is not harmed." I said: "Then such as whom?" He said: "Such as Dhū al-Rumma in his saying:
قف العيس في أطلال ميّة واسأل ... رسوما كأخلاق الرّداء المسلسل
(Halt the camels at the ruins of Mayya and question traces like the worn-out rags of a threadbare cloak.)
His speech was complete; then he needed the rhyme and said: المسلسل ('threadbare'), and so added something. And his saying:
أظن الذي يجدي عليك سؤالها ... دموعا كتبديد الجمان المفصّل
(I think that what questioning them will bring you is tears like the scattering of pearls from a strung necklace separated by beads.)
He completed his speech; then he needed the rhyme and said «المفصل» ('separated by beads'), and also added something." There is no disagreement among people that Imruʾ al-Qays was the first to originate this idea, in his saying describing the horse:
إذا ماجرى شأوين وابتل عطفه ... تقول: هزيز الريح مرت بأثأب
(When he has run two heats and his flank is wet, you would say: the roar of the wind passing through the athʾab trees.)
He went to the utmost in describing it, presenting it in this state after it has run two heats and its flank has become wet with sweat; then he added «الأثأب» as a penetration in its description: it is a tree in whose folded branches the wind makes a great rustling and a loud sound. Zuhayr ibn Abī Sulmā followed him and said:
كأن فتات العهن في كل منزل ... نزلن به حبّ الفنا لم يحطّم
(As though the shreds of dyed wool at every halt where they alighted were fanā berries not yet crushed.)
So he penetrated deeply in the simile by likening the scattered shreds of purple wool to fanā berries not yet crushed, because it is red outside and white inside; if it is not crushed, no white at all appears in it, and it is pure red. Al-Aʿshā followed them both and said, describing a woman:
غرّاء فرعاء مصقول عوارضها ... تمشي الهوينى كما يمشي الوجي الوحل
(Radiant, long-haired, her side-teeth polished; she walks slowly, as one with sore hooves walks stuck in mud.)
He penetrated with his saying «الوحل» ("stuck in mud") after having said «الوجي» ("sore-footed"). Al-Rashīd greatly admired the saying of Ṣarīʿ al-Ghawānī:
إذا ما علت منّا ذؤابة شارب ... تمشّت به مشي المقيّد في الوحل
(When it rises to the forelock of a drinker among us, it makes him walk like a fettered man in mud.)
And he would say: "May Allah fight him! It was not enough for him to make him fettered until he put him in mud."
2- Precautionary īghāl (īghāl iḥtiyāṭ):
It is that the speaker completes the meaning of his speech before ending it, and when he wishes to bring the close he brings something conveying an additional meaning to complete the hyperbole, as in the saying of the Exalted: «ولا تسمع الصم الدعاء» ("nor can you make the deaf hear the call"); then He, Mighty and Majestic, knew that the speech needed a verse-ending matching the endings of what is before and after it, so He brought it conveying a meaning additional to the meaning of the speech, where He said: «إذا ولّوا مدبرين» ("when they turn their backs, retreating"). If it is said: what is the meaning of مدبرين, when the mention of turning away has made it unnecessary? We say: that does not make it unnecessary, since turning away may be with one side rather than another, as aversion may be. More of it will come when discussing Sūrat al-Naml, if Allah the Exalted wills.

dervis-irab:95-95.t:
* Vocabulary:
(حُرُمٌ): plural of حرام. In حرام masculine and feminine are the same.
You say: "this is a man in the sacred state (حرام)" and "this is a woman in the sacred state (حرام)"; but if محرم is said, then for the woman محرمة is said. Iḥrām is entering into it; one says: أحرم القوم ("the people entered the sacred state") when they enter the sacred month or the sacred precinct. So the interpretation of the words is: do not kill game while you are in iḥrām for Ḥajj or ʿUmra.
(عَدْلٍ): an equivalent.
(وَبالَ): al-wabāl, with fatḥa on the wāw: the hateful thing and the harm that reaches someone in the outcome of an evil deed, because of its heaviness upon him. Al-Rāghib said: al-wābil is rain with heavy drops, and in consideration of heaviness, a matter whose harm is feared is called wabāl. Allah the Exalted said:
«فذاقوا وبال أمرهم». And one says: "unwholesome food" (طعام وبيل) and "unwholesome pasture" (كلأ وبيل), whose ill effect is feared. Allah the Exalted said: «فأخذناه أخذا وبيلا». And استوبلت الأرض: I disliked the land for fear of its ill effects.

* I'rab:
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا تَقْتُلُوا الصَّيْدَ وَأَنْتُمْ حُرُمٌ): resumptive speech brought to begin explaining what the word "transgression" in the previous verse includes.
لا is prohibitive; تقتلوا is an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by the prohibitive لا; the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); الصيد is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); وأنتم: the wāw is circumstantial, أنتم is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and حرم its khabar (predicate), and the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of تقتلوا.
