(وَمَنْ قَتَلَهُ مِنْكُمْ مُتَعَمِّداً فَجَزاءٌ مِثْلُ ما قَتَلَ مِنَ النَّعَمِ): the wāw is resumptive; من is a jussive conditional noun in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ, whose khabar is the clause of the condition and the apodosis; قتله is a past verb, a latent (mustatir) agent and a direct object, in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); منكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted ḥāl from the agent of قتل; متعمدا is also a ḥāl from the agent of قتل, i.e. mindful of his iḥrām, or knowing that what he kills is among what is forbidden to him to kill — the details are in the books of jurisprudence. فجزاء: the fāʾ links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); جزاء is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, i.e. "then upon him is a compensation"; the reverse is also possible, i.e. "then what is obligatory upon him is a compensation"; and the clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis. مثل is a naʿt (adjective) of جزاء; ما is a relative noun in the position of the genitive in construct with مثل; the clause قتل is the ṣila (relative clause); and من النعم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl from مثل. (يَحْكُمُ بِهِ ذَوا عَدْلٍ مِنْكُمْ هَدْياً بالِغَ الْكَعْبَةِ): the clause يحكم is a second adjective of جزاء; به is attached to يحكم; ذوا is an agent in the nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the alif because it is a dual; عدل is muḍāf ilayhi; منكم is attached to an omitted adjective of «ذوا»; هديا is a ḥāl from جزاء, or accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "he offers it as an offering", or accusative as tamyīz (specification) — the three views are equally weighty; and بالغ الكعبة is an adjective of «هديا», because the construct is not pure, and it does not convey [Translator's note: the text reads «لا تقيد», evidently a misprint for «لا تفيد».] definiteness, as will come in the section on benefits. (أَوْ كَفَّارَةٌ طَعامُ مَساكِينَ أَوْ عَدْلُ ذلِكَ صِياماً): أو is conjunctive; كفارة is conjoined to جزاء; طعام مساكين is a badal (substitute) from كفارة; أو is a conjunction; عدل is conjoined to كفارة; ذلك is muḍāf ilayhi; and صياما is a tamyīz of العدل, as in your saying: "I have the like of him as a man" (لي مثله رجلا). (لِيَذُوقَ وَبالَ أَمْرِهِ عَفَا اللَّهُ عَمَّا سَلَفَ): the lām is causal; يذوق is an imperfect verb in the accusative by an implied أن after the causal lām; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the [notion of] being established (al-istiqrār) latent in the khabar, i.e. "upon him is the compensation so that he may taste"; they may also be attached to طعام or صيام, or to «جزاء», i.e. "it is upon him to be requited so that he may taste the evil outcome of his violation of the sanctity of iḥrām". The clause عفا الله is resumptive, i.e. He has not taken you to task for the game you hunted before in the state of iḥrām, before it was made forbidden; عما is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to عفا; and the clause سلف is the ṣila of the relative. (وَمَنْ عادَ فَيَنْتَقِمُ اللَّهُ مِنْهُ وَاللَّهُ عَزِيزٌ ذُو انْتِقامٍ): the wāw is resumptive; من is a jussive conditional noun in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ; عاد is a past verb in the position of the jussive as the protasis; the fāʾ is linking; ينتقم الله is an imperfect verb and its agent, and the clause is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "then he — Allah takes vengeance on him"; the nominal clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis; and the protasis and its apodosis are the khabar of «من». منه is attached to ينتقم; the wāw is resumptive; الله is a mubtadaʾ; عزيز is a first khabar and ذو انتقام a second khabar.

* Rhetoric:
Tasting in the verse is a dependent implicit metaphor (istiʿāra makniyya tabaʿiyya): the evil outcome resulting from violating the sanctity of iḥrām is likened to unwholesome, indigestible food that he tastes; the thing likened [Translator's note: the text reads «فحذف المشبه»; in an implicit metaphor it is normally the thing likened-to (al-mushabbah bihi) that is omitted.] was omitted and something of its properties was kept, namely tasting. Similar cases have preceded.

* Benefits:
Construct (iḍāfa) is of three kinds:
1- A kind that conveys definiteness of the muḍāf through the muḍāf ilayhi if it is definite, or specification of it if it is indefinite, such as "ʿAlī's book" (كتاب علي) and "a student's book" (كتاب تلميذ).
2- A kind that conveys specification of the muḍāf without definiteness. Its criterion is that the muḍāf be deeply immersed in vagueness, such as غير ("other than"), مثل ("like") and شبه ("similar to"). The construct in these two kinds is called pure (maḥḍa) or genuine (ḥaqīqiyya); and the meaning of their saying "pure" is that it is free from the implication of separation.
3- A kind that conveys nothing of definiteness or specification, namely when the muḍāf is an adjective resembling the imperfect verb in denoting the present or the future, such as the active participle, the passive participle and the resembling adjective (al-ṣifa al-mushabbaha). An indefinite noun may be described by it, as in the verse we are dealing with: هديا is an indefinite noun in the accusative as a ḥāl, and بالغ الكعبة is its adjective; the meaning of «بالغ الكعبة» is that it is slaughtered in the sacred precinct; and an indefinite noun is not described by a definite one. Among its properties also is that it can come as a ḥāl, as in:
«ثاني عطفه», where ثاني is a ḥāl, as will come; and the ḥāl must be indefinite. Of this kind are the words of Abū Kabīr al-Hudhalī:
فأتت به حوش الفؤاد مبطّنا ... سهدا إذا ما نام ليل الهوجل
(She bore him keen of heart, lean of flank, wakeful when the sluggard sleeps at night.) حوش is a resembling adjective meaning "sharp of heart", and it is put in the accusative as a ḥāl because it has acquired neither definiteness nor specification. Among its properties also is that «ربّ» may enter upon it, as in the words of Jarīr:
يا ربّ غابطنا لو كان يطلبكم ... لاقى مباعدة منكم وحرمانا
(How many a one who envies us — were he to seek you, he would meet with distance from you and deprivation!) He put «ربّ» before «غابطنا», and had it been definite, that would not have been correct. For this reason this construct is called verbal (lafẓiyya), because it conveys a merely verbal matter, namely the dropping of the tanwīn and of the nūn of the dual and plural — matters that go back to the wording alone.
There are other discussions relating to construct, which may be consulted in their proper places in the books of grammar.

dervis-irab:52-53.t:
* Vocabulary:
(دائِرَةٌ): الدائرة is one of the predominant attributes with which the thing described is not mentioned. Al-Rāghib in his Mufradāt distinguished between الدائرة and الدولة: الدائرة is the encircling line; then it was used to express an event, and it is said only of what is disliked, whereas الدولة is said of what is liked. It is reported that ʿUbāda ibn al-Ṣāmit said to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "I have allies among the Jews, many in number, and I declare myself free before Allah and His Messenger of their alliance, and I take Allah and His Messenger as allies." ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy said: "I am a man who fears turns of fortune (الدوائر); I will not declare myself free of the alliance of my allies." They were the Jews of Banū Qaynuqāʿ.
(حَبِطَتْ): i.e. the works which they used to affect in people's view became void.

* I'rab:
(فَتَرَى الَّذِينَ فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ مَرَضٌ يُسارِعُونَ فِيهِمْ): the fāʾ may be resumptive, with the speech resumptive, brought to show the manner of their alliance, its cause, and what their affair and their destiny would come to. It may also be conjunctive, with the speech conjoined to His saying: «إن الله لا يهدي القوم الظالمين». In either case it has no grammatical position. ترى is an imperfect verb, and the seeing is either visual or cognitive; الذين is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); في قلوبهم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted, fronted khabar (predicate), and مرض is a delayed mubtadaʾ (subject); the nominal clause is the ṣila (relative clause). The clause يسارعون is either a ḥāl (circumstantial), if the seeing is visual, or a second mafʿūl bihi, if the seeing is cognitive; and فيهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يسارعون. (يَقُولُونَ نَخْشى أَنْ تُصِيبَنا دائِرَةٌ): the clause is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl of the pronoun of «يسارعون»; the clause نخشى is in the position of an accusative as the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl); the interpreted maṣdar from أن and what is in its scope is the object of نخشى; نا is an attached pronoun in the position of an accusative as mafʿūl bihi; and دائرة is the fāʿil (agent). (فَعَسَى اللَّهُ أَنْ يَأْتِيَ بِالْفَتْحِ أَوْ أَمْرٍ مِنْ عِنْدِهِ): the fāʾ is resumptive; عسى is one of the verbs of hope and operates like «كان»; الله is its noun, and أن يأتي is an interpreted maṣdar as its khabar. It has preceded that the khabar of عسى is most commonly an imperfect verb joined with أن. بالفتح is attached to يأتي; أو أمر is conjoined to الفتح; and من عنده is attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of أمر. (فَيُصْبِحُوا عَلى ما أَسَرُّوا فِي أَنْفُسِهِمْ نادِمِينَ): the fāʾ is conjunctive or causative; يصبحوا is conjoined to يأتي, or accusative by an implied أن after the causative fāʾ, because it is preceded by عسى, which is for hope. يصبحوا is a defective (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb and the wāw is its noun; على ما is attached to نادمين; the clause أسروا has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila; في أنفسهم is attached to أسروا; and نادمين is the khabar of «أصبح». (وَيَقُولُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا: أَهؤُلاءِ الَّذِينَ أَقْسَمُوا بِاللَّهِ جَهْدَ أَيْمانِهِمْ): the wāw is resumptive, and the speech is resumptive, brought to state what the believers say.
يقول الذين is an imperfect verb and its fāʿil, and the clause آمنوا is the ṣila. It has been read with يقول in the accusative, conjoined to «أن يأتي», and it has been read without the wāw, so it is also resumptive. The hamza is for the interrogative of wonder; the demonstrative is a mubtadaʾ and الذين the khabar; the clause is in the position of an accusative as the object of saying; the clause أقسموا is the ṣila; بالله is attached to أقسموا; and جهد أيمانهم is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) or a ḥāl. (إِنَّهُمْ لَمَعَكُمْ): the clause has no grammatical position because it is the answer to the oath; inna and its noun; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); and معكم is an adverb attached to the omitted khabar of إنّ. (حَبِطَتْ أَعْمالُهُمْ فَأَصْبَحُوا خاسِرِينَ): a resumptive clause. It has been said that it is the speech of Allah, and most analysts hold this; it has also been said that it is the speech of the believers, and al-Zamakhsharī and Abū Ḥayyān hold this. أعمالهم is the fāʿil of حبطت; the fāʾ is conjunctive; أصبحوا is a defective past verb, the wāw is its noun, and خاسرين its khabar.

* Rhetoric:
In the saying of the Exalted: «حبطت أعمالهم فأصبحوا خاسرين» there is an art which Qudāma called al-ighrāb wa-l-ṭurfa (the rare and the novel). It is of three kinds:
1- A kind in which the rarity lies in the wording, and it is plentiful.
2- A kind in which the rarity lies in the meaning, as in the saying of al-Mutanabbī:
يطمّع الطير فيهم طول أكلهم ... حتى تكاد على أحيائهم تقع
(Their long feeding on them makes the birds covet them, until they almost alight upon their living.)
He took the well-known idea that birds alight only on the slain and follow armies, trusting they will be sated, and went beyond it, by an increase of hyperbole made pleasing by its being joined with «تكاد» ("almost"), to what he said; so his verse attained a rarity and novelty that no other attains.
3- And a kind in which the rarity is neither in its meaning nor in the outward form of its wording, but in its interpretation: it is that which, if taken in its outward sense, would make the speech faulty, but if interpreted, the interpretation returns it to a pattern of eloquent speech and removes the fault from its outward form.
The noble verse is of this kind, for one might say: the word «أصبحوا» ("they became by morning") is outwardly padding with no benefit, for these who are reported to be losers were in the evening in the same state as in the morning; and if you said: "the honey became sweet by morning" (أصبح العسل حلوا), the word «أصبح» would be redundant padding with no benefit, because it was likewise in the evening.
Al-Rummānī devised for this word an interpretation by which the great benefit is obtained, which would not be obtained without its coming. It is that, when he said: since the sick man who has spent the night suffering severe pains has his condition assessed in the morning — if by morning he is recovering and relieved of those pains, good is hoped for him, and his cure and recovery from that illness are thought most likely; and if by morning he is as he was in the evening, his perishing is certain, by the established pattern that illnesses flare up at night and subside in the morning [Translator's note: the sentence in the source, beginning «وهي أنه لما قال», has no main clause for لما; it is translated as it stands]. The state of the wretched has been likened to the sick man who by morning is in the same pain as in the evening, so he is one whose amendment is despaired of. On this basis the word «فأصبحوا» conveys a fine and beautiful meaning and ceases to be useless padding. And when Allah, glorified is He, reported that their works had become void, it was known conclusively that they had become losers; so no other word is fit in the place of «أصبحوا», and the meaning is not complete without it. As for the example given by al-Rummānī, «أصبح العسل حلوا وقد أمسى كذلك» ("the honey became sweet by morning, having been so in the evening") [Translator's note: in the source this example was earlier attributed to an objector, not to al-Rummānī], this is said only of matters occurring in the abode of this world, because its time has morning and evening; when a thing is in the morning in the state in which it is in the evening, mentioning morning and evening in it is padding with no benefit. But as for the Day of Resurrection, in which there is no evening, likening it to what is in the morning in a time accompanied by an evening is a likening that does not correspond to it.

dervis-irab:96-96.t:
* Vocabulary:
(وَلِلسَّيَّارَةِ): i.e. travellers. It is the plural of سيار, and is made feminine in the sense of a company or group.

* I'rab:
(أُحِلَّ لَكُمْ صَيْدُ الْبَحْرِ وَطَعامُهُ مَتاعاً لَكُمْ وَلِلسَّيَّارَةِ): أحل is a passive past verb; لكم is attached (mutaʿalliq) to أحل; صيد البحر is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); طعامه is conjoined to «صيد»; متاعا is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), i.e. for the sake of your enjoyment, and it may also be a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e. "He has given you enjoyment (متعكم تمتيعا)". لكم is attached to «متاعا»; للسيارة is conjoined to «لكم»; and the clause is resumptive. (وَحُرِّمَ عَلَيْكُمْ صَيْدُ الْبَرِّ ما دُمْتُمْ حُرُماً): the wāw is conjunctive; حرم is a passive past verb; عليكم is attached to حرم; the clause is conjoined to the preceding clause; صيد البر is the deputy agent; ما دمتم: [دام is] a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb, and «ما» together with what follows it is in the position of the accusative as an adverbial (ẓarf), and the adverb is attached to حرم; the tāʾ is the noun of ما دام, and حرما is its khabar (predicate). (وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ الَّذِي إِلَيْهِ تُحْشَرُونَ): the wāw is conjunctive; اتقوا الله is an imperative verb and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); الذي is a naʿt (adjective); إليه is attached to تحشرون; تحشرون is a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is the deputy agent; and the clause تحشرون is the ṣila (relative clause).

dervis-irab:97-98.t:
* I'rab:
(جَعَلَ اللَّهُ الْكَعْبَةَ الْبَيْتَ الْحَرامَ قِياماً لِلنَّاسِ وَالشَّهْرَ الْحَرامَ وَالْهَدْيَ وَالْقَلائِدَ): resumptive speech brought to explain the Kaʿba, which is the Sacred House. As for «جعل», you may consider it to be in the sense of «صيّر» ("to make into") or in the sense of «خلق» ("to create"). جعل الله is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); الكعبة is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); البيت الحرام is a badal (substitute) from الكعبة, the benefit of the substitution being praise; قياما is, on the first view, a second direct object, and on the second, a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الكعبة. It is from the roots with wāw [as the middle radical]; and it was said: قياما [is written with yāʾ] because of the kasra of the qāf, and it is originally قواما and صواما [Translator's note: the passage is compressed in the source; the point is that قيام was originally قِوام, the wāw becoming yāʾ after kasra, like صيام from صِوام.]. للناس is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «قياما», i.e. they maintain, by repairing to it, the affair of their livelihoods and benefits. الشهر is conjoined to الكعبة; الحرام is a naʿt (adjective); and الهدي and القلائد are also conjoined to الكعبة. (ذلِكَ لِتَعْلَمُوا أَنَّ اللَّهَ يَعْلَمُ ما فِي السَّماواتِ وَما فِي الْأَرْضِ): the clause is resumptive, and the demonstrative is a mubtadaʾ (subject).
The reference is to the whole of what has been mentioned before. لتعلموا: the lām is the causal lām, and تعلموا is an imperfect verb in the accusative by an implied أن after the lām; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted khabar (predicate) of ذلك, i.e. "that ruling is the truth and nothing else". It was also said: ذلك is in the position of the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "the ruling that We have established is that". The demonstrative may also be accusative by an implied verb, with لتعلموا attached to it, i.e. "We have legislated that". All the views are equally weighty. أن and what follows it stand in place of the two objects of تعلموا; أن and its noun; the clause يعلم is its khabar; ما is a relative noun, a direct object; في السموات is attached to an omitted ṣila (relative clause); and ما في الأرض is conjoined to «ما في السموات». (وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ): conjoined to the first «أن»; أن and its noun; بكل شيء is attached to «عليم»; and عليم is the khabar of أن. (اعْلَمُوا أَنَّ اللَّهَ شَدِيدُ الْعِقابِ وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ): conjoined to what precedes; and غفور رحيم are two khabars of أن.

dervis-irab:99-100.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الْخَبِيثُ): the opposite of good (al-ṭayyib). The plural is خبث with two ḍammas, and خبثاء, أخباث and خبثة with two fatḥas. خبثت نفسه: his soul became heavy and nauseated. The khāʾ and the bāʾ, as the first and second radicals of a verb, have a remarkable property, namely that they indicate effect and speed in concealment. One says خبّ, i.e. he deceived and corrupted, and the meaning of effect upon the one deceived and his corruption in it is not hidden; الخبب is a kind of running and going; خبأ الشيء: he covered and concealed the thing; خبر الشيء يخبره خبرا, with ḍamma on the khāʾ, and خبرا with kasra: he knew it through experience; خبز الخبز: he made the bread; خبس فلانا حقه: he wronged him and oppressed him; خبش الأشياء: he took things from here and there; خبص الشيء بالشيء: he mixed it; خبّص, with doubling: he made khabīṣa or khabīṣ, i.e. mixed sweetmeat; خبطه خبطا: he struck him a violent blow; خبله and خبّله, with doubling: he corrupted him; خبن الثوب: he folded the garment and sewed it; and خبن الشاعر: the poet used khabn in his poetry, which is the dropping of the second, quiescent [letter]. This is among the wonders of our noble language and its unique properties.

* I'rab:
(ما عَلَى الرَّسُولِ إِلَّا الْبَلاغُ): the speech is resumptive, brought to stress the obligation of carrying out what has been commanded, i.e. the proof has been established against you and obedience has become binding on you, so you have no excuse if you overstep the limits. This saying has come to function as a proverb, and it will be discussed in detail in the section on rhetoric. ما is negating; على الرسول is a preposition and its genitive noun attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted fronted khabar (predicate); إلا is a particle of restriction; and البلاغ is a delayed mubtadaʾ (subject). (وَاللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ ما تُبْدُونَ وَما تَكْتُمُونَ): the wāw is resumptive; الله is a mubtadaʾ; the clause يعلم is the khabar; ما is a relative noun, the object of تعلمون [Translator's note: so in the text; the verb in the verse is «يعلم».]; the clause تبدون is the ṣila (relative clause); and ما تكتمون is conjoined to His words ما تبدون. (قُلْ لا يَسْتَوِي الْخَبِيثُ وَالطَّيِّبُ): the clause is resumptive; قل is an imperative verb; and the clause لا يستوي الخبيث والطيب is in the position of the accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). This clause too is among those that have become current as proverbs. (وَلَوْ أَعْجَبَكَ كَثْرَةُ الْخَبِيثِ): the wāw is circumstantial; لو is conditional; أعجبك is a past verb and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); كثرة الخبيث is the fāʿil (agent) of أعجبك; and the clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of لا يستوي, i.e. they are not equal, whatever their state. The apodosis of لو is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, i.e. "then they are not equal". (فَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ يا أُولِي الْأَلْبابِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تُفْلِحُونَ)
The fāʾ is the faṣīḥa ("disclosing") fāʾ, i.e. "if this has become clear to you, then fear Allah". اتقوا الله is a verb, its agent and its direct object; يا is a vocative particle; أولي الألباب is a vocative in construct (munādā muḍāf); لعلكم: لعل and its noun; and the clause تفلحون is its khabar.

* Rhetoric:
In the verse there is irsāl al-mathal (sending forth a proverb), which consists in the speaker bringing, in part of his speech, something that functions like a current proverb, whether a piece of wisdom, a description or otherwise. Of this kind are the words of Abū al-Ṭayyib al-Mutanabbī:
لأن حلمك حلم لا تكلفه ... ليس التكحل في العينين كالكحل
(Because your forbearance is a forbearance you do not affect: applying kohl to the eyes is not like eyes naturally dark.)
Abū al-Ṭayyib became famous for this feature until it became proverbial. He said:
خذ ما تراه ودع شيئا سمعت به ... في طلعة الشمس ما يغنيك عن زحل
(Take what you see and leave something you have merely heard of: in the rising of the sun there is what makes you do without Saturn.)
There will come of his proverbs what astonishes the mind; for now it is sufficient for us to cite selections from the ode of Ibn Zaydūn:
ما على ظني بأس ... يجرح الدهر وياسو
ولقد ينجيك إغفا ... ل ويرديك احتراس
ولكم أجدى قعود ... ولكم أكدى التماس
وكذا الحكم إذا ما ... عزّ ناس ذلّ ناس
لا يكن عهدك وردا ... إن عهدي لك آس فأدر ذكري كأسا ... ما امتطت كفّك
كاس واغتنم صفو الليالي ... إنما العيش اختلاس
(There is no harm in my thinking: time wounds and heals. Heedlessness may save you, and caution may ruin you. How often has sitting still availed, and how often has seeking come to nothing! Such is the rule: when some people rise to might, others fall low. Let not your pledge be a rose [that fades]; my pledge to you is a myrtle [that stays green]. So pass round the cup of my remembrance as long as a cup rides upon your palm, and seize the clear moments of the nights: life is nothing but snatched moments.)
2- Antithesis (ṭibāq) between «تبدون» and «تكتمون». [Translator's note: the source numbers this point "2" without a preceding "1"; the first point is evidently the irsāl al-mathal above.]

dervis-irab:20-21.t:
* I'rab:
(وَإِذْ قالَ مُوسى لِقَوْمِهِ): resumptive speech introduced to set out what they did and what issued from some of them after the covenant was taken. (إذ) is an adverb of past time attached to an omitted «اذكر» (remember); the address is to the Prophet, so that what issued from them may be recounted to him. The clause (قال موسى), of verb and fāʿil (agent), is in the position of genitive by annexation; (لقومه) is attached to (قال).
(يا قَوْمِ اذْكُرُوا نِعْمَتَ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ): the clause is in the position of accusative as the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl). (يا) is a vocative particle; (قوم) is a vocative annexed to the omitted yāʾ of the speaker; (اذكروا نعمة الله) is an imperative verb, its agent and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and (عليكم) is attached to (نعمة).
(إِذْ جَعَلَ فِيكُمْ أَنْبِياءَ وَجَعَلَكُمْ مُلُوكاً): (إذ) is an adverb of past time attached to «النعمة»; the clause (جعل) is in the position of genitive by annexation; (فيكم) is attached to (جعل) as being its first object «[Translator's note: so in the text; i.e. the prepositional phrase (فيكم) occupies the place of the first object]», and (أنبياء) is its second object; (وجعلكم ملوكا) is conjoined to what precedes, and (ملوكا) is a second object.
(وَآتاكُمْ ما لَمْ يُؤْتِ أَحَداً مِنَ الْعالَمِينَ): the wāw is a conjunction; (آتاكم) is a verb and its first object, the agent being «هو»; (ما) is a relative noun, the second object; the clause (لم يؤت أحدا) is the ṣila (relative clause) of «ما»; (من العالمين) is attached to an omitted ṣila «[Translator's note: so in the text; it is more naturally an omitted naʿt (adjective) of (أحدا)]». What is meant by "the worlds" is the nations that had passed up to their time and the world of their time: [the favours] such as the parting of the sea, the shading by clouds, the manna and the quails, and other great matters.
(يا قَوْمِ ادْخُلُوا الْأَرْضَ الْمُقَدَّسَةَ): the clause is resumptive; (ادخلوا) is an imperative verb and its agent; (الأرض) is a direct object by extension of usage (ʿalā al-saʿa), or accusative by removal of the preposition, the [implied] preposition and its genitive noun being attached to (ادخلوا); and (المقدسة) is a naʿt of (الأرض).
(الَّتِي كَتَبَ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ): (التي) is a second adjective of (الأرض); the clause (كتب الله) is the ṣila; and (لكم), a preposition and its genitive noun, is attached to (كتب).
(وَلا تَرْتَدُّوا عَلى أَدْبارِكُمْ): the wāw is a conjunction; (لا) is prohibitive; (ترتدوا) is an imperfect verb, jussive by (لا), the wāw being the agent; and (على أدباركم) is attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of (ترتدوا).
(فَتَنْقَلِبُوا خاسِرِينَ): the fāʾ is a conjunction, and (تنقلبوا) is conjoined to (ترتدوا), so it is jussive like it. The fāʾ may also be the causative fāʾ (al-sababiyya), since a prohibition precedes it, so that [the verb] is accusative by an implied «أن» after it. (خاسرين) is a ḥāl.

* Benefits:
The vocative annexed to the yāʾ of the speaker is of four kinds:
1- That which has one dialectal form: it is the word ending in a weak letter, yāʾ or alif; its yāʾ to which it is annexed must be retained and given fatḥa, e.g. «يا قاضيّ» and «يا فتايَ».
2- That which has two forms: it is the adjective resembling the imperfect verb, by which we mean the active and passive participles and the intensive forms of the active participle; its yāʾ is always retained, either with fatḥa or with sukūn «[Translator's note: the text reads «مكسورة» (with kasra); the standard rule is fatḥa or sukūn]», e.g. «يا مكرمي» and «يا ضاربي».
3- That which has six forms: it is everything other than that, which is neither «أب» nor «أم», e.g. «يا غلامي». The most common is to drop the yāʾ and make do with the kasra, e.g.:
«يا غلامِ»; then retaining it with sukūn as in the original, e.g. «يا غلامِيْ»; or with fatḥa, e.g. «يا غلامِيَ». Then turning the kasra into fatḥa and the yāʾ into alif, e.g. «يا حسرتا».
Then dropping the converted alif and making do with the fatḥa, so you say «يا حسرةَ»; then dropping the yāʾ, relying on its being intended, and giving ḍamma to the noun annexed to the yāʾ, as in «يا غلامُ».
4- That which has ten forms: it is «الأب» and «الأم». In them, in addition to the six forms mentioned, there are four other forms: that you substitute the tāʾ of the feminine for the yāʾ of the speaker and give it kasra, which is the most common; or give it fatḥa; or give it ḍamma, which is rare; and sometimes the tāʾ and the alif are combined, so that it is said: «يا أبتا» and «يا أمتا».

dervis-irab:22-23.t:
* Vocabulary:
(جَبَّارِينَ): «الجبار» is the insolent rebel; of the pattern «فعّال», from «جبره على الأمر» in the sense of «أجبره عليه» (he compelled him to it); he is the one who compels people to what he wants. What is meant here is that they were possessed of strength.

* I'rab:
(قالُوا: يا مُوسى إِنَّ فِيها قَوْماً جَبَّارِينَ): the clause is resumptive; (قالوا) is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); the vocative clause and what follows it is the object of their saying (maqūl al-qawl); (فيها) is attached to the omitted fronted khabar (predicate) of (إن); (قوما) is its delayed noun; and (جبارين):
is a naʿt (adjective) of «قوما».
(وَإِنَّا لَنْ نَدْخُلَها حَتَّى يَخْرُجُوا مِنْها): the wāw conjoins to what precedes; (إن) with its noun; the clause (لن ندخلها) is its khabar; (حتى) is a particle of limit and a preposition; (يخرجوا) is an imperfect verb in the accusative by an implied «أن» after it, and the preposition and its genitive noun [the interpreted maṣdar] are attached to (ندخلها); and (منها) is attached to (يخرجوا).
(فَإِنْ يَخْرُجُوا مِنْها فَإِنَّا داخِلُونَ): the fāʾ is resumptive; (إن) is conditional; (يخرجوا) is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the fāʾ is linking, because the clause after it is nominal and not fit to be an apodosis [without it]; (إن) with its noun, and (داخلون) its khabar; the clause is in the position of jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ).
(قالَ رَجُلانِ مِنَ الَّذِينَ يَخافُونَ أَنْعَمَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِمَا): the clause is resumptive; (قال رجلان):
a verb and its agent; (من الذين), a preposition and its genitive noun, is attached to an omitted adjective; the clause (يخافون) has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause); the clause (أنعم الله) is a second adjective, or parenthetical (muʿtariḍa), in which case it has no grammatical position. Ibn Hishām has a view on it which we present in the section on benefits. (عليهما) is attached to (أنعم).
(ادْخُلُوا عَلَيْهِمُ الْبابَ): the clause is in the position of accusative as the object of the two men's saying.
(فَإِذا دَخَلْتُمُوهُ فَإِنَّكُمْ غالِبُونَ): the fāʾ is resumptive; (إذا) is a future adverb containing the meaning of condition, attached to «غالبون»; the clause (دخلتموه) is in the position of genitive by annexation; the fāʾ links the answer of (إذا); (إن) with its noun, and (غالبون) its khabar.
(وَعَلَى اللَّهِ فَتَوَكَّلُوا إِنْ كُنْتُمْ مُؤْمِنِينَ): the wāw is resumptive, and the clause is resumptive, introduced to counsel them to rely on Allah first, and to take the means of caution and wariness second. The fāʾ in His saying «فتوكلوا» is the answer to an omitted command that must be supplied: "take heed, then rely on Allah." (على الله) is attached to (توكلوا), just as the Arabs said «زيدا فاضرب», its implied form being "take heed, then strike Zayd"; very often what is governed by [the verb] after the fāʾ comes placed before it. (إن) is conditional; (كنتم) is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb in the position of jussive as the protasis, the tāʾ its noun and (مؤمنين) its khabar; and the apodosis is omitted, indicated by what precedes, i.e. "then rely [on Him]."

* Benefits:
1- Ibn Hishām said, at the beginning of his discussion of this verse: [As for] the saying of the Exalted:
«قال رجلان من الذين يخافون أنعم الله عليهما», the clause «أنعم الله عليهما» may be a supplication, in which case it is parenthetical, or a statement, in which case it is a second adjective. Its being a ḥāl (circumstantial) is weak in terms of meaning, though not weak in terms of grammatical technique, because [the noun] has been described.» This is what Ibn Hishām said. Ibn Hishām, may Allah have mercy on him, did not explain the reason for the weakness in terms of meaning: making it a ḥāl would require that their saying took place only at the time of His bestowing favour, whereas their saying is not restricted by that. In sum, being a ḥāl requires restricting the governing word, whereas the meaning is not one of restriction.
2- The wording of al-Samīn: al-Shihāb al-Ḥalabī, known as al-Samīn, said:
In this clause there are five views. The most evident is that it is a second adjective, so its position is nominative; here the more eloquent of the two usages was employed, in that the description by a prepositional phrase was placed before the description by a clause, because it is closer to the single word. The second: that it is parenthetical «[Translator's note: the printed text has «متعرضة», a misprint for «معترضة»]», and this too is evident. The third: that it is a ḥāl from the pronoun in «يخافون»; Makkī said this.
The fourth: that it is a ḥāl from «رجلان», the ḥāl coming from an indefinite noun because it has been specified by description. The fifth: that it is a ḥāl from the latent pronoun in the preposition and its genitive noun, namely «من الذين», because it occurs as the adjective of a described noun. If you make it a ḥāl, then «قد» must be implied with the past verb, according to a disagreement on the question.
3- The two men on whom Allah bestowed favour are Yūshaʿ ibn Nūn (Joshua), who was made a prophet after Mūsā, and Kālib ibn Yūqannā (Caleb); «كالب» with fatḥa or kasra on the lām.

dervis-irab:24-26.t:
* Vocabulary:
(أَبَداً): an adverb of time; here it ties the emphasised negation to long-extended time.
(يَتِيهُونَ): they travel through the land bewildered, finding no way.
«التيه»: the open desert in which one gets lost.
(تَأْسَ): you regret and grieve; «الأسى» is grief. Its final radical may be from wāw, given their saying «رجل أسواة», i.e. much given to grief; or it may be from yāʾ, for «رجل أسيان» has been reported. In Mukhtār al-Ṣiḥāḥ:
«أسي على مصيبته», of the pattern of «صدي», i.e. he grieved; and «قد أسي له», i.e. he grieved for him.

* I'rab:
(قالُوا: يا مُوسى إِنَّا لَنْ نَدْخُلَها أَبَداً ما دامُوا فِيها): resumptive speech introduced to indicate their persistence in disobedience. (قالوا): a verb and its fāʿil (agent); the vocative clause and what follows it is in the position of accusative as the object of their saying (maqūl al-qawl); (إن) with its noun; the clause (لن ندخلها) is the khabar (predicate); (أبدا) is an adverb of time attached to (ندخلها). In (ما داموا), «ما»:
is maṣdariyya ẓarfiyya (a temporal maṣdar particle); (داموا) is the defective (nāqiṣ) «دام», the wāw its noun, and (فيها) is attached to its omitted khabar. This adverbial [phrase] is a badal (substitute) of «أبدا», because it serves as its explanation; so it is a corresponding substitute, i.e. whole for whole. It has also been said: it is a substitute of part for whole, because «الأبد» covers all future time, while the remaining of the tyrants in it is part of it.
(فَاذْهَبْ أَنْتَ وَرَبُّكَ فَقاتِلا): the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa, as though they harboured speech implying contempt and mockery of Allah and His Messenger. (اذهب) is an imperative verb whose agent is latent (mustatir), implied as «أنت»; (أنت) is a tawkīd (emphasis) of the latent agent; (ربك) is conjoined to the latent agent in «اذهب», and this is permitted because of the emphasis by the pronoun, as Ibn Mālik stated in al-Khulāṣa [the Alfiyya]:
وإن على ضمير رفع متصل ... عطفت فافصل بالضمير المنفصل
(If you conjoin to an attached nominative pronoun, separate [them] with the detached pronoun.)
(فقاتلا) is conjoined to «اذهب», and the alif is the agent of (قاتل).
(إِنَّا هاهُنا قاعِدُونَ): the clause is resumptive, introduced to show their insistence that they would not advance. (إن) with its noun; the hāʾ is for drawing attention (tanbīh), and (هنا) is a demonstrative in the position of accusative as an adverb of place, attached to «قاعدون»; and (قاعدون) is the khabar of (إن).
(قالَ: رَبِّ إِنِّي لا أَمْلِكُ إِلَّا نَفْسِي وَأَخِي): the clause is resumptive, introduced to pour out [his grief] and complain to Allah, with sorrow and tenderness of heart, which are among the means by which mercy is sought and victory brought down. (قال) is a past verb, the agent being «هو»; (رب) is a vocative annexed to the omitted yāʾ of the speaker — the vocative annexed to the yāʾ of the speaker has been discussed at length before; (إن) with its noun, and the clause is the object of saying; the clause (لا أملك) is the khabar of (إن); (إلا) is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); (نفسي) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (أخي) is one of the curiosities of i'rab: it admits the nominative, the accusative and the genitive, all equally.

The nominative readings:
The nominative is on three grounds:
1- That it is conjoined to the latent pronoun in «أملك».
2- That it is conjoined to the position of (إن) with its noun.
3- That it is a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar is omitted, the implied form being: "and my brother has power only over himself."

The two accusative readings:
The accusative is on two grounds:
1- That it is conjoined to the noun of (إنّ).
2- That it is conjoined to (نفسي).

The genitive reading:
The genitive is on one ground:
that it is conjoined to the yāʾ which is genitive by the annexation of (نفس) to it.
(فَافْرُقْ بَيْنَنا وَبَيْنَ الْقَوْمِ الْفاسِقِينَ): the fāʾ is resumptive; (افرق) is a verb of supplication meaning: judge for us with what we deserve, and judge against them with what they deserve.
(بيننا) is an adverb attached to «افرق», and (بين القوم الفاسقين) is conjoined to «بيننا».
(قالَ فَإِنَّها مُحَرَّمَةٌ عَلَيْهِمْ أَرْبَعِينَ سَنَةً يَتِيهُونَ فِي الْأَرْضِ): the clause is resumptive; the agent of «قال» is latent, its implied form being "Allah the Exalted"; the fāʾ is redundant in i'rab, for strengthening the emphasis; (إن) with its noun, and (محرمة) its khabar; (عليهم) is attached to (محرمة); (أربعين) is an adverb of time attached to (يتيهون), in which case the prohibition is not limited to this period; or it is attached to (محرمة), in which case the prohibition is restricted to this period. (سنة) is a tamyīz (specification); the clause (فإنها محرمة) is the object of saying; and the clause (يتيهون في الأرض) is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), i.e. while they are wandering lost, travelling through the wastes of the earth and the expanses of the deserts, sorrow buffeting them and bewilderment overtaking them by turns.
(فَلا تَأْسَ عَلَى الْقَوْمِ الْفاسِقِينَ): the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa, i.e. if you know this, then do not grieve. (لا) is prohibitive; (تأس) is an imperfect verb, jussive by the prohibitive (لا), the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the weak letter; (على القوم) is attached to «تأس»; and (الفاسقين) is an adjective of (قوم).

* Benefits:
Someone may ask: how did Mūsā say "I have power only over myself and my brother," when the two men mentioned, namely Yūshaʿ and Kālib, were with them? The answer is that he did not feel assured of their steadfastness after he had seen the overwhelming majority persisting in obstinacy; and prophethood had not yet descended upon Yūshaʿ ibn Nūn, so he mentioned with himself only the infallible prophet, namely his brother Hārūn. There are lengthy stories here, for which the reader may refer to the extended works of exegesis.

dervis-irab:101-102.t:
* I'rab:
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا تَسْئَلُوا عَنْ أَشْياءَ إِنْ تُبْدَ لَكُمْ تَسُؤْكُمْ): resumptive speech brought to forbid asking much about matters that do not concern them, because being charged with them is among the things that burden souls. In this there is a loftiness worthy of taking heed and of good manners. لا is prohibitive; تسألوا is an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by لا; the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); عن أشياء is a preposition and its genitive noun attached (mutaʿalliq) to تسألوا; أشياء is a diptote, and it will be discussed at length in the section on benefits. إن is conditional; تبد is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and it is passive, its nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) referring [Translator's note: the text has the misprint «بعود» for «يعود».] to أشياء; لكم is attached to «تبد»; تسؤكم is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and the kāf is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and the conditional clause is a naʿt (adjective) of «أشياء». (وَإِنْ تَسْئَلُوا عَنْها حِينَ يُنَزَّلُ الْقُرْآنُ تُبْدَ لَكُمْ): the wāw is conjunctive; إن is conditional; تسألوا is the protasis; حين is an adverb of time attached to تسألوا; the clause ينزل القرآن is in the position of the genitive by construct (iḍāfa); تبد is the apodosis; and لكم is attached to «تبد».
(عَفَا اللَّهُ عَنْها وَاللَّهُ غَفُورٌ حَلِيمٌ): the clause عفا الله عنها is resumptive, brought to show that the prohibition concerning them was only because of their exhaustive detail and the impossibility of carrying them out in the most perfect way, and Allah has pardoned [you] concerning them. The clause may also be a second adjective of «أشياء». The wāw is resumptive; الله is a mubtadaʾ (subject); غفور is a first khabar (predicate) and حليم a second khabar. (قَدْ سَأَلَها قَوْمٌ مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ ثُمَّ أَصْبَحُوا بِها كافِرِينَ).
The clause is either resumptive, which is preferable, or you may make it a second adjective of «أشياء». سألها is a past verb and a fronted direct object, the pronoun referring back to «أشياء»; a muḍāf must be implied, i.e. "asked about the like of them", considering them similar to them in consequence and in bringing on ill effects. They have spoken at length about the referent of the pronoun to no benefit. قوم is the agent; من قبلكم is attached to an omitted adjective of قوم; ثم is a conjunction for sequence with delay; أصبحوا is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb, and the wāw is its noun; بها is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «كافرين»; and كافرين is the khabar of أصبحوا.

* Benefits:
1- It is related that Surāqa ibn Mālik, or ʿUkkāsha ibn Miḥṣan, said:
"O Messenger of Allah, is the Ḥajj [due] from us every year?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ turned away from him, until he repeated his question three times. Then he ﷺ said:
"Woe to you! What makes you safe from my saying yes? By Allah, had I said yes, it would have become obligatory; and had it become obligatory, you would not have been able [to do it]; and had you abandoned it, you would have disbelieved. So leave me alone as long as I leave you alone, for those who were before you were destroyed only by their much questioning and their disagreeing with their prophets. So when I command you to do something, do of it what you are able, and when I forbid you from something, avoid it."
2- أشياء: it is a diptote. The scholars of language and grammar have delved into the reason for its being diptote, and what they have set forth can be summed up in the following views:
1- The view of Sībawayh, al-Khalīl and the majority of the Basrans:
It is diptote because of the extended alif of femininity. It is a collective noun (ism jamʿ) of «شيء», and the original form is «شيئاء» on the pattern فعلاء; the lām [i.e. the hamza, the final radical] was placed before the alif out of dislike for two hamzas coming together with an alif between them.
2- The view of al-Farrāʾ:
أشياء is a plural of «شيء», and its original form is «أشيئاء»; when two hamzas came together with an alif between them, they dropped the first hamza for lightness.
3- The view of al-Kisāʾī:
He held that the pattern of أشياء is أفعال, and that they made it diptote only by likening it to what has the alif of femininity at its end.
There are other views which we have passed over because they do not go beyond this substance.

dervis-irab:103-103.t:
* Vocabulary:
(بَحِيرَةٍ): with fatḥa on the bāʾ and kasra on the ḥāʾ; it is on the pattern faʿīla in the sense of mafʿūla (passive), and the tāʾ was attached to it irregularly, because it was stripped of its adjectival character and came to have the sense of concrete nouns. The lexicographers differed greatly about it. The strongest view about it is that the people of the Jāhiliyya, when a she-camel had produced five births, the last of them male, would slit her ear and forbid riding her; she would not be driven away from water or pasture, and when an exhausted person came upon her he would not ride her. It varies with the varying customs of the Arabs.
(سائِبَةٍ): in the Jāhiliyya a man among them would say: "If I return from my journey, or recover from my illness, then my she-camel is sāʾiba (set loose)." It was also said: when a man freed a slave, he would say: "He is sāʾiba." It is an active participle from ساب يسيب, i.e. to go loose, like the flowing of water (سيّب الماء); it is the reflexive (muṭāwiʿ) of سيّبته; one says: سيّبه فساب وانساب ("he let it loose, so it went loose and flowed").
(وَصِيلَةٍ): they differed sharply over its meaning, beyond what the present context has room for. The closest thing said about it is that the people of the Jāhiliyya, when a ewe bore a female, it was theirs, and if it bore a male, it was for their gods. It is faʿīla in the sense of fāʿila (active), so its tāʾ is regular.
(حامٍ): an active participle from حمى يحمي, when he prevents. The disagreement about it is sharp. They used to say: when ten births have been produced from the loins of a stallion, its back has become protected (ḥamā), so it is not ridden, nothing is loaded on it, and it is not prevented from water or pasture. All of these are customs, none of which Allah commanded, and He did not legislate them.

* I'rab:
(ما جَعَلَ اللَّهُ مِنْ بَحِيرَةٍ وَلا سائِبَةٍ وَلا وَصِيلَةٍ وَلا حامٍ): resumptive speech brought to condemn innovated customs and practices among their customs and practices, which Allah neither commanded nor legislated. ما is negating; جعل is in the sense of خلق ("to create"), so it takes one object, or in the sense of صيّر ("to make into"), so it takes two, the second being omitted, i.e. "made it legislated". الله is the fāʿil (agent); من is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition; بحيرة is "genitive in form" (majrūran lafẓan) [Translator's note: so in the text, «مجرورا لفظا», in the accusative case; the expected form is «مجرور».], a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) accusative in position; and what follows it is conjoined to it. (وَلكِنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا يَفْتَرُونَ عَلَى اللَّهِ الْكَذِبَ وَأَكْثَرُهُمْ لا يَعْقِلُونَ): the wāw is conjunctive or circumstantial; لكن and its noun; the clause كفروا is the ṣila (relative clause) with no grammatical position.
The clause يفترون is the khabar (predicate) of لكن; على الله is attached (mutaʿalliq) to يفترون; and الكذب is the direct object. The wāw is conjunctive or circumstantial; أكثرهم is a mubtadaʾ (subject); and the clause لا يعقلون is the khabar of أكثرهم.

dervis-irab:54-54.t:
* I'rab:
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مَنْ يَرْتَدَّ مِنْكُمْ عَنْ دِينِهِ فَسَوْفَ يَأْتِي اللَّهُ بِقَوْمٍ يُحِبُّهُمْ وَيُحِبُّونَهُ): resumptive speech, brought to show the state of apostates in general. The i'rab of the vocative has preceded many times. من is a conditional noun that makes the verb jussive, in the position of a nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); يرتد is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), jussive (majzūm), the sign of its jussive being the sukūn, and it was given the fatḥa because of its lightness, as has preceded under the rule of the doubled verb. منكم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). It has been read «يرتدد», with the assimilation undone. عن دينه is attached to يرتد; the fāʾ links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); the clause سوف يأتي الله is in the position of a jussive as the apodosis; and the protasis with its apodosis is the khabar (predicate) of «من». يأتي الله is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); بقوم is attached to يأتي; the clause يحبهم is a naʿt (adjective) of قوم; and the clause يحبونه is conjoined to the clause يحبهم. On Allah's love for the servant and the servant's love for Allah there are engaging discussions about which disagreement has raged; this is not the place to examine them, so let the reader refer to them in the long works. (أَذِلَّةٍ عَلَى الْمُؤْمِنِينَ أَعِزَّةٍ عَلَى الْكافِرِينَ): أذلة is a second naʿt of قوم; على المؤمنين is attached to أذلة, which is an assimilated adjective (ṣifa mushabbaha); أعزة is a third naʿt; and على الكافرين is attached to أعزّة. (يُجاهِدُونَ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ وَلا يَخافُونَ لَوْمَةَ لائِمٍ): the clause يجاهدون is a fourth naʿt of قوم, and the clause ولا يخافون is conjoined to the clause يجاهدون, so it is in effect a fifth naʿt. (ذلِكَ فَضْلُ اللَّهِ يُؤْتِيهِ مَنْ يَشاءُ وَاللَّهُ واسِعٌ عَلِيمٌ): the clause is resumptive; the demonstrative is a mubtadaʾ and فضل الله its khabar. «ذلك» may be used to point to the singular, the dual and the plural, and here it points to the qualities of which the first is: يحبهم ويحبونه. The clause يؤتيه is a second khabar, or you may make it resumptive; the hāʾ is the first mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and من is a relative noun in the position of an accusative as the second mafʿūl bihi of يؤتيه. The wāw is resumptive; الله is a mubtadaʾ, واسع a first khabar, and عليم a second khabar.

* Rhetoric:
1- The servant's love for Allah is by his obedience to Him; this is the kind of majāz (figurative usage) in which the effect is named by the cause.
2- Ṭibāq (antithesis) between أذلة and أعزّة.

dervis-irab:55-56.t:
* I'rab:
(إِنَّما وَلِيُّكُمُ اللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُ وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا): resumptive speech, brought to establish the ruling concerning one who takes Allah, His Messenger and the believers as allies. إنما is the restraining (kāffa) ما with the restrained particle; وليكم is a fronted khabar (predicate) and الله a nominative mubtadaʾ (subject), and the reverse is also permissible; رسوله is conjoined to الله, and likewise الذين آمنوا; and the clause آمنوا is the ṣila (relative clause). (الَّذِينَ يُقِيمُونَ الصَّلاةَ وَيُؤْتُونَ الزَّكاةَ): the relative noun is a badal (substitute) for الذين; the clause يقيمون is the ṣila, and الصلاة is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and يؤتون الزكاة is conjoined to what precedes it. (وَهُمْ راكِعُونَ): the wāw is circumstantial; هم is a mubtadaʾ and راكعون the khabar; the clause is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). The wāw may also be conjunctive, with the clause conjoined to what preceded it, so that it falls within the ṣila of the relative noun [Translator's note: the source has «في خبر الصلة», literally "in the predicate of the ṣila"]. (وَمَنْ يَتَوَلَّ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا): the wāw is resumptive; من is a conditional noun that makes the verb jussive, in the position of a nominative as mubtadaʾ; يتولّ is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ) and الله its object; رسوله is conjoined to الله, and الذين آمنوا is also conjoined. (فَإِنَّ حِزْبَ اللَّهِ هُمُ الْغالِبُونَ): the fāʾ links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); inna and its noun; هم is a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl) with no grammatical position, and الغالبون is the khabar of إنّ. Or «هم» is a mubtadaʾ and الغالبون the khabar of «هم», and the clause «هم الغالبون» is the khabar of «إن». The clause joined with the fāʾ is in the position of a jussive (majzūm) as the apodosis, and the protasis with its apodosis is the khabar of «من». It is also possible that the apodosis is omitted because the speech indicates it, i.e. "he will prevail", with His saying «فإن حزب الله هم الغالبون» indicating it; Ibn Hishām preferred this view in al-Mughnī.

dervis-irab:57-58.t:
* I'rab:
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا تَتَّخِذُوا الَّذِينَ اتَّخَذُوا دِينَكُمْ هُزُواً وَلَعِباً): resumptive speech, brought to address some of the believers and warn them against the hypocrites.
The i'rab of the vocative word has preceded. لا is prohibitive; تتخذوا is an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by لا, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); الذين is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause اتخذوا is the ṣila (relative clause); دينكم is the first mafʿūl bihi, هزوا the second mafʿūl bihi, and لعبا is conjoined to «هزوا». (مِنَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتابَ مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ وَالْكُفَّارَ أَوْلِياءَ): من الذين: the preposition and its genitive noun are a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the first relative noun, or of the fāʿil of اتخذوا; the clause أوتوا is the ṣila; أوتوا is a passive imperfect verb [Translator's note: so in the source; أُوتُوا is a passive past verb], and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); الكتاب is the second mafʿūl bihi; and من قبلكم is attached to (mutaʿalliq) أوتوا. الكفار is conjoined to الذين أوتوا; it has also been read in the genitive, conjoined to the relative noun made genitive by من. Makkī said: "Were it not for the agreement of the majority on the accusative, I would have chosen the genitive, for its strength in i'rab and in meaning." أولياء is the second mafʿūl bihi of تتخذوا. (وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ مُؤْمِنِينَ): the wāw is conjunctive; اتقوا الله is an imperative verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi; إن is conditional; كنتم is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb in the position of a jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), the tāʾ is its noun, and مؤمنين is the khabar (predicate) of كنتم; the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, i.e. "then fear Allah". (وَإِذا نادَيْتُمْ إِلَى الصَّلاةِ اتَّخَذُوها هُزُواً وَلَعِباً): the wāw is conjunctive, joining to the ṣila of الذين, which is a mafʿūl bihi. إذا is an adverb of future time that includes the meaning of condition; the clause ناديتم is in the position of a genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); إلى الصلاة is attached to ناديتم; the clause اتخذوها has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition; the wāw is the fāʿil, the hāʾ the first mafʿūl bihi, هزوا the second mafʿūl bihi, and لعبا is conjoined to it. (ذلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمْ قَوْمٌ لا يَعْقِلُونَ): the demonstrative is a mubtadaʾ (subject); the bāʾ is a preposition; أنّ with its noun and its khabar is to be interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun) made genitive by the bāʾ; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted khabar; لا is negative; يعقلون is an imperfect verb and the wāw its fāʿil; and the clause is a naʿt (adjective) of قوم.

dervis-irab:59-59.t:
* Vocabulary:
(تَنْقِمُونَ): the imperfect of نقم, in which there are two dialect forms. The more eloquent, reported by Thaʿlab in his Faṣīḥ, is نقم with fatḥa on the qāf, ينقم with kasra on it; the other is نقم with kasra on the qāf, ينقم with fatḥa on the qāf, reported by al-Kisāʾī. Its meaning is "you resent and dislike"; it has also been said: "you disapprove". ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Qays al-Ruqayyāt said:
ما نقموا من بني أمية إلّا ... أنّهم يحلمون إن غضبوا
(They resented nothing in Banū Umayya except that they are forbearing when they are angered.)

* I'rab:
(قُلْ: يا أَهْلَ الْكِتابِ): resumptive speech, brought to address the People of the Book among the Children of Israel. قل is an imperative verb; يا is a vocative particle; and أهل الكتاب is a vocative in genitive construct (munādā muḍāf). (هَلْ تَنْقِمُونَ مِنَّا إِلَّا أَنْ آمَنَّا بِاللَّهِ): the clause is the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl). هل is a particle of the interrogative of disapproval; تنقمون is an imperfect verb and the wāw its fāʿil (agent); منا is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) تنقمون; إلا is a particle of restriction; أن with what follows it is to be interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun) that is the object of تنقمون. It has been said that the maṣdar is accusative as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), with the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) omitted; the first view is preferable. بالله is attached to آمنا. The meaning is: you dislike nothing in us but faith; or: you are angry with us only because of our faith. (وَما أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْنا وَما أُنْزِلَ مِنْ قَبْلُ): conjoined to the interpreted maṣdar; the clause أنزل is the ṣila (relative clause); إلينا is attached to أنزل; the second «ما» is conjoined to the first «ما»; the clause أنزل is the ṣila; and من قبل is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). (وَأَنَّ أَكْثَرَكُمْ فاسِقُونَ): the wāw is conjunctive. The majority read «أن» with fatḥa, so it is to be interpreted as a maṣdar whose position is nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), with the khabar (predicate) omitted, the implied form being: "and your transgression is established and known to you", because you know that we are upon the truth and that you are upon falsehood; but your racialism and your love of leadership and of amassing wealth have driven you to mount this rough mount. It is possible that the position of the maṣdar is accusative, conjoined to «أن آمنا», the meaning being: "and you resent nothing in us except the combination of our faith with your rebellion and your departure from faith". Or the wāw is of accompaniment, with the interpreted maṣdar a mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment), the implied form being: "and you resent nothing in us except faith, along with the fact that most of you are transgressors". It is also possible that its position is genitive, conjoined to الله, i.e. "and you resent nothing in us except faith in Allah, in what was sent down, and in the fact that most of you are transgressors".

* Rhetoric:
In this verse there is a delightful art: confirming praise by what resembles blame (taʾkīd al-madḥ bi-mā yushbih al-dhamm).
It is an art of widespread fame, but with few examples, and I have found in the Qur'an only this verse. For the exception after the interrogative, which functions as a rebuke for the faith with which they found fault in the believers, gives the impression that after the interrogative there will come something for which its doer deserves to be resented, by which he is blamed; so when after the interrogative there came something that requires praise of its doer, the speech contained confirmation of praise by what resembles blame. The scholars of rhetoric have defined this art as the exception of an attribute of praise from an attribute of blame negated of a thing, by supposing it to be included in the negated attribute of blame. An instance is the saying of al-Nābigha al-Dhubyānī:
ولا عيب فيهم غير أن سيوفهم ... بهن فلول من قراع الكتائب
(There is no fault in them, except that their swords have notches from clashing with the battalions.)
The confirmation in it is clear: he mentioned the particle of exception, «غير», before mentioning what follows it, giving the impression of excluding something from what precedes it; then, when an attribute of praise follows it, the confirmation comes. Notches in swords from much striking in wars belong to the domain of boasting and are signs of courage. Of this type also is that you affirm an attribute of praise for a thing and follow it with a particle of exception followed by another attribute of praise for that thing, as in the saying of the Messenger ﷺ: «أنا أفصح العرب بيد أني من قريش» ("I am the most eloquent of the Arabs, except that I am from Quraysh").
He mentioned the particle of exception, «بيد», which matches «غير» in pattern and meaning, before mentioning what follows it; then following it with another attribute of praise — his being from Quraysh, who are the most eloquent of the Arabs — adds beauty to the confirmation of the meaning. Al-Nābigha said, of this kind:
فتى كملت أوصافه غير أنه ... جواد فما يبقي على المال باقيا
(A youth whose qualities are perfect, except that he is generous, so he leaves nothing of wealth remaining.)

dervis-irab:60-60.t:
* I'rab:
(قُلْ: هَلْ أُنَبِّئُكُمْ بِشَرٍّ مِنْ ذلِكَ مَثُوبَةً عِنْدَ اللَّهِ): resumptive speech, brought to address the Jews in a manner befitting their defiance, their obstinacy and their deep penetration into disbelief.
قل is an imperative verb, and the interrogative clause is the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl). هل is an interrogative particle; أنبئكم is an imperfect verb in the position of an accusative [Translator's note: so in the source; أنبئكم is in fact a nominative (marfūʿ) imperfect verb, and it is the clause that is in the position of an accusative as the object of saying], and the kāf is its first object; بشرّ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) something omitted that is the second object; من ذلك is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «شرّ», because it is an elative noun (ism tafḍīl); مثوبة is a tamyīz (specification) of شر, and it is a tamyīz of relation (tamyīz nisba), because الشر applies to persons; more detail will come in the section on Rhetoric. عند ذلك [Translator's note: so in the source; the Quranic text is عند الله] is attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). (مَنْ لَعَنَهُ اللَّهُ وَغَضِبَ عَلَيْهِ): من is a relative noun in the position of a nominative as the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject); for when He said: "Shall I inform you of what is worse than that?", it is as though someone said: "Who is that?" and it was said: "He is the one whom Allah has cursed"; the clause has no grammatical position because it is explicative. The position of «من» may also be genitive as a badal (substitute) for «شر». The clause لعنه الله has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause), and the clause غضب عليه is conjoined to the ṣila. (وَجَعَلَ مِنْهُمُ الْقِرَدَةَ وَالْخَنازِيرَ وَعَبَدَ الطَّاغُوتَ): the wāw is conjunctive; جعل is conjoined to لعنه الله; منهم is attached to something omitted that is the first mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and القردة is the second object; الخنازير is conjoined to القردة. عبد is a past verb, conjoined to the ṣila of «ما» [Translator's note: so in the source; the relative noun here is «من»], as though it were said: "and whoever worshipped the ṭāghūt"; the relative noun was omitted and the attribute (ṣifa) set in its place. (أُولئِكَ شَرٌّ مَكاناً وَأَضَلُّ عَنْ سَواءِ السَّبِيلِ): the clause is explicative with no grammatical position; the demonstrative is a mubtadaʾ and شر the khabar; مكانا is a tamyīz; أضل is conjoined to شر; and عن سواء السبيل is attached to أضلّ.

* Rhetoric:
This verse contains several kinds of rhetoric, which we set out below:
1- al-majāz al-mursal (non-metaphorical figurative usage) in His saying: «مثوبة» ("recompense"), the relation being contrariety, like: «فبشرهم بعذاب أليم» ("so give them glad tidings of a painful punishment"). What is intended by this majāz is sarcasm (tahakkum). The overall meaning is: Say, O Muḥammad, to these who have taken your religion as play and amusement, of those who were given the Book before you and the disbelievers: "Shall I inform you of what is worse than the people of that which you resent in us, and worse than its recompense?", i.e. its punishment. The speech was framed according to their saying and their belief; otherwise there is no sharing between the believers and them in the very fact of punishment, such that it could be said that the punishment of one of the two parties is worse than that of the other. But they judged that the religion of Islam was evil, so it was said to them: suppose the matter is so; yet the curse of Allah the Exalted and His anger, being kept far from His mercy, being driven out of the court of His good pleasure, and the transformation of form into the ugliest and vilest kinds of animal, are worse than that which you claim is evil. And you know what baseness and vileness belong to the two kinds, apes and swine, and what ugliness, deformity, hideousness of appearance, meanness of soul, lowliness of worth, baseness of nature, repulsiveness of form and character, ugliness of voice and lowness of aspiration they have in the minds of common people and elite alike — such as no other kinds of animal have.
2- Sarcasm (tahakkum): it is contained within the majāz mursal. Sarcasm has been discussed in detail before.
3- al-majāz al-mursal in His saying: «شر مكانا» ("worse in place"), its relation being locality (maḥalliyya): He mentioned the place and meant its people. This too has preceded.

* Benefits:
You may say: an elative noun must have something preferred and something over which it is preferred, so how can it be said that they are worse than the believers, when the believers have no evil at all?
The answer is that it came by way of concession and granting the opponent his claim, to silence him and proclaim against him the crushing argument; or that it is specific to the disbelievers, who are of differing grades in the measure of evil ascribed to them.

dervis-irab:61-62.t:
* I'rab:
(وَإِذا جاؤُكُمْ قالُوا آمَنَّا): the wāw is resumptive, and the clause is resumptive, brought to address the Prophet ﷺ and those with him. إذا is an adverb of future time that includes the meaning of condition; the clause جاءوكم is in the position of a genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); جاءوكم is a verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause قالوا has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition; and the clause آمنا is in the position of an accusative as the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl). (وَقَدْ دَخَلُوا بِالْكُفْرِ وَهُمْ قَدْ خَرَجُوا بِهِ): the wāw is circumstantial and قد is a particle of realisation (taḥqīq); the clause دخلوا is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the wāw in «قالوا»; بالكفر is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl of the fāʿil of دخلوا. The second wāw is also circumstantial, and the clause is likewise in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl of the wāw in «قالوا»; به is attached to an omitted ḥāl of the fāʿil of خرجوا, i.e. "they entered as disbelievers and left as disbelievers". (وَاللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ بِما كانُوا يَكْتُمُونَ): the wāw is resumptive; الله is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and أعلم the khabar (predicate); بما is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أعلم; the clause كانوا has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause); and the clause يكتمون is in the position of an accusative as the khabar of كانوا. (وَتَرى كَثِيراً مِنْهُمْ يُسارِعُونَ فِي الْإِثْمِ وَالْعُدْوانِ): the wāw is conjunctive or resumptive; ترى is an imperfect verb; كثيرا is a mafʿūl bihi; منهم is attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective); the clause يسارعون is a ḥāl of «كثيرا», or a naʿt of it; في الإثم is attached to يسارعون; and العدوان is conjoined to الإثم. (وَأَكْلِهِمُ السُّحْتَ لَبِئْسَ ما كانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ): أكلهم is conjoined to الإثم and العدوان; السحت is the mafʿūl bihi of the maṣdar (verbal noun), which is «أكل»; the lām is in answer to an omitted oath; بئس is an inflexible (jāmid) past verb for expressing blame; ما is a complete indefinite noun in the position of an accusative as a tamyīz (specification), or a relative noun, in which case it is the fāʿil; the clause كانوا has no grammatical position on either view; and the clause يعملون is in the position of an accusative as the khabar of كانوا.

dervis-irab:104-105.t:
* I'rab:
(وَإِذا قِيلَ لَهُمْ: تَعالَوْا إِلى ما أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ وَإِلَى الرَّسُولِ): the wāw is resumptive or conjunctive; إذا is an adverb of future time containing the sense of a condition, attached (mutaʿalliq) to the coming apodosis; the clause تعالوا is in the position of the accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); إلى ما أنزل الله: the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to تعالوا; أنزل الله is a verb and its fāʿil (agent), and the clause is a ṣila (relative clause); and إلى الرسول is conjoined to it. (قالُوا حَسْبُنا ما وَجَدْنا عَلَيْهِ آباءَنا): the clause قالوا has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition; حسبنا is a mubtadaʾ (subject); ما is a relative noun in the position of the nominative as khabar (predicate); the clause وجدنا has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila; عليه is attached to وجدنا; and آباءنا is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (أَوَلَوْ كانَ آباؤُهُمْ لا يَعْلَمُونَ شَيْئاً وَلا يَهْتَدُونَ): the hamza is for the interrogative of disapproval and rebuke; the wāw is conjunctive, [conjoining] to something implied, its implied form being "Is that sufficient for them?", or circumstantial, i.e. "even if their fathers were ignorant and astray". لو is conditional and its apodosis is omitted, its implied form being "they say that". كان and its noun; the clause لا يعلمون is its khabar; شيئا is a direct object; and the clause لا يهتدون is conjoined to the clause لا يعلمون. (يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا عَلَيْكُمْ أَنْفُسَكُمْ): the clause is resumptive, brought to show that every person is responsible for himself. It cannot be objected to this that it offers a way out of commanding right and forbidding wrong, because that is contingent upon capacity.
He ﷺ said: "Whoever among you sees a wrong, let him change it with his hand; if he is unable, then with his tongue; and if he is unable, then with his heart." عليكم is a transferred verbal noun of command (ism fiʿl amr manqūl) in the sense of "hold to" (الزموا), and أنفسكم is the direct object of the verbal noun. (لا يَضُرُّكُمْ مَنْ ضَلَّ إِذَا اهْتَدَيْتُمْ): the clause is resumptive; لا is negating; يضركم is an imperfect verb, and the kāf is the direct object; من is a relative noun in the position of the nominative as the agent of يضركم [Translator's note: the text has the misprint «بضركم».]; the clause ضل is the ṣila; إذا is an adverb of future time containing the sense of a condition, attached to the implied apodosis, i.e. "then he does not harm you"; and the clause اهتديتم is in the position of the genitive by construct (iḍāfa). (إِلَى اللَّهِ مَرْجِعُكُمْ جَمِيعاً فَيُنَبِّئُكُمْ بِما كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ): the clause is resumptive; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted fronted khabar; مرجعكم is a delayed mubtadaʾ; جميعا is a ḥāl (circumstantial); فينبئكم: the fāʾ is conjunctive, and ينبئكم is a verb, a latent (mustatir) agent and a direct object; بما is attached to ينبئكم; the clause كنتم is the ṣila; the tāʾ is the noun of كان; and the clause تعملون is its khabar.

* Benefits:
The grammarians differed about the pronoun attached to «عليكم», «إليكم», «لديكم» and «مكانكم». The correct view is that it is in the position of the genitive, as it was before the word was transferred to [the function of] incitement (ighrāʾ); it is either genitive by the preposition, as in «عليكم», according to what it was, or by construct, as in «لديكم». It was also said: the kāf is a particle of address, and this view is, in my opinion, simpler; Ibn Bābashādh supported it. We give here an important summary of verbal nouns (asmāʾ al-afʿāl); they are of two kinds:
1- Improvised (murtajal): that which was coined as such from the outset, i.e. as a name for the verb, such as شتان ("how far apart!"), أفّ ("ugh!") and صه ("hush!").
2- Transferred (manqūl): that which was coined from the outset for something other than a verbal noun and was then transferred from it to that. It is of three kinds:
a- From a preposition and its genitive noun, such as عليك in the sense of "hold to" (الزم).
b- From an adverb of place, such as دونك الكتاب, i.e. "take it"; مكانك, i.e. "stay firm"; أمامك, i.e. "go forward"; and وراءك, i.e. "step aside".
c- Transferred from a maṣdar (verbal noun), such as رويد خالدا, i.e. "give Khālid time", and بله هذا الأمر, i.e. "leave this matter aside".
A poet said, describing swords:
تذر الجماجم ضاحيا هاماتها ... بله الأكفّ كأنها لم تخلق
(They leave the skulls with their crowns laid bare — let alone the hands — as if they had never been created.)
And Abū al-Ṭayyib al-Mutanabbī used it, saying:
أقلّ فعالي بله أكثره مجد ... وذا الجد فيه نلت أم لم أنل جدّ
(The least of my deeds — let alone the most of them — is glory; and this earnestness is earnestness, whether I attained good fortune or not.)
Verbal nouns have other details, which may be consulted in their proper places.

dervis-irab:106-108.t:
* Vocabulary:
(ضَرَبْتُمْ فِي الْأَرْضِ): i.e. you travelled.
(الْأَوْلَيانِ): dual of الأولى, i.e. the two most entitled to give testimony because of their kinship and their knowledge.

* I'rab:
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا شَهادَةُ بَيْنِكُمْ إِذا حَضَرَ أَحَدَكُمُ الْمَوْتُ حِينَ الْوَصِيَّةِ اثْنانِ ذَوا عَدْلٍ مِنْكُمْ): resumptive speech brought to set out rulings relating to the affairs of this world, after setting out the states relating to the affairs of the Hereafter. شهادة is a mubtadaʾ (subject); بينكم is muḍāf ilayhi; إذا is an adverb of future time containing the sense of a condition, attached (mutaʿalliq) to the omitted apodosis, i.e. "then [it is] the testimony of two"; the clause حضر أحدكم الموت is in the position of the genitive by construct (iḍāfa); حين الوصية is an adverb attached to حضر; and اثنان is the khabar (predicate) of شهادة. An omitted muḍāf must be implied so that the mubtadaʾ and the khabar correspond, because the testimony cannot itself be the two [men], since a concrete being cannot be a khabar of a maṣdar (verbal noun). Al-Zamakhsharī allowed شهادة to be a mubtadaʾ with the khabar omitted, i.e. "among what has been prescribed for you is testimony", with اثنان being the fāʿil (agent) of شهادة, i.e.
"that two should testify". This is also what Ibn Hishām followed. ذوا عدل is a naʿt (adjective) of «اثنان», and منكم is also an adjective. (أَوْ آخَرانِ مِنْ غَيْرِكُمْ إِنْ أَنْتُمْ ضَرَبْتُمْ فِي الْأَرْضِ): أو is a conjunction; آخران is conjoined to «اثنان»; من غيركم is attached to an omitted adjective of «آخران», i.e. from other than your religious community; إن is conditional; أنتم is the agent of an omitted verb explained by what follows it; the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, i.e. "then the two witnesses are two others"; the clause ضربتم is explicative with no grammatical position; في الأرض is attached to ضربتم; and the conditional clause is parenthetical with no grammatical position. (فَأَصابَتْكُمْ مُصِيبَةُ الْمَوْتِ تَحْبِسُونَهُما مِنْ بَعْدِ الصَّلاةِ): the fāʾ is conjunctive, for sequence with immediacy; أصابتكم is conjoined to ضربتم; مصيبة الموت is the agent of أصابتكم; تحبسونهما is an imperfect verb and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). They differed about the position of this clause; the most apparent view is that it is an adjective of «آخران».
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: what is the position of تحبسونهما? I say: it is a resumption of speech, as if it were said, after the stipulation of probity in them: 'So what are we to do if we have doubts about them?' and it was said: 'Detain them.'" Abū Ḥayyān commented on that, saying:
"What al-Zamakhsharī said about resumption is more apparent than the adjectival reading, because of the long separation, by the condition and what is conjoined to it, between the thing described and its adjective; and there is nothing necessitating this claim." [Translator's note: so in the text; the last clause appears to sit oddly with the preceding one.]
من بعد الصلاة is attached to تحبسونهما. (فَيُقْسِمانِ بِاللَّهِ إِنِ ارْتَبْتُمْ لا نَشْتَرِي بِهِ ثَمَناً وَلَوْ كانَ ذا قُرْبى): the fāʾ is conjunctive; يقسمان is conjoined to تحبسونهما; بالله is attached to يقسمان; إن is conditional; ارتبتم is a verb and its agent in the position of the jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the apodosis is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, its implied form being: "if you have doubts about them, then make them swear". The protasis and its implied apodosis form a clause with no grammatical position, because it is parenthetical between the oath and its answer. This verse is not among those in which a condition and an oath come together so that the earlier of the two is answered and the answer of the other is omitted because the answer of the condition indicates it, because that case is conditional on the oath being fit to serve as the answer of the condition, so that it stands in place of its answer, as in: "By Allah, if you visit me I will surely honour you" — for if you imply "If you visit me, I will honour you", it is correct. Here, the answer of the condition is not implied as being what is the answer of the oath; rather its answer is implied as an independent oath. Do you not see that its implied form here is "if you have doubts, make them swear", and that if you implied something other than that it would not be correct! Others said: there is an omitted saying, its implied form being: "then they swear by Allah and say this saying in their oaths".
The Arabs often leave the saying implied, as in His words, the Exalted: «والملائكة يدخلون عليهم من كل باب سلام», i.e. saying: «سلام عليكم». لا is negating; نشتري is an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), and the clause has no grammatical position because it is the answer of the oath; به is attached to نشتري; ثمنا is the direct object; the wāw is circumstantial; لو is conditional; كان is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb, its noun latent (mustatir), i.e. the one for whom the oath is sworn; ذا قربى is the khabar of كان; the apodosis of «لو» is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, i.e.
"then we will not sell it"; and the conditional clause of لو and what is in its domain is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). (وَلا نَكْتُمُ شَهادَةَ اللَّهِ إِنَّا إِذاً لَمِنَ الْآثِمِينَ): the wāw is conjunctive, and the clause لا نكتم is conjoined to what is arranged with it under the ruling of the oath; شهادة الله is the direct object; إن and its noun; إذن is an inoperative particle of answer and requital; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); من الآثمين is attached to an omitted khabar of إن; and the clause إن and what is in its domain has no grammatical position, serving as the cause for not concealing. (فَإِنْ عُثِرَ عَلى أَنَّهُمَا اسْتَحَقَّا إِثْماً): the fāʾ is resumptive; إن is conditional; عثر is a passive past verb in the position of the jussive as the protasis; على أنهما is a preposition and its genitive noun as nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), i.e. "if it is discovered that they deserved sin"; أن and its noun; the clause استحقا is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of أن; the alif is the agent of استحقا; and إثما is the object of استحقا. (فَآخَرانِ يَقُومانِ مَقامَهُما مِنَ الَّذِينَ اسْتَحَقَّ عَلَيْهِمُ الْأَوْلَيانِ): the fāʾ links the apodosis; آخران is a mubtadaʾ — beginning with it is permissible because it is a description — or it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ; the clause يقومان is in the position of the nominative as khabar on the first view, or an adjective on the second; مقامهما is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); من الذين is an adjective of «آخران»; the clause استحق has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause); عليهم is attached to استحق; الأوليان is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "they are the two most entitled", or the agent of استحق; and the clause فآخران is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis. (فَيُقْسِمانِ بِاللَّهِ لَشَهادَتُنا أَحَقُّ مِنْ شَهادَتِهِما): the fāʾ is conjunctive; يقسمان is an imperfect verb in the nominative, conjoined to يقومان; the alif is the agent; بالله is attached to يقسمان; the lām occurs in the answer of the oath; شهادتنا is a mubtadaʾ and أحق the khabar; من شهادتهما is attached to أحق; and the clause شهادتنا has no grammatical position because it occurs as the answer of the oath. (وَمَا اعْتَدَيْنا إِنَّا إِذاً لَمِنَ الظَّالِمِينَ): the wāw is resumptive; ما is negating; اعتدينا is a past verb and its agent; إن and its noun; إذن is an inoperative particle of answer and requital; من الظالمين is the khabar of إن; and the clause is causal (taʿlīliyya) with no grammatical position. (ذلِكَ أَدْنى أَنْ يَأْتُوا بِالشَّهادَةِ عَلى وَجْهِها): the demonstrative is a mubtadaʾ and أدنى the khabar, and the clause is resumptive; أن and what follows it are interpreted as a maṣdar in construct with أدنى; بالشهادة is attached to يأتوا; and على وجهها is attached to an omitted ḥāl.
