(أَوْ يَخافُوا أَنْ تُرَدَّ أَيْمانٌ بَعْدَ أَيْمانِهِمْ): أو is a conjunction; يخافوا is conjoined to يأتوا; أن and what follows it are interpreted as a maṣdar, the object of يخافوا; أيمان is the deputy agent of ترد; the adverb بعد is attached to «ترد»; and أيمانهم is muḍāf ilayhi. (وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَاسْمَعُوا وَاللَّهُ لا يَهْدِي الْقَوْمَ الْفاسِقِينَ): the wāw is resumptive; اتقوا الله is an imperative verb, its agent and its direct object; اسمعوا is conjoined to اتقوا; the wāw is resumptive; الله is a mubtadaʾ; the clause لا يهدي is the khabar; القوم is the direct object; and الفاسقين is an adjective of القوم.

* Benefits:
These three verses have greatly occupied the exegetes and the parsers, and they have spoken at length, though there is nothing calling for length. Makkī ibn Abī Ṭālib mentioned in his book called «al-Kashf» that these verses, in their readings, i'rab, exegesis, meanings and rulings, are among the most difficult verses of the Qur'an. Al-Sakhāwī said:
"I have not seen anyone among the scholars whose discussion of them came out clear from beginning to end." Al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī said: "I seek Allah's help in accounting for their i'rab, the derivation of their single words, the morphology of their words, their readings and knowledge of their composition; as for the rest of their sciences, we ask Allah for help in refining it." We for our part have tried to be as brief as possible, and have confined ourselves to the reading of Ḥafṣ; as for the rest of their rulings, one must consult the books of ḥadīth and the lengthy books of exegesis.

dervis-irab:27-29.t:
* Vocabulary:
(قُرْباناً): «القربان», with ḍamma on the qāf; there are two views on it:
1- It is a noun for that by which one draws near to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, whether charity, a sacrifice or other than that; like «الحلوان», also with ḍamma on the ḥāʾ: the name of what is given (yuḥlā, i.e. given).
One says: «قرّب صدقة» and «تقرّب بها», because «تقرّب» is the reflexive (muṭāwiʿ) of «قرّب».
2- That it was originally a maṣdar (verbal noun), and was then applied to the thing by which one draws near, as in their saying «نسج اليمن» (the weave of Yemen, i.e. what is woven). Evidence for this is that it was not put in the dual, though the place calls for the dual, because each of Qābīl and Hābīl had his own offering, and the base form would be to say «قربانين». The holders of the first view said: there is no proof in this, because the meaning is: when each one of them offered an offering, as in the saying of the Exalted: «فاجلدوهم ثمانين جلدة» (then flog them eighty lashes), i.e. each one of them eighty lashes.
(تَبُوءَ): you return [bearing].

* I'rab:
(وَاتْلُ عَلَيْهِمْ نَبَأَ ابْنَيْ آدَمَ بِالْحَقِّ): the clause is conjoined to the implied verb in His saying «وإذ قال موسى لقومه», meaning: "mention, O Muḥammad, to your people and tell them the account of the two sons of Ādam," namely Hābīl and Qābīl, and the story of the offering and its cause. The story of Qābīl's killing of Hābīl fills the lengthy works of exegesis.
(اتل) is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the weak letter; (عليهم) is attached to «اتل»; (نبأ) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (ابني) is annexed to «نبأ», the nūn having been dropped because of annexation; (آدم) is annexed to «ابني»; (بالحق) is attached to an omitted adjective of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "a recitation bound up with the truth"; or [it is] a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent), so the implied form is: "while you are bound up with the truth," i.e. with truthfulness; or from the direct object, i.e. "recite their account as bound up with truth and truthfulness."
(إِذْ قَرَّبا قُرْباناً فَتُقُبِّلَ مِنْ أَحَدِهِما وَلَمْ يُتَقَبَّلْ مِنَ الْآخَرِ): (إذ) is an adverb of past time attached to (نبأ), i.e. "recite their story and their account that took place at that time"; or it is a badal (substitute) from it, i.e. "and recite to them the account, the account of that time," supposing the omission of the muḍāf. The clause (قربا) is in the position of genitive by annexation; (قربا) is a verb and its agent, and (قربانا) is the direct object. In (فتقبل): the fāʾ is a conjunction, and (تقبل) is a past verb in the passive; the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent (mustatir), implied as «هو», referring to «قربانا»; (من أحدهما), a preposition and its genitive noun, is attached to (تقبل); and (ولم يتقبل من الآخر) is conjoined to (تقبل).
(قالَ: لَأَقْتُلَنَّكَ قالَ: إِنَّما يَتَقَبَّلُ اللَّهُ مِنَ الْمُتَّقِينَ): the clause (لأقتلنك) is in the position of accusative as the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl). The lām prepares for the oath (al-lām al-muwaṭṭiʾa); (أقتلنك) is an imperfect verb, indeclinable on fatḥa because it must be emphasised with the heavy nūn; the kāf is the direct object. (إنما) is [inna] with the restraining «ما» (kāffa wa-makfūfa); and the clause (إنما يتقبل الله من المتقين) is the object of saying.
(لَئِنْ بَسَطْتَ إِلَيَّ يَدَكَ لِتَقْتُلَنِي ما أَنَا بِباسِطٍ يَدِيَ إِلَيْكَ لِأَقْتُلَكَ): the lām prepares for the oath; (إن) is conditional; (بسطت) is a past verb in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), the tāʾ being the agent; (إلي) is attached to (بسطت); (يدك) is the direct object; and the clause is resumptive, explaining what he meant to say. In (لتقتلني), the lām is the causal lām; (تقتلني) is an imperfect verb in the accusative by an implied «أن» after the causal lām; the nūn is the nūn of protection (wiqāya), and the yāʾ the direct object; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (بسطت). (ما) is the Ḥijāzī negative, operating like «ليس»; (أنا) is its noun; the bāʾ is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition; (باسط) is a noun genitive in form and accusative in position as its khabar (predicate); (يدي) is the direct object of (باسط), because it is an active participle; (إليك) is attached to (باسط). In (لأقتلك), the lām is the causal lām, and (أقتلك) is an imperfect verb in the accusative by an implied «أن» after the causal lām. The clause is the answer to the oath because [the oath] precedes the condition, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted because the answer to the oath indicates it.
(إِنِّي أَخافُ اللَّهَ رَبَّ الْعالَمِينَ): the clause is causal (taʿlīliyya); (إن) with its noun, and the clause (أخاف الله) its khabar; and (رب العالمين) is a badal from (الله) or an adjective.
(إِنِّي أُرِيدُ أَنْ تَبُوءَ بِإِثْمِي وَإِثْمِكَ فَتَكُونَ مِنْ أَصْحابِ النَّارِ): the clause is a second reason for his refraining from fighting, after the first reason. (إن) with its noun; the clause (أريد) is its khabar, the agent being latent, implied as «أنا»; (أن تبوء) is an interpreted maṣdar in the position of accusative as the direct object of (أريد); (بإثمي), a preposition and its genitive noun, is attached to an omitted [element] in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from the agent of (تبوء), i.e. "you return carrying it," or "bound up with it." In (فتكون), the fāʾ is a conjunction, and (تكون) is a defective (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb conjoined to (تبوء), following it in the accusative; its noun is «أنت»; and (من أصحاب النار) is attached to the omitted khabar of (تكون).
(وَذلِكَ جَزاءُ الظَّالِمِينَ): the wāw is resumptive; (ذلك) is a demonstrative in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject); and (جزاء الظالمين) is the khabar.

* Rhetoric:
1- In His saying «إنما يتقبل الله من المتقين» there is comprehensive, all-encompassing speech (al-kalām al-jāmiʿ al-māniʿ): this clause gathers many meanings in brief words, for it contains the gist of the story from beginning to end, and the story is long; the reader will find it in the lengthy works. The gist of the meaning is that Allah the Exalted accepts obedience only from a God-fearing believer. It is reported of ʿĀmir ibn ʿAbd Allāh that he wept when death came to him, and it was said to him:
"What makes you weep? You were such-and-such and such-and-such." He said: "I hear Allah saying: «إنما يتقبل الله من المتقين»."
2- In His saying «إني أريد أن تبوء بإثمي وإثمك» there is the device of ittisāʿ (amplitude).
It is that the speaker brings speech in which interpretation is wide, according to what its words can bear, so that its interpretation widens according to people's intellects and the differences in their understanding. In the verse it lies in his wanting his brother's sin, because its meaning is: "I do not want to kill you and be punished."
Since one of two things had to be wanted — either his own sin, supposing that he defended himself and killed his brother, or his brother's sin, supposing that he surrendered — and he did not want the first, he was compelled to the second. So he did not then want his brother's sin for its own sake; rather he meant that sin lies in defending oneself in a way that leads to killing, which was not lawful at that time, and from that it followed that he wanted his brother's sin. This is like a person's wishing for martyrdom.
Its meaning is that the unbeliever returns bearing his killing and the sin he incurs thereby; but [the martyr] did not intend the unbeliever's sin for its own sake; he only wanted to give himself in the way of Allah, hoping [for that], the unbeliever's sin in killing coming implicitly and consequentially. What indicates this is that there is no difference in attaining the rank of martyrdom and its merit between the killer dying in unbelief and his life being sealed with faith, so that the sin of the killing, through which the martyr became a martyr, is annulled for him — I mean, whether the sin remains on his killer or is annulled for him, that neither diminishes nor increases the merit of his martyrdom. If the unbeliever's sin in killing were intended, the wish would differ according to its remaining or being annulled. So this shows that it is a necessary, consequential matter, not an intended one.

Views of the scholars:
The scholars of exegesis, grammar and rhetoric have spoken at length «[Translator's note: the printed text has «أقاض», a misprint for «أفاض»]» on this verse. What they have presented comes down to three interpretations:
a- That it is with the omission of the interrogative hamza, i.e. «إني أريد أأن تبوء؟» (do I want that you should return…?); and it is a disapproving question, because wanting disobedience is disobedience.
b- That «لا» is omitted, the implied form being «إني أريد أن لا تبوء بإثمي» (I want that you not return with my sin), like the saying of the Exalted: «يبين الله لكم أن تضلوا» (Allah makes clear to you lest you go astray), i.e. that you not go astray.
c- That the wanting is as it stands, being either figurative or real wanting; wanting that was permissible for him for reasons the exegetes mentioned, among them that indications appeared to him showing that his death was near, that his brother was an unbeliever, and that wanting punishment for an unbeliever is good.
3- The condition came in the form of a verb, namely His saying «بسطت», and the answer in the form of an active participle, namely His saying «ما أنا بباسط», to convey that he does not do what would earn this abominable deed; therefore He emphasised it with the redundant bāʾ that emphasises the negation.
Al-Mutanabbī and ittisāʿ:
In any case, this verse and the ittisāʿ in it appear to be among the things subtle for the understanding; but it is a necessary subtlety, containing many meanings drawn out from the speech. Al-Mutanabbī gazed toward its heaven, and he very often inclined to this kind of eloquence, so that his speech became subtle. Among his ittisāʿ is his saying:
لولا مفارقة الأحباب ما وجدت ... لها المنايا إلى أرواحنا سبلا
(Were it not for parting from loved ones, the fates would not have found for themselves paths to our souls.)
The outward form of the speech suggests at first glance that «لها» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «وجدت»; but that would involve the verb of an overt [agent] passing to that agent's own attached pronoun, which is not allowed. So it must be taken as originally an adjective of «سبلا», which became a ḥāl when it was placed before it; and His saying «إلى أرواحنا» is likewise, since the meaning is: "paths travelled to our souls." You also have a strange view on «لها»: that you take «لها» as the plural of «لهاة» (uvula), like «حصى» and «حصاة», with «المنايا» annexed to it; ascribing uvulas to the fates is then a metaphor, likening them to something that swallows people; and he put «اللها» in place of mouths because the uvulas are adjacent to the [sense of] taste «[Translator's note: the text reads «للنعم»; perhaps a misprint for «للطعم» (taste) or «للفم» (the mouth)]». «اللهاة», with fatḥa, is the piece of flesh overhanging the throat at the far end of the roof of the mouth.
Of this kind is his saying in love poetry:
كشفت ثلاث ذوائب من شعرها ... في ليلة فأرت ليالي أربعا
واستقبلت قمر السماء بوجهها ... فأرتني القمرين في وقت معا
(She uncovered three locks of her hair in one night, and showed four nights; and she faced the moon of the sky with her face, and showed me the two moons at one time together.)
The meaning is not as people think, that he saw two moons at one time, the moon and her face; rather, the accurate view is that when she faced the moon of the sky, its image was imprinted on her face, so he saw both at one time, just as shapes face a mirror and the image is imprinted in it, so you see the mirror and the shapes imprinted in it at one time together.
Al-Tibrīzī erred when he explained the verse, saying: it is possible that he meant a moon and a moon, because two real moons do not come together in one night, just as the sun and moon do not come together. One of the poets clung to the fringes of al-Mutanabbī and composed two verses most like sleight-of-hand and tricks:
رأت قمر السماء فذكرتني ... ليالي وصلها بالرقمتين
كلانا ناظر قمرا ولكن ... رأيت بعينها ورأت بعيني
(She saw the moon of the sky and reminded me of the nights of her union at al-Raqmatayn; each of us gazes at a moon, but I saw with her eye and she saw with mine.)
The best that can be said about them is that "two moons" means a real moon, which is the moon of the sky, and a figurative moon, which is the face of the beloved. So he says: she saw the figurative moon, which is the moon of the sky, and I saw her face, which is the real moon; because she looked at the moon of the sky and he looked at her face, so it holds true that he saw with her eye and she saw with his. This is hyperbole and excess in description; but the poets have customarily made the beloved the real moon and the one in the sky the figurative moon. Others said in explaining them:
This poet alludes «[Translator's note: the printed text has «يتسير», apparently a misprint for «يشير»]» to the moon of the sky being one of his beloved's lovers, and that his beloved saw it one night and, by her seeing it, clothed it with the light of her beauty and the charms of her qualities, cast her likeness upon it, and lent it her name. So she reminded this lover of those nights of union at al-Raqmatayn, and that by her union with him she annihilated him and overcame him with her qualities, until she became with him like a single moon, and both look at it. Hence he said "each of us gazes at a moon," i.e. a single moon whose manifestation became multiple; but she looks at it with his eye, which is the eye of love, because the lover has become beloved; and he looks with her eye, because she lent him an eye with which he saw her, so it is as though the one who sees her is she herself. The discussion of ittisāʿ is long; we content ourselves here with what has been said.

dervis-irab:30-31.t:
* Vocabulary:
(طوّعت): made easy and made attractive; from «طاع المرعى له», when the pasture became ample for him.
(سَوْأَةَ): «السوءة», with fatḥa on the sīn: the private parts, and what of the body may not be uncovered. «السوءة» is also disgrace. The «سوءة» was singled out for mention because concern for covering it is greater.

* I'rab:
(فَطَوَّعَتْ لَهُ نَفْسُهُ قَتْلَ أَخِيهِ فَقَتَلَهُ فَأَصْبَحَ مِنَ الْخاسِرِينَ): the fāʾ is a conjunction; (طوعت) is a past verb; (له) is attached to (طوعت); (نفسه) is the fāʿil (agent); (قتل أخيه) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (فقتله) is also conjoined, and (فأصبح) is also conjoined, its noun being a latent (mustatir) pronoun implied as «هو»; and (من الخاسرين): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to its omitted khabar (predicate).
(فَبَعَثَ اللَّهُ غُراباً يَبْحَثُ فِي الْأَرْضِ): the fāʾ is a conjunction; (بعث) is a past verb, (الله) the agent and (غرابا) the direct object; the clause (يبحث في الأرض) is in the position of accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of «غرابا»; and (في الأرض), a preposition and its genitive noun, is attached to (يبحث).
(لِيُرِيَهُ كَيْفَ يُوارِي سَوْأَةَ أَخِيهِ): the lām is causal; (يريه) is an imperfect verb in the accusative by an implied «أن» after the causal lām, and the hāʾ is the direct object; (كيف) is an interrogative noun in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (بعث), so the latent pronoun in the verb refers to Allah; they may also be attached to (يبحث), i.e. it digs and stirs up the earth in order to show, so the latent pronoun refers to the raven. The interrogative clause suspends (muʿalliqa) the visual seeing, so it is in the position of accusative as a second object, standing in its place; because «رأى» of sight, before being made transitive by the hamza, takes one object, and by the hamza it acquired another object, which is the first object. Its like has come before in the saying of the Exalted:
«رب أرني كيف تحيي الموتى» (My Lord, show me how You give life to the dead).
(قالَ يا وَيْلَتى أَعَجَزْتُ أَنْ أَكُونَ مِثْلَ هذَا الْغُرابِ): the clause is resumptive, as though said as an answer to an implied question, as if it were asked: what did he say when he saw the raven doing that? (يا) is a vocative particle; (ويلتا) is a word of anguish and sorrow. He called it as though woe were not present with him, so he called it to come: "O woe, come, for this is the time for your coming."
You may also take the one addressed as omitted and make «الويل» accusative as a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb which the Arabs let fall out of use; the alif is a substitute for the yāʾ of the speaker; and the clause is the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl). The hamza is for interrogation and wonder, as though he wondered at himself:
how was he not guided to what the raven was guided to? (عجزت) is a verb and its agent, and the clause is included in the object of saying. (أن) is a maṣdar-forming and accusative-governing particle; (أكون) is a defective (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb, accusative by (أن); the interpreted maṣdar is accusative by removal of the preposition, the [implied] preposition and its genitive noun being attached to (عجزت), i.e. «أعجزت [عن]»; the noun of (أكون) is a latent pronoun implied as «أنا»; (مثل) is the khabar of (أكون); (هذا) is a demonstrative, the muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); and (الغراب) is a badal (substitute) of the demonstrative.
(فَأُوارِيَ سَوْأَةَ أَخِي فَأَصْبَحَ مِنَ النَّادِمِينَ): the fāʾ is a conjunction, and (أواري) is an imperfect verb conjoined to (أن أكون). This is preferable to making it causative (sababiyya) because it is preceded by an interrogative, [in which case] (أواري) would be an imperfect verb in the accusative by an implied «أن» after the causative fāʾ; for the fāʾ that occurs as the answer to an interrogative forms, from the interrogative clause and the answer, a condition and its consequence, and here that is not formed. You say: «أتزورني فأكرمك» (will you visit me so that I honour you?), meaning: «إن تزرني أكرمك» (if you visit me I will honour you). But if you said here: «إن أعجز عن أن أكون مثل هذا الغراب أوار سوءة أخي» (if I am unable to be like this raven, I will cover my brother's corpse), it would not be correct, because the covering does not result from his inability to be like the raven. For this reason we have considered the conjunction preferable. (سوءة أخي) is the direct object. In (فأصبح) the fāʾ is a conjunction; (أصبح) is a defective past verb, its noun a latent pronoun implied as «هو», and (من النادمين) its khabar.

* Rhetoric:
Figurative usage (majāz) in His saying «يا ويلتا», because he called upon something that does not reason, whereas the basis of the vocative is that it be addressed to one who reasons.

* Benefits:
This story which the Quran has presented is fit to be the kernel of a great story; it needs a creative pen to make of it a splendid work of art. It is reported that Ādam remained for a hundred years after the killing of Hābīl without laughing, and that he lamented him in poetry; this is a falsely attributed lie, for it is established that the prophets do not compose poetry. Maymūn ibn Mihrān reported from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said: whoever says that Ādam composed poetry has lied; rather he would mourn over him and describe his grief in prose speech resembling an elegy; then the centuries handed it down, and when it reached Yaʿrub ibn Qaḥṭān, who was the first to write in Arabic, he put it into verse and said:
تغيّرت البلاد ومن عليها ... فوجه الأرض مغير قبيح
(The lands and those upon them have changed; the face of the earth is dust-covered and ugly.)
They mentioned six verses after this one; and not content with that, they fabricated a report whose content is that Iblīs answered him in the same metre and rhyme with five verses. Al-Zamakhsharī said: «All of that is sheer lies, and the poetry is nothing but falsely attributed and full of grammatical errors.» Al-Zamakhsharī is pointing to the second verse, which is:
تغيّر كل ذي لون وطعم ... وقل بشاشة الوجه المليح
(Everything of colour and taste has changed, and the cheerfulness of the comely face has diminished.)
They transmitted it with iqwāʾ (a vowel fault in the rhyme), i.e. with «المليح» in the genitive. Some transmit it with «بشاشة» in the accusative without nunation and «الوجه المليح» in the nominative, and then it is not an error; they explained it as the dropping of the nunation from «بشاشة» and its being accusative as a tamyīz (specification). Our philosopher-poet Abū al-ʿAlāʾ al-Maʿarrī alluded to this story in Risālat al-Ghufrān; refer to it if you wish — and may Allah protect you. He singled out the Children of Israel with this story, as will come, because killing was their habit, even reaching the prophets.

dervis-irab:109-110.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الْأَكْمَهَ): the blind person whose sight is wiped out.

* I'rab:
(يَوْمَ يَجْمَعُ اللَّهُ الرُّسُلَ فَيَقُولُ: ماذا أُجِبْتُمْ): resumptive speech brought to set out what took place between Him and all the messengers. يوم is an adverb of time attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted [verb], its implied form being "remember" (اذكر); the clause يجمع is in the position of the genitive by construct (iḍāfa); الله is the fāʿil (agent); الرسل is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the fāʾ is a conjunction; يقول is an imperfect verb conjoined to يجمع; ماذا is an interrogative noun in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e. "with what answer were you answered?" You may also parse «ما» as an interrogative noun in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and «ذا» as a relative noun, the khabar (predicate) of «ما»; the clause أجبتم has no grammatical position in either case; similar cases have preceded. The clause ماذا أجبتم is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
(قالُوا: لا عِلْمَ لَنا إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ عَلَّامُ الْغُيُوبِ): قالوا is a verb and its agent, and the clause is resumptive; لا is the lā of generic negation; علم is its noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa; لنا is attached to its omitted khabar; the clause لا علم لنا is in the position of the accusative as the object of the saying; إن and its noun; أنت is a mubtadaʾ and علام الغيوب the khabar of أنت, and the clause is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of إن; and the clause إن and what is in its domain is causal (taʿlīliyya) with no grammatical position. (إِذْ قالَ اللَّهُ يا عِيسَى ابْنَ مَرْيَمَ): إذ is an adverb of past time, attached to what يوم is attached to, because it is a badal (substitute) from it; the clause قال is in the position of the genitive by construct; يا is a vocative particle; عيسى is a single proper-name vocative, indeclinable on an implied (muqaddar) ḍamma on the alif, in the position of the accusative; ابن is a badal from, or a naʿt (adjective) of, عيسى; and مريم is muḍāf ilayhi. (اذْكُرْ نِعْمَتِي عَلَيْكَ وَعَلى والِدَتِكَ): the whole clause is in the position of the accusative as the object of the saying; اذكر is an imperative verb; نعمتي is the direct object; عليك is attached to نعمتي; and على والدتك is conjoined to «عليك». (إِذْ أَيَّدْتُكَ بِرُوحِ الْقُدُسِ تُكَلِّمُ النَّاسَ فِي الْمَهْدِ وَكَهْلًا): the adverb is a badal of inclusion (badal ishtimāl) from نعمتي, and it may also be attached to نعمتي; the clause أيدتك is in the position of the genitive by construct; بروح القدس is attached to أيدتك; the clause تكلم الناس is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the kāf in أيدتك; في المهد is attached to an omitted ḥāl, i.e. while you were an infant; and كهلا is conjoined to it, so it too is a ḥāl. The meaning is: joining the state of infancy to the state of maturity in perfection of intellect and completeness of reflection. (وَإِذْ عَلَّمْتُكَ الْكِتابَ وَالْحِكْمَةَ وَالتَّوْراةَ وَالْإِنْجِيلَ): the wāw is a conjunction; the adverb is conjoined to إذ أيدتك; the clause علمتك is in the position of the genitive by construct, and it is a verb, its agent and its first direct object; الكتاب is a second direct object, i.e. writing; and what follows it is conjoined to it. (وَإِذْ تَخْلُقُ مِنَ الطِّينِ كَهَيْئَةِ الطَّيْرِ بِإِذْنِي): the adverb is conjoined to what preceded it; the clause تخلق is in the position of the genitive by construct; من الطين is attached to تخلق; كهيئة: the kāf is a noun in the sense of مثل ("like"), in the position of the accusative as the direct object of تخلق; هيئة is muḍāf ilayhi and is itself muḍāf; الطير is muḍāf ilayhi; and بإذني is attached to an omitted ḥāl. (فَتَنْفُخُ فِيها فَتَكُونُ طَيْراً بِإِذْنِي)
The fāʾ is a conjunction; تنفخ is conjoined to تخلق; فيها is attached to تنفخ; فتكون is conjoined to فتنفخ; طيرا is the khabar of تكون; and بإذني is attached to an omitted ḥāl. (وَتُبْرِئُ الْأَكْمَهَ وَالْأَبْرَصَ بِإِذْنِي): conjoined to what precedes. (وَإِذْ تُخْرِجُ الْمَوْتى بِإِذْنِي): likewise conjoined. (وَإِذْ كَفَفْتُ بَنِي إِسْرائِيلَ عَنْكَ): likewise conjoined; بني إسرائيل is the object of كففت; and عنك is attached to «كففت». (إِذْ جِئْتَهُمْ بِالْبَيِّناتِ فَقالَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مِنْهُمْ إِنْ هذا إِلَّا سِحْرٌ مُبِينٌ): the adverb is attached to كففت, not with regard to the coming with clear proofs alone, but with regard to what followed that and resulted from it, when they intended to kill him; the clause جئتهم is in the position of the genitive by construct; بالبينات is attached to جئتهم; فقال: the fāʾ is conjunctive, and قال is a past verb conjoined to جئتهم; الذين is the agent; the clause كفروا is the ṣila (relative clause); منهم is attached to كفروا; إن is negating; هذا is a demonstrative in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ; إلا is a particle of restriction; سحر is the khabar of هذا; مبين is a naʿt; and the clause is in the position of the accusative as the object of the saying.

dervis-irab:111-113.t:
* Vocabulary:
(مائِدَةً): al-māʾida is the table (khiwān) when there is food on it; if there is no food on it, it is not a māʾida. This is the well-known view, as al-Thaʿālibī stated; however, al-Rāghib said: al-māʾida is the tray on which there is food, and it is also said of the food itself. But this goes against what is well known and widely recognized among the scholars of language.
This matter has parallels in the language: a khiwān is not called māʾida unless there is food on it — otherwise it is a khiwān, with the khāʾ vowelled in three ways. One does not say kaʾs unless there is wine in it — otherwise it is a qadaḥ (cup). One does not say dhanūb or sajl unless there is water in it — otherwise it is a dalw (bucket). One does not say jirāb unless it is tanned — otherwise it is ihāb (raw hide). One does not say:
qalam unless it is sharpened — otherwise it is unbūb (a reed tube). One does not say kūz unless it has a handle — otherwise it is kūb. One does not say farw unless there is wool on it — otherwise it is its skin. One does not say rayṭa unless it is of two joined pieces — otherwise it is mulāʾa (a sheet). One does not say:
rumḥ unless it has a spearhead on it — otherwise it is qanāt (a shaft). One does not say laṭīma unless it carries perfume — otherwise it is ʿīr (a caravan). One does not say khātam unless it has a stone set in it — otherwise it is fatkha. This is what al-Thaʿālibī mentioned, transmitting from Abū ʿUbayda.
And it is transmitted from leading lexicographers other than Abū ʿUbayda: one does not say nafaq unless it has an exit — otherwise it is sarab (a burrow). One does not say ʿihn unless it is dyed — otherwise it is ṣūf (wool). One does not say khidr unless it encloses a young woman — otherwise it is sitr (a curtain). One does not say rakiyya unless there is water in it, little or much — otherwise it is biʾr (a well). One does not say waqūd unless fire has gone forward in it — otherwise it is ḥaṭab (firewood).
One does not say siyāʿ unless there is straw in it — otherwise it is ṭīn (clay). One does not say ʿawīl unless there is raising of the voice in it — otherwise it is bukāʾ (weeping). One does not say tharā unless it is moist — otherwise it is turāb (dust). One does not call a slave ābiq unless his going is without fear or toil of work — otherwise he is hārib (a fugitive). One does not call the water of the mouth ruḍāb except as long as it is in the mouth — otherwise it is buzāq (spittle). One does not call a brave man kamiyy unless he is fully armed — otherwise he is baṭal (a hero). And one does not call a woman ẓaʿīna except as long as she is riding in the howdah. Further, the lexicographers differed on the derivation of māʾida. Abū ʿUbayda said — and al-Zamakhsharī chose it — that it is fāʿila in the sense of mafʿūla, derived from مادة, i.e. "he gave him", and امتاده in the sense of "he asked him for a gift"; so it has the sense of mafʿūla, like «عيشة راضية» ("a pleasing [i.e. pleasant] life").

* I'rab:
(وَإِذْ أَوْحَيْتُ إِلَى الْحَوارِيِّينَ أَنْ آمِنُوا بِي وَبِرَسُولِي): the wāw is a conjunction, and the speech is conjoined to what precedes; the clause أوحيت is in the position of the genitive by construct (iḍāfa); أن is explicative, because it has come after something with the meaning of saying but not its letters; and the clause آمنوا has no grammatical position because it is explicative. (قالُوا آمَنَّا وَاشْهَدْ بِأَنَّنا مُسْلِمُونَ): the clause is resumptive; the clause آمنا is in the position of the accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); the bāʾ is a preposition, and أن and what is in its domain are interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the genitive by the bāʾ; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached (mutaʿalliq) to «اشهد»; and مسلمون is the khabar (predicate) of أنّ. (إِذْ قالَ الْحَوارِيُّونَ يا عِيسَى ابْنَ مَرْيَمَ): the clause is resumptive, recounting a past situation; the adverb is attached to an omitted [verb], its implied form being "remember" (اذكر); the clause قال is in the position of the genitive by construct; الحواريون is the fāʿil (agent); يا is a vocative particle; عيسى is a single proper-name vocative, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma; ابن is a badal (substitute) from «عيسى», following its form or its position, so the nūn may take ḍamma or fatḥa [Translator's note: so in the text; according to the rule set out in the Benefits below, the two options of ḍamma and fatḥa apply to the vocative noun itself, while ابن is accusative in either case.], as will come in the section on benefits; and مريم is muḍāf ilayhi. (هَلْ يَسْتَطِيعُ رَبُّكَ أَنْ يُنَزِّلَ عَلَيْنا مائِدَةً مِنَ السَّماءِ): the clause is in the position of the accusative as the object of the saying; هل is an interrogative particle; يستطيع ربك is an imperfect verb and its agent; أن ينزل: the maṣdariyya أن and what follows it are interpreted as a maṣdar, the object of يستطيع; مائدة is the object of ينزل; and من السماء is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ينزل, and there is no harm in their being attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of مائدة. (قالَ اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ مُؤْمِنِينَ): the clause is resumptive, brought to show what he said to them regarding their request. The clause اتقوا الله is in the position of the accusative as the object of the saying; إن is conditional; كان, its noun and its khabar; كان is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the apodosis is omitted, understood from the context, i.e. "if you believe in His power, the Exalted, and in the truth of my prophethood, then avoid these obstinate questions". (قالُوا: نُرِيدُ أَنْ نَأْكُلَ مِنْها وَتَطْمَئِنَّ قُلُوبُنا): the speech is resumptive, brought to show what they said as a justification [Translator's note: the text reads «تسويفا», apparently a misprint for «تسويغا» ("justification").] of their request; the clause نريد is in the position of the accusative as the object of the saying; أن and what is in its domain are an interpreted maṣdar, the object of نريد; منها is attached to نأكل; and تطمئن قلوبنا: the clause is conjoined to «أن نأكل منها». (وَنَعْلَمَ أَنْ قَدْ صَدَقْتَنا وَنَكُونَ عَلَيْها مِنَ الشَّاهِدِينَ): the wāw is conjunctive; نعلم is conjoined to نأكل and تطمئن — and that it be a proof for us before those of the Children of Israel who did not witness it, so that the believers may grow firmer in faith, doubt may vanish from the breasts of the doubters and waverers, and the disbelievers may believe. أن is lightened from the heavy [أنّ], its noun being the omitted pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), and the clause قد صدقتنا is its khabar; نكون is conjoined to نعلم; the noun of نكون is latent (mustatir), implied as "we" (نحن); من الشاهدين is attached to an omitted khabar of نكون; and عليها is attached to الشاهدين.

* Benefits:
If the one addressed (munādā) is a single proper name followed by «ابن» with nothing separating them, and «ابن» is in construct with a proper name, two options are permitted in the vocative: ḍamma, as indeclinable, and fatḥa, following the vowel of «ابن». ʿAmr ibn Kulthūm said:
بأي مشيئة عمرو بن هند ... تطيع بنا الوشاة وتزدرينا
(By what will, O ʿAmr son of Hind, do you obey the slanderers against us and scorn us?)

dervis-irab:63-64.t:
* I'rab:
(لَوْلا يَنْهاهُمُ الرَّبَّانِيُّونَ وَالْأَحْبارُ عَنْ قَوْلِهِمُ الْإِثْمَ وَأَكْلِهِمُ السُّحْتَ): resumptive speech, brought to urge and to put fear into the scholars and rabbis among them for their turning away from enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong. In it there is a generalisation of the rebuke to the scholars of every nation and creed for this shameful trait. For this reason Ibn ʿAbbās said: "This is the severest verse in the Qur'an", meaning with respect to the scholars, for their negligence in forbidding evils. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: "There is no verse in the Qur'an more fearsome to me than it." لولا is a particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ) meaning «هلّا» ("why not"); ينهاهم الربانيون is an imperfect verb, its mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and its fāʿil (agent); الأحبار is conjoined to His saying «الربانيون»; عن قولهم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ينهاهم; الإثم is the mafʿūl bihi of «قول»; أكلهم is conjoined to قولهم; and السحت is the mafʿūl bihi of أكل. (لَبِئْسَ ما كانُوا يَصْنَعُونَ): its i'rab has preceded shortly before. One does not say صنع ("craft") of a deed unless it has become a habit and a custom. (وَقالَتِ الْيَهُودُ: يَدُ اللَّهِ مَغْلُولَةٌ): the wāw is resumptive; قالت اليهود is a verb and its fāʿil; يد الله is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and مغلولة the khabar (predicate); and the clause is in the position of an accusative as the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl). (غُلَّتْ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَلُعِنُوا بِما قالُوا): the clause is an imprecation and parenthetical; غلت is a passive past verb and أيديهم the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); and لعنوا is conjoined to غلت أيديهم. (بَلْ يَداهُ مَبْسُوطَتانِ يُنْفِقُ كَيْفَ يَشاءُ): بل is a particle of digression (iḍrāb) and conjunction; يداه is a mubtadaʾ and مبسوطتان the khabar; and the clause is conjoined to the clause يد الله مغلولة. The clause ينفق may be resumptive, brought to emphasise the perfection of His generosity, glorified is He; the meaning is: His spending is according to what His will requires, for He is the One who withholds and the One who extends. I do not know how they permitted it to be a second khabar of «يداه», following Abū Ḥayyān. كيف here is conditional, in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). (وَلَيَزِيدَنَّ كَثِيراً مِنْهُمْ ما أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْكَ مِنْ رَبِّكَ طُغْياناً وَكُفْراً): the wāw is the wāw of the omitted oath, and the omitted [thing sworn by] is genitive by the wāw [Translator's note: the source says «والقسم المحذوف مجرور بالواو», "and the omitted oath is genitive by the wāw", meaning the omitted noun sworn by]; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to something omitted, its implied form being "I swear". The lām occurs in the answer to the oath; يزيدن is an imperfect verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa because it is joined to the heavy nūn of emphasis, and the clause has no grammatical position because it is the answer to the oath. كثيرا is a mafʿūl bihi; منهم is attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective); ما is a relative noun, the fāʿil of يزيدن — what is meant is that they increase in rancour and in persistence in denial; the clause أنزل has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause); إليك is attached to أنزل; من ربك is attached to an omitted ḥāl; طغيانا is a tamyīz (specification) or the second mafʿūl bihi of يزيدن; and كفرا is conjoined to «طغيانا». (وَأَلْقَيْنا بَيْنَهُمُ الْعَداوَةَ وَالْبَغْضاءَ إِلى يَوْمِ الْقِيامَةِ): the wāw is resumptive; ألقينا is a verb and its fāʿil; بينهم is an adverb attached to ألقينا; العداوة is a mafʿūl bihi and البغضاء is conjoined to العداوة; and إلى يوم القيامة is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl. (كُلَّما أَوْقَدُوا ناراً لِلْحَرْبِ أَطْفَأَهَا اللَّهُ): كلما is accusative as an adverb of time, and the clause is in the position of a genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); نارا is a mafʿūl bihi; للحرب is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أوقدوا; the clause أطفأها الله has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition; and the whole clause is also resumptive. (وَيَسْعَوْنَ فِي الْأَرْضِ فَساداً): the wāw is resumptive; يسعون is an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; في الأرض is attached to يسعون; فسادا may be a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), it may be a ḥāl meaning "corrupting", or a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), i.e. "they strive for the sake of corruption". The three views are equally weighty. (وَاللَّهُ لا يُحِبُّ الْمُفْسِدِينَ): the wāw is resumptive; الله is a mubtadaʾ, the clause لا يحب is the khabar, and المفسدين is a mafʿūl bihi.

* Rhetoric:
This verse is full of kinds of rhetoric, which we summarise below:
1- al-majāz al-mursal (non-metaphorical figurative usage) in the fettering of the hand and its extending, for stinginess and generosity. The relation of this majāz is causality, because the hand is the cause of spending; and the benefit of this majāz is depicting the reality in a sensory image that usually accompanies it. Some made His saying «بل يداه مبسوطتان» a metaphor (istiʿāra): the thing borrowed is the extending, that from which it is borrowed is the hand of the spender, and that for which it is borrowed is the hand of the Real (al-Ḥaqq) — so that the hearer imagines that there are two hands extended in spending, while in reality there are no hands and no extending.
The effect of the sense of sight: that is because sensory depiction makes it more firmly fixed in the mind and more effective. The sense of sight is foremost among the senses that appreciate beauty, perceive it and convey it to the soul. In this regard «Guyau» [Translator's note: the source writes «جوير»; presumably the French thinker Jean-Marie Guyau], the well-known modern critic, says: The sensations that most fully deserve to be described as beautiful are visual sensations. Indeed «Descartes», the French philosopher, went further than that and defined beauty by saying: It is what pleases the eye. Since generosity and stinginess are abstract and not perceived by the senses, and are accompanied by two images that are perceived by the senses — the extending of the hand for generosity and its fettering for stinginess — they were expressed by what accompanies them, for the benefit of clarification and of moving from abstractions to sensibles.
2- al-mushākala (resemblance of expression): in His saying «غلت أيديهم» ("their hands are fettered"), for He invoked against them the very thing they had falsely alleged and spread rumours about. Hence the Jews became the stingiest of Allah's creation absolutely, and the most given to amassing wealth from whatever source it came. The Arabs used to avoid this blameworthy description and refrain from it; al-Ashtar said:
بقّيت وفري وانحرفت عن العلا ... ولقيت أضيافي بوجه عبوس
(May I keep my wealth and turn away from lofty deeds, and meet my guests with a frowning face.) [Translator's note: the line is an oath-imprecation on the poet himself, i.e. may this befall me if I do not do what he swears to do.]
Most of Ahl al-Sunna held that the Hand of Allah is one of the attributes of His essence, glorified is He, like hearing, sight and the Face; so we must believe in it and affirm it of Him without asking how and without likening.
3- al-tankīt (pointed subtlety): in His saying «بل يداه مبسوطتان» ("rather, His two hands are extended"). The context required Him to say: يده مبسوطة ("His hand is extended"), for they expressed it in the singular by saying: «يد الله مغلولة»; but He departed from correspondence for a subtle point too fine for primitive understandings: the negation of corporeality from Him, glorified is He. For they meant that He gives with His hand, whereas a man does not give with both his hands; so He answered them, invalidating that He has anything of a known body, with a right hand and a left hand. When He affirmed that both are a hand, He negated corporeality, because both of them are equal in generosity and giving.
4- al-kināya (metonymy): in kindling war, for war and its flaring up.
5- al-ṭibāq (antithesis): between kindling and extinguishing.

dervis-irab:65-65.t:
* I'rab:
(وَلَوْ أَنَّ أَهْلَ الْكِتابِ آمَنُوا وَاتَّقَوْا): the wāw is resumptive, and the speech is resumptive, brought to show their state in the Hereafter. لو is a non-jussive conditional particle; أنّ with its noun and its khabar (predicate) is in the position of a nominative as the fāʿil (agent) of an omitted verb — this has been discussed before. The clause آمنوا is the khabar of «أن», and the clause اتقوا is conjoined to the clause آمنوا. (لَكَفَّرْنا عَنْهُمْ سَيِّئاتِهِمْ وَلَأَدْخَلْناهُمْ جَنَّاتِ النَّعِيمِ): the lām occurs in the apodosis of «لو»; كفرنا is a verb and its fāʿil, and the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition; عنهم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) كفرنا; سيئاتهم is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and the clause ولأدخلناهم is conjoined to the clause لكفرنا. جنات is a second mafʿūl bihi by extension of usage (ʿalā al-saʿa), or accusative by removal of the preposition (manṣūb bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ), the preposition and its genitive noun being attached to أدخلناهم; and النعيم is a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

dervis-irab:66-66.t:
* I'rab:
(وَلَوْ أَنَّهُمْ أَقامُوا التَّوْراةَ وَالْإِنْجِيلَ وَما أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْهِمْ مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ): the wāw is resumptive; أنهم أقاموا التوراة والإنجيل: its i'rab has preceded shortly before. ما is conjoined to التوراة and الإنجيل, and the clause أنزل is the ṣila (relative clause); by the relative noun He meant other Books besides the two, such as the Book of Isaiah, the Book of Daniel and the Psalms of David. إليهم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) أنزل, and من ربهم is attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). (لَأَكَلُوا مِنْ فَوْقِهِمْ وَمِنْ تَحْتِ أَرْجُلِهِمْ): the lām occurs in the apodosis of لو; the clause أكلوا has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition; من فوقهم is attached to أكلوا, and من تحت أرجلهم is conjoined to «من فوقهم». The secret of the omission of the object will come in the section on Rhetoric. (مِنْهُمْ أُمَّةٌ مُقْتَصِدَةٌ وَكَثِيرٌ مِنْهُمْ ساءَ ما يَعْمَلُونَ): the clause is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl; منهم is attached to an omitted, fronted khabar (predicate); أمة is a delayed mubtadaʾ (subject), and مقتصدة a naʿt (adjective). In وكثير the wāw is conjunctive; كثير is a mubtadaʾ, and beginning with it was permissible because it is qualified by the preposition and its genitive noun; the clause ساء ما يعملون is the khabar of كثير; and the clause يعملون is the ṣila of «ما».

* Rhetoric:
In this verse there are two eloquent omissions, falling within the domain of majāz (figurative usage), which is the element and elixir of eloquence. They are:
1- The omission of the muḍāf in His saying: «أقاموا التوراة والإنجيل»; what is meant is the rulings of the Torah and the Gospel and their limits, and the far-reaching rulings and widespread lessons contained in them.
2- The omission of the mafʿūl bihi (direct object), whose subtleties are ever renewed. The saying of the Exalted: «لأكلوا من فوقهم ومن تحت أرجلهم» reaches the furthest limits of eloquence: the object of «أكلوا» is omitted with the intent of generality, or with the intent of the act itself, as in their saying: "So-and-so loosens and binds, ratifies and annuls, harms and benefits". The basis in all of this is affirming the meaning intended in your mind for the thing absolutely. In the omission under discussion there are three views:
a- That He would pour upon them the blessings of the heaven and the blessings of the earth.
b- That He would multiply fruit-bearing trees and productive crops.
c- That He would provide them with gardens of ripe fruit, from which they would pick what hangs down from the tops of the trees and gather what has fallen to the ground beneath their feet.

dervis-irab:67-67.t:
* I'rab:
(يا أَيُّهَا الرَّسُولُ): its i'rab has preceded. (بَلِّغْ ما أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْكَ مِنْ رَبِّكَ): resumptive speech, brought to console the Prophet ﷺ when he felt distressed by the call. بلغ is an imperative verb and its fāʿil (agent) is "you"; ما is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause أنزل is the ṣila (relative clause); إليك is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) أنزل; and من ربك is attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). (وَإِنْ لَمْ تَفْعَلْ فَما بَلَّغْتَ رِسالَتَهُ): the wāw is resumptive; إن is conditional; لم تفعل is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the fāʾ links the apodosis; ما is negative; and the clause بلغت is in the position of a jussive (majzūm) as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). In the identity of protasis and apodosis there is a wonderful secret, which we shall set out in the section on Rhetoric. رسالته is a mafʿūl bihi. (وَاللَّهُ يَعْصِمُكَ مِنَ النَّاسِ): the wāw is resumptive; الله is a mubtadaʾ (subject), the clause يعصمك is its khabar (predicate), and من الناس is attached to يعصمك. (إِنَّ اللَّهَ لا يَهْدِي الْقَوْمَ الْكافِرِينَ): inna and its noun; the clause لا يهدي is its khabar; القوم is a mafʿūl bihi, and الظالمين is a naʿt (adjective) [Translator's note: so in the source; the word in this verse is الكافرين].

* Rhetoric:
In the identity of protasis and apodosis there is a secret without equal. That is because the consequence must differ from the condition for a benefit to be obtained; when they are identical the speech becomes defective, because outwardly it comes down to: "and if you do not do, then you have not done". But here He intended them to be identical, because not conveying the message is a matter known to people and settled in minds as something enormous and hideous for which its perpetrator is condemned; and because a scholar's failure to spread knowledge is something that deserves blame — so what then of the Message? So He made the consequence the very same as the condition, so that the extent of the concern for conveying would become clear. It has also been said in this regard: i.e. if you leave out anything, you have left out everything, and what you have conveyed becomes of no account; so the meaning becomes: and if you do not fully convey what you were commanded to convey, your ruling in disobedience and non-compliance is the ruling of one who has conveyed nothing at all.

dervis-irab:68-68.t:
* I'rab:
(قُلْ يا أَهْلَ الْكِتابِ لَسْتُمْ عَلى شَيْءٍ): resumptive speech, brought to negate their false conjectures that they follow the Torah. قل is an imperative verb; يا أهل الكتاب is a vocative in genitive construct (munādā muḍāf); لستم is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb, the tāʾ is its noun, and على شيء is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) its omitted khabar (predicate). More about ليس will come in the section on Benefits. (حَتَّى تُقِيمُوا التَّوْراةَ وَالْإِنْجِيلَ وَما أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْكُمْ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ): حتى is a particle of limit and a preposition; تقيموا is an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after حتى; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «لستم»; التوراة is the object of تقيموا, and a muḍāf must be supplied, i.e. "their rulings and the lofty ideals they contain". (وَلَيَزِيدَنَّ كَثِيراً مِنْهُمْ ما أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْكَ مِنْ رَبِّكَ طُغْياناً وَكُفْراً): the wāw is resumptive and the lām is in answer to an omitted oath; يزيدن is an imperfect verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa because it is joined to the heavy nūn of emphasis, and the clause has no grammatical position because it is the answer to the oath; كثيرا is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); منهم is attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of «كثيرا»; ما is a relative noun, the fāʿil (agent) of يزيدن; من ربك is attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); طغيانا is a second mafʿūl bihi or a tamyīz (specification); and كفرا is conjoined to طغيانا. (فَلا تَأْسَ عَلَى الْقَوْمِ الْكافِرِينَ): the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (implying an omitted condition), i.e. "if you know this, then do not grieve"; لا is prohibitive; تأس is an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by لا, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the weak letter; على القوم is attached to تأس; and الكافرين is a naʿt.

* Rhetoric:
The tanwīn in «شيء» conveys paucity and disparagement, i.e. "you stand on nothing worth counting until you uphold the rulings of the Torah and the Gospel".

* Benefits:
(لَسْتُمْ): the middle radical of «ليس», the yāʾ, was dropped because of the meeting of two vowelless letters, i.e. the yāʾ and the sīn. Its original form is لَيِسَ with kasra on the yāʾ; then the yāʾ was made vowelless for lightness, and the fāʾ was not changed as analogy would require [Translator's note: so in the source, «ولم تقلب الفاء»; what is meant is that the yāʾ was not changed into an alif], because lightening by making vowelless is easier in an inflexible (jāmid) word than changing the letter. When it was joined to a vowelled nominative pronoun, the final radical [Translator's note: the source says «العين», the middle radical; the letter made vowelless is the sīn, the final radical] was made vowelless, so two vowelless letters met, the yāʾ and the sīn, and the yāʾ was dropped because of the meeting of the two vowelless letters.

dervis-irab:69-69.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الصَّابِئُونَ): from صبأ, i.e. he left his religion. They were a people who worshipped the stars, whose seat was in Ḥarrān in Mesopotamia; from them came scholars, philosophers and astrologers, among them the secretary and poet Abū Isḥāq al-Ṣābiʾ.

* I'rab:
(إِنَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَالَّذِينَ هادُوا): resumptive speech, brought to set out those who believe in Allah and do righteous deeds. inna and its noun; the clause آمنوا is the ṣila (relative clause); and الذين هادوا is conjoined to الذين آمنوا. (وَالصَّابِئُونَ وَالنَّصارى مَنْ آمَنَ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ وَعَمِلَ صالِحاً): the wāw is resumptive; الصابئون is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), its khabar (predicate) is omitted, and it is intended to come after what is in the scope of «إنّ», its noun and its khabar, as though it were said: "Those who believe, those who are Jews and the Christians — their ruling is such-and-such, and the Sabians likewise." This is what Sībawayh preferred regarding the departure from the expected case, and he cited as evidence for it:
وإلّا فاعلموا أنّا وأنتم ... بغاة ما بقينا على شقاق
(Otherwise, know that we — and you — are transgressors as long as we remain in discord.)
i.e. "know that we are transgressors, and you likewise". The conjunction is then of the type of conjoining clauses: الصابئون with its omitted khabar is a clause conjoined to the clause of His saying إن الذين آمنوا, and it has no grammatical position, just as the clause to which it is conjoined has none. «الصابئون» was put forward only to draw attention to the fact that these are deeper in error and further gone in straying, because they were stripped of every creed. Other views on this departure in case will come in the section on Benefits. النصارى is conjoined to الذين, and من is a relative noun, a badal (substitute) for الذين. You may also parse النصارى as a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is «فلا خوف عليهم», with the clause the khabar of «إن» [Translator's note: so in the source; the sense of this alternative is unclear as printed]. The clause آمن بالله is the ṣila; اليوم الآخر is conjoined to الله; عمل is conjoined to آمن; and صالحا is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), or a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e. "a righteous deed". (فَلا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلا هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ): the clause is the khabar of إنّ, and the fāʾ entered because of the hint of condition in the relative noun; خوف is a mubtadaʾ, and beginning with it was permissible because the negation precedes it; عليهم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) its omitted khabar; and ولا هم يحزنون is conjoined to what precedes.

* Benefits:
We have given the preferred view, held by al-Khalīl, Sībawayh and the grammarians of Basra, on the i'rab of «والصابئون». There are other views, which we set out briefly below:
a- The wāw is conjunctive, and الصابئون is conjoined to the position of the noun of إنّ, because before «إنّ» entered it was in the position of a nominative. This is the school of al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ.
b- It is nominative, conjoined to the nominative pronoun in «هادوا»; this is reported from al-Kisāʾī.
c- That «إنّ» means نعم ("yes"), i.e. a particle of reply, and what follows it is nominative as mubtadaʾ, so «والصابئون» is conjoined to what precedes it.

What Ibn Hishām says:
Ibn Hishām's account of the verse comes down to two things:
a- The khabar of «إنّ» is omitted, i.e. "rewarded" or "safe" or "joyful", and الصابئون is a mubtadaʾ with what follows it as its khabar. Evidence for it is the saying:
خليليّ هل طبّ فإني وأنتما ... وإن لم تبوحا بالهوى نفان
(My two friends, is there any cure? For I and you two, even if you do not disclose your love, are [wasted with love].) [Translator's note: the last word is printed «نفان» in the source; the verse is usually cited with «دنفان», "two wasted with love".]
It is weakened by the fact that the omission is from the first because the second indicates it, whereas what is common is the reverse.
b- The khabar mentioned is that of «إنّ», and the khabar of «الصابئون» is omitted. Evidence for it is the saying:
فمن يك أمسى بالمدينة رحله ... فإني وقيار بها لغريب
(Whoever has his lodging in Madīna by evening — I, and Qayyār, am a stranger there.)
since the lām does not enter the khabar of a mubtadaʾ unless it is fronted, as in: القائم لزيد [Translator's note: so in the source]. It is weakened by putting the conjoined clause before part of the clause to which it is conjoined.

dervis-irab:114-115.t:
* Vocabulary:
(عِيداً): al-ʿīd (festival) is well known. It is derived from al-ʿawd (returning), because it returns [Translator's note: the text has «يعول», evidently a misprint for «يعود».] every year. Its first radical has kasra only because the wāw came after a kasra; the original form is:
عويد, just as ميزان was originally موزان, and the wāw was changed to yāʾ because it came after a kasra.

* I'rab:
(قالَ عِيسَى ابْنُ مَرْيَمَ): resumptive speech brought for his beginning the supplication after their sincerity had become clear to him. قال عيسى is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); ابن is a badal (substitute) or naʿt (adjective); and مريم is muḍāf ilayhi. (اللَّهُمَّ رَبَّنا أَنْزِلْ عَلَيْنا مائِدَةً مِنَ السَّماءِ): اللهم was originally يا الله; the vocative particle was dropped and the doubled mīm was substituted for it — this has been discussed before. ربنا is a second vocative; أنزل is an imperative verb for supplication, and its agent is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, implied as "You" (أنت); علينا is attached (mutaʿalliq) to أنزل; مائدة is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and من السماء is attached to an omitted adjective of مائدة, or is also attached to أنزل.
(تَكُونُ لَنا عِيداً لِأَوَّلِنا وَآخِرِنا وَآيَةً مِنْكَ): the clause تكون is a second adjective of مائدة, i.e. the day of its descent will be a festival; the noun of تكون is latent, implied as "it" (هي); عيدا is the khabar (predicate) of تكون; لنا is attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), because it was originally an adjective placed before the thing it describes, namely His word «عيدا»; لأولنا: the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted badal from «لنا», with repetition of the governing element; آخرنا is conjoined to «أولنا»; آية is conjoined to «عيدا»; and منك is attached to an omitted adjective of آية. (وَارْزُقْنا وَأَنْتَ خَيْرُ الرَّازِقِينَ): the wāw is a conjunction; ارزقنا is an imperative verb for supplication, its agent latent, and نا is an attached pronoun in the position of the accusative as direct object; the wāw is resumptive or circumstantial; أنت is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and خير الرازقين the khabar; and the clause has no grammatical position because it is resumptive, or is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl. (قالَ اللَّهُ: إِنِّي مُنَزِّلُها عَلَيْكُمْ): resumptive speech brought to show Allah's answering of his supplication. إني and what is in its domain are in the position of the accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); إن and its noun; منزلها is the khabar; and عليكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to منزلها, because it is an active participle. (فَمَنْ يَكْفُرْ بَعْدُ مِنْكُمْ): the fāʾ is resumptive; من is a jussive conditional noun and a mubtadaʾ; يكفر is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); بعد is an adverb cut off from construct in wording but not in meaning, so it is indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma, and it is attached to يكفر; and منكم is attached to an omitted ḥāl. (فَإِنِّي أُعَذِّبُهُ عَذاباً لا أُعَذِّبُهُ أَحَداً مِنَ الْعالَمِينَ): the fāʾ links the apodosis; إن and its noun; the clause أعذبه is its khabar; the clause إني أعذبه is in the position of the jussive (majzūm) as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); عذابا is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), being a noun of the maṣdar (ism maṣdar) in the sense of التعذيب; لا is negating; أعذبه is an imperfect verb, and the pronoun in the second «أعذبه» stands in for the absolute object because it refers back to it — the implied sense being "I will punish him with a punishment such that I will not punish anyone with the like of that punishment"; أحدا is the direct object; the negated clause is an adjective of «عذابا»; and من العالمين is attached to an omitted adjective of «أحدا».
The clause of the protasis and its apodosis is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ «من».

* Benefits:
Thirteen things stand in for the maṣdar (verbal noun) and are given its ruling. They are:
1- The noun of the maṣdar (ism al-maṣdar): أعطيتك عطاء ("I gave you a gift").
2- Its adjective: «اذكروا الله كثيرا».
3- Its pronoun referring back to it: as in the preceding verse.
4- Its synonym: فرح جذلا ("he rejoiced with glee").
5- A maṣdar that meets it in derivation: «أنبتكم نباتا».
6- What indicates its kind: رجع القهقرى ("he went back walking backwards"), and the words of al-Aʿshā:
غراء فرعاء مصقول عوارضها ... تمشي الهويني كما يمشي الوجي الوحل
(Fair-faced, long-haired, her teeth polished, she walks slowly, as one with sore hooves walks in mud.)
7- What indicates its instrument: ضربت اللص سوطا ("I struck the thief with a whip").
8- Interrogative أيّ, and interrogative or predicative كم, as in: «وسيعلم الذين ظلموا أيّ منقلب ينقلبون», and the words of al-Mutanabbī: كم قد قتلت وكم قد متّ عندكم ... ثم انتفضت فزال القبر والكفن (How often have I been slain, and how often have I died among you; then I shook myself, and the grave and the shroud were gone!)
9- What indicates its number: «فاجلدوا كلّ واحد منهما مئة جلدة».
10- The conditionals ما, مهما and أي: ما تفعل أفعل ("whatever you do, I do"), مهما تقف أقف ("however you stand, I stand"), and أي عمل تعمله تجاز عليه ("whatever deed you do, you will be requited for it").
11- The words كل and بعض in construct with the maṣdar: «فلا تميلوا كل الميل», and اجتهد بعض الاجتهاد ("he strove somewhat").
12- The demonstrative, pointing to the maṣdar: اجتهدت ذلك الاجتهاد ("I strove with that striving").
13- The أيّ of perfection (al-kamāliyya): that which indicates the meaning of perfection when it occurs in construct with the maṣdar, as in اجتهدت أي اجتهاد ("I strove with what a striving!"). When it occurs after an indefinite noun it is an adjective of it, as in the words of Abū al-ʿAtāhiya:
إنّ الشّباب والفراغ والجده ... مفسدة للمرء أيّ مفسده
(Youth, leisure and wealth are a corruption for a man — what a corruption!)
So «أي» is an adjective of «مفسدة». And when it occurs after a definite noun it is a ḥāl, as in: مررت بعبد الله أيّ رجل ("I passed by ʿAbdallāh — what a man!").

dervis-irab:32-32.t:
* Vocabulary:
(أَجْلِ): «الأجل», with sukūn on the jīm, is a maṣdar (verbal noun). One says «أجل عليهم شرا», i.e. he committed evil against them and stirred it up; then it came to be used for crimes, as in their saying «من جراك فعلته» (I did it on your account), i.e. "from the fact that I committed it [for you]," i.e. I perpetrated it; then its use was broadened, and it came to be used for every [expression of] cause.

* I'rab:
(مِنْ أَجْلِ ذلِكَ كَتَبْنا عَلى بَنِي إِسْرائِيلَ): the clause is resumptive; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (كتبنا), and (على بني إسرائيل), a preposition and its genitive noun, is also attached to (كتبنا); i.e. We legislated retaliation (qiṣāṣ) upon the killer, so that the legitimacy of retaliation would be a fixed ruling in all nations. He singled out the Children of Israel only — as we mentioned just now — because killing was the habit and custom of the Children of Israel, to the point that they ventured to kill prophets and messengers; because the purpose is to console the Prophet ﷺ and comfort him on account of their attempts to assassinate him and his Companions.
(أَنَّهُ مَنْ قَتَلَ نَفْساً بِغَيْرِ نَفْسٍ أَوْ فَسادٍ فِي الْأَرْضِ): (أن) and what falls within its scope is interpreted as a maṣdar, the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of (كتبنا). The hāʾ is the noun of (أنّ), and it is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn). (من) is a jussive-governing conditional noun, a mubtadaʾ (subject); (قتل) is a past verb in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); (نفسا) is the direct object; (بغير نفس), a preposition and its genitive noun, is attached to (قتل), or to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent pronoun in «قتل», i.e. "he killed it wrongfully"; (أو) is a conjunction; (فساد) is conjoined to (نفس), which is genitive by the annexation of (غير) to it; and (في الأرض) is attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of (فساد).
(فَكَأَنَّما قَتَلَ النَّاسَ جَمِيعاً): the fāʾ links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (كأنما) is [kaʾanna] with the restraining «ما» (kāffa wa-makfūfa); (قتل الناس) is a past verb, a latent (mustatir) agent and the direct object; (جميعا) is a ḥāl; the clause joined with the fāʾ is in the position of jussive as the apodosis; the protasis and its apodosis form the khabar (predicate) of «من»; and the conditional clause is in the position of nominative as the khabar of «أنه».
(وَمَنْ أَحْياها فَكَأَنَّما أَحْيَا النَّاسَ جَمِيعاً): the parsing of its like has been given.
(وَلَقَدْ جاءَتْهُمْ رُسُلُنا بِالْبَيِّناتِ): the wāw is a conjunction; the lām occurs in the answer to an omitted oath; (قد) is a particle of affirmation (taḥqīq); the clause (قد جاءتهم):
has no grammatical position because it is the answer to the oath; (رسلنا) is the fāʿil (agent); and (بالبينات) is attached to (جاءتهم).
(ثُمَّ إِنَّ كَثِيراً مِنْهُمْ بَعْدَ ذلِكَ فِي الْأَرْضِ لَمُسْرِفُونَ): (ثم) is a conjunction for sequence with delay; (إن) with its noun; (منهم) is attached to an omitted adjective of «كثيرا»; the adverb is attached to an omitted ḥāl; (ذلك) is a demonstrative in the position of genitive by annexation; (في الأرض), a preposition and its genitive noun, is attached to «مسرفون»; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); and (مسرفون) is the khabar of «إن».

* Rhetoric:
Representative simile (tashbīh tamthīlī): the basis of the simile is that the two acts of killing share in violating the sanctity of blood, in audacity against Allah, and in encouraging people to kill. The point of the simile is to make the matter of killing appear dreadful and to magnify the matter of saving life, by depicting each of them in an image befitting it.

dervis-irab:33-34.t:
* I'rab:
(إِنَّما جَزاءُ الَّذِينَ يُحارِبُونَ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ): resumptive speech introduced to set out the ruling of Allah concerning every highway robber, whether unbeliever or Muslim, because waging war on the Muslims is in the ruling of waging war on Allah and His Messenger. It was originally revealed concerning the ʿUranīs.
(إنما) is [inna] with the restraining «ما» (kāffa wa-makfūfa); (جزاء) is a mubtadaʾ (subject); (الذين) is the muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause (يحاربون) is the ṣila (relative clause); (الله) is its object; and (رسوله) is conjoined to (الله).
(وَيَسْعَوْنَ فِي الْأَرْضِ فَساداً): (يسعون) is conjoined to (يحاربون); (في الأرض), a preposition and its genitive noun, is attached to (يسعون). (فسادا) may properly be a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), i.e. they wage war and strive for the sake of corruption, the conditions for the accusative being met. It may also be a maṣdar (verbal noun) standing in the place of a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "and they strive in the land as corrupters," or "possessed of corruption"; they were made corruption itself, by way of hyperbole.
It may also be accusative as a maṣdar, i.e. it is a kind of the governing verb before it, because «يسعون في الأرض» really means «يفسدون» (they corrupt); so (فسادا) is a noun of the maṣdar (ism maṣdar) standing in place of «الإفساد», the implied form being: "they corrupt in the land by their striving, a corrupting."
(أَنْ يُقَتَّلُوا أَوْ يُصَلَّبُوا أَوْ تُقَطَّعَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَأَرْجُلُهُمْ مِنْ خِلافٍ أَوْ يُنْفَوْا مِنَ الْأَرْضِ): the interpreted maṣdar from (أن) and what falls within its scope is the khabar (predicate) of (جزاء). (أو) is a conjunction; (يصلبوا) is conjoined to (يقتلوا); (أو) is a conjunction; (تقطع) is also conjoined to (يقتلوا). (أيديهم) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of (تقطع); (أرجلهم) is conjoined to (أيديهم); and (من خلاف) is attached to an omitted ḥāl from (أيديهم) and (أرجلهم), i.e. "cut off alternately," meaning that his right hand and his left foot are cut off.
(ينفوا) is also conjoined, and (من الأرض) is attached to (ينفوا).
(ذلِكَ لَهُمْ خِزْيٌ فِي الدُّنْيا): the clause is resumptive, setting out the purpose of these punishments. The demonstrative is in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ; (لهم), a preposition and its genitive noun, is attached to an omitted fronted khabar; (خزي) is the delayed mubtadaʾ; (في الدنيا) is attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of (خزي); and the nominal clause is the khabar of the demonstrative. «خزي» may also be parsed as the khabar of «ذلك», with (لهم) attached to an omitted [element] in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from (خزي), because it was originally its adjective, and when it was placed before it, it became a ḥāl.
(وَلَهُمْ فِي الْآخِرَةِ عَذابٌ عَظِيمٌ): the wāw is a conjunction; (لهم) is attached to an omitted fronted khabar; (في الآخرة) is attached to an omitted ḥāl; (عذاب) is the delayed mubtadaʾ; and (عظيم) is an adjective.
(إِلَّا الَّذِينَ تابُوا مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ تَقْدِرُوا عَلَيْهِمْ): the clause of exception is accusative as a ḥāl from those being punished «[Translator's note: so in the text; the usual parsing is that (الذين) is accusative as the excepted (mustathnā)]»; (إلا) is a particle of exception; (الذين) is the excepted; the clause (تابوا) is the ṣila; (من قبل) is attached to (تابوا), «قبل» being made genitive with kasra because of annexation; (أن تقدروا) is an interpreted maṣdar in the position of genitive by annexation; and (عليهم), a preposition and its genitive noun, is attached to (تقدروا).
(فَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ): the fāʾ is resumptive; (اعلموا) is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, the wāw being the fāʿil (agent); and (أن) with its noun and its two predicates stands in place of the two objects of «اعلموا».

* Benefits:
«أو» is a conjunction with meanings which the author of al-Mughnī brought to twelve; we content ourselves with the following principal meanings: 1- Doubt: to make the hearer doubt about a matter the speaker intends, so he leaves it vague to him while he himself knows it. From it is the saying of the Exalted: «وأرسلناه إلى مائة ألف أو يزيدون» (And We sent him to a hundred thousand or more).
2- Choice (takhyīr): as in "take a garment or ten dirhams." Allah the Exalted said:
«فكفارته إطعام عشرة مساكين من أوسط ما تطعمون أهليكم أو كسوتهم أو تحرير رقبة» (its expiation is feeding ten poor persons from the average of what you feed your families, or clothing them, or freeing a slave). He made one of these three obligatory, and the reins of choice are in the hand of the one charged; whichever of them he does, he has expiated and discharged the obligation, and he is not required to combine them.
3- Permission (ibāḥa): "sit with so-and-so or so-and-so"; and the saying of the Exalted: «ولا تطع منهم آثما أو كفورا» (and do not obey from among them a sinner or an ingrate).
4- Division and diversification, as in the verse, i.e. dividing their punishment in a division distributed according to their situations and crimes. Al-Shāfiʿī said: «أو» throughout the Quran is for choice, except in this verse.
2- «[Translator's note: so numbered in the text; this is a second benefit after the four meanings of «أو».]» The interpreters differed on the meaning of the banishment (nafy) which Allah the Exalted mentioned in this place. Some of them said: the meaning of banishment is banishing him from one town to another, and confining him in prison in the town to which he is banished. The original meaning of «النفي» in the speech of the Arabs is driving away. Aws ibn Ḥajar said:
تنفون عن طرق الكرام كما ... تنفي المطارق ما يلي القرد
(You are driven away from the paths of the noble, as the beating-rods drive off what adjoins the matted wool.)
«القرد», with two fatḥas: the hair and wool that has fallen off, become matted and whose ends have knotted; it is the refuse of wool. From this, base dirhams and the like are called «النفاية» (refuse).

dervis-irab:35-37.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الْوَسِيلَةَ): everything by which one seeks access (yutawassalu), i.e. draws near, whether kinship, a favour done, or other than that; it was then borrowed for that by which one seeks access to Allah the Exalted, namely doing acts of obedience and abandoning acts of disobedience. Labīd ibn Rabīʿa said:
أرى الناس لا يدرون ما قدر أمرهم ... ألا كل ذي لبّ إلى الله وأسل
(I see people not knowing the measure of their affair; indeed, everyone of understanding is seeking to draw near to Allah.)
In al-Miṣbāḥ: «وسلت إلى الله أسل», of the pattern of «وعد»: I desired and drew near; from it «الوسيلة» is derived, which is that by which one draws near to a thing; the plural is «الوسائل». «الوسيل» is said to be a plural of «وسيلة», and also said to be a dialectal form of it. From it is the saying of ʿAntara to a woman who reproached him over a horse which he preferred to the rest of his horses and to which he gave the milk of his camels to drink:
لا تذكري مهري وما أطعمته ... فيكون جلدك مثل جلد الأجرب
إنّ الغبوق له وأنت مسوءة ... إن كنت سائلتي غبوقا فاذهبي
إن الرجال لهم إليك وسيلة ... إن يأخذوك تكحلي وتخضبي
ويكون مركبك العقود وحدجه ... وابن النعامة يوم ذلك مركبي
(Do not mention my colt and what I fed him, lest your skin become like the skin of a mangy [camel]. The evening milk is his, though you be displeased; if you are asking me for evening milk, then go. The men have a way of access to you: if they seize you, you will be adorned with kohl and henna; your mount will then be the young camel and its litter, while Ibn al-Naʿāma [my horse] on that day is my mount.)

* I'rab:
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا): the parsing of its likes has been given many times.
(اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَابْتَغُوا إِلَيْهِ الْوَسِيلَةَ): resumptive speech introduced to set out God-fearing and seeking the means of access to Allah, after He had shown the enormity of killing and corruption in the land and pointed to those who are forgiven after their repentance. (اتقوا الله) is an imperative verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (ابتغوا) is conjoined to (اتقوا); (إليه) is attached to (ابتغوا) or to (الوسيلة), because it is of the pattern «فعيلة» in the sense of a passive participle, i.e. "that by which access is sought," and is not a maṣdar (verbal noun), such that it would be impossible «[Translator's note: the printed text has «يستنع», a misprint for «يمتنع»]» for what it governs to precede it; and (الوسيلة) is the direct object.
(وَجاهِدُوا فِي سَبِيلِهِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تُفْلِحُونَ): conjoined to what precedes; (لعل) with its noun; the clause (تفلحون) is its khabar (predicate); and the clause of hope is circumstantial (ḥāliyya).
(إِنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لَوْ أَنَّ لَهُمْ ما فِي الْأَرْضِ جَمِيعاً): resumptive speech introduced to emphasise the obligation of complying with the preceding commands and to encourage the believers to hasten to take the means of access to Him. (إن) with its noun; (لو) is conditional; (أن) is a particle resembling the verb; (لهم), a preposition and its genitive noun, is attached to the omitted fronted khabar of «أن»; (ما) is a relative noun, its delayed noun; (أن) and what falls within its scope is a maṣdar in the nominative as the agent of an omitted verb whose implied form is:
«ثبت» (it were established) «[Translator's note: the printed text has «نبت», a misprint for «ثبت»]», or in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject); this has been discussed in detail before. (في الأرض) is attached to an omitted [element] which has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause); the condition and its answer form the khabar of «إن»; and (جميعا) is a ḥāl (circumstantial).
(وَمِثْلَهُ مَعَهُ لِيَفْتَدُوا بِهِ مِنْ عَذابِ يَوْمِ الْقِيامَةِ): you may make the wāw a conjunction, with (مثله) conjoined to the noun of (أن), namely the relative «ما». You may also make the wāw denote accompaniment (maʿiyya), with (مثله) a mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment), governed in the accusative by the verb omitted before the agent, or by a similar verb if you parse (أن) and what follows it as a nominal clause. (معه) is an adverb of place attached to an omitted ḥāl. The lām is the causal lām; (يفتدوا) is an imperfect verb in the accusative by an implied «أن» after the causal lām; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the [notion of] being-established to which the khabar, namely «لهم», is attached; (به) is attached to (يفتدوا); and (من عذاب يوم القيامة) is also attached to (يفتدوا), since their meanings differ. The pronoun is singular although what it refers back to is two things, because the pronoun is in the sense of a demonstrative, i.e. «بذلك» (with that); or in the sense of «مع», so that what is referred to becomes single; or it is of the type of the saying of ʿUmayr ibn Ḍābiʾ al-Burjumī:
فمن يك أمنى بالمدينة رحله ... فإني وقيّار بها لغريب
(Whoever has his abode in Medina — I and Qayyār are strangers there.) «[Translator's note: the printed text has «أمنى»; the well-known wording is «أمسى».]»
The explanation of this verse will come in the section on benefits.
(ما تُقُبِّلَ مِنْهُمْ وَلَهُمْ عَذابٌ أَلِيمٌ): (ما تقبل منهم): the clause has no grammatical position because it is the answer of a non-jussive condition; the answer came, as is most common, without a lām because it is negated. The wāw is resumptive or conjunctive; (لهم), a preposition and its genitive noun, is attached to an omitted fronted khabar; (عذاب) is the delayed mubtadaʾ; and (أليم) is an adjective.
(يُرِيدُونَ أَنْ يَخْرُجُوا مِنَ النَّارِ وَما هُمْ بِخارِجِينَ مِنْها): the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya); (يريدون) is an imperfect verb and its agent; (أن) and what falls within its scope is interpreted as a maṣdar, the direct object of (يريدون); (من النار) is attached to (يخرجون) «[Translator's note: so in the text; the verb in the verse is (يخرجوا)]»; the wāw is circumstantial; (ما) is the Ḥijāzī negative, operating like «ليس»; (هم) is a detached pronoun in the position of nominative as its noun; the bāʾ is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition; (خارجين) is genitive in form by the bāʾ and accusative in position because it is the khabar of the Ḥijāzī «ما»; and the clause is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl.
(وَلَهُمْ عَذابٌ مُقِيمٌ): the wāw is resumptive or conjunctive; (لهم) is attached to an omitted fronted khabar; (عذاب) is the delayed mubtadaʾ; and (مقيم): an adjective.

* Rhetoric:
In His saying «ليفتدوا به» there is a representative metaphor (istiʿāra tamthīliyya) for the punishment's clinging to them and its permanence upon them, and that they have no way of escaping it. In the noble ḥadīth: «It will be said to the unbeliever on the Day of Resurrection: Do you think that if you had the earth's fill of gold you would ransom yourself with it? He will say: Yes. It will be said to him: You were asked for what was easier than that.»

* Benefits:
The saying of ʿUmayr ibn Ḍābiʾ al-Burjumī in the verse, «وقيار»: Qayyār is the name of his horse; it is also said his camel, and also said his servant. It is a mubtadaʾ, or conjoined to the position of (إن) with its noun. If it is parsed as a mubtadaʾ, its khabar is omitted for brevity, because what is mentioned indicates it by the conjunction; this involves conjoining before the completion of what is conjoined to, which is based on hearing (samāʿī) and may not be taken as a basis for analogy. It is not permissible to make «غريب» a khabar for both, lest two governing words converge on a single governed word; and it is not permissible to make it a khabar of «قيار», because the lām of initiation (lām al-ibtidāʾ) does not enter upon the khabar.
