We have brought it as evidence that [the predicate] is omitted from the second because what is in the first indicates it.

dervis-irab:116-120.t:
* I'rab:
(وَإِذْ قالَ اللَّهُ: يا عِيسَى ابْنَ مَرْيَمَ): the wāw is a conjunction, and the speech is coordinated with «إذ قال الحواريون»; so the adverb is attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted [verb], its implied form being:
"remember" (اذكر). The clause قال الله is in the position of the genitive by construct (iḍāfa), and the clause يا عيسى بن مريم is in the position of the accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). (أَأَنْتَ قُلْتَ لِلنَّاسِ اتَّخِذُونِي وَأُمِّي إِلهَيْنِ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ)
The hamza is interrogative; أنت is a mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause قلت للناس is the khabar (predicate); and the interrogative clause is the object of the saying. The clause اتخذوني, consisting of the imperative verb, the fāʿil (agent) and the mafʿūl bihi (direct object), is in the position of the accusative as the object of the saying. وأمي: the wāw is of accompaniment or conjunction, and أمي is a mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment) or conjoined to the yāʾ; إلهين is a second direct object of اتخذوني; and من دون الله is attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of إلهين, i.e.
"being besides Him, the Exalted". There is nothing to prevent attaching them to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of اتخذوني, i.e. "passing over [Allah]". (قالَ: سُبْحانَكَ ما يَكُونُ لِي أَنْ أَقُولَ ما لَيْسَ لِي بِحَقٍّ): the clause is resumptive, brought to disavow what was attributed to him.
قال is a past verb; سبحانك is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), and the clause is the object of the saying; ما is negating; يكون is a defective (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb; لي is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to the omitted fronted khabar of يكون; أن and what follows it are interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun), the delayed noun of يكون; the clause ما يكون لي is resumptive; the clause ليس has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause); the noun of ليس is latent (mustatir), implied as "it" (هو); بحق: the bāʾ is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition, and حق is the khabar of ليس; لي is attached to an omitted ḥāl because it precedes what it describes; and ما is a relative noun, the object of أقول, because it contains the meaning of a clause. There are other parsings which we have passed over. (إِنْ كُنْتُ قُلْتُهُ فَقَدْ عَلِمْتَهُ): the clause is resumptive; إن is conditional; كنت is a defective past verb, the tāʾ is its noun, and the defective verb is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the clause «قلته» is the khabar of كنت; the fāʾ is linking; the clause قد علمته is in the position of the jussive (majzūm) as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of the jussive condition; and علمته is a verb, its agent and its direct object. (تَعْلَمُ ما فِي نَفْسِي وَلا أَعْلَمُ ما فِي نَفْسِكَ): the clause is resumptive; ما is a relative noun in the position of the accusative as direct object; في نفسي is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ṣila; and the clause ولا أعلم ما في نفسك is conjoined to what precedes. (إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ عَلَّامُ الْغُيُوبِ): إن and its noun; أنت is a mubtadaʾ and علام الغيوب the khabar, and the clause is the khabar of «إن»; or «أنت» is a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl) [Translator's note: the text reads «ضمير فعل», a misprint for «ضمير فصل».] and علام is the khabar of «إن»; the nominal clause is the khabar of إن [Translator's note: so in the text, repeating the first analysis.]; and the clause إنك and what follows it has no grammatical position because it is causal (taʿlīliyya). (ما قُلْتُ لَهُمْ إِلَّا ما أَمَرْتَنِي بِهِ): ما is negating; قلت is a verb and its agent; لهم is attached to قلت; إلا is a particle of restriction; ما is a relative noun, the object of قلت; and the clause أمرتني به is the ṣila. (أَنِ اعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ رَبِّي وَرَبَّكُمْ): the interpreted maṣdar is a badal (substitute) from «ما», or from the hāʾ in «به», or the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being «هو». Some made it explicative, and affirmed that ʿĪsā, upon him be peace, conveyed the meaning of Allah's speech in this wording, as if he said: "I said nothing to them other than Your saying to me: Say to them, worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord." ربي is a badal from الله or an adjective. More on the i'rab of these words will come in the section on benefits. (وَكُنْتُ عَلَيْهِمْ شَهِيداً ما دُمْتُ فِيهِمْ): the wāw is a conjunction; كان and its noun; شهيدا is its khabar; عليهم is attached to «شهيدا»; ما دمت: [دام is] a defective past verb, the tāʾ is its noun, and فيهم is attached to its omitted khabar; and the adverb formed from ما دمت is attached to «شهيدا», i.e. "for the duration of my remaining settled among them". (فَلَمَّا تَوَفَّيْتَنِي كُنْتَ أَنْتَ الرَّقِيبَ عَلَيْهِمْ وَأَنْتَ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ شَهِيدٌ): the fāʾ is resumptive; لما is temporal (ḥīniyya) or linking, so it is either an adverb or a particle containing the sense of a condition; the clause توفيتني is in the position of the genitive by construct, or has no grammatical position; توفيتني is a verb, its agent and its direct object, i.e.
"You took me fully, by raising [me] to heaven", which is the original sense of wafāh. The clause كنت has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition; كان and its noun; أنت is a detached pronoun in the position of the nominative as tawkīd (emphasis) of the pronoun in كنت, and you may parse it as a detached pronoun with no grammatical position; الرقيب is the khabar of كنت; عليهم is attached to الرقيب; the wāw is resumptive or circumstantial; أنت is a mubtadaʾ and شهيد the khabar; and على كل شيء is attached to شهيد. (إِنْ تُعَذِّبْهُمْ فَإِنَّهُمْ عِبادُكَ وَإِنْ تَغْفِرْ لَهُمْ فَإِنَّكَ أَنْتَ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ): إن is conditional; تعذبهم is the protasis; the hāʾ is the direct object; the fāʾ links the apodosis; the clause joined to the fāʾ is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis; إن, its noun and its khabar; and the conditional sentence is resumptive, brought by way of seeking compassion — which is why he did not say "If You punish them, they have disobeyed You". (قالَ اللَّهُ هذا يَوْمُ يَنْفَعُ الصَّادِقِينَ صِدْقُهُمْ): resumptive speech brought to conclude what the discourse began with when He said: يوم يجمع الله الرسل. The demonstrative clause is in the position of the accusative as the object of the saying; هذا is a mubtadaʾ and يوم the khabar; the clause ينفع is in the position of the genitive by construct; الصادقين is a fronted direct object; and صدقهم is a delayed agent. (لَهُمْ جَنَّاتٌ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهارُ خالِدِينَ فِيها أَبَداً): the clause is resumptive, brought to explain the benefit mentioned; لهم is attached to an omitted fronted khabar; جنات is a delayed mubtadaʾ; the clause تجري is an adjective of جنات; من تحتها is attached to تجري; الأنهار is the agent; خالدين is a ḥāl; and أبدا is an adverb of time attached to خالدين. (رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمْ وَرَضُوا عَنْهُ ذلِكَ الْفَوْزُ الْعَظِيمُ): the clause is a supplication, parenthetical with no grammatical position; the clause ورضوا عنه is conjoined to it; ذلك is a mubtadaʾ, الفوز the khabar, and العظيم an adjective. (لِلَّهِ مُلْكُ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَما فِيهِنَّ وَهُوَ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ): the clause is resumptive, brought to establish the truth; لله is attached to an omitted fronted khabar; ملك السماوات والأرض is a delayed mubtadaʾ; the wāw is conjunctive; ما is a relative noun conjoined to الملك; فيهن is attached to an omitted ṣila; «ما» was used giving preponderance to non-rational beings, because it indicates greatness more strongly; هو is a mubtadaʾ and قدير its khabar; and على كل شيء is attached to قدير.

* Rhetoric:
In His words «إن تعذبهم فإنهم عبادك وإن تغفر لهم فإنك أنت العزيز الحكيم» there is one of the arts of rhetoric, matchless and difficult to grasp; one who contemplates it needs a great deal of fineness of perception and refinement of disposition. It is called the art of takhyīr (selection). The scholars of rhetoric defined it as the poet or prose-writer bringing a passage of speech or a verse of poetry which could acceptably be rhymed with various rhymes, and choosing from them one rhyme that is preferred over the rest; his preferring it is taken as evidence of his good choice and true perception. First intuition may dictate that it should be other than what he chose, but he refrained from that for a subtle secret, as in the words of one of them:
إنّ الغريب الطويل الذيل ممتهن ... فكيف حال غريب ما له قوت
(The stranger, though long of train [i.e. well-off], is humiliated; so what of a stranger who has no sustenance?)
It would have been acceptable for him to say: "who has no wealth", or "who has no master", or "who has no one".
But if you look at what he said, namely «ما له قوت» ("who has no sustenance"), you find it more eloquent than all of them, more indicative of poverty and want, more closely touching on the mention of need, more moving to the heart, and more apt to elicit compassion. For that [Translator's note: the text reads «فذلك», apparently for «فلذلك» ("for that reason").] it was preferred over the others.

Discussion of the verse:
Returning, after this brief introduction to this art, to the verse we are dealing with, we say: first, primitive intuition would dictate that the closing phrase (fāṣila) be:
«إنك أنت الغفور الرحيم», because of its suitability to His words «إن تغفر» and the correspondence between forgiveness (ghufrān) and the All-Forgiving (al-Ghafūr). But the effect of this illusion arising from that intuition quickly vanishes when the one under the illusion remembers that these people have deserved punishment rather than forgiveness, so the closing phrase must be «العزيز الحكيم»; for if «الغفور الرحيم» had come after the mention of forgiveness — while He does not forgive them — [Translator's note: the sentence is left incomplete in the source.] so the closing phrase had to be as it came, because Allah, glory be to Him, is unassailable by any compulsion or opposition, and al-ʿAzīz is the unassailable one; and after describing Himself with might, He must describe Himself with wisdom, because He is the All-Wise who puts everything in its place.

Al-Aṣmaʿī's anecdote:
Al-Aṣmaʿī's anecdote has come up before: he mentioned that one day he was reciting, and recited: «والسارق والسارقة فاقطعوا أيديهما جزاء بما كسبا نكالا من الله والله غفور رحيم», and a Bedouin was listening to him; he objected and declared him mistaken. Al-Aṣmaʿī checked the verse again, and it was «والله عزيز حكيم». He said to the Bedouin: "How did you know that?" He said: "O you, He was mighty, so He judged, so He cut off; had He forgiven and shown mercy, He would not have cut off." Al-Aṣmaʿī was astonished and silenced.

This secret was hidden from Abū Ḥayyān:
The secret of this art was hidden from Abū Ḥayyān, despite his eminence. He said in «al-Baḥr», attempting to account for the objection, the following verbatim: "Abū Bakr Ibn al-Anbārī said: Someone attacked the Qur'an by saying that His words «فإنك أنت العزيز الحكيم» do not suit His words «وإن تغفر لهم», because what suits it is «فإنك أنت الغفور الرحيم». The answer is that it admits of nothing but what Allah the Exalted revealed, and whenever it is transferred to what this attacker said, its meaning becomes weak, for then «الغفور الرحيم» would be confined to the second condition and would have no connection with the first condition.
It is what Allah the Exalted revealed, and what the Muslims have agreed upon in reciting." We say: had Abū Ḥayyān known this art, he would have answered with what we have presented, and would not have resorted to far-fetched answers.

* Benefits:
Between Ibn Hishām and al-Zamakhsharī:
Ibn Hishām mentioned in «Mughnī al-Labīb» the following: "Al-Zamakhsharī mentioned regarding His words, the Exalted, «ما قلت لهم إلا ما أمرتني به أن اعبدوا الله» that it may be an explicative [أن] explaining the saying, on its interpretation as a command, i.e. 'I commanded them only what You commanded me: that they worship Allah' — and this is good. On this basis it is said in the criterion: that the letters of saying be in it, unless the saying is interpreted as something else [Translator's note: the wording of the criterion is compressed in the source.]. In the verse it may not be explicative of أمرتني, because it is not correct to say 'Worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord' as said by Allah the Exalted; so it cannot be explicative of His command, because what is explained is identical with its explanation."

Ibn Yaʿīsh's wording:
Ibn Yaʿīsh's wording: "So «أن» is in the sense of «أي» ('that is'), and it is an explanation of «ما أمرتني به», because the command has the meaning of saying; and because, when this is explicative, [it has] three conditions [Translator's note: a word such as «لها» appears to be missing in the source.]:
1- The first is that the verb which it explains and expresses contain the meaning of saying without being [the verb of] saying.
2- The second is that nothing of the complement of the verb which it explains be attached to «أن», because if anything of that is attached to it, it becomes part of its clause and is not an explanation of it — as in أوعزت إليه بأن قم ('I instructed him to stand') and كتبت إليه بأن قم ('I wrote to him to stand'), because the bāʾ here is attached to the verb, and when it is attached to it, it becomes part of its clause, while explanation is only by a clause other than the first.
3- The third is that what precedes it be a complete utterance, because of what we mentioned, namely that it and what follows it are a clause explaining a clause before it. For that reason they said regarding His words, the Exalted:
«أن الحمد لله رب العالمين» that «أن» in it is lightened from the heavy [أنّ], the meaning being:
'that praise be to Allah' (أنه الحمد لله); it is not explicative, because what precedes it is not a complete clause — do you not see that if you stopped at His words «وآخر دعواهم» it would not be a complete utterance?"
I say: for this reason we inclined to what we chose in parsing it as maṣdariyya, to avoid falling into these pitfalls.
2- When «ما» occurs before «ليس», «لم» or «لا», or after «إلّا», it is a relative noun; when it occurs after the kāf of comparison it is maṣdariyya; when it occurs after the bāʾ it admits both; and when it occurs between two verbs, the first being [a verb of] knowing, awareness or looking, it admits being relative or interrogative. [Translator's note: the preceding discussion is unnumbered in the source, which then continues with "2-".]
3- Every noun of time that is vague and refers to the past may be put in construct with a clause; if what follows it is indeclinable, then indeclinability on the fatḥa is preferable, for harmony. Al-Nābigha said: على حين عاتبت المشيب على الصبا ... وقلت: ألمّا أصح والشيب وازع (At the time I reproached grey hair for [my] youthful passion, and said: "Have I not yet sobered up, while grey hair restrains?")
«على حين» is related in the genitive as declinable, and «على حين» indeclinable on the fatḥa, which is preferable. If what follows it is a declinable verb or a nominal clause, then declinability is preferable, as came in the verse: «هذا يوم ينفع».

dervis-irab:38-39.t:
* Vocabulary:
(نَكالًا): In al-Miṣbāḥ it says: «نكل به ينكل», of the pattern of «قتل», «نكلة قبيحة»: he afflicted him with a calamity [as an exemplary punishment]. «نكّل به», with doubling, is intensive; and the noun is «النكال».

* I'rab:
(وَالسَّارِقُ وَالسَّارِقَةُ فَاقْطَعُوا أَيْدِيَهُما): resumptive speech introduced to begin setting out the ruling on theft. (السارق) is a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is omitted, its implied form being:
"among what is recited to you," or "among what has been prescribed for you, [is] the male thief and the female thief," i.e.:
the ruling concerning them. So the muḍāf, namely «حكم» (ruling), was omitted, and the muḍāf ilayhi, namely «السارق والسارقة», was put in its place; and the khabar, which is the preposition and its genitive noun, was omitted, because the fāʾ after it prevents its being accusative by ishtighāl (preoccupation of the verb), as is the rule, since the accusative is preferred before a request «[Translator's note: the sentence is reproduced as printed]»; and it — i.e. the fāʾ, which came because of its resemblance to a condition — prevents what follows it from being the khabar, because it never enters upon it; so nothing remains but the nominative. This is a chapter which Sībawayh devoted in his Book, and the reader will see its summary in the section on benefits. This is the reading of the majority. Al-Akhfash, al-Mubarrad and a group held that the khabar is the imperative clause, namely His saying «فاقطعوا», and that the fāʾ entered the khabar only because it resembles a condition, since the alif and lām in it are relative, in the sense of «الذي» and «التي», and the adjective is its ṣila (relative clause); so it has the force of your saying: "and he who steals and she who steals, cut off…". Al-Zamakhsharī permitted that, though he preferred what Sībawayh held. (السارقة) is conjoined to (السارق); the fāʾ occurs in the answer to the relative «ال»; (اقطعوا) is an imperative verb, the wāw being the fāʿil (agent); and (أيديهما) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
(جَزاءً بِما كَسَبا نَكالًا مِنَ اللَّهِ): (جزاء) is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), i.e. "for the sake of recompense," the conditions for the accusative being met. It may also be accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun) by an implied verb, i.e. "recompense them a recompense." It may also be parsed as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent, i.e. "recompensing them with cutting off." In (بما), the bāʾ is a preposition whose meaning is causality, i.e.:
because of their earning; (ما) is maṣdariyya, interpreted together with what follows it as a maṣdar genitive by the bāʾ; and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (جزاء). (ما) may also be relative, i.e. "because of what they earned through theft, which is done by the hands," the clause being the ṣila. (نكالا) is accusative in the same way as (جزاء), or it is a badal (substitute) from it; and (من الله) is attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of «نكالا».
(وَاللَّهُ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمٌ): the wāw is resumptive; (الله) is a mubtadaʾ; (عزيز) is a first khabar and (حكيم) a second. A delightful story of one of the Bedouins will come, which the reader will see in the section on benefits.
(فَمَنْ تابَ مِنْ بَعْدِ ظُلْمِهِ وَأَصْلَحَ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ يَتُوبُ عَلَيْهِ): the fāʾ is resumptive; (من) is a jussive-governing conditional noun, a mubtadaʾ; (تاب) is a past verb in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the fāʾ links the apodosis; (إن) with its noun, and the clause (يتوب) its khabar; and the protasis and its apodosis form the khabar of (من).
(إِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ): the clause is resumptive; (إن) with its noun and its two predicates.

* Benefits:
1- We present below a summary of the delightful section that Sībawayh included in his Book, for its novelty, its benefit and the agility of mind it shows. He said in the chapter entitled:
«The Chapter of Command and Prohibition», after mentioning the places where the accusative is chosen — the summary of which is that whenever the noun is built upon an imperative verb, that is a place where the accusative is chosen. Then he said, as though clarifying how this verse is distinguished from those where he chose the accusative:
"As for the saying of the Mighty and Majestic: «والسارق والسارقة فاقطعوا» (the verse), and His saying:
«الزانية والزاني فاجلدوا» (the verse), this is not built upon the verb; rather it comes on the pattern of the saying of the Exalted: «مثل الجنة التي وعد المتقون» (the description of the Garden promised to the God-fearing).
Then He said after it: «فيها أنهار» (in it are rivers)." Thus Sībawayh means to distinguish these verses from the places in which he set out the choice of the accusative. The point of the distinction is that in speech where the accusative is chosen, the noun is built upon the verb, whereas in these verses it is not built upon it, so the choice of the accusative is not required. Then he said: "The description (al-mathal) was placed only for the account that follows it; He mentioned reports and stories, so it is as though He said:
'and among the stories is the description of the Garden'; so this is taken as an implied [element], and Allah knows best.
Likewise «الزانية والزاني», as He, majestic is His praise, said: «سورة أنزلناها وفرضناها» (a sūra which We have sent down and made obligatory); [it is as though] He said: among the obligations [are] the female and male fornicator; then came:
«فاجلدوا», after the nominative had already been applied to them." Sībawayh means: the noun was not built upon the verb mentioned afterwards, but upon an omitted preceding [element], and the verb came incidentally. He resumed his words and said: "Just as there came: «وقائلة خولان فانكح فتاتهم» (and many a woman saying: 'Khawlān — so marry their girl'): he brought the verb after the implied [element] had governed it. Likewise His saying:
«والسارق والسارقة»: 'and among what has been prescribed for you [are] the male thief and the female thief'; these nouns entered only after stories and accounts. Some people read:
«والسارقَ والسارقةَ» in the accusative, and in Arabic this has the strength I mentioned to you; but the generality [of readers] insisted on the nominative." Sībawayh means that in the accusative reading the noun is built upon the verb without relying on what precedes, so the accusative is strong relative to the nominative [in a case] where the noun relies on the omitted preceding [element]. For he has shown that this takes it out of the chapter in which the accusative is chosen; so how could it be understood from him that he preferred it over it? The chapter differs between the two readings, and preference occurs only after equality within the chapter. So the accusative is preferable to the nominative where the noun is built upon the verb, and the nominative is required — we do not say [merely preferred] — where the noun is built upon preceding speech. «[Translator's note: this sentence is somewhat garbled in the print; rendered according to its evident sense.]» Then Sībawayh substantiated this implied [element] by [pointing out] that the speech occurs after stories and reports. If it were as al-Zamakhsharī thought, Sībawayh would not have needed an implied element; rather he would have made it nominative as a mubtadaʾ and made the command its khabar, as al-Zamakhsharī parsed it.
We have summarised this section with commentary on it only because some exegetes thought that Sībawayh prefers the accusative reading without this qualification. The summary of all of this: the accusative is on one ground, namely building the noun upon the imperative verb; and the nominative is on two grounds: one weak, namely [taking it as] a mubtadaʾ with the speech built upon the verb; and the other strong, like the ground for the accusative, namely its being nominative as [part of] a nominal sentence whose [other part] is omitted, indicated by the context. Whenever two grounds for the nominative conflict for us, one strong and the other weak, the reading must be taken on the strong one, as Sībawayh parsed it.

Al-Fakhr al-Rāzī responds:
Al-Fakhr al-Rāzī set out to refute Sībawayh and said: «What Sībawayh held is nothing, and several considerations show its unsoundness.» After lengthy discussion he presented five considerations, which this book has no room to include in full.

Abū Ḥayyān responds to al-Rāzī:
Abū Ḥayyān undertook to refute al-Rāzī, and in his tafsīr al-Baḥr al-Muḥīṭ he refuted at excessive length the five considerations he had presented. At the end of the discussion he said: «It is astonishing, this man and his boldness toward the sciences, to the point that he composed a book on grammar which he called al-Muḥarrar, and in it followed a strange method, far removed from the terminology of the grammarians and from their aims.» Let the reader refer to this discussion, for it is very fine.

A view of Ibn Jarīr al-Ṭabarī:
We have found that Ibn Jarīr al-Ṭabarī gives a delightful explanation for choosing the nominative, which we include here: He, majestic is His praise, says, in meaning: "whoever steals, man or woman, cut off his hand, O people." For this reason «السارق» and «السارقة» are nominative, because they are not specified; had a specific male thief and female thief been meant, the proper form of speech would have been the accusative.
2- «الأيدي» is plural because each thief has one right hand, which is the one exposed to being cut off for theft; and male thieves have hands, and female thieves have hands; it is as though He said: cut off the right hands of the two kinds. The dual of the pronoun is only for the two kinds.
3- It is reported that a Bedouin heard al-Aṣmaʿī reciting this verse, and he recited at its end: «والله غفور رحيم». The Bedouin denied that this was Quran.
Al-Aṣmaʿī said: I went back to the muṣḥaf, and it was: «والله عزيز حكيم». When I told the Bedouin that, he said: Yes — He is mighty, so He judged and cut off; had He forgiven and shown mercy, He would not have cut off. This is one of the lofty leaps of the mind.

dervis-irab:40-41.t:
* I'rab:
(أَلَمْ تَعْلَمْ أَنَّ اللَّهَ لَهُ مُلْكُ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ): resumptive speech introduced to address the Messenger, though everyone is meant by it, [stating] that He alone disposes of the matters of punishment and of forgiveness for whom He wills. The hamza is for the interrogative of affirmation (taqrīr) of what follows the negation; (لم) is a particle of negation, inversion [of tense] and jussive; (تعلم) is an imperfect verb, jussive by (لم); (أن) and what falls within its scope stands in place of the two objects of (تعلم). (أن) with its noun; (له), a preposition and its genitive noun, is attached to an omitted fronted khabar (predicate); (ملك السموات) is the delayed mubtadaʾ (subject); (الأرض) is conjoined to the muḍāf ilayhi (السموات); and the nominal clause is the khabar of (أن).
(يُعَذِّبُ مَنْ يَشاءُ وَيَغْفِرُ لِمَنْ يَشاءُ وَاللَّهُ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ): the verbal clause is a second khabar of (أن), or circumstantial (ḥāliyya). Punishment was placed first only because the context is one of threat, so it is fitting to put first the deterrents that suit it. (من) is a relative noun, the object of (يعذب); the clause (يشاء) is the ṣila (relative clause); (يغفر) is conjoined to (يعذب); (لمن يشاء) is attached to (يغفر); the wāw is resumptive; (الله) is a mubtadaʾ; (على كل شيء) is attached to (قدير); and (قدير) is the khabar of (الله).
(يا أَيُّهَا الرَّسُولُ لا يَحْزُنْكَ الَّذِينَ يُسارِعُونَ فِي الْكُفْرِ): resumptive speech introduced to address the Messenger ﷺ, cautioning him against being affected by what the unbelievers do to grieve him. The parsing of (يا أيها الرسول) has been given many times. (لا) is prohibitive; (يحزنك) is an imperfect verb, jussive by (لا); the kāf is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (الذين) is a relative noun in the position of nominative as the fāʿil (agent); the clause (يسارعون) has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila; and (في الكفر), a preposition and its genitive noun, is attached to (يسارعون).
(مِنَ الَّذِينَ قالُوا: آمَنَّا بِأَفْواهِهِمْ وَلَمْ تُؤْمِنْ قُلُوبُهُمْ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); the clause (قالوا) has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila; the clause (آمنا) is the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl); (بأفواههم) is attached to (قالوا), i.e. their saying does not go beyond their mouths; the wāw is circumstantial; (لم) is a particle of negation, inversion and jussive; (تؤمن) is an imperfect verb, jussive by (لم); (قلوبهم) is the agent; and the clause is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl.
(وَمِنَ الَّذِينَ هادُوا سَمَّاعُونَ لِلْكَذِبِ سَمَّاعُونَ لِقَوْمٍ آخَرِينَ): the wāw is a conjunction, and (من الذين هادوا) is conjoined to (من الذين قالوا), so it is a ḥāl explaining a single thing. It has also been said: the wāw is resumptive, (من الذين) is a fronted khabar and (سماعون) a delayed mubtadaʾ, so the explanation is of two things. On the first view, «سماعون» is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. «هم سماعون» (they are eager listeners). (للكذب) is attached to (سماعون); the second «سماعون» is a badal (substitute) of the first «سماعون» or a tawkīd (emphasis) of it; (لقوم) is attached to «سماعون»; and (آخرين) is an adjective.
(لَمْ يَأْتُوكَ): the clause is a second adjective of (قوم); (لم) is a particle of negation, inversion and jussive; and (يأتوك) is an imperfect verb in the jussive, with its agent and its direct object.
(يُحَرِّفُونَ الْكَلِمَ مِنْ بَعْدِ مَواضِعِهِ): the clause is a third adjective. A muḍāf must be supposed omitted, i.e. "the ruling of the words." (من بعد مواضعه) is attached to an omitted ḥāl, i.e. "while it is after Allah had set the words in their places." Its meaning may also be "they distort the words from their places," so that «بعد» has been put in place of «عن», as one says «جئتك عن فراغي من الشغل», meaning "after my finishing work." Those meant by them are the Jews.
(يَقُولُونَ: إِنْ أُوتِيتُمْ هذا فَخُذُوهُ): the clause is a fourth adjective. (يقولون) is an imperfect verb in the nominative, the sign of its nominative being the retention of the nūn, the wāw being the agent; (إن) is conditional; (أوتيتم) is a passive past verb in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); (هذا) is the second object, the first being the tāʾ, which is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the fāʾ links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); the clause (خذوه) is in the position of jussive as the apodosis — it was not fit to be an apodosis [without the fāʾ] because it is a request; and the conditional clause is in the position of accusative as the object of saying.
(وَإِنْ لَمْ تُؤْتَوْهُ فَاحْذَرُوا): the wāw is a conjunction; (إن) is conditional; (لم) is a particle of negation, inversion and jussive; (تؤتوه) is an imperfect verb, jussive by (لم), and at the same time it is the protasis; the wāw is the deputy agent and the hāʾ the second object. In (فاحذروا) the fāʾ links the apodosis, and the clause (احذروا) is in the position of jussive as the apodosis.
(وَمَنْ يُرِدِ اللَّهُ فِتْنَتَهُ فَلَنْ تَمْلِكَ لَهُ مِنَ اللَّهِ شَيْئاً): the wāw is resumptive; (من) is a jussive-governing conditional noun in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ; (يرد) is the protasis; (الله) is the agent; (فتنة) is the direct object; the fāʾ links the apodosis; (لن) is a particle of negation, accusative and futurity; (تملك) is an imperfect verb, accusative by (لن); the clause is in the position of jussive as the apodosis; (له) is attached to (تملك); (من الله) is attached to an omitted ḥāl from «شيئا», because it was originally an adjective and was placed before it; (شيئا) is a direct object or a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); and the protasis and its apodosis form the khabar of «من».
(أُولئِكَ الَّذِينَ لَمْ يُرِدِ اللَّهُ أَنْ يُطَهِّرَ قُلُوبَهُمْ): the clause is resumptive, introduced to announce how far the hypocrites have gone
in corruption and how deeply they have plunged into misguidance. The demonstrative is a mubtadaʾ; (الذين) is the khabar; the clause (لم يرد الله) is the ṣila; (أن) and what falls within its scope is in the position of accusative as the object of (يرد); and (قلوبهم) is the direct object of (يطهر).
(لَهُمْ فِي الدُّنْيا خِزْيٌ وَلَهُمْ فِي الْآخِرَةِ عَذابٌ عَظِيمٌ): (لهم) is attached to an omitted fronted khabar; (في الدنيا) is attached to an omitted ḥāl; (خزي) is the delayed mubtadaʾ; the clause is a second khabar of the demonstrative; and (ولهم في الآخرة عذاب عظيم) is conjoined to what precedes.

dervis-irab:70-71.t:
* I'rab:
(لَقَدْ أَخَذْنا مِيثاقَ بَنِي إِسْرائِيلَ): resumptive speech, brought to set out other examples of their crimes, which proclaim that faith is not to be expected of them. The lām is in answer to an omitted oath; قد is a particle of realisation (taḥqīq); أخذنا is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); ميثاق is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and بني إسرائيل is a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). (وَأَرْسَلْنا إِلَيْهِمْ رُسُلًا): the wāw is a conjunction; أرسلنا is a verb and its fāʿil; إليهم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) أرسلنا; and رسلا is a mafʿūl bihi. (كُلَّما جاءَهُمْ رَسُولٌ بِما لا تَهْوى أَنْفُسُهُمْ): كلما is an adverb of time that includes the meaning of condition, attached to its omitted apodosis, i.e. "they disobeyed him"; جاءهم is a verb and a fronted mafʿūl bihi, and رسول is a delayed fāʿil; بما is attached to جاءهم; and the clause لا تهوى أنفسهم is the ṣila (relative clause). (فَرِيقاً كَذَّبُوا وَفَرِيقاً يَقْتُلُونَ): فريقا is a fronted object of كذبوا, and the second فريقا is a fronted object of يقتلون. The clause is resumptive, arising as the answer to a question that arises from the first apodosis, as though it were said: "What did they do with them?" and it was said: "A party of them they denied, without exposing them to harm, and another party of them they killed." (وَحَسِبُوا أَلَّا تَكُونَ فِتْنَةٌ): the wāw is conjunctive; حسبوا is a verb and its fāʿil; أن is a maṣdar-forming particle that makes the verb accusative; لا is negative; تكون is a complete (tāmm) imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by أن, and فتنة is the fāʿil; and أن with what follows it stands in place of the two objects of حسبوا. It has also been read with «تكون» in the nominative, in which case «أن» is lightened from the heavy أنّ, and its noun is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), its implied form being أنه. (فَعَمُوا وَصَمُّوا ثُمَّ تابَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِمْ): the fāʾ is conjunctive; عموا is conjoined to حسبوا, and صموا is conjoined to His saying فعموا; ثم is a conjunction of sequence with delay; تاب الله is a verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is conjoined to His saying فعموا وصموا; and عليهم is attached to تاب. (ثُمَّ عَمُوا وَصَمُّوا كَثِيرٌ مِنْهُمْ وَاللَّهُ بَصِيرٌ بِما يَعْمَلُونَ): ثم عموا وصموا is conjoined to what preceded; كثير is a badal (substitute) for the pronoun in عموا or صموا; منهم is attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of كثير; the wāw is resumptive; الله is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and بصير its khabar (predicate); بما is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to بصير; and the clause يعملون is the ṣila.

* Rhetoric:
In the verse there is a kind of eloquent iltifāt (shift) in His saying: «فريقا كذبوا وفريقا يقتلون»: a shift from reporting with the past verb to reporting with the imperfect verb. This is among the subtlest of matters, and it is available in usage only to one who knows the secrets of eloquence and rhetoric.
The Noble Qur'an brims with it. He brought the past verb first, establishing something that had happened; then He brought يقتلون as the narration of a past state (ḥikāyat ḥāl māḍiya), to present the killing as hideous and to bring that ghastly scene before the mind, so as to wonder at it and draw the lesson from its folds.
Wondrous instances of it will come in the Qur'an. On this pattern came the saying of Taʾabbaṭa Sharran:
بأنّي قد لقيت الغول تهوي ... بسهب كالصحيفة صحصحان
فأضربها بلا دهش فخرّت ... صريعا لليدين وللجران
(That I met the ghoul swooping over a plain flat as a page, a bare expanse; and I strike her without alarm, and she fell, felled on her hands and her breast.)
He intended to depict for his people the state that had come upon him until he plucked up courage to strike the ghoul, as though he were embodying it for them, to arouse their admiration at his boldness in that terror. Examples of this are too many to be counted. Of this style is what came in the account of al-Zubayr ibn al-ʿAwwām at the battle of Badr. He said: "I met ʿUbayda ibn Saʿīd ibn al-ʿĀṣ on a horse, wearing complete armour, nothing of him visible but his eyes, saying: 'I am Abū Dhāt al-Kuʾūs.' In my hand was a short spear (ʿanaza) — something like half a spear — and I thrust it into his eye, and he fell; and I tread with my foot on his cheek; the ʿanaza came out bent." His saying «فأطعن بها في عينه، وأطأ برجلي» ("and I thrust it into his eye, and I tread with my foot") is turned from the past form to the imperfect, to represent to the hearer the scene in which he did what he did, in his daring and boldness in killing that armoured horseman.

dervis-irab:72-72.t:
* I'rab:
(لَقَدْ كَفَرَ الَّذِينَ قالُوا إِنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ الْمَسِيحُ ابْنُ مَرْيَمَ): the lām is in answer to an omitted oath; قد is a particle of realisation (taḥqīq); and the oath clause is resumptive. كفر الذين is a verb and its fāʿil (agent), and the clause has no grammatical position because it is the answer to an omitted oath; the clause قالوا has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذين; the clause إن الله is in the position of an accusative as the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl). inna and its noun; هو is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and المسيح the khabar (predicate) of هو; the nominal clause is the khabar of إنّ; ابن is a badal (substitute) for المسيح, and مريم is a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). (وَقالَ الْمَسِيحُ: يا بَنِي إِسْرائِيلَ اعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ رَبِّي وَرَبَّكُمْ): the wāw is circumstantial; قال المسيح is a verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the wāw in «قالوا»; يا بني إسرائيل is a vocative in genitive construct (munādā muḍāf); the clause اعبدوا الله is in the position of an accusative as the object of al-Masīḥ's saying; ربي is a badal for الله, and ربكم is conjoined to ربي. (إِنَّهُ مَنْ يُشْرِكْ بِاللَّهِ فَقَدْ حَرَّمَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ الْجَنَّةَ): the clause is resumptive. inna and its noun; من is a conditional noun that makes the verb jussive, in the position of a nominative as mubtadaʾ; يشرك is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); بالله is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) يشرك; the fāʾ links the apodosis; the clause فقد حرم is in the position of a jussive (majzūm) as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); the protasis with its apodosis is the khabar of «من»; and the whole conditional clause is in the position of a nominative as the khabar of إنّ. حرم الله is a verb and its fāʿil; عليه is attached to حرّم; and الجنة is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (وَمَأْواهُ النَّارُ وَما لِلظَّالِمِينَ مِنْ أَنْصارٍ): the wāw is resumptive; مأواه is a fronted khabar and النار a delayed mubtadaʾ, and the reverse is also permissible. The wāw is conjunctive; ما is negative; للظالمين is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted, fronted khabar; من is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition; and أنصار is genitive in form and nominative in position, because it is a delayed mubtadaʾ.

dervis-irab:73-75.t:
* Vocabulary:
(يُؤْفَكُونَ): they are turned away.

* I'rab:
(لَقَدْ كَفَرَ الَّذِينَ قالُوا: إِنَّ اللَّهَ ثالِثُ ثَلاثَةٍ): the clause is resumptive, and the lām is in answer to an omitted oath. The clause كفر الذين قالوا has no grammatical position because it is the answer to the oath; the clause قالوا is the ṣila (relative clause); inna and its noun, and ثالث ثلاثة is its khabar (predicate); and the clause headed by إنّ is in the position of an accusative as the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl). (وَما مِنْ إِلهٍ إِلَّا إِلهٌ واحِدٌ): the wāw is circumstantial; ما is negative; من is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition; إله is genitive in form and nominative in position as a mubtadaʾ (subject); the khabar is omitted, i.e. "existent"; the second إله is a badal (substitute) for the pronoun in it [Translator's note: i.e. the pronoun in the omitted khabar]; and إلا is a particle of restriction. This i'rab has passed in detail in the formula of testimony (kalimat al-shahāda). The meaning is: "while the case is that there is no god existing or present except One God". (وَإِنْ لَمْ يَنْتَهُوا عَمَّا يَقُولُونَ): the wāw is resumptive; إن is conditional; لم ينتهوا is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); عما is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ينتهوا; and the clause يقولون is the ṣila. (لَيَمَسَّنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مِنْهُمْ عَذابٌ أَلِيمٌ): the lām occurs in the answer to an omitted oath; يمسّن is an imperfect verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, and the clause has no grammatical position because it is the answer to the oath; الذين is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause كفروا is the ṣila; منهم is attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); and عذاب أليم is the fāʿil (agent). The apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, the answer to the oath standing in its place, because the implied form is: ولئن لم ينتهوا; the rule is that when a condition and an oath come together, the answer belongs to whichever comes first. We resorted to this only because of the presence of the lām that prepares for the oath (al-lām al-muwaṭṭiʾa lil-qasam) [Translator's note: so in the source; in the verse as written that lām is not present, and it is the implied form ولئن that contains it]. (أَفَلا يَتُوبُونَ إِلَى اللَّهِ وَيَسْتَغْفِرُونَهُ وَاللَّهُ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ): the clause is resumptive, brought to express wonder at their persistence. The hamza is for the interrogative of wonder and disapproval; the fāʾ is conjunctive, joining to something implied, i.e. "Do they not desist, and so not repent?"; إلى الله is attached to يتوبون; يستغفرونه is conjoined to يتوبون; the wāw is circumstantial; الله is a mubtadaʾ, and غفور رحيم are two khabars of it; and the clause is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl. (مَا الْمَسِيحُ ابْنُ مَرْيَمَ إِلَّا رَسُولٌ قَدْ خَلَتْ مِنْ قَبْلِهِ الرُّسُلُ): resumptive speech, brought to establish the truth. ما is negative, and it does not operate like ليس because the negation is broken by إلا; المسيح is a mubtadaʾ, and ابن مريم is a badal or a naʿt (adjective); إلا is a particle of restriction; رسول is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ; the clause قد خلت is a naʿt; من قبله is attached to خلت, i.e. "passed away and perished"; and الرسل is the fāʿil. (وَأُمُّهُ صِدِّيقَةٌ كانا يَأْكُلانِ الطَّعامَ): the wāw is conjunctive; أمه is a mubtadaʾ and صديقة the khabar; the clause كانا is explicative with no grammatical position; the alif of the dual is the noun of كان, the clause يأكلان is the khabar of كانا, and الطعام is a mafʿūl bihi. (انْظُرْ كَيْفَ نُبَيِّنُ لَهُمُ الْآياتِ ثُمَّ انْظُرْ أَنَّى يُؤْفَكُونَ): the clause is resumptive; كيف is an interrogative noun in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl; the interrogative clause is in the position of an accusative as the object of انظر, «كيف» having suspended «انظر» from operating overtly on what follows it. نبين لهم الآيات is a verb, a latent fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi. ثم is a conjunction of sequence and delay; the meaning is that the clarification of these signs was a wonder, and their turning away from them and their aversion to reflecting on them was more wondrous. أنى is an interrogative noun meaning كيف, in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl; and يؤفكون is an imperfect verb, the wāw being the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).

* Rhetoric:
In His saying: «كانا يأكلان الطعام» ("they both used to eat food") there is a kināya (metonymy) for the fact that they both, Allah's blessings be upon them, were human beings, because eating food is followed by digestion and evacuation; so He sufficed with mentioning the eating of food for all this, out of refinement and decorum. This is one of the rare metonymies in the Arabic language. We have said much about kināya before, and here attention must be drawn to the fact that kināya — wherever it occurs — is shared by two aspects, the literal (ḥaqīqa) and the figurative (majāz), and it may be taken in both together, as in the saying of the Exalted: «أو لامستم النساء» ("or you have touched women"). It is permissible to take the kināya there literally or figuratively, and the meaning is sound with each without the expression being impaired. Whoever took it literally, like al-Shāfiʿī, considered touching to be the contact of body with body and made ablution obligatory — and that is the literal sense of touching. Whoever took it figuratively, like Abū Ḥanīfa, considered touching to be intercourse — and that is the figurative sense. More on kināya and its delights will come in this book.
2- Repetition in His saying «انظر» first, and then «ثم انظر» second. In this there is evidence of concern for looking and reflecting, even though the two looks differ: the first concerns how Allah makes the signs clear to His creation, and the second concerns their turning away from them and their aversion to reflecting on their aims and purposes.

dervis-irab:76-77.t:
* Vocabulary:
(لا تَغْلُوا): do not exceed the limit. الغلاء is rising high. Al-Ḥārith ibn Ḥilliza al-Yashkurī said in his Muʿallaqa:
أو منعتم ما تسألون فمن حدّ ... ثتموه له علينا الغلاء
(Or if you were denied what you ask, then who is it, you tell of, who has the upper hand over us?)
(الأهواء): plural of هوى, which is what the desire of the soul calls to. Abū ʿUbayda said: «We have not found الهوى used except in the place of evil, because one does not say "فلان يهوى" [Translator's note: i.e. of something good]; rather one says: "he loves good".» When the hāʾ and the wāw are the first and second radicals of a word, they denote the meaning of falling and descending to one side. One says: هوى من الجبل, "he fell from the mountain"; هوت الدلو من البئر هويّا, with fatḥa on the hāʾ, "the bucket fell down the well"; طاح في المهواة والهاوية, "he was flung into the chasm", which is what lies between two mountains; تهاووا فيها, "they fell into it one after another"; هذه هوة عميقة, "this is a deep pit"; «وأمه هاوية» ("his mother will be the abyss"); جلست عنده هويا, i.e. "for a good while"; مضى هوي من الليل, "a portion of the night passed"; and «استهوته الشياطين» ("the devils have lured him"). Among figurative usages is their saying of a coward: إنه الهواء, "he is air", i.e. his heart is empty of boldness. Shawqī seized on this linguistic curiosity and said:
فاتقوا الله في قلوب العذارى ... فالعذارى قلوبهنّ هواء
(Fear Allah concerning the hearts of maidens, for maidens — their hearts are air.)
One says: رجل أهوج, a brave man who throws himself into perils and destruction; ناقة هوجاء, a she-camel as though touched with recklessness, which in her speed does not watch where her hooves fall on the ground; ريح هوجاء and رياح هوج, violent wind(s); هاد الرجل وتهوّد, "the man became a Jew", and هوّد ابنه, "he made his son a Jew"; هوّر البناء فتهوّر, i.e. "it collapsed" — to the end of this material.
All this is among the special features of our noble language.

* I'rab:
(قُلْ: أَتَعْبُدُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ ما لا يَمْلِكُ لَكُمْ ضَرًّا وَلا نَفْعاً): resumptive speech, brought to command the Prophet ﷺ to silence them and bind them by the argument. قل is an imperative verb; the hamza is a particle of the interrogative of rebuke and wonder; the clause أتعبدون is in the position of an accusative as the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl); من دون الله is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); ما is a relative noun in the position of an accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object), though some chose that it be a qualified indefinite noun (nakira mawṣūfa); the clause لا يملك is, on the first view, the ṣila (relative clause) with no grammatical position, or in the position of an accusative as a naʿt (adjective), and perhaps this is preferable. لكم is attached to يملك; ضرا is the mafʿūl bihi of يملك; and ولا نفعا is conjoined to «ضرا». (وَاللَّهُ هُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ): the wāw is circumstantial, the link between the ḥāl and its owner being the wāw; the coming of the ḥāl after this speech suits what the situation requires. الله is a mubtadaʾ (subject); هو is a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl) with no grammatical position, or a detached pronoun in the position of a nominative as mubtadaʾ; and السميع العليم are two khabars (predicates) of «الله» or of «هو». Its parallels have preceded. (قُلْ يا أَهْلَ الْكِتابِ لا تَغْلُوا فِي دِينِكُمْ غَيْرَ الْحَقِّ): the clause of saying is resumptive, and what follows it is in the position of an accusative as the object of saying; لا is prohibitive; تغلوا is an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by لا; في دينكم is attached to تغلوا; غير الحق is a naʿt of an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e. "an exceeding other than the truth"; it may properly be a ḥāl of the agent pronoun, the wāw, i.e. "overstepping the truth". It has been said that the accusative is by connected exception, and it has been said: by disconnected exception. (وَلا تَتَّبِعُوا أَهْواءَ قَوْمٍ قَدْ ضَلُّوا مِنْ قَبْلُ وَأَضَلُّوا كَثِيراً): the wāw is conjunctive; لا is prohibitive; تتبعوا is an imperfect verb in the jussive by «لا»; أهواء is a mafʿūl bihi and قوم a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause قد ضلوا is a naʿt of قوم; من قبل is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ضلوا, and قبل is indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma because the adverb is cut off from its genitive construct in wording but not in meaning; أضلوا is conjoined to قد ضلوا, and كثيرا is a mafʿūl bihi. (وَضَلُّوا عَنْ سَواءِ السَّبِيلِ): conjoined to what preceded.

dervis-irab:78-79.t:
* I'rab:
(لُعِنَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مِنْ بَنِي إِسْرائِيلَ عَلى لِسانِ داوُدَ وَعِيسَى ابْنِ مَرْيَمَ): the speech is resumptive. لعن is a passive past verb and الذين the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause كفروا is the ṣila (relative clause); من بني إسرائيل is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); على لسان is attached to لعن — on the singular form of لسان there is an engaging discussion which will come in the section on Benefits; داود is a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); عيسى is conjoined to داود; ابن is a badal (substitute) or a naʿt (adjective); and مريم is a muḍāf ilayhi. (ذلِكَ بِما عَصَوْا وَكانُوا يَعْتَدُونَ): the demonstrative is a mubtadaʾ (subject); بما is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted khabar (predicate); ما is maṣdariyya, interpreted with what follows it as a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "because of their disobedience"; and the clause is resumptive. ما may also be a relative noun; in either case the clause عصوا has no grammatical position. The clause كانوا is conjoined to عصوا and falls under its ruling; the wāw is the noun of كان, and the clause يعتدون is its khabar. (كانُوا لا يَتَناهَوْنَ عَنْ مُنكَرٍ فَعَلُوهُ): the clause has no grammatical position because it explains the disobedience and transgression; كان and its noun; the clause لا يتناهون is its khabar; عن منكر is attached to يتناهون; and the clause فعلوه is a naʿt of منكر. (لَبِئْسَ ما كانُوا يَفْعَلُونَ): the lām is in answer to an omitted oath; بئس is an inflexible (jāmid) past verb for expressing blame; ما is a complete indefinite noun in the position of an accusative as a tamyīz (specification), or a relative noun in the position of a nominative as fāʿil (agent), i.e. "that which they did"; the clause كانوا is a naʿt of ما, or has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila; and the clause يفعلون is in the position of an accusative as the khabar of كانوا.

* Rhetoric:
The rebuke of the Jews contained a report of two things extremely ugly and repulsive: the first, the evils they used to commit; the second, their aversion to forbidding one another these evils and to not inclining to them in the future. This is indicated by the saying of the Exalted: «فعلوه» ("which they did"); for were it not mentioned, someone might imagine that forbidding evil is only when it deserves to be forbidden and when one is about to engage in it. So its mention comprises both matters together, in an eloquent manner and a lofty style, which is the summit of eloquence. What is meant by التناهي is not that each one of them should forbid the other the evil he commits, as is the immediate and well-known sense of the form tafāʿul; rather what is meant is merely that forbidding should issue from multiple persons, without regard to each one being both forbidder and forbidden. So failure in mutual forbidding, after it had been commanded, was disobedience.

* Benefits:
The rule says: when two single parts of their two owners are put in genitive construct with both of them without separation, three ways are permissible in them:
1- The plural form; you say: قطعت رؤوس الكبشين ("I cut off the heads of the two rams").
2- The dual form; you say: قطعت رأسي الكبشين.
3- The singular form; you say: قطعت رأس الكبشين.
And His saying in the verse, على لسان داود وعيسى, is in the singular, not the dual or the plural.

dervis-irab:80-81.t:
* I'rab:
(تَرى كَثِيراً مِنْهُمْ يَتَوَلَّوْنَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا): resumptive speech, brought to address the Prophet concerning the Children of Israel who allied themselves with the disbelievers of the people of Makka.
ترى is an imperfect verb, its fāʿil (agent) a latent (mustatir) pronoun whose implied form is "you"; كثيرا is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); منهم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted naʿt (adjective) of «كثيرا»; the clause يتولون is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), because the seeing here is visual; الذين is a mafʿūl bihi; and the clause كفروا is the ṣila (relative clause). (لَبِئْسَ ما قَدَّمَتْ لَهُمْ أَنْفُسُهُمْ أَنْ سَخِطَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِمْ): the lām occurs in the answer to an omitted oath; بئس is an inflexible (jāmid) past verb for expressing blame, its fāʿil a latent pronoun explained by the word «ما», and «ما» is a complete indefinite noun in the position of an accusative as a tamyīz (specification). «ما» may also be a relative noun in the position of a nominative as fāʿil. The clause of blame has no grammatical position because it is the answer to the oath; the clause قدمت is a naʿt on the first view and the ṣila on the second; لهم is attached to قدمت, and أنفسهم is the fāʿil. أن سخط: أن with what is in its scope is to be interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun), a delayed mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is the clause of the oath [Translator's note: so in the source; what is meant is the clause of blame, بئس ما قدمت], as though it were said: "Evil is their provision for the Hereafter: Allah's anger with them." Some said: the maṣdar is not the specific object of blame (al-makhṣūṣ bil-dhamm), because the anger itself, ascribed to the Creator, Mighty and Majestic, cannot be said to be the thing specifically blamed; rather it is the cause of the anger; on this basis they parsed it as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ. (وَفِي الْعَذابِ هُمْ خالِدُونَ): the wāw is conjunctive; في العذاب is attached to «خالدون»; هم is a mubtadaʾ and خالدون the khabar. (وَلَوْ كانُوا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِاللَّهِ وَالنَّبِيِّ وَما أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْهِ): the wāw is resumptive; لو is conditional; كان and its noun, and the clause يؤمنون is its khabar; بالله is attached to يؤمنون; النبي is conjoined to الله, and ما أنزل إليه is also conjoined. (مَا اتَّخَذُوهُمْ أَوْلِياءَ وَلكِنَّ كَثِيراً مِنْهُمْ فاسِقُونَ): the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition; أولياء is the second object of اتخذ; and لكنّ with its noun and its khabar.

dervis-irab:82-82.t:
* Vocabulary:
(قِسِّيسِينَ): plural of قسّيس, with kasra on the qāf and a doubled sīn with kasra, meaning القسّ, with fatḥa on the qāf and a doubled sīn: one whose rank is between the bishop and the deacon; he is also the priest (الكاهن). It has the plural قسوس; and قسّيس also has the plurals قسّان, with ḍamma on the qāf, أقسّة and قساوسة. Al-Farrāʾ said: it is like مهالبة; the sīns became many, so they changed one of them into a wāw.
Al-Rāghib said: قسيسين is the plural of قسيس, on the pattern فعّيل, a form of intensity like صدّيق; here it is the head of the Christians and their learned man. Its origin is from تقسّس الشيء, when one follows a thing and seeks it out at night; one says تقسّست أصواتهم, i.e. "I tracked their voices at night". Another said: القسّ, with fatḥa on the qāf, is following a thing; from it the learned man of the Christians was called قسيس, because he follows knowledge. One says قسّ الأثر and قصّه, with ṣād too ("he followed the track"). One says قَس and قِس, with fatḥa and kasra on the qāf, and قسيس. As for Quss ibn Sāʿida al-Iyādī, with ḍamma on the qāf, it is a proper name; it may be one of the forms altered by way of becoming a proper name, its origin being قَس or قِس, with fatḥa or kasra on the qāf. He was the most learned of the people of his time.
(رُهْباناً): it may be singular or plural. When it is plural, its singular is راهب, and راهب is then an active participle from the saying: رهب الله فلان, meaning "so-and-so feared Him", يرهبه رهبا with two fatḥas and رهبا with fatḥa on the rāʾ and sukūn on the hāʾ. Among the evidence that it may be a plural among the Arabs is the saying of Kuthayyir ʿAzza:
رهبان مدين والذين عهدتهم ... يبكون من حذر العذاب قعودا
لو يسمعون كما سمعت كلامها ... خرّوا لعزّة ركّعا وسجودا
(The monks of Madyan, and those I knew weeping, seated, for fear of the punishment — if they heard her speech as I heard it, they would fall down before ʿAzza bowing and prostrating.)
الرهبان may also be singular; when it is singular, its plural is رهابين, like قربان and قرابين, and it may also be pluralised as رهابنة when it is so. Among the evidence that it may be a plural among the Arabs [Translator's note: so in the source; the context requires "a singular", as the verse shows] is the saying of the rajaz poet:
لو عاينت رهبان دير في القلل ... لانحدر الرهبان يمشي ونزل
(Had a monk of a monastery on the mountain-tops seen her, the monk would have come down, walking, and descended.)

* I'rab:
(لَتَجِدَنَّ أَشَدَّ النَّاسِ عَداوَةً لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا الْيَهُودَ وَالَّذِينَ أَشْرَكُوا): resumptive speech, brought to classify the People of the Book with respect to affection for the believers, to repeat the vile deeds of the Jews, and the gentleness of temper of the Christians and their readiness to yield to the truth. The lām is in answer to an omitted oath; تجدن is an imperfect verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, and the clause has no grammatical position because it is the answer to the oath; أشد الناس is the first object of تجد; عداوة is a tamyīz (specification); للذين is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) أشد; اليهود is the second mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the reverse is also permissible; الذين is conjoined to اليهود; and the clause أشركوا is the ṣila (relative clause).
(وَلَتَجِدَنَّ أَقْرَبَهُمْ مَوَدَّةً لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا الَّذِينَ قالُوا: إِنَّا نَصارى): the wāw is conjunctive, and the clause is conjoined to what preceded; its i'rab has preceded; and the clause إنا نصارى is in the position of an accusative as the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl). (ذلِكَ بِأَنَّ مِنْهُمْ قِسِّيسِينَ وَرُهْباناً): the clause is resumptive and explanatory; the demonstrative is a mubtadaʾ (subject); the bāʾ is a preposition; أنّ with what is in its scope is to be interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun) made genitive by the bāʾ; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the omitted khabar (predicate) of ذلك; منهم is attached to the omitted, fronted khabar of أنّ; قسيسين is the noun of أنّ; and رهبانا is conjoined to قسيسين. (وَأَنَّهُمْ لا يَسْتَكْبِرُونَ): conjoined to «بأن منهم», and the clause لا يستكبرون is the khabar of أنّ.
[Volume Three]
[Continuation of Sūrat al-Māʾida]

dervis-irab:1-1.t:
* Vocabulary:
(وفى) with a promise: wafāʾ; and أوفى به, īfāʾ: that is, he brought it complete, with nothing lacking. The poet combined the two:
أما ابن طوف فقد أوفى بذمته ... كما وفى بقلاص النجم حاديها
(As for Ibn Ṭawf, he has fulfilled his pledge, as the driver of the she-camels of the star fulfilled [his duty] toward them.)
Of one who does not give full measure it is said: أخسر الكيل ("he shorted the measure"); and of one who does not fulfil the covenant: غدر ("he betrayed") and نقض ("he broke"). And نقض the covenant and the promise are one and the same thing.
(العقود): the plural of عقد (with fatḥa on the first letter), a verbal noun used as a noun and then pluralised. It is the firmly bound covenant, likened to the tying (ʿaqd) of horses and the like. Al-Ḥuṭayʾa said:
قوم إذا عقدوا عقدا لجارهم ... شدّوا العناج وشدّوا فوقها الكربا
(A people who, when they make a pact for their neighbour, tighten the cord and tighten the knots above it.)
In origin it is applied to solid bodies, such as the knot of a rope and the bonding of a building, and then it is borrowed for abstract things, such as the contract of sale, the covenant and the like. The ʿaqd is therefore more specific than the ʿahd (covenant); and what is meant by العقود is what they bind themselves to by contract.
(البهيمة): every four-legged creature on land and sea; and it was said: whatever has no speech, because of the indistinctness (ibhām) in its voice. But by common usage it is restricted to what is other than beasts of prey and birds. So said al-Rāghib. It is reported from al-Zajjāj that the bahīma, among animals, is whatever has no intellect at all. In al-Qāmūs: the bahīma is every creature with four legs even in water, or every living thing that does not discriminate; its plural is bahāʾim.
(الْأَنْعامِ): these are camels, cattle, sheep and goats, and buffaloes. The annexation of بهيمة to الأنعام is for clarification (li-l-bayān), like "the arāk tree" (شجر الأراك); that is: "the eating of the bahīma that is of the livestock has been made lawful for you". Some held that the annexation is in the sense of comparison, that is: "the bahīma that resembles the livestock has been made lawful for you"; it was said: in chewing the cud and in lacking fangs. It is better to say that the point of resemblance that necessitates lawfulness is that they are among the good things (ṭayyibāt), which are the basis of lawfulness. Al-Ḥarīrī said in Durrat al-Ghawwāṣ: "Among that is that they suppose الأنعام to mean النَّعَم; yet the Arabs distinguished between them, making النعم a name for camels specifically, or for the herd in which camels are, and making الأنعام a name for the kinds of livestock, so that some even included in it gazelles and wild asses, clinging to the saying of the Exalted: «أحلت لكم بهيمة الأنعام»." Al-Rāghib said: النعم is specific to camels, and its plural is أنعام. They were so named because they are among the greatest blessings (niʿam) in their eyes. But الأنعام is said of camels, cattle and sheep and goats, and it is not called أنعام unless camels are among its number." Ibn Barrī said: it is a case of predominance (taghlīb), since they gave النعم predominance over the rest; and there is in reality no difference between them, and it is all-inclusive.

* I'rab:
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا أَوْفُوا بِالْعُقُودِ) A resumptive speech, introduced to call for fulfilment of what the contract requires. The i'rab of the vocative has already been given. أوفوا is an imperative verb and its fāʿil; بالعقود is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أوفوا.
(أُحِلَّتْ لَكُمْ بَهِيمَةُ الْأَنْعامِ) The sentence is explicative, because it is a detailing after a general statement, on the basis that العقود includes all the rulings that Allah the Exalted has legislated and commanded those under obligation to fulfil. أحلت is a passive past verb; ولكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أحلت; وبهيمة is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); and الأنعام is a muḍāf ilayhi.
(إِلَّا ما يُتْلى عَلَيْكُمْ غَيْرَ مُحِلِّي الصَّيْدِ وَأَنْتُمْ حُرُمٌ) إلا is a particle of exception, and ما is the excepted. It was said: it is a disconnected exception (munqaṭiʿ), because the expression is not of the genus of the bahīma, and the prohibition is due to something that supervenes, such as death and the like. The sentence يتلى عليكم is the ṣila of the relative. غير is a ḥāl from the pronoun in «لكم»; ومحلي is a muḍāf to «غير», and الصيد is a muḍāf ilayhi to «محلي». The sentence وأنتم حرم, of mubtadaʾ and khabar, is a ḥāl from «محلي الصيد», as if it were said: "We have made lawful for you some of the livestock while you refrain from game, being in iḥrām, so that there be no hardship upon you."
(إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَحْكُمُ ما يُرِيدُ) The sentence gives the reason for the ruling. إن and its ism; the sentence يحكم is its khabar. ما may be a maṣdar particle or a relative, and in either case it is accusative by removal of the preposition (nazʿ al-khāfiḍ), that is: "He rules by His will," or "by that which He wills"; and there is no frivolity in His rulings, nor any defect, nor any injustice.

* Benefits:
The scholars and exegetes expounded at length on what is meant by العقود. In our view it is general, comprising all the covenants of Allah that He entrusted to His servants, of acts of worship and dealings, by which the affairs of this world and the next are together ordered. Fine is the saying of al-Rāghib:
"Contracts, with regard to the thing contracted and the contracting party, are of three kinds: a contract between Allah the Exalted and the servant, a contract between the servant and himself, and a contract between the servant and others among mankind."
The jurists and the scholars of legislation have gone into it extensively, composing long works on it and treating the legal rulings relating to it, which are easy to consult in their proper places.

An eloquent sentence:
The foundation on which contracts rest in Islam is this eloquent, concise and meaningful sentence, «أوفوا بالعقود». It indicates, with force and grace, that every believer must fulfil what he has contracted and bound himself to, and that no one may restrict what the Lawgiver has left unrestricted except by a text from Him. Every saying or deed that people count as a contract is a contract that they must fulfil, as Allah the Exalted commanded, provided it does not involve forbidding what is lawful or permitting what is forbidden, of what is established in the Sharia, such as a contract under compulsion, or to burn someone's house or a tree in an orchard, or for an indecency, or to consume some of people's property wrongfully, such as usury, gambling (maysir) and bribery.

Custom and mutual consent:
All worldly matters are ordered under this, such as sale, hire, partnerships and other worldly dealings. The basis in them is people's custom and their mutual consent, so long as it does not contradict a ruling of the Sharia. This is perfectly clear and firm. Shaykh al-Islām Ibn Taymiyya composed a book called «Madārik al-Qiyās» on the subject of contracts, in which he covered this subject exhaustively, supported by evidence from the Book, the Sunna and the reports of the righteous predecessors; let whoever wishes consult it.

A report on the philosopher al-Kindī:
They mention that the philosopher al-Kindī was told by his companions: "O sage, make for us the like of this Qur'an." He said: "Yes, I shall make the like of part of it." Then he withdrew for many days, and came out and said: "By Allah, I cannot, and no one can bear it. I opened the Mushaf and Sūrat al-Māʾida came out. I looked, and behold, it speaks of fulfilment, forbids breach of faith, makes lawful with a general permission, then makes an exception, then tells of His power and wisdom, in two lines. No one can produce the like of this except in volumes (ajlād)."
That is, in many large volumes.

dervis-irab:2-2.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الشعائر): the plural of شعيرة, which is the mark or sign. It was then made a sign for the rites of the Hajj and its ceremonies.
(الهدي): what is sent as a gift to the Kaʿba, to be slaughtered there and by which one draws near to Allah. He said:
يقولون: من هذا الغريب بأرضنا ... أما والهدايا إنني لغريب
(They say: "Who is this stranger in our land?" By the sacrificial gifts, I am indeed a stranger.)
(القلائد): the plural of قلادة, which is what is hung on the neck. They used to hang on the necks of the camels of the hady a sandal, or a rope, or the loop of a water-skin, or tree bark and the like, so that it would be recognised and no one would molest it. It is therefore on the basis of an omitted muḍāf, that is: "and the owners of the garlands" (ولأصحاب القلائد).
(آمِّينَ) with shadda on the mīm, which has kasra, that is: "heading for, intending".
(يَجْرِمَنَّكُمْ): the imperfect of جرمه الشيء, when he made him bear it and caused him to commit it; that is, to earn it and do it. It runs in the course of «كسب» ("to earn") in taking one object or two.
(الشنآن): intensity of hatred. One says شنئت الرجل أشنؤه, that is, "I hated him". This maṣdar is transmitted (samāʿī) and contrary to the analogical rule in two respects: its verb is transitive and its middle radical is vowelled with kasra, since it is analogical only in intransitive verbs vowelled with fatḥa. It has many maṣdars, which some counted up to thirteen, the best known of which are: شنئا, شنئا, شنئا, شنأة, شنآنا, شنآنا, مشنأ, مشنأة and مشنوءة. [Translator's note: the source prints the first three forms, and the fourth and fifth, identically, because the vowel marks that distinguish them are missing; they are rendered as printed.]

* I'rab:
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا تُحِلُّوا شَعائِرَ اللَّهِ) The i'rab of «يا أيها الذين آمنوا» has been given many times. لا is prohibitive, and تحلوا is an imperfect verb, jussive because of it, the wāw being the fāʿil; and شعائر الله is the mafʿūl bihi.
(وَلَا الشَّهْرَ الْحَرامَ وَلَا الْهَدْيَ وَلَا الْقَلائِدَ وَلَا آمِّينَ الْبَيْتَ الْحَرامَ)
ولا الشهر الحرام is conjoined to شعائر, and الحرام is a naʿt of الشهر. It is the month of the Hajj, which is Dhū al-Qaʿda; al-Ṭabarī insisted that it is Rajab. What follows it is also conjoined to it. ولا آمّين: that is, "and do not violate [the sanctity of] a people heading for ..." (ولا تحلوا قوما آمّين); it is thus a naʿt of an omitted modified noun, and the meaning is: "do not make fighting them lawful so long as they are making for the Sacred House." This is a symbol of the peace to which the Qur'an called. And البيت is the mafʿūl of آمّين, because it is an active participle.
(يَبْتَغُونَ فَضْلًا مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ وَرِضْواناً) The sentence is a ḥāl from the pronoun in «آمّين», that is: "while those heading there are seeking bounty". And فضلا is a mafʿūl bihi; ومن ربهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يبتغون, or to an omitted naʿt of «فضلا»; and رضوانا is conjoined to it.
(وَإِذا حَلَلْتُمْ فَاصْطادُوا) The wāw is a conjunction; إذا is an adverb of future time containing the sense of a condition; the sentence حللتم is in the position of the genitive by annexation; the fāʾ links the apodosis of إذا; and اصطادوا ...
(وَلا يَجْرِمَنَّكُمْ شَنَآنُ قَوْمٍ أَنْ صَدُّوكُمْ عَنِ الْمَسْجِدِ الْحَرامِ أَنْ تَعْتَدُوا) The wāw is a conjunction; لا is prohibitive; ويجرمنكم is an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa, in the position of the jussive because of لا, and the kāf is its first object; وشنآن قوم is the fāʿil. أن صدوكم is an interpreted maṣdar, accusative by removal of the preposition, being the reason for the hatred and attached to it; وعن المسجد is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to صدوكم. أن تعتدوا is an interpreted maṣdar, the second object of يجرمنكم. The meaning is: "Let not hatred of a people, because they barred you from the Sacred Mosque, earn you transgression, nor make you bear it" (ولا يكسبنكم بغض قوم لأنهم صدوكم عن المسجد الحرام الاعتداء ولا يحملنكم عليه).
(وَتَعاوَنُوا عَلَى الْبِرِّ وَالتَّقْوى) The wāw is a conjunction; وتعاونوا is an imperative verb, the wāw being the fāʿil; وعلى البر is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تعاونوا; and التقوى is conjoined to البر.
(وَلا تَعاوَنُوا عَلَى الْإِثْمِ وَالْعُدْوانِ) The wāw is a conjunction; لا is prohibitive; وتعاونوا is an imperfect verb from which one of the two tāʾs has been omitted, jussive because of لا, that is: لا تتعاونوا; وعلى الإثم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to it; and العدوان is conjoined to it.
(وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ إِنَّ اللَّهَ شَدِيدُ الْعِقابِ) Also a conjunction; and the sentence of إن with its ism and khabar has no grammatical position, because it is a giving of reasons.

* Benefits:
The Arabs were agreed on honouring Dhū al-Qaʿda and Dhū al-Ḥijja, and differed about Rajab, so the Exalted made His command strict. This is the reason for singling it out by mention.
It was also said that الشهر is a singular defined by the generic al-, so that what is meant is all the sacred months, which are Dhū al-Qaʿda, Dhū al-Ḥijja, Muḥarram and Rajab.

dervis-irab:3-3.t:
* Vocabulary:
(أُهِلَّ لِغَيْرِ اللَّهِ): ihlāl is raising the voice with it for other than Allah, which is their saying at the slaughter: "In the name of al-Lāt and al-ʿUzzā". One says "so-and-so made ihlāl for the Hajj" (أهلّ فلان بالحج) when he raised his voice in the talbiya; and from it comes "the infant cried out" (استهلّ الصبيّ) when he raises his voice in crying at birth.
(الْمُنْخَنِقَةُ): the author of al-Qāmūs said: خنقه خنقا (like كتف), so he is خنق; and the sheep انخنقت by itself. The rule of the reflexive-passive (muṭāwaʿa) does not apply to this verb; the muṭāwiʿ is rather اختنق. On this basis المنخنقة includes the animal they strangled until it died, or that was strangled by some cause; the details are in the books of fiqh.
(الْمَوْقُوذَةُ): the one they beat severely with a stick or a blunt stone until it died. He said in al-Qāmūs: al-waqdh is severity of beating. And he said in its commentary, Tāj al-ʿArūs: the mawqūdha is the one that is killed with a stick or stones with no edge, until its strength dissolves and it dies. The torment of the animal contained in waqdh is not hidden.
(الْمُتَرَدِّيَةُ): the one that fell from a high place and died.
(النَّطِيحَةُ): the one that another gored and which died from the goring.
An enjoyable discussion of this form will come in the section on Benefits.
(ذَكَّيْتُمْ): that is, you reached its slaughter while it was still convulsing and its jugular veins were gushing.
Dhakāt and tadhkiya in the original language mean the completion of a particular act. One says: ذكت النار تذكو ذكوّا وذكا وذكاء when its kindling is complete; ذكت الشمس when its heat became intense; and ذكى and ذكي (like رمى and رضي) when his sharp-wittedness was complete. He said in al-Lisān: "al-dhakāʾ is the intensity of the blaze of fire. One says ذكيت النار when you completed its kindling and raised it; and al-dhakā is the completion of kindling a fire, shortened (maqṣūr), written with alif." And dhakāʾ in understanding is for the understanding to be complete and quick to accept.
(النُّصُبِ): al-Rāghib said in his Mufradāt: naṣb of a thing is setting it up so that it projects, like setting up a spear, a building or a stone; and al-naṣīb is stones set up over something, its plural being naṣāʾib and nuṣub (with two ḍammas). The Arabs had stones that they worshipped and slaughtered upon. He said: «كأنّهم إلى نصب يوفضون» ("as though they were rushing to a goal"). Its plural is sometimes said to be anṣāb. And he said in al-Lisān: "al-naṣb (with fatḥa), al-nuṣb (with ḍamma) and al-nuṣub (with two ḍammas) mean sickness, affliction and evil, and in the Revelation: «مسّني الشيطان بنصب وعذاب» ("Satan has touched me with hardship and torment"). And al-naṣība and al-nuṣub (with two ḍammas) are everything set up and made into a sign. So al-nuṣub is both singular and plural." Al-Aʿshā said:
وذا النّصب المنصوب لا تعبدنّه ... لعاقبة والله ربّك فاعبدا
(And the erected stone idol, do not worship it for any outcome; but worship Allah, your Lord.)
Its use today for the commemorative monument (al-naṣb al-tadhkārī) is sound and open to no objection.
(الأزلام): the plural of zalam, with two fatḥas, or like ṣurad, that is, with ḍamma then fatḥa: a small arrow-shaft without feathers or head. These were arrows by which they sought a division of fortune in the Jāhiliyya; its plural is azlām. When one of them wished to travel, raid, trade, marry, or undertake an important matter, he struck the shafts, that is, he shook them. There were three, written on one of which: "My Lord has commanded me"; on the second: "My Lord has forbidden me"; and the third was blank, with nothing on it. If the commanding one came out, he went ahead with his purpose (ṭiyya), that is, the intention he had formed; if the forbidding one came out, he did not act and held back; and if the blank came out, he repeated the casting of lots.
(المخمصة): famine.
(مُتَجانِفٍ): deviating, inclining, from al-janaf, which is inclination and injustice.

* I'rab:
(حُرِّمَتْ عَلَيْكُمُ الْمَيْتَةُ وَالدَّمُ وَلَحْمُ الْخِنْزِيرِ) A resumptive speech, introduced to explain what He stated in general terms earlier, namely His saying the Exalted: «إلا ما يتلى عليكم».
حرمت is a passive past verb; وعليكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to حرمت; والميتة is the nāʾib fāʿil; and الدم and لحم الخنزير are conjoined to الميتة.
(وَما أُهِلَّ لِغَيْرِ اللَّهِ بِهِ) Also a conjunction. ما is a relative noun; أهل is a passive past verb, its nāʾib fāʿil being "he" (هو); the sentence is the ṣila of the relative; ولغير الله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أهل; and به is likewise attached to أهلّ.
(وَالْمُنْخَنِقَةُ وَالْمَوْقُوذَةُ وَالْمُتَرَدِّيَةُ وَالنَّطِيحَةُ وَما أَكَلَ السَّبُعُ) All of these are conjoined, entering into the ruling of the forbidden things.
(إِلَّا ما ذَكَّيْتُمْ) إلا is a particle of exception; ما is a relative noun, the excepted, connected (muttaṣil), accusative; the sentence ذكيتم is the ṣila of the relative; and the sentence of exception is a ḥāl clause.
(وَما ذُبِحَ عَلَى النُّصُبِ) The sentence is conjoined to the forbidden things.
(وَأَنْ تَسْتَقْسِمُوا بِالْأَزْلامِ) The interpreted maṣdar is also conjoined, that is: "and seeking division by the divining arrows is forbidden to you" (وحرم عليكم الاستقسام بالأزلام).
(ذلِكُمْ فِسْقٌ) A mubtadaʾ and khabar, and the sentence is resumptive. The demonstrative refers specifically to seeking division by the divining arrows; and it was said: to everything that has preceded.
(الْيَوْمَ يَئِسَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مِنْ دِينِكُمْ) اليوم is an adverb of time attached to يئس, and by it He meant time in the general sense, not one particular day, in line with the saying of Abū al-ʿAlāʾ al-Maʿarrī:
الآن لما ابيضّ مسربتي ... وعضضت من نابي على جذم
حلبت هذا الدهر أشطره ... وأتيت ما آتي على علم
(Now that my chest-hair has turned white, and I have bitten down on a stump where my canine was, I have milked the teats of this age, and I do what I do with knowledge.)
By his word «الآن» he meant the present time. The masraba is the hair of the chest, which is the last part of a person to turn grey; so the whitening of the masraba is a metonymy for his reaching the end of the course in greying and the close of the circuit of life. The meaning of the two verses: it has become my habit to do what I do with knowledge I have from the length of my experience of the events of time. The sentence is resumptive; الذين is a relative noun, the fāʿil; the sentence كفروا is the ṣila; and ومن دينكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يئس, that is: "of nullifying the matter of your religion".
(فَلا تَخْشَوْهُمْ وَاخْشَوْنِ) The fāʾ is the eloquent one (al-fāʾ al-faṣīḥa); لا is prohibitive; وتخشوهم is an imperfect verb, jussive because of لا; واخشوني is an imperative verb with its fāʿil and mafʿūl bihi; and the sentence has no grammatical position.
(الْيَوْمَ أَكْمَلْتُ لَكُمْ دِينَكُمْ) اليوم is an adverb of time attached to أكملت; ولكم is likewise attached to it; ودينكم is the mafʿūl bihi of أكملت; and the sentence is resumptive.
(وَأَتْمَمْتُ عَلَيْكُمْ نِعْمَتِي) Conjoined to what has preceded; وعليكم is attached to أتممت; and نعمتي is the mafʿūl bihi of أتممت.
