(وَرَضِيتُ لَكُمُ الْإِسْلامَ دِيناً) The wāw is resumptive; رضيت is a verb and fāʿil; لكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl, because it was originally a naʿt of «دينا»; and دينا is a mafʿūl bihi or a tamyīz, because the meaning of رضيت is "I made" (جعلت). If it is in the sense of being pleased, then «دينا» is a ḥāl from الإسلام and لكم is attached to رضيت.
(فَمَنِ اضْطُرَّ فِي مَخْمَصَةٍ) The fāʾ is resumptive; من is a conditional noun, jussive-governing, a mubtadaʾ; اضطر is a passive past verb in the position of the jussive as the protasis, its nāʾib fāʿil being "he", referring to من; and في مخمصة is attached to اضطر.
(غَيْرَ مُتَجانِفٍ لِإِثْمٍ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ) غير متجانف is accusative as a ḥāl; ولإثم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to متجانف; the fāʾ links the apodosis; and إن with its ism and its two khabars [Translator's note: the source says «وخبراها» ("its two khabars"), meaning غفور and رحيم]; the sentence joined by the fāʾ is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis; and the protasis together with its apodosis is the khabar of «من».

* Benefits:
When the form faʿīl has the sense of mafʿūl, masculine and feminine are alike in it, and no feminine marker is attached to it. The Arabs say: ʿayn kaḥīl, not kaḥīla ("a kohl-darkened eye"), and kaff khaḍīb, not khaḍība ("a henna-dyed palm"). How, then, was the tāʾ attached to «نطيحة» when it has the sense of manṭūḥa? It has been said in reply that the tāʾ here is for transfer from the adjectival to the nominal, or that faʿīl here has the sense of fāʿil, as if He had said: "and the goring one that dies from goring", that is, it gores another and the other gores it, and it dies. The Kufans said: attaching the tāʾ to faʿīl in the sense of mafʿūl is prevented only when it is an adjective of a mentioned modified noun, as in ʿayn kaḥīl; but when the modified noun has not been mentioned before, attaching the tāʾ is not prevented. This is a fine explanation, for "dhabīḥa" and "naṭīḥa" and the like, when no modified noun precedes them, would not be known to be masculine or feminine. For example: "I saw a wounded one" (رأيت جريحة). But when it is known, no: for example, "I saw a wounded woman" (رأيت امرأة جريحا), or "I saw a wounded female cast on the road" (رأيت جريحا ملقاة في الطريق).

farraa:1-1.t:
Of His saying, Blessed and Exalted: ﴿أَوْفُواْ بِٱلْعُقُود﴾ — He means: the covenants. [Al-ʿuqūd] and al-ʿuhūd are one and the same.
His saying: ﴿أُحِلَّتْ لَكُمْ بَهِيمَةُ ٱلأَنْعَامِ﴾ — these are wild cattle, gazelles and wild asses.
His saying: ﴿إِلاَّ مَا يُتْلَىٰ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ — it is in the position of the accusative by exception; the nominative is permissible, just as "qāma al-qawmu illā Zaydan" and "illā Zaydun" are permissible. The meaning in it is: except what We make clear to you of the prohibition of what is forbidden while you are in the state of iḥrām, or in the sacred precinct. That is His saying ﴿غَيْرَ مُحِلِّي ٱلصَّيْدِ﴾ — He is saying: these are made lawful for you, while you do not hold game to be lawful ﴿وَأَنْتُمْ حُرُمٌ﴾. Similar to it is ﴿إلَى طَعَامٍ غَيْرَ ناظِرِينَ إنَاهُ﴾. It is equivalent to your saying: "This thing is made lawful for you, neither being excessive in it nor transgressing."
When you put (غير) in place of (لا), the accusative that comes after «لا» passes to «غير». Had it been (محلِّين الصيد), you would have put it in the accusative, as Allah, Majestic and Mighty, said ﴿ولا آمِّين الْبَيْتَ الحَرَامَ﴾; and in the reading of ʿAbdallāh: (ولا آمِّى البيتِ الحرامِ).
﴿إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَحْكُمُ مَا يُرِيدُ﴾: He decrees what He wills.

farraa:19-19.t: His saying: ﴿يُبَيِّنُ لَكُمْ عَلَىٰ فَتْرَةٍ مَّنَ ٱلرُّسُلِ أَن تَقُولُواْ﴾ — its meaning is: lest you say: ﴿مَا جَآءَنَا مِن بَشِيرٍ﴾; like what He said: ﴿يُبَيِّنُ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ أَنْ تَضِلّوا﴾.

farraa:2-2.t:
His saying: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ لاَ تُحِلُّواْ شَعَآئِرَ ٱللَّهِ﴾ — most of the Arabs did not consider al-Ṣafā and al-Marwa to be among the rites, and did not go between them. So Allah, Blessed and Exalted, sent down: do not regard abandoning that as lawful.
His saying: ﴿وَلاَ ٱلشَّهْرَ ٱلْحَرَامَ﴾: nor fighting in the sacred month.
﴿وَلاَ ٱلْهَدْيَ﴾ — this is the sacrificial animal of the polytheists: [do not] interfere with it, nor frighten anyone who has garlanded his camel. When one of the Arabs wanted to travel outside the sacred months, he would garland his camel and thereby be safe. So He said: do not frighten anyone who has put on a garland. The people of Mecca used to garland with tree bark, and the rest of the Arabs with camel hair and [goat] hair.
His saying: ﴿وَلاۤ آمِّينَ ٱلْبَيْتَ﴾ — He is saying: and do not prevent any of the polytheists who are heading for the Sacred House or intend it. Then this verse was abrogated by the one in [Sūrat] al-Tawba: ﴿فاقْتُلُوا الْمُشْرِكينَ حَيْثُ وَجَدتُّمُوهُمْ﴾ to the end of the verse.
His saying: ﴿وَلاَ يَجْرِمَنَّكُمْ﴾ — Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb and al-Aʿmash read it "wa-lā yujrimannakum", from ajramtu. The speech of the Arabs and the reading of the readers is ﴿يَجرِمنكم﴾ with fatḥa on the yāʾ. The exegesis has come: "and let not hatred of a people drive you." Al-Farrāʾ said: I heard the Arabs say: "So-and-so is the jarīma of his family," meaning: the earner for his family; and "he went out to yajrimuhum," i.e. to earn for them. The meaning in it is close: "let not hatred of a people earn you [i.e. lead you to] doing evil." So (أن) is in the position of the accusative. [Translator's note: «فى وضع تصب» in the text is evidently a misprint for «فى موضع نصب».]
If you place (على) before (أن), you take it in the sense of: "let not their hatred drive you to such-and-such — to not being just"; so it is fine to drop (على), just as you say: "It drove me to ask (an asʾala)" and "to asking (ʿalā an asʾala)."
﴿وَلاَ يَجْرِمَنَّكُمْ شَنَآنُ قَوْمٍ﴾ — some read «الشنآن» heavy [i.e. shanaʾān, with a vowel on the nūn], and most of the readers read it light [shanʾān].
Both the light and the heavy form have been transmitted from al-Aʿmash. It means: "let not hatred of a people drive you." The proper way, when it is a maṣdar (verbal noun), is to make it heavy; and if you mean by it "one who is hated by a people", you say: shanʾān.
And ﴿أَن صَدُّوكُمْ﴾ is in the position of the accusative because a preposition is fit [to be supplied] before it. Had it been read with kasra in the sense of a condition (jazāʾ), it would have been correct. In the text (ḥarf) of ʿAbdallāh it is (إِن يَصدُّوكم). If you read it with kasra, you make the verb future; if with fatḥa, you make it past. If you make it a condition with kasra, that is fine, as in His saying ﴿أفَنَضْرِبُ عَنْكُمُ الذِّكْرَ صَفْحاً إِنْ كُنْتُمْ﴾, where [it is read] «أن» with fatḥa and with kasra. Likewise ﴿أَوْلِيَاءَ إِن اسْتَحَبُّوا الكُفْرَ عَلَى الإيمَانِ﴾ is read with kasra, and had it been with fatḥa it would have been correct. And His saying ﴿باخِعٌ نَفْسَكَ أَلاَّ يَكُونُوا مُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ [admits] both fatḥa and kasra. As for His saying ﴿بَلِ اللّهُ يَمُنُّ عَلَيْكُم أَنْ هَدَاكُمْ لِلإيمانِ﴾, (أَنْ) has fatḥa because its meaning is past, as though you said: "He has favoured you in that He guided you." Had you intended the future, kasra would be permissible in it; but fatḥa is the proper way because the first of the two verbs is past. If you say "I honoured you because you came to me (an ataytanī)," kasra of «أن» is not permissible, because the verb is past.
His saying: ﴿وَتَعَاوَنُواْ﴾ — it is in the position of the jussive, because it is a command, and it is not conjoined to ﴿تَعْتَدُواْ﴾.

farraa:3-3.t:
His saying: ﴿وَمَآ أُهِلَّ لِغَيْرِ ٱللَّهِ بِهِ﴾ — ﴿وَمَآ﴾ is in the position of the nominative by the verb whose agent is not named [i.e. as nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of the passive «حُرِّمت»].
﴿وَٱلْمُنْخَنِقَةُ﴾: that which was strangled and died and was not reached [in time to be slaughtered].
﴿وَٱلْمَوْقُوذَةُ﴾: that which was beaten until it died and was not ritually slaughtered.
﴿وَٱلْمُتَرَدِّيَةُ﴾: that which fell from the top of a mountain or into a well, and was not reached in time for its ritual slaughter.
﴿وَٱلنَّطِيحَةُ﴾: that which was gored to death. All of that is forbidden if its ritual slaughter was not reached in time.
His saying: ﴿إِلاَّ مَا ذَكَّيْتُمْ﴾ — accusative and nominative [are both possible].
﴿وَمَا ذُبِحَ عَلَى ٱلنُّصُبِ﴾: what was slaughtered for the idols. (ما ذبح) is in the position of the nominative and nothing else.
﴿وَأَنْ تَسْتَقْسِمُواْ﴾ — nominative by the verb whose agent is not named. Al-istiqsām: there used to be arrows in the Kaʿba; on some of them [was written] "My Lord has commanded me", (and in its place: "My Lord has forbidden me"). When one of them wanted to travel, he would take out two arrows and shuffle them; if the one on which was "My Lord has commanded me" came out, he went out; and if the one on which was "My Lord has forbidden me" came out, he stayed and refrained from going out.
Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: ﴿ذٰلِكُمْ فِسْقٌ ٱلْيَوْمَ﴾ — the statement breaks off at «الفسق», and ﴿ٱلْيَوْمَ﴾ is accusative by (يئِس), not by «الفسق».
﴿اليومَ أُحِلَّ لَكُمُ الطّيِّباتُ﴾ — (اليوم) is accusative by (أُحِلّ).
His saying: ﴿غَيْرَ مُتَجَانِفٍ لإِثْمٍ ﴾ is like His saying ﴿غير محلّى الصيد﴾ — He is saying: not deliberately inclining to sin. (غير) is accusative because it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of (مَنْ), and it comes out of the noun [the pronoun] that is in (اضطرّ).

farraa:4-4.t:
His saying: ﴿وَمَا عَلَّمْتُمْ مِّنَ ٱلْجَوَارِحِ﴾ — He means the dogs. And ﴿مُكَلِّبِينَ﴾ is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) coming out of (لكم); by «مكلِّبين» He means the men who own the hunting dogs. One of them is called mukallib and kallāb. The position of (ما) is nominative.
His saying: ﴿تُعَلِّمُونَهُنَّ﴾: you train them not to eat their catch.
Then He, Blessed and Exalted, said ﴿فَكُلُواْ مِمَّآ أَمْسَكْنَ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ — of what they have not eaten from. If it [the dog] has eaten, it is not lawful, because it held it only for itself.

farraa:6-6.t:
His saying: ﴿وَأَرْجُلَكُمْ﴾ — it is referred back to «الوجوه» [i.e. accusative, conjoined to the faces to be washed]. Al-Farrāʾ said: Qays ibn al-Rabīʿ related to me from ʿĀṣim, from Zirr, from ʿAbdallāh ibn Masʿūd, that he read (وأرجلكم) [as being] placed out of order [i.e. belonging, in meaning, with the washed limbs]. Al-Farrāʾ said: Muḥammad ibn Abān al-Qurashī related to me from Abū Isḥāq al-Hamdānī, from a man, from ʿAlī, that he said: "The Book came down with wiping, and the Sunna is washing." Al-Farrāʾ said: Abū Shihāb related to me from a man, from al-Shaʿbī, who said: "Gabriel ﷺ came down to Muhammad — may Allah bless them both and all the prophets — with wiping." Al-Farrāʾ said: The Sunna is washing.
His saying: ﴿أَوْ جَآءَ أَحَدٌ مِّنْكُمْ مِّنَ ٱلْغَائِطِ﴾ — an allusion to a man's going off alone when he wants to relieve himself.

farraa:8-8.t: His saying: ﴿ٱعْدِلُواْ هُوَ أَقْرَبُ لِلتَّقْوَىٰ﴾ — had (هو) not been in the utterance, (أقرب) would have been accusative. In this position the action is referred to by «هو» and by «ذلك»; both are fit. He said in another place: ﴿إِذَا نَاجَيْتُمُ الرَّسُولَ فَقَدِّمُوا بَيْنَ يَدَىْ نَجْواكُم صَدَقَةً ذَلِكَ خَيْرٌ لَكُمْ وَأَطْهَرُ﴾, and in [Sūrat] al-Ṣaff ﴿ذَلِكُمْ خَيْرٌ لَكُمْ﴾. Had neither (هو) nor (ذلك) been in the utterance, it would have been accusative, as in His saying ﴿انْتَهُوا خَيْراً لَكُمْ﴾.

farraa:20-20.t:
His saying: ﴿إِذْ جَعَلَ فِيكُمْ أَنْبِيَآءَ﴾ — He means the seventy whom Moses chose to go with him to the mountain; He called them prophets for this reason.
﴿وَجَعَلَكُمْ مُّلُوكاً﴾ — He is saying: each of you is a king in his own house; no one enters upon him except with permission.
﴿وَآتَاكُمْ مَّا لَمْ يُؤْتِ أَحَداً مِّن ٱلْعَٱلَمِينَ﴾ — He shaded you with the white clouds and sent down to you manna and quails.

farraa:21-21.t: His saying: ﴿ادْخُلُوا الأَرْضَ المُقَدَّسَةَ﴾ — it is mentioned that the Holy Land is Damascus, Palestine (Filasṭūn) and part of al-Urdunn (with a doubled nūn).

farraa:24-24.t:
His saying: ﴿فَٱذْهَبْ أَنتَ وَرَبُّكَ فَقَاتِلاۤ﴾ — He said (أنت); had (أنت) been dropped, so that it were said "idhhab wa-rabbuka fa-qātilā", it would have been correct, because in one of the two readings it is (إِنه يراكم وقبِيلُه) without (هو), while [the other] has «هو». But (اذهب أنت وربك) is more frequent in the speech of the Arabs. That is because conjoining [a noun] to a nominative noun that is only implied is disliked, for the nominative is hidden in the verb; it is not like the accusative, because the accusative appears: you say "ḍarabtuhu" and "ḍarabtuka", while for the nominative you say "qāma" and "qāmā", so that you do not see a noun separate from the verb in its basic form. That is why expressing it is preferred. Yet Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said ﴿أَئِذَا كُنّا تُرَاباً وَآبَاؤُنَا﴾ and did not say (نحن); and all of it is correct.
When you separate [the verb] from the conjoined noun by something on which the verb has fallen, it becomes fairly acceptable.
Of that is your saying: "I struck Zayd, and you [did too] (wa-anta)." Were there no "Zayd", you would say "qumtu anā wa-anta"; "qumtu wa-anta" is rare. Had it been (إِنا ها هنا قاعدين) [in the accusative], it would have been correct.

farraa:26-26.t:
His saying: ﴿أَرْبَعِينَ سَنَةً﴾ — it is accusative by «التحريم» [i.e. by «مُحَرَّمة»]. Had you cut off the statement [after «عليهم»] and put it in the accusative by His saying (يَتِيهُونَ), it would have been correct.
Similar to it in speech is your saying: "la-uʿṭiyannaka thawban tarḍā" ("I will surely give you a garment you will be pleased with"): you put «ثوب» in the accusative by the giving; and had you put it in the accusative by «الرضا», cutting it off from (لأعطينك), it would have been correct. [Translator's note: «صوبا» in the text is evidently a misprint for «صوابا».]

farraa:27-27.t: His saying: ﴿فَتُقُبِّلَ مِن أَحَدِهِمَا وَلَمْ يُتَقَبَّلْ مِنَ ٱلآخَرِ قَالَ لأَقْتُلَنَّكَ﴾ — He did not say "the one from whom it was not accepted said (لأقتلنَّك)", because the meaning shows that the one from whom it was not accepted is the one who said, out of envy of his brother, "I will surely kill you." Similar to it in speech is your saying: "When the fool and the forbearing man come together, he is praised," meaning by the praise the forbearing one; and "When you see the wrongdoer and the wronged, you help," meaning "you help the wronged," because the meaning is unambiguous. But if you said "A man and a woman passed by me, and I helped," meaning one of them, it would not be permissible until you made it clear, because there is no sign in them by which one can infer where the help went — unless you mean: "and I helped them both."

farraa:30-30.t: His saying: ﴿فَطَوَّعَتْ لَهُ نَفْسُهُ قَتْلَ أَخِيهِ﴾ — He means: it went along with him.

farraa:32-32.t:
His saying: ﴿مِنْ أَجْلِ ذٰلِكَ﴾ — it is the answer to [i.e. follows from] the son of Adam's killing his companion.
His saying: ﴿وَمَنْ أَحْيَاهَا﴾ — He is saying: whoever pardons it; "giving life" here is pardoning.

farraa:33-33.t:
His saying: ﴿إِنَّمَا جَزَآءُ ٱلَّذِينَ يُحَارِبُونَ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ وَيَسْعَوْنَ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ فَسَاداً أَن يُقَتَّلُوۤاْ أَوْ يُصَلَّبُوۤاْ أَوْ تُقَطَّعَ﴾ — (أن) is in the position of the nominative [as the khabar (predicate)].
When a man has shed blood, taken property and made the road unsafe, he is crucified. When he has killed but not taken property, he is killed. When he has taken property but not killed, his right hand and left foot are cut off "on opposite sides". In place of (مِن) [in «مِن خلاف»], «على», the bāʾ and the lām are also fit.
His banishment (nafy) is that it be proclaimed: "Whoever kills him, his blood may be shed with impunity." This is the banishment.

farraa:38-38.t:
His saying: ﴿وَٱلسَّارِقُ وَٱلسَّارِقَةُ فَٱقْطَعُوۤاْ أَيْدِيَهُمَا﴾ — both are nominative by the pronoun that refers back to them. The accusative is permissible in them, just as "a-Zaydun ḍarabtahu?" and "a-Zaydan ḍarabtahu?" are permissible. The Arabs prefer the nominative in "the male thief and the female thief" only because they are [not] specific; so they were treated like a conditional, as in your saying: "Whoever steals, cut off his hand," where (من) can only be nominative. Had you meant a particular male thief or a particular female thief, the accusative would be the proper form of speech. Similar to it is ﴿واللذانِ يأتيانها مِنكم فآذوهما﴾. In the reading of ʿAbdallāh: "والسارقون والسارقات فاقطعوا أيمانهما".
He said (أيدِيهما) [plural] only because every single member of the human body, when mentioned as annexed to two or more, is put in the plural. Thus it is said: "I smashed their [two] heads (ruʾūsahumā)," and "I filled their [two] backs and bellies (ẓuhūrahumā wa-buṭūnahumā) with blows."
Similar to it is ﴿إِن تَتُوبَا إِلى الله فقَدْ صَغَتْ قُلُوبُكُما﴾.
The plural was preferred over the dual only because most of the limbs in a human being come in twos: the two hands, the two feet and the two eyes. Since most of them follow this pattern, a single member, when annexed to two [persons], was treated in the manner of the dual. The dual is also permissible; Abū Dhuʾayb said:
فتخالسا نَفْسَيهِما بنوافذ * كنوافِذِ العُبُط التى لا ترقَع
(So the two snatched each other's lives with piercing thrusts, like the rents in [garments] torn fresh that cannot be patched.)
This is also permissible in what is not a part of the human body: you say to two men "khallaytumā nisāʾakumā" ("you have let your wives go"), meaning two women, and "kharaqtumā qumuṣakumā" ("you have torn your shirts").
I have mentioned that only because some grammarians used to permit it only for parts of the human body, whereas all are the same. It is also permissible to say in speech: "As for the male and female thief, cut off their right hand (yamīnahumā)," because the meaning is: the right hand of each of them; as the poet said:
كُلُوا فى نصف بطنِكم تعِيشوا * فإنَّ زمانكم زمن خمِيص
(Eat to half [the capacity] of your belly [singular] and you will live, for your time is a time of hunger.)
And another said:
الواردون وتَيْم فى ذرى سبأٍ * قد عضَّ أعناقهم جِلدُ الجوامِيس
(Those who come down to water, and Taym, in the shelter of Sabaʾ — the hide of the buffaloes [i.e. the yokes] has bitten their necks.)
Whoever says (ذَرَى) [darā] takes Sabaʾ as a people, and whoever says (ذُرَى) [durā] means a place.
It is permissible in speech to say: "Bring me the head of two sheep (raʾsa shātayni)" and "the head of a sheep". When you say "the head of a sheep", you mean two heads of this kind; and when you say "the head of two sheep", you mean by it the head of each sheep. The poet said, on another matter:
كأنه وَجْه تركِيَّينِ قد غضِبا * مستهدف لِطعانٍ غيرِ تذبيب
(As though it were the face [singular] of two Turks who have become angry, exposed to thrusts that do not falter.)

farraa:41-41.t: His saying: ﴿وَمِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ هَادُواْ سَمَّاعُونَ لِلْكَذِبِ﴾ — if you wish, you can make His saying "سمَّاعون للكذب" nominative by «مِن» [i.e. as the mubtadaʾ (subject) with the prepositional phrase as its khabar (predicate)], without making (مِن) connected in meaning to what precedes it, as Allah said: ﴿فمِنهم ظالِم لِنفسِهِ ومِنهم مقتصِد﴾. And if you wish, the meaning is: "Let not those who hasten into unbelief grieve you — of these, and ﴿وَمِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ هَادُواْ﴾"; you then make (سمَّاعون) nominative as a fresh start (istiʾnāf). It is then like His saying ﴿لِيستأذِنكم الذِين ملكت أيمانُكُمْ والذِين لم يبلغوا الحُلُم مِنكم﴾, after which He, Blessed and Exalted, said: ﴿طوَّافون عليكم﴾. Had "sammāʿīna" and "ṭawwāfīna" been said, it would have been correct, as He said ﴿ملعونِين أينما ثُقِفوا﴾, and as He said ﴿إن المتَّقِين في جَنَّاتٍ وعُيونٍ﴾ and then said ﴿آخِذين، وفاكِهِين، ومتكئِين﴾. The accusative is more frequent. He also said, with the nominative: ﴿ كلاَّ إِنها لظى نزَّاعة لِلشوى﴾, putting (نزَّاعة) in the nominative as a fresh start, although it is an indefinite describing a definite. Likewise His saying ﴿لا تبقِى ولا تذر لَوَّاحَة﴾. And in the reading of Ubayy: "إِنها لإِحدا الكُبَر نِذير لِلبشرِ" without alif [i.e. nominative «نذير»]. So whatever of this kind comes to you in speech, you may put in the accusative or the nominative. Its accusative is by qaṭʿ (cutting off) or as a ḥāl (circumstantial). When praise or blame fits it, that is a third way; and when you put it in the accusative for blame or praise, it is fine to put its definite form in the accusative just as you did its indefinite. Likewise His saying ﴿سمَّاعون لِلكذبِ أكَّالون لِلسُّحتِ﴾ follows what I have mentioned to you.

farraa:45-45.t:
His saying: ﴿وَكَتَبْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ فِيهَآ أَنَّ ٱلنَّفْسَ بِٱلنَّفْسِ﴾ — (النفس) is put in the accusative because (أَنّ) falls on it. In His saying ﴿وَٱلْعَيْنَ بِٱلْعَيْنِ وَٱلأَنْفَ بِٱلأَنْفِ﴾ up to His saying ﴿وَٱلْجُرُوحَ قِصَاصٌ﴾ you have the choice: if you wish, you use the nominative, and if you wish, the accusative. Ḥamza used the accusative and al-Kisāʾī the nominative. Al-Farrāʾ said: Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Yaḥyā related to me from Abān ibn Abī ʿAyyāsh, from Anas, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ read: (والعين بِالعين) in the nominative. Al-Farrāʾ said: If you put «العين» in the nominative, the rest of the statement follows «العين»; and if you put it in the accusative, that is permissible. Some used to put all of it in the accusative, and when they reached ﴿وَٱلْجُرُوحَ قِصَاصٌ﴾ they used the nominative. All is correct; except that the nominative and accusative in what is conjoined to inna and anna are easy only when there are verbs [i.e. predicates] with the nouns, as in His saying ﴿وإذا قيل إن وعد اللّهِ حق والساعة لا ريب فِيها﴾: the accusative was easy because after «الساعة» comes its khabar. Similar is ﴿إن الأرض لِلّهِ يورِثها من يشاء مِن عبادِهِ والعاقِبة لِلمتقِين﴾, and similar is ﴿وإِن الظالِمِين بعضُهم أولياءُ بعضٍ والله وَلِىُّ المتقِين﴾. But when there is no khabar after the second noun, you put it in the nominative, as in His saying, Mighty and Majestic, ﴿أنَّ الله برئ مِن المشرِكِين ورسوله﴾ and His saying ﴿فإن الله هو مولاه وجِبرِيل وصالِح المؤمِنين﴾. Likewise you say: "inna akhāka qāʾimun wa-Zaydun" — you put (زيد) in the nominative by making it follow the implied pronoun in «قائم». Build on this. [Translator's note: «نصبنه» in the text is evidently for «نصبته».]
His saying: ﴿فَمَن تَصَدَّقَ بِهِ فَهُوَ كَفَّارَةٌ لَّهُ﴾ — He referred (to [the act] with «هو»); this is [done] with an act from which faʿala and yafʿalu are formed, as you say: "The caravan has arrived, and I was glad of it," meaning: of its arrival.
His saying ﴿كَفَّارَةٌ لَّهُ﴾ — He means: [an expiation] for the one who inflicted the wound and committed the offence, and a reward for the wounded one.

farraa:46-46.t:
His saying: ﴿وَآتَيْنَاهُ ٱلإِنجِيلَ فِيهِ هُدًى﴾, then He said ﴿وَمُصَدِّقاً﴾ — if you wish, you can make ﴿مُصَدِّقاً﴾ a description of Jesus, and if you wish, a description of the Gospel.
His saying ﴿وَهُدًى وَمَوْعِظَةً لِّلْمُتَّقِينَ﴾ follows «المصدّق» in its accusative; had you put it in the nominative, making it follow His saying ﴿فِيهِ هُدًى وَنُورٌ﴾, it would have been correct.

farraa:47-47.t: His saying: ﴿وَلْيَحْكُمْ أَهْلُ ٱلإِنْجِيلِ﴾ — Ḥamza and others read it with the accusative, the lām being taken in the sense of «كى» (in order that). And ﴿وَلْيَحْكُمْ﴾ has been read with the jussive, as a lām of command.

farraa:49-49.t: His saying: ﴿وَأَنِ ٱحْكُم بَيْنَهُمْ﴾ — this is evidence that His saying (وليحكم) is jussive, because it is speech in which one part is conjoined to another.

farraa:53-53.t: His saying: ﴿وَيَقُولُ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ﴾ — it is a fresh start, in the nominative. Had it been put in the accusative, referring it back to His saying ﴿فعسى الله أَن يأْتِى بِالفتحِ أَو أَمرٍ مِن عِندِهِ﴾, it would have been correct. In the codices of the people of Medina it is (يقول الذين آمنوا) without the wāw.

farraa:54-54.t: His saying: ﴿يُحِبُّهُمْ وَيُحِبُّونَهُ أَذِلَّةٍ عَلَى ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ — genitive: you make it a naʿt (adjective) for (لقوم). Had you put it in the accusative by qaṭʿ (cutting off) from their pronouns in ﴿يُحِبُّهُمْ وَيُحِبُّونَهُ﴾, it would have been a valid way. In the reading of ʿAbdallāh: (أَذلَّة على المؤمنين غلظاء على الكافرين). "Adhilla" means: merciful to them.

farraa:57-57.t: His saying: ﴿وَٱلْكُفَّارَ أَوْلِيَآءَ﴾ — in the reading of Ubayy: (ومن الكفار). Whoever puts it in the accusative refers it back to ﴿ٱلَّذِينَ ٱتَّخَذُواْ﴾.

farraa:59-59.t: His saying: ﴿وَأَنَّ أَكْثَرَكُمْ فَاسِقُونَ﴾ — (أنّ) is in the position of the accusative, on the basis of His saying ﴿هَلْ تَنقِمُونَ مِنَّآ﴾ [anything] except our faith and your iniquity. (أن) is in the position of a maṣdar (verbal noun). Had you begun afresh, (وإن اكثركم فاسقون), with kasra, it would have been correct.

farraa:60-60.t:
His saying: ﴿قُلْ هَلْ أُنَبِّئُكُمْ بِشَرٍّ مِّن ذٰلِكَ مَثُوبَةً﴾ — (مثوبة) is accusative because it is explanatory [i.e. tamyīz (specification)], as in His saying ﴿أَنا أَكثر مِنك مالا وأَعزُّ نَفَرا﴾.
His saying: ﴿مَن لَّعَنَهُ ٱللَّهُ ﴾ — (من) is in the position of the genitive, referring it back to (بِشرّ). If you wish, you can begin afresh with it and put it in the nominative, as He said: ﴿قل أَفَأُنبئكم بِشر مِن ذلِكم النار وعدها الله الذِين كفروا﴾. You could also put (من) in the accusative according to your saying "I will inform you of (من)", as you say "I informed you of good" and "I informed you that Zayd was standing (Zaydan qāʾiman)". But the proper way is the genitive.
His saying ﴿وَعَبَدَ ٱلطَّاغُوتَ﴾ is on the basis of His saying: "and He made of them apes [and swine] and whoever worshipped the ṭāghūt". In the reading of Ubayy and ʿAbdallāh it is (وعبدوا), in the plural. The companions of ʿAbdallāh used to read "وعَبَد الطاغوتِ" on the pattern faʿal, annexing it to «الطاغوت», and explaining it as: the servants of the ṭāghūt. Some people intended this meaning and gave the ʿayn a ḍamma, saying "ʿubudu al-ṭāghūti", like thimār and thumur — a plural of a plural.
Had a reader read (وعَبَد الطاغوتِ), it would be correct and good: he would mean "ʿabadat al-ṭāghūt" ("worshippers of the ṭāghūt"), dropping the hāʾ [i.e. the tāʾ marbūṭa] because of the annexation; as the poet said:
* قام وُلاَها فسقَوها صَرْخدا *
(Her keepers rose and gave her Ṣarkhad wine to drink.)
He means: wulātuhā. As for His saying (وعَبُد الطاغوت): if there is a dialect form in it like ḥadhir and ḥadhur and ʿajul, then it is a valid way; otherwise he meant — and Allah knows best — [what is in] the poet's saying:
أَبَنِى لُبَيْنَى إِنّ أمَّكُمُ * أَمَةٌ وإِن أباكم عَبُد
(O sons of Lubaynā, your mother is a slave-woman and your father is a slave.)
This is permissible in poetry by the necessity of rhymes; but in Quranic reading it is not.

farraa:64-64.t:
His saying: ﴿وَقَالَتِ ٱلْيَهُودُ يَدُ ٱللَّهِ مَغْلُولَةٌ﴾ — they meant: withheld from spending and from bestowing abundantly upon us. It is like His saying ﴿ولا تجعلْ يَدَكَ مَغْلُولَةً إِلى عُنُقك ولا تَبْسُطْها كلَّ البَسْطِ﴾, concerning spending.
﴿بَلْ يَدَاهُ مَبْسُوطَتَانِ﴾ — in the text of ʿAbdallāh: (بل يداه بُِسْطَانِ). The Arabs say: "Meet your brother with an open (mabsūṭ) face," and "with an open (busṭ / basṭ) face."

farraa:66-66.t: His saying: ﴿لأَكَلُواْ مِن فَوْقِهِمْ وَمِن تَحْتِ أَرْجُلِهِم﴾ — He is saying: from the rain of the sky and the growth of the earth, its fruits and other things. It is also said that this is by way of [expressing] abundance, as you say: "He is in good from his head to his foot."

farraa:69-69.t:
His saying: ﴿إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ وَٱلَّذِينَ هَادُواْ وَٱلصَّابِئُونَ وَٱلنَّصَارَىٰ﴾ — (الصابِئين) is put in the nominative as being conjoined to (الذين). (الذين) is a word with one form in its nominative, accusative and genitive; so since its case-form is one, and since the accusative of (إنّ) is a weak accusative — its weakness being that it falls on (the noun and does not fall on) its khabar (predicate) — the nominative of «الصابئين» became permissible.
I do not like to say "inna ʿAbdallāhi wa-Zaydun qāʾimāni", because the case is visible in «عبدالله». Al-Kisāʾī used to permit it, because of the weakness of inna. They have recited this verse to us both with the nominative and with the accusative:
فمن يك أمسى بالمدينةِ رحلُهُ * فإنِى وقَيَّارا بها لغرِيب
(Whoever has his lodging in Medina [is at home], but I and Qayyār are strangers there.)
— and «وقَيَّارٌ». This is not evidence for al-Kisāʾī in his permitting "inna ʿAmran wa-Zaydun qāʾimāni", because «قيار» has been conjoined to a pronoun, and the pronoun has no [visible] case-ending; so that was made easy (in it, just as it was made easy) in (الذين) when (الصابئون) is conjoined to it. Indeed this is stronger in permissibility than (الصابئون), because the nominative is never visible in the pronoun, whereas with (الذين) one sometimes says «اللذون», so that it is nominative in one case.
Someone recited to me:
وإلاَّ فاعلموا أَنَّا وأَنتم * بُغَاة ما حيِينا فى شِقاقِ
(Otherwise know that we and you [nominative] are rebels, as long as we live, in discord.)
And another said:
يا ليتنى وأَنتِ يا لَمِيسُ * ببلدٍ ليس به أنِيس
(Would that I and you, O Lamīs, were in a land where there is no one.)
And someone recited to me:
يا ليتنى وهما نخلو بمنزِلةٍ * حتى يرى بعضُنا بعضا ونأتلِف
(Would that I and they [two] were alone in some place, until we could see one another and be reconciled.)
Al-Kisāʾī said: I put (الصابِئون) in the nominative by making it follow the noun [the pronoun] in «هادوا», taking it from His saying (إنا هدنا إليك) ("we have turned back to You"), not from Judaism. But the exegesis came otherwise, because He described those who believed with their mouths while their hearts did not believe, then mentioned the Jews and the Christians and said: whoever of them believes shall have such-and-such; so He made them Jews and Christians. [Translator's note: «يأفواههم» in the text is evidently a misprint for «بأفواههم».]

farraa:71-71.t:
His saying: ﴿فَعَمُواْ وَصَمُّواْ ثُمَّ تَابَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيْهِمْ ثُمَّ عَمُواْ وَصَمُّواْ كَثِيرٌ مِّنْهُمْ﴾ — the nominative of «الكثير» can be from two directions. One is that you repeat the verb upon it, meaning: "many of them became blind and deaf." And if you wish, you make ﴿عَمُوا وصَمُّوا﴾ the verb of «الكثير», as the poet said:
يلوموننى فى اشترائى النخيـ * لَ أَهلِى فكلُّهم أَلْوَمُ
(They blame me for buying the palm trees — my family — and all of them are most blameworthy.)
This is for one who says "qāmū qawmuka" ("your people stood", with the plural verb before the agent). And if you wish, you make «الكثير» a maṣdar (verbal noun) and say: i.e. that is much [found] among them; this is a third way. Had it been put in the accusative in this sense, it would have been correct. Similar to it is the poet's saying:
وسوَّد ماءُ المَرْدِ فاها فلونه * كَلَون النَؤُور وهى أدماء سارُها
(The juice of the unripe fruit has blackened her mouth, so that its colour is like the colour of kohl-soot, while she is tawny — most of her.)
Similar to it is the saying of Allah, Blessed and Exalted: ﴿وأَسَرّوا النَّجْوَى الذِين ظلموا﴾ — if you wish, you make (وأسَرّوا) a verb for His saying ﴿لاهِيةً قلوبُهم وأسَرّوا النجوى﴾ and then begin (الذين) afresh in the nominative. If you wish, you make it genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of «الناس» in His saying "اقترب لِلناسِ حِسابهم". And if you wish, it is nominative, just as "dhahabū qawmuka" is permissible.

farraa:101-101.t:
His saying: ﴿لاَ تَسْأَلُواْ عَنْ أَشْيَآءَ إِن تُبْدَ لَكُمْ تَسُؤْكُمْ﴾ — the Prophet ﷺ addressed the people and told them that Allah, Blessed and Exalted, had made the Hajj obligatory for them. A man stood up and said: "O Messenger of Allah, (is it) every year?" He turned away from him.
Then he repeated (and said: "Is it every year?" He turned away from him; then he repeated it), and the Prophet ﷺ said to him: "What makes you safe from my saying (yes), so that it becomes obligatory for you, and then you do not do it and so disbelieve? Leave me alone as long as I leave you alone."
(أشياء) is in the position of the genitive and is diptote (lā tujrā). Some grammarians have said of it: it became frequent in speech while being [on the pattern] (afʿāl), and so it resembled faʿlāʾ and was not declined, just as ḥamrāʾ is not declined; and its plural is ashāwā — as they made the plural of ʿadhrāʾ ʿadhārā and of ṣaḥrāʾ ṣaḥārā — and ashyāwāt, as one says ḥamrāwāt. But if it were by mere fancied analogy (tawahhum), the stronger of the two ways would be to decline it, because when a word is frequently used it becomes light; just as naming people Yazīd became frequent and so they declined it, although it has an augment yāʾ that prevents declension. Rather, we hold that ashyāʾ was formed as a plural on the pattern afʿilāʾ, as layyin has the plural alyināʾ; a hamza was dropped from the middle of ashyāʾ, which should have been ashyiʾāʾ, and the hamza was dropped because of its frequency. The Arabs have said: "This is of the abnāwāt of Saʿd," and "I commend you to the protection of the asmāwāt of Allah," whose singulars asmāʾ and abnāʾ are declined. So if I denied ashyāʾ declension because they made its plural ashyāwāt, I would have to decline neither asmāʾ nor abnāʾ, since they were made plural as asmāwāt and abnāwāt.

farraa:103-103.t:
His saying: ﴿مَا جَعَلَ ٱللَّهُ مِن بَحِيرَةٍ وَلاَ سَآئِبَةٍ وَلاَ وَصِيلَةٍ وَلاَ حَامٍ﴾ — there has been disagreement about the sāʾiba. It was said: a man would set loose (yusayyib) whatever he wished of his property and take it to those who attended to the service of their gods. Some said: the sāʾiba is when a she-camel has borne ten litters, all of them female; she was set loose, not ridden, her hair not shorn, and none drank her milk except her offspring or a guest, until she died. When she died, men and women ate her, and the ear of her daughter's daughter was slit (buḥirat) — he means: pierced. So the baḥīra is the daughter of the sāʾiba, and she has the same status as her mother. As for the waṣīla, it is from sheep: when a ewe had borne seven litters of female kids in pairs, and in her seventh bore a female kid and a male kid, it was said: "She has joined (waṣalat) her brother"; so women did not drink her milk, which was for the men, and she was treated like the sāʾiba.
As for the ḥāmī, it is the stallion camel: when the offspring of his offspring had conceived, his back was protected (ḥamā); he was not ridden, his hair was not shorn, he was not kept from any pasture, and whatever camels he covered, he was not kept away from them.
So Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said ﴿مَا جَعَلَ ٱللَّهُ مِن بَحِيرَةٍ﴾ — it is you who made it so.
Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said ﴿وَلَـٰكِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ يَفْتَرُونَ عَلَىٰ ٱللَّهِ ٱلْكَذِبَ وَأَكْثَرُهُمْ لاَ يَعْقِلُونَ﴾.

farraa:105-105.t:
His saying: ﴿عَلَيْكُمْ أَنْفُسَكُمْ﴾ — this is a command from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, as in your saying: "Look after yourselves." The Arabs give commands using prepositions (ṣifāt) such as ʿalayka, ʿindaka, dūnaka and ilayka. They say "ilayka ilayka," meaning "Get back," as you say "warāʾaka warāʾaka". These particles are many. Al-Kisāʾī claimed that he heard "baynakumā al-baʿīra fa-khudhāhu" ("Between you two is the camel — take it"); so he permitted it with all the prepositions that can stand alone, but did not permit it with the lām, the bāʾ or the kāf. And he heard one of the Arabs say "kamā anta Zaydan" and "makānaka Zaydan". Al-Farrāʾ said: I heard [some of] the Banū Sulaym say in their speech: "kamā antanī" and "makānakanī", meaning: wait for me where you are. [Translator's note: «بغليك» in the text is evidently a misprint for «بعليك».]
Never put what these particles govern in the accusative before them, because they are nouns, and a noun does not govern anything in the accusative before it. You say "ḍarban Zaydan" ("strike Zayd!"), but you do not say "Zaydan ḍarban". If you do say it, you put «زيد» in the accusative by a verb implied before it in the same way. The poet said:
* يأيها المائِح دلوى دونكا *
(O you who fill [the bucket] at the bottom of the well — my bucket: here it is for you!)
If you wish, you put (الدلو) in the accusative by an implied [verb] before it; and if you wish, you make it nominative, meaning: "This is my bucket, so take it."
﴿لاَ يَضُرُّكُمْ﴾ is nominative; had it been jussive, it would have been correct, as He said (فاضرِبْ لهم طَرِيقا فِى البحر يَبَسا لا تخَفْ، ولا تخافُ) — both are permissible.

farraa:106-106.t:
His saying: ﴿شَهَادَةُ بَيْنِكُمْ إِذَا حَضَرَ أَحَدَكُمُ ٱلْمَوْتُ حِينَ ٱلْوَصِيَّةِ ٱثْنَانِ﴾ — He is saying: two witnesses or two executors; there has been disagreement about it. «الاثنين» is nominative by «الشهادة», i.e. let two of the Muslims witness for you.
﴿أَوْ آخَرَانِ مِنْ غَيْرِكُمْ﴾ — from other than your religion. This is on a journey, and there is a long story about it. But the meaning in His saying ﴿مِن الذِين استَحَقَّ عليهِم الأَوْلَيانِ﴾: whoever reads «الأَوليان» means the two next of kin of the deceased, who take the place of the two Christians when the latter are suspected of having been dishonest; so they swear after the two Christians have sworn and their dishonesty has been exposed. This is a reading that ʿAlī read, and it is reported from Ubayy ibn Kaʿb. Al-Farrāʾ related to us, saying: Qays ibn al-Rabīʿ related to me from ʿAbd al-Malik, from ʿAṭāʾ, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that he said (الأَوَّلِين), making it a naʿt (adjective) of «الذين»; and he said: "Do you think that if the two next of kin were children, how could they take their place?" His saying (استحقَّ عليهِم) means "among them" (fīhim), as He said ﴿واتَّبعوا ماتَتْلُو الشياطِينُ على مُلْكِ سُلَيمان﴾, i.e. in the kingdom; and like His saying ﴿ولأُصَلِّبَنَّكُمْ فِى جُذُوع النخل﴾, where the exegesis came: "on the trunks of the palm trees". Al-Ḥasan read (الأوّلان), meaning: the two became liable because of what became due against them through the exposure of their dishonesty. ʿAbdallāh ibn Masʿūd read (الأَوّلِين), like the saying of Ibn ʿAbbās. «الأَوليان» here may also be the two Christians — and Allah knows best — so that one puts them in the nominative by (استَحَقَّ) and makes them "the two more entitled" to the oath, because the oath was incumbent upon them, while the proof was incumbent upon the claimant; so they were called "al-awlayān" by virtue of the oath. This is in the sense of al-Ḥasan's reading.
And His saying ﴿تُرَدَّ أَيْمَان﴾ [with] «أن»: [that] the oaths of others be returned against their oaths and invalidate them.

farraa:109-109.t: His saying: ﴿قَالُواْ لاَ عِلْمَ لَنَآ﴾ — they said [this] because of the terror of the Day of Resurrection that is mentioned. Then they said: "except what You have taught us." If it is as mentioned, then (ما) after (إلا) is in the position of the accusative, because it is good to pause at His saying (لا علم لنا); the nominative is also permissible.

farraa:110-110.t:
His saying: ﴿إِذْ أَيَّدتُّكَ﴾ — on the pattern faʿʿaltuka, as you say "qawwaytuka" ("I strengthened you"). Mujāhid read (آيدتك), on the pattern afʿaltuka. Al-Kisāʾī said: [it may be] fāʿaltuka, and that is permissible, on the model of ʿāwantuka ("I helped you").
His saying: ﴿فِي ٱلْمَهْدِ﴾ — He is saying: as a child; ﴿وَكَهْلاً﴾ — He referred «الكهل» back to the description [i.e. made it accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) corresponding to the prepositional phrase], as in His saying ﴿دعانا لجنبِهِ أَو قاعِدا أَو قائِما﴾.

farraa:111-111.t: His saying: ﴿وَإِذْ أَوْحَيْتُ إِلَى ٱلْحَوَارِيِّينَ أَنْ آمِنُواْ بِي وَبِرَسُولِي﴾ — He is saying: I inspired them; as He said ﴿وأَوحى ربُّك إِلى النحلِ أَنِ اتخِذِى مِن الجبال بيوتا﴾, i.e. He inspired it.

farraa:112-112.t: His saying: ﴿هَلْ يَسْتَطِيعُ رَبُّكَ﴾ — [read] with tāʾ and with yāʾ. The people of Medina, ʿĀṣim ibn Abī al-Najūd and al-Aʿmash read it with yāʾ: (يستطيع ربُّك). That may be on the model of your saying: "Is so-and-so able to stand with us?" when you know that he is able to; this is one interpretation. It is reported of ʿAlī and ʿĀʾisha, may Allah have mercy on them, that they read (هل تستطيعُ ربَّك) with tāʾ; and it is reported of Muʿādh that he said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ taught me to read (هل تستطيع ربَّكَ) with tāʾ." It is a good interpretation, i.e. are you able to ask your Lord ﴿أَن يُنَزِّلَ عَلَيْنَا مَآئِدَةً مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ﴾?

farraa:114-114.t:
His saying: ﴿تَكُونُ لَنَا عِيداً﴾ — (and «تَكُن لَنا»). In the reading of ʿAbdallāh it is (تكْن لنا عِيدا), without the wāw. Whenever there is an indefinite noun upon which a command has fallen, both the jussive and the nominative are permissible in the verb after it.
As for the table (al-māʾida), it is mentioned that it did come down, and that it was bread and fish. It came down — according to what is mentioned — on Sunday, twice; that is why they took it as a festival. Some exegetes said: it did not come down, because He made it a condition for them that if He sent it down and they did not believe, He would punish them; so they said: "We have no need of it."

farraa:116-116.t:
His saying: ﴿يٰعِيسَى ٱبْنَ مَرْيَمَ﴾ — (عيسى) is in the position of the nominative, and if you wish you may use the accusative. As for (ابن), only the accusative is permissible in it. You do the same with every name you address by its name and trace to its father, as in your saying "yā Zaydu bna ʿAbdillāh" and "yā Zayda bna ʿAbdillāh"; the accusative in (زيد) is more frequent in the speech of the Arabs.
If you use the nominative, the utterance consists of two addresses; and if you use the accusative, it is one address. If you say "yā Zaydu akhā Tamīm" ("O Zayd, brother of Tamīm") or "yā Zaydu bna al-rajuli al-ṣāliḥ" ("O Zayd, son of the righteous man"), you put the first in the nominative and the second in the accusative, as in the poet's saying:
يا زِبْرِقانُ أخا بنى خَلَفٍ * ما أنتَ ويلَ أبيك والفَخْرُ
(O Zibriqān, brother of the Banū Khalaf — what have you, woe to your father, to do with boasting?)

farraa:119-119.t:
His saying: ﴿هَـٰذَا يَوْمُ يَنفَعُ ٱلصَّادِقِينَ﴾ — you put (اليوم) in the nominative by (هذا), and it is permissible to put it in the accusative, because it is annexed to something that is not a noun; as the Arabs said: "maḍā yawma-idhin bi-mā fīhi" ("that day passed with what was in it") [with yawma in the accusative form]. They do that with it in the genitive position too; the poet said:
رددنا لشعثاءَ الرسولَ ولا أرى * كيوْمَئِذٍ شيئا تُردّ رسائِله
(We sent the messenger back to Shaʿthāʾ, and I see nothing like that day [yawma-idhin] whose messages are sent back.)
Likewise the reading in His saying ﴿مِن عذابِ يومَئِذٍ﴾ and ﴿ومن خزىِ يومَئذ﴾. It is permissible to put it in the genitive in a genitive position, just as it was permissible to put it in the nominative in a nominative position. Whatever is annexed to a clause that contains nothing in the genitive, treat it as you treated this; as in the poet's saying:
على حينَِ عاتبتُ المشيب على الصِبا * وقلتُ أَلَمَّا تَصْحُ والشيب وازِع
(At the time [ḥīna, with either vowel] when I reproached grey hair for [my] youthful folly, and said: "Have you not yet sobered up, while grey hair restrains?")
You do the same with yawm (day), layla (night), ḥīn (time), ghadāt (morning), ʿashiyya (evening), zaman (time), azmān, ayyām and layālin. His saying ﴿هَـٰذَا يَوْمُ يَنفَعُ ٱلصَّادِقِينَ﴾ may be like that. And His saying ﴿هذا يوم لا ينطِقون﴾ has in it what is in His saying (يوم ينفع). If you say "hādhā yawmun yanfaʿu al-ṣādiqīna", taking it as indefinite, as Allah said ﴿واتقوا يوما لا تَجْزِى نَفْسٌ﴾, it is correct.
The accusative in this kind of thing is disliked in the description; yet it is still permissible, but it is not fit in Quranic reading.

farraa:73-73.t:
His saying: ﴿لَّقَدْ كَفَرَ ٱلَّذِينَ قَالُوۤاْ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ ثَالِثُ ثَلاَثَةٍ﴾ — it is in a genitive construct (muḍāf). Nunation of (ثالث) with «الثلاثة» in the accusative is not permissible. Likewise you say "one of two" and "one of three"; do you not see that one cannot be second to oneself or third to oneself? But if you said "You are the third of two" [i.e. the one who makes two into three], it would be permissible to say "anta thālithu ithnayni" with the construct, and also with nunation and the accusative of «الاثنين»; likewise if you said "You are the fourth of three" (rābiʿun thalāthatan), that would be permissible, because it is an action that falls [on an object].
His saying: ﴿وَمَا مِنْ إِلَـٰهٍ إِلاَّ إِلَـٰهٌ وَاحِدٌ﴾ — His saying (إِله واحِد) can only be nominative, because the meaning is "there is no god but one God"; so you refer what comes after (إلا) back to the meaning. Do you not see that if (مِن) is missing from the beginning of the statement, you use the nominative? One of the poets said:
ما من حوِىّ بين بدرٍ وصاحةٍ * ولا شُعْبةٍ إلا شِبَاعٌ نسورها
(There is no hollow between Badr and Ṣāḥa, nor any ravine, but its vultures are sated [nominative].)
I saw that al-Kisāʾī permitted the genitive in it although it comes after «إلا», treating (إلا) together with the negation as equivalent to «غير». But that is nothing, because he treated it like the poet's saying:
أبنِى لبينى لستُم بِيدٍ * إِلا يدٍ ليست لها عُضد
(O sons of Lubaynā, you are not a hand — except a hand that has no upper arm.)
This is permissible, because the bāʾ can occur in negation with both definite and indefinite nouns: one says "mā anta bi-qāʾimin" ("you are not standing"), where «القائم» is indefinite, and "mā anta bi-akhīnā" ("you are not our brother"), where «الأخ» is definite; but it is not permissible to say "mā qāma min akhīka" as you say "mā qāma min rajulin".

farraa:75-75.t: His saying: ﴿وَأُمُّهُ صِدِّيقَةٌ﴾ — [the description of] affirming the truth (taṣdīq) applies to her as it applies to the prophets. That is because of the saying of Allah, Blessed and Exalted: ﴿فأَرسلنا إِليها رُوحَنَا فَتَمَثّلَ لها﴾. When Gabriel ﷺ spoke to her and she believed him, the term "message" came to apply to her, and she was like a prophet.

farraa:82-82.t: His saying: ﴿ذٰلِكَ بِأَنَّ مِنْهُمْ قِسِّيسِينَ﴾ — it was revealed concerning those of the Christians who embraced Islam. It is said: it is al-Najāshī (the Negus) and his companions. Al-Farrāʾ said: it is also pronounced al-Nijāshī.

farraa:87-87.t: His saying: ﴿لاَ تُحَرِّمُواْ طَيِّبَاتِ مَآ أَحَلَّ ٱللَّهُ لَكُمْ وَلاَ تَعْتَدُوۤاْ﴾ — they were a group of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ who wanted to renounce the world and to castrate themselves (yajubbū anfusahum). So Allah, Blessed and Exalted, sent down: ﴿لاَ تُحَرِّمُواْ طَيِّبَاتِ مَآ أَحَلَّ ٱللَّهُ لَكُمْ وَلاَ تَعْتَدُوۤاْ﴾, i.e. do not castrate yourselves. [Translator's note: the first occurrence is printed «ويحبوا أنفسهم» ("love themselves"), evidently a misprint for «ويجبّوا أنفسهم», as the second occurrence shows.]

farraa:89-89.t:
His saying: ﴿فَصِيَامُ ثَلاَثَةِ أَيَّامٍ﴾ — in the text of ʿAbdallāh: "ثلاثة أيام متتابعات" ("three consecutive days"). Had you given «الصيام» nunation, you would have put «الثلاثة» in the accusative, as Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: ﴿أو إِطعامٌ فِى يومٍ ذِى مَسْغَبةٍ. يتيما﴾ — (يتيما) is accusative because the feeding falls upon it. Similar is His saying ﴿أَلَمْ نجعلِ الأرض كِفَاتاً أحياءً وأمواتا﴾: it gathers them in, living and dead. Likewise His saying ﴿فجزاءٌ مِثلُ ما قتل من النعم﴾: had you put (مثل) in the accusative, it would have been correct. In the reading of ʿAbdallāh it is "فجزاؤه مثل ما قتل", and some of the people of Medina read it "فجزاءُ مِثلِ ما قَتَل"; all of that is correct.
As for His saying ﴿ولا نَكْتُم شهادةَ اللّهِ﴾: had you given «الشهادة» nunation, the accusative would be permissible in the case of (اللّه), meaning: "and we will not conceal from Allah any testimony." As for one who swears by Allah with a question [hamza] and says (اللّهِ), he puts (اللّهِ) in the genitive just as the oath is put in the genitive, not by annexing «الشهادة» to it.

farraa:90-90.t: His saying: ﴿1649؛لْخَمْرُ وَٱلْمَيْسِرُ﴾ — al-maysir is gambling of every kind; al-anṣāb are the idols; and al-azlām are arrows that were in the Kaʿba, with which they would draw lots in their affairs; the singular is zalam. [Translator's note: the quotation is printed with a stray «1649؛» in place of «إِنَّمَا ٱ»; it is reproduced as it stands.]

farraa:93-93.t: His saying: ﴿إِذَا مَا ٱتَّقَواْ﴾ — i.e. they guarded against drinking wine, and believed in its prohibition.

farraa:94-94.t: His saying: ﴿تَنَالُهُ أَيْدِيكُمْ وَرِمَاحُكُمْ﴾ — what the hands can reach is ostrich eggs and chicks, and what the spears can reach is all other wild game.

farraa:95-95.t:
His saying: ﴿فَجَزَآءٌ مِّثْلُ مَا قَتَلَ مِنَ ٱلنَّعَمِ يَحْكُمُ بِهِ ذَوَا عَدْلٍ مِّنْكُمْ﴾ — He is saying: whoever kills game, forgetting his iḥrām but intending the game, two just arbiters versed in law judge him. They ask him: "Have you killed game before this?" If he says "Yes," they do not judge him, but say: "Allah will take vengeance on you." If he says "No," they judge him. If the value of their judgement reaches the price of a sacrificial camel or a sheep, they impose that on him ﴿هَدْياً بَالِغَ ٱلْكَعْبَةِ﴾. If it does not reach the price of a sheep, they impose on him the value of what he killed in dirhams; then they value it in food, and he feeds the poor with it, half a ṣāʿ for each poor person. If he cannot find [the means], they rule that he must fast one day in place of each half ṣāʿ.
His saying: ﴿أَو عَدْلُ ذٰلِكَ صِيَاماً﴾ — al-ʿadl is what is equivalent to a thing from outside its kind, and al-ʿidl is its like. Thus you say: "I have the ʿidl of your slave-boy and the ʿidl of your sheep," when it is a slave-boy equal to a slave-boy or a sheep equal to a sheep. If you mean its value in something of another kind, you give the ʿayn fatḥa. [Translator's note: «نضبت» in the text is evidently a misprint for «نصبت».]
Some Arabs may say "ʿidluhu" [in this sense], and it seems to be an error on their part, owing to the closeness of the meaning of ʿadl to ʿidl. They are agreed that the singular of aʿdāl is ʿidl. Your putting «الصيام» in the accusative is as an explanation (tafsīr) [i.e. tamyīz (specification)], as you say: "I have two raṭls of honey (ʿasalan)" and "a houseful of fodder (qattan)". This is something to explain to the beginner: let him look at (مِن); if it fits well there and has then been dropped, use the accusative. Do you not see that you say: "He owes the equivalent of that in fasting (min al-ṣiyām)"? Likewise the saying of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, ﴿فلَنْ يُقْبَل مِن أحَدِهِم مِلءُ الأرْضِ ذهبا﴾.

farraa:96-96.t: His saying: ﴿أُحِلَّ لَكُمْ صَيْدُ ٱلْبَحْرِ وَطَعَامُهُ﴾ — "its game" is what you catch, and "its food" is what the water has receded from and left on the surface of the land.

harrat-mujtaba:1-1.t: (إلا ما يتلى عليكم غير محلي الصيد) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] «ما» is a relative noun, excepted; «غير» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun in «لكم»; «محلي» is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive by the yāʾ. The clause «وأنتم حرم» is a ḥāl of the pronoun in «لكم».

harrat-mujtaba:2-2.t: His saying «آمِّين» is a noun conjoined to «القلائد» with a muḍāf omitted, i.e.: nor fighting those heading for [the House], and «البيت» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of «آمِّين». The clause «يبتغون» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun in «آمِّين», in the position of the accusative. The maṣdar (verbal noun) «أن صدُّوكم» is accusative by removal of the preposition, the lām, and the maṣdar «أن تعتدوا» is accusative by removal of the preposition («على»). The clause «وإذا حللتم فاصطادوا» is conjoined to the clause ﴿لا تُحِلُّوا﴾ and has no grammatical position. The clause «وتعاونوا» is conjoined to the preceding reply to the vocative. The clause «واتقوا الله» is conjoined to the clause «ولا تعاونوا». The clause «إن الله شديد العقاب» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:3-3.t: «إلا» is a particle of exception, and «ما» is a relative, a disconnected excepted (mustathnā munqaṭiʿ). His saying «وما»: a relative noun conjoined to «ما أكل», and the maṣdar (verbal noun) «أن تستقسموا» is conjoined to «ما ذبح». The clause «ذلكم فسق» is resumptive. The clause «فلا تخشوهم» is resumptive. His saying «واخشون»: the wāw is a conjunction, [the verb is] an imperative verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, the wāw is the fāʿil (agent), the nūn is for protection (al-wiqāya), and the implied (muqaddar) yāʾ is the object of the verb. The clause «أكملت» is resumptive. His saying «ديناً»: a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «الإسلام», accusative. «فمن اضطرّ»: the fāʾ is resumptive, «مَنْ» is a conditional noun, mubtadaʾ (subject), and the preposition phrase «في مخمصة» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl of the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), which is the latent pronoun in «اضطرّ». «غير متجانف»: a ḥāl of the pronoun in «اضطرّ», and «متجانف» is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the preposition phrase «لإثم» is attached to «متجانِف», which is an active participle from a verb of more than three radicals: «تجانَفَ».

harrat-mujtaba:4-4.t: «ما» is an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject), and «ذا» is a relative noun, khabar (predicate). The clause «ماذا أحلّ» is the second object of the asking, which is suspended (muʿallaq) by the interrogative, because asking is a means to knowledge. His saying «وما علّمتم»: a relative noun conjoined to «الطيّبات», and the preposition phrase «من الجوارح» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the implied resumptive pronoun, i.e.: you taught it, being of the hunting animals. «مكلّبين»: a ḥāl of the fāʿil (agent) of «علّمتم», and the clause «تُعلّمونهن» is a ḥāl of the fāʿil of «علّمتم». The clause «فكلوا» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:5-5.t: The adverb «اليوم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أحلّ». The clause «وطعام الذين..حل» is conjoined to the resumptive clause «أحلَّ لكم الطيّبات». His saying «والمحصنات من المؤمنات»: mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is omitted, i.e.: lawful; the preposition phrase is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «المحصنات», and the second «المحصنات» is conjoined to the first. His saying «حلٌّ»: a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the sense of «الحَلال» (lawful); for that reason it is not made feminine, dual or plural. «إذا آتيتموهن»: «إذا» is a pure adverb attached to «أحلّ», and «محصنين غير» are two ḥāls of the fāʿil (agent) of «آتيتم». «متخذي» is a noun conjoined to «مسافحين». The preposition phrase «في الآخرة» is attached to «الخاسرين», and the clause «وهو من الخاسرين» is conjoined to the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), in the position of the jussive.

harrat-mujtaba:6-6.t:
- {يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِذَا قُمْتُمْ إِلَى الصَّلاةِ فَاغْسِلُوا وُجُوهَكُمْ وَأَيْدِيَكُمْ إِلَى الْمَرَافِقِ وَامْسَحُوا بِرُءُوسِكُمْ وَأَرْجُلَكُمْ إِلَى الْكَعْبَيْنِ وَإِنْ كُنْتُمْ جُنُبًا فَاطَّهَّرُوا وَإِنْ كُنْتُمْ مَرْضَى أَوْ عَلَى سَفَرٍ أَوْ جَاءَ أَحَدٌ مِنْكُمْ مِنَ الْغَائِطِ أَوْ لامَسْتُمُ النِّسَاءَ فَلَمْ تَجِدُوا مَاءً فَتَيَمَّمُوا صَعِيدًا طَيِّبًا فَامْسَحُوا بِوُجُوهِكُمْ وَأَيْدِيكُمْ مِنْهُ مَا يُرِيدُ اللَّهُ لِيَجْعَلَ عَلَيْكُمْ مِنْ حَرَجٍ وَلَكِنْ يُرِيدُ لِيُطَهِّرَكُمْ وَلِيُتِمَّ نِعْمَتَهُ عَلَيْكُمْ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَشْكُرُونَ}
The conditional clause «إذا قمتم..» is resumptive, the reply to the vocative. His saying «وأرجلكم» is a noun conjoined to «أيديكم». The preposition phrase «أو على سفر» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted item conjoined to «مرضى», i.e.: or being on a journey; the preposition phrase «منكم» is attached to a naʿt (adjective) of «أحد»; and the preposition phrase «من الغائط» is attached to «جاء». The first object of «يريد» is omitted, i.e.: hardship, and the maṣdar (verbal noun) «ليجعل» is genitive, attached to «يريد». «حرج» is mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and «من» is redundant (zāʾida) because it enters upon an indefinite noun and is preceded by a negation. The second object of «يريد» is omitted, i.e.: ease; the clause «ولكن يريد» is conjoined to the clause «يريد»; and the clause «لعلكم تشكرون» is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

harrat-mujtaba:7-7.t: «إذ قلتم» is an adverb of time attached to (mutaʿalliq) «واثقكم», and the clause «قلتم» is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). The clause «إن الله عليم» is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

harrat-mujtaba:8-8.t: The preposition phrase «لله» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «قوَّامين», and His saying «شهداء» is a second khabar (predicate); the preposition phrase «بالقسط» is attached to «شهداء». The clause «ولا يجرمنّكم» is conjoined to the clause «كونوا» and has no grammatical position. The maṣdar (verbal noun) «ألا تعدلوا» is genitive by «على», attached to «يجرمنّكم». The clause «هو أقرب» is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

harrat-mujtaba:9-9.t: The clause «لهم مغفرة» explains the second object of «وعد», the implied form being: He promised them Paradise; it is a case of explaining the effect by its cause, for Paradise is caused by forgiveness and reward.

harrat-mujtaba:10-10.t: The clause «والذين كفروا..» is conjoined to the preceding clause ﴿وَعَدَ﴾. The clause «أولئك أصحاب» is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject), in the position of the nominative.

harrat-mujtaba:11-11.t: His saying «إذ همَّ قوم»: an adverbial noun in the position of the accusative, a badal (substitute) of inclusion (badal ishtimāl) of «نعمة». The clause «همَّ» is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), in the position of the genitive, and the maṣdar (verbal noun) «أن يبسطوا» is accusative by removal of the preposition, the bāʾ. The fāʾ in «فليتوكل» is redundant (zāʾida), and the clause «وعلى الله فليتوكل المؤمنون» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:12-12.t: The clause «ولقد أخذ الله» is resumptive, and the clause «لقد أخذ» is the reply to an implied oath. His saying «اثني عشر»: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative by the yāʾ because it is treated like the dual; «عشر» is a part indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa with no grammatical position; «نقيباً» is tamyīz (specification). The clause «لئن أقمتم» is resumptive within the scope of the speech, and the clause «لأكفرن» is the reply to the oath, with no grammatical position. The preposition phrase «منكم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of «كفر», and His saying «سواء» is an adverb of place meaning «وسط» (middle).

harrat-mujtaba:13-13.t: (فبما نقضهم ميثاقهم) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The fāʾ is resumptive, «ما» is redundant (zāʾida), and the preposition phrase is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «لعنّاهم»; «ميثاقهم» is the object of the breaking; the two objects of «جعلنا» are «قلوبهم قاسية»; the clause «يحرفون» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the hāʾ in «لعنّاهم»; the clause «نسوا» is conjoined to «يحرفون»; the clause «لا تزال» is conjoined to «ذُكِّروا»; the clause «تطلع» is the khabar (predicate) of «زال», in the position of the accusative; and the clause «فاعف» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:14-14.t: The preposition phrase «من الذين» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أخذنا», and the clause «أخذنا» is conjoined to the clause ﴿أَخَذَ﴾ in verse (12); the preposition phrase «ممَّا» is attached to a naʿt (adjective) of «حظا», and the preposition phrase «إلى يوم» is attached to «أغرينا». The clause «وسوف ينبئهم» is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

harrat-mujtaba:15-15.t: The clause «يبين» is in the position of the accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial) of «رسولنا». His saying «كثيراً» is mafʿūl bihi (direct object). The preposition phrase «مما» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «كثيرا». The clause «قد جاءكم نور» is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

harrat-mujtaba:16-16.t: The clause «يهدي» is a second naʿt (adjective) of «كتاب», in the position of the nominative. His saying «رضوانه» is the object of «اتبع». «سبل» is the second object of «يهدي». The preposition phrase «بإذنه» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the hāʾ in «يخرجهم».

harrat-mujtaba:17-17.t: «هو» is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl) with no grammatical position. His saying «قل فمن يملك»: the fāʾ occurs in the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, i.e.: if He willed, then who would have power? The clause «إن أراد» is resumptive, and the apodosis is omitted, what precedes indicating it; and the two clauses «ولله ملك» and «يخلق» are resumptive. The adverb «بينهما» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the implied ṣila (relative clause), i.e.: is settled. The clause «والله على كل شيء قدير» is resumptive, and the preposition phrase «على كل» is attached to «قدير».

harrat-mujtaba:18-18.t: «قل فلمَ»: the fāʾ links to the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, i.e.: if your saying is correct, then why?; the lām is a preposition, and «ما» is an interrogative noun in the position of the genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يعذّبكم», its alif having been dropped because it is preceded by the preposition. The preposition phrase «ممن خلق» is attached to a naʿt (adjective) of «بشر», and the clause «يغفر» is resumptive. The clause «ولله ملك» is conjoined to the clause «يغفر», and the clause «وإليه المصير» is conjoined to the clause «ولله ملك».

harrat-mujtaba:19-19.t: The clause «يبين» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «رسولنا», in the position of the accusative; the preposition phrase «من الرسل» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «فترة»; and the maṣdar (verbal noun) «أن تقولوا» is mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), i.e.: out of dislike that. His saying «من بشير»: fāʿil (agent), and «من» is redundant (zāʾida). The clause «فقد جاءكم بشير» is conjoined to the clause «جاءكم رسولنا», with no grammatical position.

harrat-mujtaba:20-20.t: (وإذ قال موسى لقومه) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The wāw is resumptive; «إذ» is an adverbial noun, object of an implied «اذكر» (remember); and the preposition phrase «عليكم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «نعمة». His saying «إذ جعل فيكم»: an adverbial noun, a badal (substitute) of «نعمة», and the clause «جعل» is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). The two objects of «آتاكم» are the kāf and the relative «ما».

harrat-mujtaba:21-21.t: «يا قومِ»: the one addressed (munādā), a muḍāf, accusative by the implied (muqaddar) fatḥa on the letter before the yāʾ, which is dropped for lightness. His saying «فتنقلبوا خاسرين»: the fāʾ is causal, and the verb is accusative by «أن» necessarily concealed after the fāʾ; the maṣdar (verbal noun) is conjoined to a maṣdar extracted from the preceding speech, the implied form being: let there be no turning back from you, and so a turning about; and «خاسرين» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the wāw in «تنقلبوا».

harrat-mujtaba:22-22.t: The clause «فإن يخرجوا» is conjoined to the clause «إنّا لن ندخلها», in the position of the accusative.

harrat-mujtaba:23-23.t: The preposition phrase «من الذين يخافون» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «رجلان»; the clause «أنعم الله» is a second adjective (ṣifa) of «رجلان», in the position of the nominative; the clause «فإذا دخلتموه» is conjoined to the clause «ادخلوا», in the position of the accusative; the clause «توكلوا» is resumptive, and the fāʾ is redundant (zāʾida). The clause «إن كنتم مؤمنين» is resumptive, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, what precedes indicating it.

harrat-mujtaba:24-24.t: His saying «أبداً ما داموا فيها»: [«أبداً» is] an adverb of time attached to (mutaʿalliq) «ندخلها»; «ما» is temporal maṣdariyya, and the interpreted maṣdar is an adverb of time attached to «ندخلها», and it is a badal (substitute) of «أبداً». The clause «داموا» is the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle relative (al-mawṣūl al-ḥarfī). The clause «فاذهب» is resumptive. His saying «أنت»: tawkīd (emphasis) of the latent pronoun in «اذهب». His saying «وربّك»: a noun conjoined to the latent pronoun in «اذهب»; conjoining an overt noun to the latent nominative [pronoun] is permitted because of the presence of a separator. His saying «هاهنا»: «ها» is for drawing attention, and «هنا» is a demonstrative, an adverb of place attached to «قاعدون»; and the clause «إنا قاعدون» is resumptive within the scope of the speech.

harrat-mujtaba:25-25.t: The clause «فافرق» is conjoined to the clause «إنِّي لا أملك» and has no grammatical position; conjoining a performative (inshāʾ) clause to an informative (khabar) one is permitted.

harrat-mujtaba:26-26.t: His saying «قال فإنها محرمة»: the fāʾ occurs in the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, i.e.: if the matter is so, then it [is forbidden]; and the preposition phrase «عليهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «محرمة». «أربعين» is an adverb of time, accusative by the yāʾ because it is treated like the sound masculine plural, attached to «محرمة». The clause «يتيهون» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the hāʾ in «عليهم». The clause «فلا تأس» is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

harrat-mujtaba:27-27.t: The preposition phrase «بالحق» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of «اتل», i.e.: bound up with the truth. His saying «إذ قرّبا»: a badal (substitute) of inclusion (badal ishtimāl) of «نبأ», and the clause «قرّبا» is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). The clause «لأقتلنَّك» is the reply to an implied oath, and the oath with its reply is the content of what is said (maqūl al-qawl), in the position of the accusative. The last clause «قال» is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

harrat-mujtaba:28-28.t: His saying «ما أنا بباسط»: «ما» is negating, operating like «ليس»; «بباسط» is its khabar (predicate), and the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida); «يدي» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the active participle; the preposition phrase is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «باسط»; and the clause is the reply to the oath, with no grammatical position. The clause «إني أخاف» is resumptive within the scope of the speech.

harrat-mujtaba:31-31.t: The clause «كيف يواري» is the second object of the visual seeing, which is suspended (muʿallaq), the verb «رأى» having acquired a second object through the hamza. «يا ويلتا»: the one addressed (munādā), a muḍāf, accusative by the implied (muqaddar) fatḥa on the letter before the first-person yāʾ that has been turned into an alif, and the yāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause is the content of what is said (maqūl al-qawl). The interpreted maṣdar «أن أكون» is accusative by removal of the preposition («عن»). The clause «أعجزت» is resumptive within the scope of the reply to the vocative, with no grammatical position.

harrat-mujtaba:32-32.t: The maṣdar (verbal noun) «أنه من قتل» is the object of «كتب». The conditional clause is in the position of the nominative as khabar (predicate) of «أنَّ». His saying «فكأنما»: the fāʾ is linking, and [«كأنما» is] a restraining particle and restrained particle (kāffa wa-makfūfa) with no grammatical position. His saying «جميعًا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial). The clause «ولقد جاءتهم رسلنا» is resumptive, and the clause «لقد جاءتهم» is the reply to the oath, with no grammatical position. His saying «ثمَّ إنَّ كثيرًا منهم»: «ثمَّ» is a conjunction, and the preposition phrase «منهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «كثيرًا». The adverb «بعد» and the preposition phrase «في الأرض» are attached to «مسرفون», the khabar, and [the lām is] the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa).

harrat-mujtaba:33-33.t: «فسادًا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial), interpreted as «مفسدين» (corrupting), because «فسادًا» is a maṣdar (verbal noun), and a maṣdar does not occur as a ḥāl except by interpretation. The preposition phrase «من خلاف» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl of «أيديهم وأرجلهم». «ذلك لهم خزي»: the demonstrative is mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause «لهم خزي» is the khabar (predicate). The preposition phrase «في الدنيا» is attached to a naʿt (adjective) of «خزي», and the preposition phrase «في الآخرة» is attached to a ḥāl of «عذاب».

harrat-mujtaba:34-34.t: The maṣdar (verbal noun) «أن تقدروا» is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). The clause «فاعلموا» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:35-35.t: The clause «لعلكم تفلحون» is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

harrat-mujtaba:36-36.t: «لو»: a non-jussive conditional particle; «أنَّ» is an abrogating particle (nāsikha), the preposition phrase is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate), and the interpreted maṣdar is the fāʿil (agent) of an implied «ثبت» (it were established). «ما» is the noun of «أنَّ», the preposition phrase «في الأرض» is attached to the ṣila (relative clause), and His saying «جميعًا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the latent pronoun in the implied ṣila. The conditional clause is the khabar of «إن». His saying «معه»: an adverb attached to a ḥāl of «مثله». His saying «تُقُبِّل منهم»: an imperfect verb, passive, and the preposition phrase is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). [Translator's note: so in the source; «تُقُبِّل» is a past-tense form.] The clause «ولهم عذاب أليم» is conjoined to the conditional clause.

harrat-mujtaba:37-37.t: His saying «وما هم بخارجين منها»: the wāw is ḥāliyya; «ما» is negating, operating like «ليس»; «هم» is a detached pronoun, its noun; «بخارجين» is its khabar (predicate), and the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida); the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial); and the clause «ولهم عذاب» is conjoined to the clause «وما هم بخارجين», in the position of the accusative.

harrat-mujtaba:38-38.t: His saying «فاقطعوا»: the fāʾ is redundant (zāʾida), and the clause is in the position of the nominative as khabar (predicate). «جزاءً»: mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose). «نكالا»: a badal (substitute) of «جزاءً». The preposition phrase «من الله» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «نكالا».

harrat-mujtaba:40-40.t: The interpreted maṣdar «أن الله له ملك» is the object of «تعلم». The clause «له ملك» is in the position of the nominative as khabar (predicate) of «أنَّ».

harrat-mujtaba:41-41.t: The preposition phrase «من الذين قالوا» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of «يسارعون». The clause «ولم تؤمن قلوبهم» is a ḥāl of «الذين». His saying «ومن الذين هادوا»: conjoined to «من الذين قالوا». His saying «سمَّاعون»: khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e.: they; and «للكذب» is mafʿūl bihi (direct object), the lām being redundant (zāʾida) for strengthening because «سمَّاعون» is secondary (farʿ) to the verb. «سمَّاعون لقوم» is a second khabar, and «لقوم» is mafʿūl bihi, the lām being redundant; the clause «لم يأتوك» is a second naʿt (adjective) of «قوم», in the position of the genitive; the clause «يحرفون» is a third naʿt of «قوم»; and the clause «يقولون» is a ḥāl of the fāʿil of «يحرِّفون». The clause «لهم في الدنيا خزي» is a second khabar of «أولئك», and the preposition phrase «في الدنيا» is attached to a ḥāl of «خزي». The clause «ولهم عذاب» is conjoined to the clause «لهم خزي».

harrat-mujtaba:42-42.t: «سمَّاعون» is the khabar (predicate) of an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e.: they are listeners; and «للكذب» is mafʿūl bihi (direct object), the lām being redundant (zāʾida) for strengthening. His saying «أكَّالون»: a second khabar of the implied mubtadaʾ, nominative. The clause «فإن جاءوك» is resumptive, and likewise the clause «إن الله يحب».

harrat-mujtaba:43-43.t: (وكيف يحكمونك) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The wāw is resumptive, «كيف» is an interrogative noun, ḥāl (circumstantial), and the clause is resumptive. The clause «وعندهم التوراة» is a ḥāl of the wāw in «يحكمونك», and the clause «فيها حكم الله» is a ḥāl of «التوراة». The clause «وما أولئك بالمؤمنين» is a ḥāl of the wāw in «يتولَّون».

harrat-mujtaba:44-44.t: The clause «فيها هدى ونور» is in the position of the accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial) of «التوراة». The clause «يحكم بها النبيَّون» is a second ḥāl of «التوراة». The clause «وكانوا عليه» is conjoined to the clause «استحفظوا». His saying «واخشون»: the wāw is a conjunction, the verb is indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, the wāw is the fāʿil (agent), the nūn is for protection (al-wiqāya), and the implied (muqaddar) yāʾ is the object of the verb; and the clause «ومن لم يحكم» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:45-45.t: The interpreted maṣdar «أن النفس بالنفس» is the object of «كتب». In His saying «والعين بالعين», the wāw conjoins two nouns to two nouns: «العين» is conjoined to «النفس», and «بالعين» is conjoined to «بالنفس». «هم» is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl) with no grammatical position.

harrat-mujtaba:46-46.t: His saying «مصدقا لما بين يديه»: a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «عيسى»; the relative noun is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the active participle, the lām is redundant (zāʾida), and the adverb is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the implied ṣila (relative clause). The preposition phrase «من التوراة» is attached to a ḥāl of «ما». The clause «فيه هدى» is a ḥāl of «الإنجيل», and His saying «ومصدقا» is conjoined to the position of the clause «فيه هدى», accusative; His saying «وهدى وموعظة»: two nouns conjoined to the second «مصدقاً». The preposition phrase «للمتقين» is attached to an adjective (ṣifa) of «موعظة».

harrat-mujtaba:47-47.t: His saying «وليَحكم»: the wāw is resumptive, the lām is for the imperative, and the verb is jussive (majzūm). The clause «فأولئك هُمُ الفاسقون» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), in the position of the jussive, and «هم» is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl) with no grammatical position.

harrat-mujtaba:48-48.t: «مصدقا»: a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «الكتاب», and it is a second ḥāl, because His saying «بالحق» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl of «الكتاب». The preposition phrase «من الكتاب» is attached to a ḥāl of «ما», and His saying «ومُهيمِنًا عليه»: a noun conjoined to «مصدِّقًا», and the preposition phrase is attached to «مهيمنًا»; the clause «فاحكم» is conjoined to the clause «أنزلنا». The preposition phrase «عَمَّا جاءك» is attached to a ḥāl of the fāʿil (agent) of «تَتَّبِعْ», and the preposition phrase «مِن الحق» is attached to a ḥāl of the pronoun in «جاءك». His saying «لكلٍ جَعلنا منكم شِرْعَةً»: the preposition phrase «لكل» is attached to «جعلنا», and the preposition phrase «منكم» is attached to an implied verb, «أعني» (I mean); it is not attached to a naʿt (adjective) of «لكل», because that would entail separating the adjective from the qualified noun by His saying «جعلنا», which is extraneous. The clause «ولو شاء الله» is conjoined to the clause «جَعلنا», with no grammatical position. His saying «ولكن لِيبلُوَكم»: the wāw is a conjunction, «لكنْ» is a particle of rectification (istidrāk), the lām is for causation, and the verb is accusative by «أن» concealed after the lām of causation; the interpreted maṣdar is genitive, attached to something omitted, i.e.: but He divided you in order to test you; the implied clause «فرَّقكم» is conjoined to the clause «ولو شاء»; the clause «فاستبِقوا» is resumptive; the clause «إلى الله مرجعُكم» is resumptive; and the clause «فينبئُكم» is conjoined to the resumptive one.

harrat-mujtaba:49-49.t: (وأن احكم بينهم) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The wāw is a conjunction and «أنْ» is maṣdariyya; the interpreted maṣdar is conjoined to ﴿الْكِتَابَ﴾ at the beginning of the previous verse, i.e.: the Book and the ruling. The maṣdar (verbal noun) «أن يَفْتنوك» is a badal (substitute) of inclusion (badal ishtimāl) of the hāʾ in «احذرْهم», and the maṣdar «أنما يريد» stands in place of the two objects of «عَلِمَ». The maṣdar «أن يصيبهم» is mafʿūl bihi (direct object). The clause «وإن كثيرًا مِن الناس لفاسقون» is resumptive; the preposition phrase «من الناس» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «كثيرًا»; and [the lām is] the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa).

harrat-mujtaba:50-50.t: (أفحكم الجاهلية يبغون) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The hamza is for the interrogative of disapproval, the fāʾ is resumptive, and «حُكمَ» is the fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of «يبغون»; His saying «حكمًا» is tamyīz (specification); the clause «يبغون» is resumptive, and likewise the clause «ومَن أحسنُ».

harrat-mujtaba:51-51.t: The clause «بعضُهم أولياءُ» is parenthetical between the conjoined items, with no grammatical position. The clause «ومَن يَتَوَلَّهُم» is conjoined to the clause «لا تتخذوا», with no grammatical position.

harrat-mujtaba:52-52.t: The clause «فترى» is resumptive. The clause «يسارعون» is in the position of the accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial) of «الذين», and the clause «يقولون» is a ḥāl of the fāʿil (agent) of «يسارعون». «فعسى اللهُ أن يأتيَ»: the fāʾ is resumptive, «عسى» is incomplete (nāqiṣa) [and «الله» is] its noun, and the interpreted maṣdar is its khabar (predicate); the preposition phrase «على ما» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «نادمين».

harrat-mujtaba:53-53.t: «جهد أيمانهم»: a deputy of the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); it is an emphasizing maṣdar (verbal noun) governed in the accusative by «أقسموا», since it is of its meaning; the sense is: they swore a strenuous swearing. The clause «حبطت أعمالُهم» is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

harrat-mujtaba:54-54.t: (من يرتد منكم عن دينه) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] «مَن» is a conditional noun, mubtadaʾ (subject); [«يرتد» is] an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the sukūn, given a fatḥa because of the meeting of two quiescents; the preposition phrase «منكم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of «يرتد»; the preposition phrase «عن دينه» is attached to «يرتد»; and His saying «أذلةٍ» is a naʿt (adjective) of «قومٍ», genitive. The clause «يجاهدون» is an adjective (ṣifa) of «قوم», in the position of the genitive. The clause «يؤتيه» is a ḥāl, in the position of the accusative.

harrat-mujtaba:55-55.t: «الذين يقيمون»: this relative is a naʿt (adjective) of the preceding relative, and the clause «وهم راكعون» is a ḥāl (circumstantial), in the position of the accusative, of the wāw in «يؤتون».

harrat-mujtaba:56-56.t: The clause «فإنَّ حزبَ اللهِ همُ الغالبون» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), in the position of the jussive; this is permitted, even though on the surface it lacks a pronoun referring back to the conditional noun, because what is meant by «حزب الله» is in meaning the mubtadaʾ (subject) itself; the implied form is: then he is victorious, so the overt noun has been put in the place of the pronoun.

harrat-mujtaba:57-57.t: His saying «لا تَتخذوا»: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), transitive to two objects: «الذين» and «أولياء»; and the verb «اتخذوا» is transitive to two objects: «دينكم» and «هزوا». The preposition phrase «من الذين أُوتوا» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of «اتخذوا», and the preposition phrase «مِن قبلكم» is attached to «أوتوا»; the clause «إن كنتم مؤمنين» is resumptive, with no grammatical position, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, what precedes indicating it.

harrat-mujtaba:58-58.t: (وإذا ناديتم إلى الصلاة) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The conditional clause is conjoined to the preceding ṣila (relative clause) ﴿اتَّخَذُوا﴾. The clause «ذلك بأنهم قومٌ» is resumptive, and the maṣdar (verbal noun) is in the position of the genitive by the bāʾ, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate); the clause «لا يعقلون» is a naʿt (adjective) of «قومٌ».

harrat-mujtaba:59-59.t: The maṣdar (verbal noun) «أنْ آمَنَّا» is the object of «نَقِمَ». The maṣdar «وأنَّ أكثرَكم فاسقون» is conjoined to the first maṣdar «أنْ آمنا» with a muḍāf omitted, i.e.: and believing that most of them are defiantly disobedient. [Translator's note: so in the source, "most of them" (أكثرهم), whereas the verse has «أكثركم».]

harrat-mujtaba:60-60.t: His saying «شَر»: an elative (afʿal al-tafḍīl) whose hamza has been dropped for lightness; the preposition phrase «من ذلك» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «شر», and «مثوبة» is tamyīz (specification).
